entries.description: SMOKE_BALL vtable +0x08 (00498084), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). Installs TSObjVtable, deletes the shape instance at +0x34 through its own vtable +0x18 with flags 3, and Mem_Deletes this on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0040970d; class record at 00409633

entries.name: FlatObj_LoadResources
entries.description: (selector): sets the byte 00498098 to 1; with name flat for a selector of 0 and flat2 otherwise, Shape_LoadAllRoots(&g_FlatShapes, dts\<name>, 0x140008, 0), the count to g_FlatShapeCount; Resource_Load(dba\<name>) into 004a9722, BitmapArray_PackToAtlas of it into 004a9726, then GLBitmapArray_Dtor on the loaded one and 004a9722 = 0; every flat shape's +0x26 (its bound bitmap array pointer) set to 004a9722's address; g_FlatObjPool = Pool_Init of 150 elements of 0x41 bytes; g_FlatObjDeleteQueue = an 8-byte queue of 25 entries (+6 = 0x19, a 100-byte array, count 0). World_LoadTheater calls it last with World_FlatSetSelector. Docs: docs/retail/simulation/ground-shapes.md.

entries.name: Sim_FlushDeleteQueue
entries.description: One-line wrapper running ObjectPool_FlushDeleteQueue(g_FlatObjDeleteQueue, g_FlatObjPool). Registered at subsystem phase 5, which Sim_RenderFrame runs at the start of every frame's draw, and called again at the end of Mech_ComponentDamageWrite, which commits the ground shapes a lost leg or a vanishing chassis queued during the damage write.

entries.name: FlatObj_Draw
entries.description: FlatObj vtable slot 0: SimObject_ConformToTerrain, SimObject_InstallModelTransform, then the shape instance's (obj+0x34) own vtable +0x1c draw.

entries.name: FlatObj_RegisterSubsystem
entries.description: Static-init registrar for the FlatObj pool: registers Sim_FlushDeleteQueue at phase 5 and nulls g_FlatObjPool.

entries.name: FlatObj_StaticDtor
entries.description: FlatObj_RegisterSubsystem's _EXIT_ routine (Borland _EXIT_ entry 004a7c00): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr and Mem_Deletes g_FlatObjPool when it is set.

entries.name: ObjPool_FlatObj_Dtor
entries.description: ObjPool<FlatObj>'s destructor, the dtor its class record (0x8 bytes, at 0040999c) names: (pool, flags): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr; when the pool is not null, Mem_Delete of its entry buffer at +0 when that is set, then Mem_Delete of the pool when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: Meteor_FlushDeletes
entries.description: ObjectPool_FlushDeleteQueue(g_MeteorDeleteQueue, g_MeteorPool). Meteor_RegisterSubsystem registers it as the meteor module's subsystem phase-5 stub.

entries.name: Meteor_LoadResources
entries.description: Startup loader for the METEOR (drop pod) subsystem, registered into DBSIM's subsystem-loader table by Meteor_RegisterSubsystem: allocates the object pool at g_MeteorPool and its free list, loads the dts\meteor shape group and the dba\impact texture bank, and binds that bank into every shape it loaded.

entries.name: Meteor_Construct
entries.description: Builds a drop pod aimed at a picked point. It is NOT dropped straight down: it draws a random heading (kept at +0x10) and a HORIZONTAL RUN-IN of 70000 plus Math_RandomBelow(25000) units, starts that far short of the target along that heading, and flies in at a flat 2000 units per tick. The launch height is derived from the run-in -- n = runIn/2000 ticks, height = (n*n>>1)*50, so 30600 to 55200 units -- and added to the target point's own Z, with vz = -height/n, so the pod is back at the target's Z when it is over the target. Both axes are flown at constant velocity, so the descent is a straight line. Reading the 70000-95000 figure as an altitude puts the pod at twice the height it belongs at. Velocity at +0x45 (vz at +0x49); +0x32, the landed flag +0x4b, the blast latch +0x4c, the open-animation counter +0x4d and the whistle latch +0x51 cleared; delivered group at +0x55; the opening shape's TSShapeInstance at +0x41. It writes no type tag at +4, so a pod keeps the zero Pool_Init left: tag 0, which ObjList_IsBeyondDrawDistance gives its own draw distance.

entries.name: Meteor_Render
entries.description: Draws a drop pod: while falling, the plain shape; once landed (+0x4b set), builds its rotation matrix from its euler triple if stale and draws the opening-animation shape instance at +0x41 instead.

entries.name: Meteor_Tick
entries.description: The drop pod's per-tick update, called from Sim_MainTick (0045f5fb is the one call es2_xref finds). Falling phase (+0x4b clear): integrates position by the velocity at +0x45, pitches the shape to Math_Atan2Bam(2000, vz) and zeroes +0x32, plays sound 0x2f (podin2) once (latch +0x51) below absolute height 50000, and on ground contact (Terrain_HeightQuery) sets the landed flag, zeroes the pitch, snaps to ground, plays sound 0x30 (podland) and calls Damage_ExplosiveBlastSweep(pos, 3000, 10000, 0, null), setting +0x4c if that answers non-zero. Both sounds go through Sound_PlayAt at ViewObjectPtr + 4, the camera's own position, not the pod's. Landed phase: while +0x4d >> 10 is below the opening shape's (+0x41) frame count, writes it as the shape's frame and advances +0x4d by Math_IntegrateRateOverTick(0x5dc). Once it reaches the count, when the pod carries a group (+0x55): unless +0x4c is set, copies its position onto the group's leader and clears the group's +0x14 (the moment the group enters the mission); then, either way, allocates a FlatObj from g_FlatObjPool (004a9711) on g_FlatShapes root 3 at its position, without checking the allocation before writing the position. Then destroys the shape instance at +0x41 and returns 1; otherwise returns 0.

entries.name: Meteor_RegisterSubsystem
entries.description: Static-init registrar for the METEOR subsystem (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7a92, priority 0x20): registers Meteor_LoadResources at phase 2 and Meteor_FlushDeletes at phase 5, and nulls g_MeteorPool. Meteor_StaticDtor is its _EXIT_ counterpart.

entries.name: Meteor_StaticDtor
entries.description: Meteor_RegisterSubsystem's _EXIT_ routine (Borland _EXIT_ entry 004a7c06): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr and Mem_Deletes g_MeteorPool when it is set.

entries.name: ObjPool_METEOR_Dtor
entries.description: ObjPool<METEOR>'s destructor, the dtor its class record (0x8 bytes, at 00409fe4) names: (pool, flags): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr; when the pool is not null, Mem_Delete of its entry buffer at +0 when that is set, then Mem_Delete of the pool when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: Projectile_LoadResources
entries.description: The projectile module's phase-2 subsystem loader (registered by Projectile_RegisterSubsystem): builds g_ProjectilePool (Pool_Init: 160 entries of 0x66 bytes, the LoosePool<PROJECTILE> every rocket, bullet, beam tracer and grenade is drawn from) and g_ProjectileDeleteQueue (8-byte list header, capacity 0x50, over Mem_NewArray(0x140)).

entries.name: Projectile_FlushDeletes
entries.description: ObjectPool_FlushDeleteQueue(g_ProjectileDeleteQueue, g_ProjectilePool). Projectile_RegisterSubsystem registers it as the projectile module's subsystem phase-5 stub.

entries.name: Bullet_Draw
entries.description: The Bullet class's vtable slot 0. Sets DAT_004a5b1c = 0 for the duration of the call, which is what makes a projectile's textured polys draw unlit (see TSTexture4Poly_Render), installs the object's frame as the model transform, renders the shape instance at obj+0x34, and restores DAT_004a5b1c from DAT_004a5b20.

entries.name: Projectile_RegisterSubsystem
entries.description: Static-init registrar of the projectile module (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7a98, priority 0x20): registers Projectile_LoadResources at subsystem phase 2 and Projectile_FlushDeletes at phase 5, nulls g_ProjectilePool and counts one live destructor. Projectile_StaticDtor is its _EXIT_ counterpart.

entries.name: Projectile_StaticDtor
entries.description: Projectile_RegisterSubsystem's _EXIT_ routine (Borland _EXIT_ entry 004a7c0c): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr and Mem_Deletes g_ProjectilePool.

entries.name: LoosePool_PROJECTILE_Dtor
entries.description: LoosePool<PROJECTILE>'s destructor, the dtor its class record (0x8 bytes, at 0040a1b5) names: (pool, flags): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr; when the pool is not null, Mem_Delete of its buffer at +0, then Mem_Delete of the pool when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: Rocket_GetTypeRecord
entries.description: getType() accessor: returns the instance's 14-byte ROCKETS.DAT record, maybe_RocketTypeTable_Unguided + instance.typeIndex (byte @ +0x41) * 0xe.

entries.name: Rocket_HomingSteer
entries.description: Missile seeker. Steers only with a target (+0x56) and, when the owner is locally piloted (owner+0xa3), only while that target is still the owner's selected target (owner+0x1a4). Subtype 2 (ARM) steers only while the target emits (target +0x96 scanner or +0xa1 jammer). The lead is the target's component +0x5a through target vtable +0x58 when non-negative, else the aim point (vtable +0x24) or the origin; Math_EulerToward(lead, self) less the round's euler gives the pitch and heading errors. Subtype 3 sets owner+0xb5 to suppress AI weapon selection for a tick; subtypes 0, 1 and 4, while the FIRING owner's +0x9c spoof flag is set (ECM), move each error in [-0xc00, 0xbff] by 0xc00 toward the opposite sign. Each error then goes through Math_RateLimitedMoveToward at 0x500 and Math_IntegrateRateOverTick onto pitch (+0xc) and heading (+0x10).

entries.name: Rocket_PlayerSteer
entries.description: The electro-optical missile's player steer, not a ballistic variant. Gate input+0x0d is the fire trigger (0x4d2357). Held: reads the two axes the block's camera-axis pointers +0x22 and +0x26 address (the steering and throttle axes while DAT_004d25aa routes the controls to the round), subtracts Math_IntegrateRateOverTick(Math_Q8Multiply(0x500, *+0x22)) from the heading (+0x10) and adds the same of *+0x26 to the pitch (+0x0c), with no rate limit or deadband, marks the frame stale (+0x32 = 0) and zeroes the trigger and both axes, so the player's fire path never sees the trigger while a round is flown. Released: drops the round's target (+0x56) and rewrites its subtype id (+0x41) to 0. See docs/retail/simulation/rockets.md.

entries.name: Rocket_TickUpdate
entries.description: Per-tick launcher-round update, vtable +0x14. Steps the shape cell-anim frame on ROCKETS.DAT +0x08/+0x0a (the exhaust flame, NOT a seeker reacquire); age +1 vs record +0x02 in ticks; damped burn speed += Math_IntegrateRateOverTick(record +0x04) averaged with the opening speed, capped at PROJ.DAT Speed; Rocket_PlayerSteer for a locally-simulated subtype 3, raising DAT_004d25aa, else Rocket_HomingSteer; Sim_RaycastObjectList over this tick step with record +0x06 as slack. When the round ends (lifetime or hit): a locally-simulated subtype 3 round calls Input_LatchButton(1, 1) and clears the trigger 004d2357; the round in DAT_0049c394 ending before its lifetime raises DAT_0049c398. Last, on every tick: for a round whose owner is not locally piloted (owner+0xa3 clear), sound 0x32 within 40000 of ViewObjectPtr, latched at round+0x06 and re-armed when the round leaves that range.

entries.name: Rocket_LoadTypeTable_Unguided
entries.description: rocket.cpp. Loads the Type-0 rocket type table (14-byte/0xe stride, confirmed via IMUL-style indexing).

entries.name: Rocket_Construct
entries.description: Constructs the ROCKET class (rocket.cpp), the launcher round: PROJ.DAT Type 0, 5 entries, each with a real Speed, armor damage well above shield damage, and splash factor 500.

entries.name: Rocket_Fire
entries.description: Rocket_Fire(subtypeId, muzzleWorldPoint, aimEulerTriple, launcher, ownerTravelSpeed) -- spawns one PROJ.DAT Type-0 rocket from the effect pool g_ProjectilePool through Rocket_Construct(round, subtypeId); it makes no call to Grenade_Construct. A failed Pool_Alloc skips the construction and the stores below go through the null pointer. Position +0x26 = the muzzle point, euler +0xc = the aim triple, +0x32 = 0, launcher at +0x4a, speed +0x52 = ownerTravelSpeed + literal 500, +0x42..+0x49 and the age +0x54 zeroed. Lock gate: 1 when the launcher is not locally piloted (+0xa3 clear) and the subtype is 3, else the launcher's vtable +0x6c(launcher, subtype) -- Mech_MissileLockState for a machine, SimObject_MissileLockState_Always (1) for a flyer or a structure. With the gate, +0x56 = the launcher's +0x1a4 (selected target) and, when that is non-null, +0x5a = the target's vtable +0x54(target, &round+0xc), the component the round steers at; without it +0x56 = 0. A locally piloted launcher's round is stored in DAT_0049c394, the round the missile camera rides. Plays ROCKETS.DAT +0x0c + 10 at the muzzle (Sound_PlayAt).

entries.name: Rocket_RegisterSubsystem
entries.description: Static-init registrar of rocket.cpp (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7a9e, priority 0x20): registers Rocket_LoadTypeTable_Unguided at subsystem phase 2, and nothing else.

entries.name: Rocket_Dtor
entries.description: Deleting destructor of the rocket class -- slot +0x8 of RocketVtable (00498448).
entries.source: tools/ghidra_scripts/known_vtables.json (Destructor slot); disassembly of the vtable-pointer stores

entries.name: Grenade_GetTypeRecord
entries.description: (obj): g_GrenadeTypeTable + obj+0x41 (the subtype byte) * 8 -- the grenade twin of Bullet_GetTypeRecord, over an 8-byte record.

entries.name: Grenade_LoadResourcesNoOp
entries.description: The grenade module's phase-2 subsystem loader, which Grenade_RegisterSubsystem registers: a lone RET. So the grenade module loads no type table and no shapes; g_GrenadeTypeTable and g_GrenadeShapes, which Grenade_Construct reads, are not filled here.

entries.name: Grenade_Construct
entries.description: No reference found (es2_xref UNREFERENCED, no late start nearby), and the class is GRENADE -- its Borland class record at 0040acdc names it, with PROJECTILE (0040c2d0) as its one base, as for ROCKET and BULLET. See docs/retail/formats/borland-rtti.md. Constructs a PROJ.DAT Type-3 object. A whole-image scan for 0040ac3c -- every section, bare LE dword and E8/E9 rel32 targets -- finds it nowhere but its own prologue, so no caller is found; its vtable GrenadeVtable (004984fc) has Grenade_TickNoOp (return 0) in the per-tick slot, so an instance would never move or die. No weapon template's PROJ.DAT index names the retail Type-3 records 7-9, and GrenadeMount_FireDispatch calls Grenade_FireNoOp instead; see docs/retail/formats/proj-dat.md#open.

entries.name: Grenade_FireNoOp
entries.description: An empty body in the GRENADE class's code, called by GrenadeMount_FireDispatch where the other fire dispatches call Rocket_Fire or Bullet_FireBurst -- so the grenade mount spends a round and launches nothing.

entries.name: Grenade_TickNoOp
entries.description: GRENADE vtable +0x14, the tick slot: returns 0 and does nothing. For the projectile tick a non-zero return is what makes Sim_MainTick free the object (BeamTracer_LifeTick).

entries.name: Grenade_NoOp
entries.description: push ebp / mov ebp,esp / pop ebp / ret, among GRENADE's own functions. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Grenade_ReturnZero
entries.description: Returns 0, among GRENADE's own functions. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Grenade_RegisterSubsystem
entries.description: Static-init registrar of the grenade module (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7aa4, priority 0x20): registers Grenade_LoadResourcesNoOp at subsystem phase 2, and nothing else.

entries.name: Grenade_Dtor
entries.description: Deleting destructor of the projectile class whose vtable (004984fc) no constructor installs -- slot +0x8 of that table.
entries.source: tools/ghidra_scripts/known_vtables.json (Destructor slot); disassembly of the vtable-pointer stores

entries.name: Bullet_GetTypeRecord
entries.description: return DAT_004a977c + obj[0x41] * 14 -- the BULLETS.DAT record for a bullet's subtype id. The table is indexed by the PROJ.DAT record's subtype id, exactly as BEAM.DAT is.

entries.name: Bullet_LoadResources
entries.description: bullet.cpp's init (named by the BULLET.CPP string at 00498601). Loads dat\bullets into DAT_004a977c as a count plus that many 14-byte records, dts\bullets into the shape array DAT_004a9784, and dba\bullets into DAT_004a978a, packing its frames with BitmapArray_PackToAtlas; finally binds &DAT_004a978a as every bullet shape's +0x26 bound-DBA context.

entries.name: Bullet_Construct
entries.description: Constructs a travelling round, the PROJ.DAT Type-2 Bullet: SimObjectBase_Constructor on the shape the BULLETS.DAT record's model (+0x00) indexes, vtable ProjectileBaseVtable then BulletVtable (00498628), obj+4 = 3, the subtype id at obj+0x41, obj+0x4e = Proj_LookupRecord(2, subtypeId) (the PROJ.DAT record), and obj+0x59 = the BULLETS.DAT record's +0x06 animation interval. Subtype 9 is the plasma cannon's.

entries.name: Bullet_HomingSteer
entries.description: The plasma round's guidance, and a steer of the object's EULER ANGLES rather than of a velocity: takes the bearing from the shot to obj+0x5b's vtable +0x24 aim node (through the target's frame) or, when that returns none, its position +0x26, via Math_EulerToward; moves euler[0] and euler[2] toward it through Math_RateLimitedMoveToward capped at 0x280 per 125 ms, integrates over the tick, and stores 0 to the frame-valid word at obj+0x32, so the next reader rebuilds the rotation. Returns the euler[2] bearing error before this tick's move, which Bullet_TickUpdate's proximity fuze tests.

entries.name: Bullet_TickUpdate
entries.description: The travelling round's tick. Steps the shape's animation frame when the BULLETS.DAT record's +0x06 is nonzero; ages the round by Math_IntegrateRateOverTick(0x200) and returns 1 (remove) once the age +0x54 passes lifetime (+0x02) * 0x200; runs Bullet_HomingSteer when +0x5b holds a target. Moves Math_IntegrateRateOverTick(+0x52) along the frame's Y axis, sweeping that segment through Sim_RaycastObjectList with a shot record whose two damage figures are scaled Q10 by the power +0x56 when it is nonzero. Subtype 9 (plasma): a proximity fuze trips when the homing error exceeds 0x4000 in magnitude and the target is under 2000 units away, and skips the raycast; Bullet_StashDirectFireDamage stashes both figures, the record's damage and splash are zeroed, the armour figure is scaled by Damage_ScaleByDifficulty, and on contact or fuze Damage_ExplosiveBlastSweep runs at 4000 units. With no contact the round moves; contact returns 1.

entries.name: Bullet_Fire
entries.description: Bullet_Fire(subtypeId, muzzleWorldPoint, aimEulerTriple, ownerMech) -- spawns one travelling PROJ.DAT Type-2 Bullet from the effect pool g_ProjectilePool through Bullet_Construct. Copies the muzzle point to obj+0x26 (the frame's translation), stores the euler triple at obj+0x0c with components 0 and 2 displaced by (spread*2 & random) - spread from the BULLETS.DAT record's +0x0a, and zeroes the frame-valid word +0x32. Stores ownerMech at +0x4a, zeroes the 8 bytes at +0x42, the age +0x54, the power +0x56 and the homing target +0x5b, and sets +0x5f = 0x400. Sets obj+0x52 = ownerMech->vtable+0x38 (travel speed) + the PROJ.DAT record's Speed (+0x0a), truncated to 16 bits. With the BULLETS.DAT record's +0x0c nonzero, sets +0x61 = 0x400 / its lifetime (+0x02). Plays sound id record+0x08 + 10 at the muzzle point. Returns the object so Bullet_FirePowered can add to it.

entries.name: Bullet_FirePowered
entries.description: Bullet_Fire plus two writes: obj+0x56 = the capacitor charge the shot was fired at (which scales both damage figures Q10 in Bullet_TickUpdate; zero leaves them at face value), and for subtypeId 9 only (the plasma cannon) obj+0x5b = ownerMech+0x1a4, the firing machine's selected target, which is what makes that one subtype home.

entries.name: Bullet_RegisterSubsystem
entries.description: Static-init registrar of bullet.cpp (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7aaa, priority 0x20): registers Bullet_LoadResources at subsystem phase 2, and nothing else.

entries.name: Bullet_Dtor
entries.description: Deleting destructor of the bullet class -- slot +0x8 of BulletVtable (00498628).
entries.source: tools/ghidra_scripts/known_vtables.json (Destructor slot); disassembly of the vtable-pointer stores

entries.name: Beam_LoadResourceTables
entries.description: Beam module init, named by the BEAM.CPP string at 00498781. Builds the 120-entry vertex-index table BeamQuadIndexTable as (i>>1) + BeamQuadIndexOffsets[i&3]; loads dat\beam (int16 count then count x 3 int16 {halfWidth, paletteIndex, dbaFrame}) into BeamAppearanceTable; loads dba\beamtex and converts it through BitmapArray_PackToAtlas into BeamTextureDescriptors.

entries.name: BeamTracer_Ctor
entries.description: Beam tracer constructor; vtable BeamTracerVtable (004987c4), type 3. A straight beam stores two points (muzzle, hit) at +0x58, quad count 1 at +0x54, jagged flag 0 at +0x55, and arms the life timer at +0x5d to 0x38 -- 27 ms in the Q8-of-125ms tick unit, less than one SimTickDelta, so a tracer never survives a second tick. Subtype ids 1 and 7 (ELF, ELF2) take a jagged branch instead: nodeCount = (char)(Math_DistanceBetweenPoints >> 10) + 1 at +0x54 and pointCount = nodeCount*2+2 at +0x56, walking a step that is the start->end delta through Math_NormalizeVec3ToLength(0x400). The LAST node restarts from the exact endpoint rather than the walked position; every node but the FIRST -- the last one included -- is then jittered on each axis by Math_RandomNext()&0x7f, one-sided 0..127. Each node writes a pair: points[2k] with BEAM.DAT's half-width added to its z, points[2k+1] without, so the ribbon stands vertically in the world.
entries.signature: void * __cdecl BeamTracer_Ctor(void *tracer, short subtypeId, int *startPoint, int *endPoint, void *owner)

entries.name: BeamTracer_Dtor
entries.description: Beam tracer vtable +0x08. Frees the point array at +0x58 and chains to the base destructor.

entries.name: Beam_ClipSegmentToNearPlane
entries.description: Clips a pair of view-space points against the near plane DAT_006c60b0, moving whichever end is short up to the plane by Q16 interpolation. Returns 0 when both ends are behind it.

entries.name: BeamTracer_Draw
entries.description: Beam tracer vtable slot 0. Installs {0, BEAM.DAT colour index} at the graphics context's +0x22c -- which is the FILL BRUSH, since Raster_InstallRenderContext sets the clip block to ctx+4 and so ctx+0x22c is Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch's clipBlock+0x228 -- then publishes the point-list globals and loops over the object's quad count. Subtype 1/7 (ELF/ELF2) run Poly_ProjectIndexedVertices, Poly_ClipRingToNearPlane when that returns non-zero, then PolyFill_Fill: a flat fill of that palette index, no texture. THAT BRANCH DOES NOT RETURN -- control falls through into the straight-beam code below, which draws points[0]->points[1] (for a chain, node zero with and without the width: a half-width stub at the muzzle, redrawn once per quad). Straight path: both points to view space (Raster_ModelToView), near-plane clip (Beam_ClipSegmentToNearPlane), project (Raster_PerspectiveDivide / Raster_ProjectToScreen), half-width in pixels per end via Raster_PerspectiveScale floored at 2 (a HALF-width floor, so four pixels across), four vertices stepped along the segment's 2D perpendicular in Q11, UVs with u along the beam's length and v across its width, then Raster_DrawPolygon mode 0, which has no colour lookup. Writes no z.

entries.name: Bullet_FireBurst
entries.description: Fire-burst/tracer spawner, called as Bullet_FireBurst(subtypeId, shotTransform, range, ownerMech, power). Builds the shot record -- ray {transform, range, 200} plus Math_Q10Multiply(power, PROJ.DAT armor damage), Math_Q10Multiply(power, PROJ.DAT shield damage), the PROJ.DAT splash factor, the ImpactFX table pointer and the owner -- and calls Sim_RaycastObjectList synchronously to resolve the hit before any tracer visual spawns. This is the beam/hitscan (PROJ.DAT Type 4, always Speed=0) mechanism: no persisting travelling object. Splits the tracer into 5000-unit segments (BeamTracer_Ctor) over the resolved distance.

entries.name: BeamTracer_LifeTick
entries.description: Beam tracer vtable +0x14: one Math_CountdownTimerTick on the timer at +0x5c, returning true at zero. Sim_MainTick frees the object on true, and walks this pool before the machine list so a tracer spawned during a machine update is not counted down until the tick after.

entries.name: Beam_RegisterSubsystem
entries.description: Static-init registrar of beam.cpp (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7ab0, priority 0x20): registers Beam_LoadResourceTables at subsystem phase 2, and nothing else.

entries.name: ProjectileBase_Dtor
entries.description: Deleting destructor of the projectile base class -- slot +0x8 of ProjectileBaseVtable (004987a0). Reinstalls its own table at 0040c345 and then the super-base's (004a0b98) at 0040c353, which is what establishes the derivation. Takes a flags argument whose low bit asks it to free the object, via 0047743c.
entries.source: tools/ghidra_scripts/known_vtables.json (Destructor slot); disassembly of the vtable-pointer stores

entries.name: Collision_RaySphereTest
entries.description: One sphere against the ray in muzzle space. Rejects on an unsigned Y compare against the working ray length, then tests the off-axis distance against clearance + radius in 16-bit arithmetic ((ushort)(offAxis + reach) < (ushort)(reach * 2)) because the doubled reach can overflow a short. On a hit it clips DAT_004a9894 to the entry point, alongAxis - (reach - offAxis), floored at 0.

entries.name: Collision_RayNodeOriginTest
entries.description: (radius): Collision_RaySphereTest(Collision_NodeToMuzzleTransform + 0x14, radius, 0) -- the current node's origin (its transform's translation) as a sphere of the given radius against the ray, without shortening it. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Collision_ClusterBoundTest
entries.description: Tests one cluster's load-time bounding sphere against the ray: centre into muzzle space, unsigned compare of Y against radius plus the working ray length (DAT_004a9894), and Math_FastMagnitude2D of X/Z under radius plus the ray clearance (DAT_004a9898). The cheap gate before Collision_ClusterSphereTest.

entries.name: Collision_ClusterSphereTest
entries.description: Walks a cluster's child spheres, transforming each centre into muzzle space and calling Collision_RaySphereTest with update enabled. Returns the (now shortened) working ray length + 1 if any sphere was struck, 0 otherwise.

entries.name: Collision_ComputeBoundingSphere
entries.description: Builds one cluster's bounding sphere from its child spheres: AABB of the children each inflated by its own radius, center = AABB midpoint, radius = Math_FastMagnitude3D of the half-extents. That approximation runs from about 8% under to about 9% over a true Euclidean radius depending on the box's proportions, so the bound is not exactly circumscribing -- behaviour, not an artefact. Called at load, never per tick.

entries.name: Collision_ClusterReach
entries.description: (cluster, offset or null): the largest Math_FastMagnitude3D(sphere centre + offset) + radius over the cluster's spheres, as an int16 -- how far the cluster reaches from the origin once moved by offset. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Collision_ReadSphereArray
entries.description: Reads a cluster's int16 sphere count into the record's +0 and, when count & 0x1fff is nonzero, that many 8-byte { int16 x, y, z, radius } spheres into +2. The mask is only a zero-test -- the allocation and the read both use the unmasked value, and no retail record sets the top bits. Was named Collision_LoadSubMeshIndices; the 8-byte records are spheres, not mesh indices.

entries.name: Collision_CopyClusterSpheres
entries.description: (dst, src, offset): dst's sphere count (+0) = src's; when it is not zero, dst+2 = a new array of that many 8-byte spheres (Rtl_VectorNew with CollisionSphere_ElementCtor) holding src's spheres with the int16 offset triple added to each centre and the radius unchanged. dst's previous array is not freed. Collision_ReplaceClusterIfMatch calls it.

entries.name: CollisionSphere_ElementCtor
entries.description: (sphere): returns its argument -- the per-element constructor Rtl_VectorNew runs over a cluster's 8-byte {x, y, z, radius} sphere array, in Collision_ReadSphereArray and Collision_CopyClusterSpheres.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 0040c8be and its vector-new sites 0040c7f6, 0040c852

entries.name: Collision_ClusterTest
entries.description: One collision cluster against the ray: Collision_ClusterBoundTest on the load-time bounding sphere first, and Collision_ClusterSphereTest over the children only if it passes.

entries.name: Mech_ComponentGeometryTest_Candidate
entries.description: (node, object, objectToMuzzle, activeFlags): one collision-model node of Mech_SelectStruckComponent's walk, not a coarse test. Builds the node-to-muzzle transform -- a copy of objectToMuzzle for node id < 0, otherwise the node's posed transform (shape vtable +0x20 part lookup through obj+0x34, identity at 006c572c for a missing part) concatenated with it -- and points Collision_NodeToMuzzleTransform at it. Then for each of the node's 16-byte clusters (count at +4, array at +6) whose component's active flag is set, runs Collision_ClusterTest, and on a non-zero result stores it in DAT_004a989c and the cluster's component (+6) in DAT_004a98a0. Returns 0.

entries.name: Mech_SelectStruckComponent
entries.description: (model, object, rayRecord, objectToMuzzle, activeFlags): the shared sphere-model hit test, used by all three classes' direct-fire hit tests. Sets the result globals -- component DAT_004a98a0 = -1, hit DAT_004a989c = 0, working distance DAT_004a9894 = the ray length (ray+4), clearance DAT_004a9898 = ray+8 -- and runs Mech_ComponentGeometryTest_Candidate on each of the model's nodes (count at +0, 10-byte nodes at +2). Copies the hit and component to the 6-byte result at DAT_004a98a2 and returns a pointer to it, or null when nothing was hit. No randomness: the last cluster that hit is the one returned.

entries.name: Collision_FindClusterInNode
entries.description: (node, componentIndex, nodeIndexOut): linear search over one node's 16-byte clusters (count at node+4, array at node+6) for the first whose component index (+6) matches; on a match writes the node's id (+0) out and returns the cluster, otherwise returns null.

entries.name: Collision_FindClusterForComponent
entries.description: (collisionRecord, componentIndex, nodeIndexOut): walks the record's nodes (count at +0, 10-byte nodes at +2) through Collision_FindClusterInNode and returns the first cluster naming componentIndex, its node index written out, or null when no node has one.

entries.name: Collision_CollectNodeComponents
entries.description: (node, out): writes each of the node's 16-byte clusters' component index (cluster+6) to out[i] and returns the node's cluster count (+4) -- Collision_CollectNodeAnchors without the node ids and points.

entries.name: Collision_CollectNodeAnchors
entries.description: (node, components, nodeIds, points): for each of the node's int16 count (+4) 16-byte cluster records at +6, writes the record's +6 component index to components[i], a pointer to the record's +8 sphere centre to points[i] and the node's own int16 +0 to nodeIds[i]; returns the count. Collision_CollectComponentAnchors calls it per node.

entries.name: Collision_CollectComponentIds
entries.description: (model, out): Collision_CollectNodeComponents over each of the model's 10-byte nodes in turn, appending, and returns the total -- the component-index-only twin of Collision_CollectComponentAnchors. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Collision_CollectComponentAnchors
entries.description: Walks a loaded .COL model's nodes and emits one (componentIndex, nodeIndex, pointer to the cluster's load-time bounding-sphere centre) triple per cluster into three caller-supplied parallel arrays, returning the count. Per node it delegates to Collision_CollectNodeAnchors, which strides the 16-byte cluster records reading componentIndex at +6 and taking the address of the bound centre at +8. Called once, from Mech_ConfigureLoadout, feeding HercPiece_BindComponentAnchors.

entries.name: CollisionTable_Reserve
entries.description: (n): returns CollisionTable_Count (004987dc) and adds n to it -- the collision twin of DmgTable_Reserve.

entries.name: CollisionTable_Alloc
entries.description: When CollisionTable_Count is non-zero, CollisionTable_Array = Mem_NewArray(CollisionTable_Count * 6). DBSim_LoadScriptDat calls it after DmgTable_Alloc.

entries.name: Collision_ReadCluster
entries.description: Reads a cluster's component index into the record's +6, then its sphere array via Collision_ReadSphereArray into +0/+2. The component index is what makes a destroyed section stop blocking shots. Was named Collision_LoadSubSphereFlag: the value it reads is the component index, not a flag, and the branch it guards is on the read succeeding rather than on the value.

entries.name: Collision_ReadNode
entries.description: Reads one node of a collision model: int16 node index (-1 = the object's own frame, otherwise an index resolved through the shape instance's node-transform array) and int16 cluster count, then that many 16-byte clusters via Collision_ReadCluster. Was named Collision_LoadSubSpheres, which described the shape one level off.

entries.name: Collision_ComputeAllBoundingSpheres
entries.description: (node): for each of the node's int16 cluster count (+4) 16-byte clusters at +6, Collision_ComputeBoundingSphere(cluster, cluster+8) and stores the returned radius at cluster+0xe. Callers found by es2_xref: Collision_LoadRecordArray, once per node as it is read, and Collision_ReplaceClusters, on the node whose cluster it replaced.

entries.name: Collision_LoadRecordArray
entries.description: Reads one object's whole collision model: an int16 node count, then that many 10-byte nodes via Collision_ReadNode, each post-processed by Collision_ComputeAllBoundingSpheres. Called per structure type against dat/BASECOL.DAT (from Base_LoadResources, 00405fac) and per mech/flyer type against col/<NAME>.COL (from Collision_RegisterObject). Format and retail verification in docs/retail/simulation/hit-detection.md.

entries.name: Collision_RegisterObject
entries.description: collide.cpp. Top-level collision-model entry point: allocates the next slot in the fixed collision-object table, then calls Collision_LoadRecordArray.

entries.name: Collision_ReplaceClusterIfMatch
entries.description: (cluster, sources, offsets, count): finds the first i < count whose sources[i] cluster has the same component index (+6) as cluster, runs Collision_CopyClusterSpheres(cluster, sources[i], offsets[i]) for it and returns 1; returns 0 when none matches.

entries.name: Collision_ReplaceNodeCluster
entries.description: (node, sources, offsets, count): Collision_ReplaceClusterIfMatch over the node's clusters in order, stopping at the first that matches; returns whether one did.

entries.name: Collision_ReplaceClusters
entries.description: (model, sources, offsets, count): Collision_ReplaceNodeCluster over the model's nodes in order; at the first node where a cluster was replaced it reruns Collision_ComputeAllBoundingSpheres on that node and returns, so one call replaces one cluster. Mech_ConfigureLoadout calls it once per fitted weapon mount with count 1: the weapon template's cluster (template+0x12, its component index set to .GL +0x17 + 19) and WeaponMount_MuzzleOffset, which puts the weapon's own hit spheres into the chassis model's cluster for that mount.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0040cec0 and at its call in Mech_ConfigureLoadout (0041778f); docs/retail/formats/collision-spheres.md

entries.name: CollisionCluster_ElementCtor
entries.description: (cluster): returns its argument -- the per-element constructor Collision_ReadNode hands Rtl_VectorNew for a node's 16-byte cluster array; the LEA of +8 is the inlined empty constructor of the bounding-sphere centre.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 0040cf04 and its vector-new site 0040cc85

entries.name: Component_AllDependentsDestroyed
entries.description: (piece, dependentDamage): true when every entry of the piece's dependent list (count at piece+6, 4-byte entries at piece+8, internal index at entry+2) holds a negative damage value, i.e. is destroyed; true for an empty list. es2_xref finds one call, from Component_IsFullyDestroyed.

entries.name: Component_SpillIntoDependents
entries.description: (piece, dependentDamage, damage, dependentMaxima): pours damage into the piece's dependents one at a time. Each round sums the spill weight (entry+0) of every live dependent (damage >= 0); a zero total returns true at once. Otherwise it draws Math_RandomBelow(total) on the shared generator, walks the list subtracting each live entry's weight, and hands the first one that takes the draw below zero to Component_AddDamage against that internal's maximum, the excess coming back through the damage argument. A spill that destroys the dependent goes round again with the excess; a spill that leaves it standing returns false. So it returns true only once every dependent is destroyed -- which is what Component_ApplyDamageAndCascade requires before it will cascade. An internal with a maximum of 0 is destroyed by any spill, a spill of 0 included.

entries.name: HercPiece_ReadRecord
entries.description: Loads one 18-byte .DMG HercPiece record: max health, debris-flags index pair, bone id (bone/destruction-group key), destruction-flags bitfield, dependent sub-component list pointer+count.

entries.name: HercPiece_CopyRecord
entries.description: (dst, src): copies the 0x12-byte piece record, then gives dst its own copy of the dependent list: Mem_NewArray(count * 4) for the int16 count at +6, filled from src's list (+8).

entries.name: HercPiece_LoadTable
entries.description: Loads the .DMG per-mech component table: the int16 internal count (+0xa) and that many int16 internal maxima (array at +4), then the int16 piece count (+8) and that many 18-byte HercPiece records (array at +0, via HercPiece_ReadRecord).

entries.name: HercPiece_SetInternalMaxima
entries.description: (pieceTable, indices, values, count): for each i < count stores values[i] in the table's int16 internal-maximum array (+4) at indices[i]. Mech_ConfigureLoadout calls it once per weapon mount with count 1.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0040d128; table layout from HercPiece_LoadTable

entries.name: Damage_LoadMechDmgFile
entries.description: damage.cpp dispatch/setup that opens dmg\[herc].DMG (filename built from the mech's own name string) and drives HercPiece_LoadTable. Called from the mech constructor.

entries.name: DmgTable_Reserve
entries.description: (n): returns DmgTable_Count (00498856) and adds n to it. maybe_MechTypeSlot_Allocate and FlyerType_Register reserve one each.

entries.name: DmgTable_Alloc
entries.description: When DmgTable_Count is non-zero, DmgTable_Array = Mem_NewArray(DmgTable_Count * 0xc). DBSim_LoadScriptDat calls it after GunLayout_AllocTable.

entries.name: HercPiece_ReplacePieces
entries.description: (pieceTable, indices, records, count): for each i < count overwrites the 0x12-byte piece at indices[i] (array at +0) with HercPiece_CopyRecord of records[i]. The piece's previous dependent list is not freed. Mech_ConfigureLoadout calls it once per weapon mount with count 1.

entries.name: HercPiece_BindComponentAnchors
entries.description: Writes the .COL-derived anchors into the .DMG piece table: for each of count entries, piece[componentIndices[i]] at stride 0x12 gets +0x0c = nodeIndices[i] and +0x0e = points[i]. These are the two runtime-only HercPiece fields Mech_ComponentPosition reads. The write is UNGUARDED, so the last cluster naming a component wins; every retail mech .COL names each component exactly once, so it never bites.
entries.signature: void __cdecl HercPiece_BindComponentAnchors(int *pieceTable, short count, short *componentIndices, short *nodeIndices, int **points)

entries.name: Component_AllocDamageArrays
entries.description: Allocates the header of pointers at mech+0x206: a 22-entry dependent-subpiece DAMAGE array, a 29-entry main-component DAMAGE array, and a 29-entry active-flag array (all zeroed except the flag array, filled 0x01). Zeroed means undamaged, not destroyed -- these accumulate damage rather than hold remaining health. See Component_ReadDamagePercent.

entries.name: Component_LinkMaxRefData
entries.description: Wires up mech+0x212 (and neighboring fields) as a pointer into per-component maximum/reference data, sourced from the mech's own .DMG-derived pointer plus its Collision_RegisterObject registration record.

entries.name: Component_AddDamage
entries.description: (entry, maximum, damage*): adds damage to one damage entry. An entry already negative (-1, destroyed) is left alone, the damage left as it was, and the call answers destroyed. Otherwise entry + damage under the maximum is stored; at or past it the excess (entry + damage - maximum) is written back through the damage pointer and the entry becomes -1 rather than the maximum. Returns whether the entry is now negative.

entries.name: Component_DestroyAndCascade
entries.description: (damageHeader, i): takes main component i out. First looks up the component's cluster with Collision_FindClusterForComponent on the header's collision record (+0x10), keeping the node index it writes and the cluster's bound centre at cluster+8; the result is used without a null test. Returns 0 at once when the component's active flag (+8 array) is clear. Otherwise: damage entry -1, active flag 0, Component_SpillIntoDependents with a flat 32000 to finish the dependents. When the piece's +3 byte (the TSCellAnimPart sequence it drives) is not negative: while the cascade latch DAT_004a98b0 is clear, flags bit 1 releases the owner's fires (FireEffect_ReleaseForOwner) and lights FireEffect shape 0, else bit 3 lights shape 2, each on the node index and the bound centre; then that sequence's cell in the owner's shape instance is set to 2. Builds the component's frame -- the owner's world transform for node -1, otherwise the node's posed transform (shape vtable +0x20 part lookup, identity at 006c572c for a missing part) concatenated with it -- and puts the bound centre through it. While the latch is clear, explodes there: EXPLOS.DAT type 10, or 0x11 with flags bit 2, which also sets the latch. Throws the piece's +2 debris group, or group 2 when it is -1, from that frame. Then queues every component whose active flag is set and whose piece +4 parent index is i on the list at maybe_ComponentDependencyList (count byte at +5), and returns 1.

entries.name: Component_IsFullyDestroyed
entries.description: (damageHeader, i): main component i's damage entry is negative (destroyed) AND Component_AllDependentsDestroyed answers for its piece. The stricter of the two 'is this gone' tests; Mech_ComponentDamageWrite asks it of the two cockpit slots (0 and 1) as the mech's death gate.

entries.name: Component_ApplyDamageAndCascade
entries.description: Adds damage to main component i through Component_AddDamage; once that entry is destroyed, pours the excess into its dependents through Component_SpillIntoDependents. Only when no live dependent is left AND the .DMG piece's +0x05 flag bit 0 is set does it clear the major-effect latch DAT_004a98b0, call Component_DestroyAndCascade(i), and drain the pending parent-index queue (count byte at +5 of the list at maybe_ComponentDependencyList) through the same call. Returns 1 only when it cascaded. A piece with bit 0 clear reads destroyed but keeps its active flag and runs no destruction.

entries.name: Component_ReadOverallDamage
entries.description: One object's whole damage as a Q8 fraction, 0 pristine and 256 destroyed: every main component and every dependent weighed once against its own maximum, a destroyed one counting as its full maximum. Reached through the object's vtable +0x40 and printed by the MFD status screen's integrity readout.

entries.name: Component_ReadDamagePercent
entries.description: (damageHeader, i): main component i's ACCUMULATED DAMAGE as Q8, 0 = pristine and 0x100 = destroyed -- not health. Starts from the piece's armour (+0) as the maximum and its damage entry, a negative entry counting as the armour, then adds every dependent the piece lists: its damage (a negative entry counting as its maximum) and its maximum from the .DMG maxima array (dmg table +4). Returns (totalDamage << 8) / totalMaximum, divided unguarded.

entries.name: Component_TotalArmor
entries.description: Everything a component has to lose: its own armour plus the maximum of every internal mapped onto it, walking the piece's mapped-internals list. The denominator Component_ReadDamagePercent divides by, and the scale Mech_SpreadImpactDamage multiplies by. Args derived from disassembly: [EBP+8] pointer, [EBP+0xc] word.

entries.name: STACK_short_Dtor
entries.description: STACK<short>'s destructor, the dtor its class record (0x6 bytes, at 0040dcd2) names: (stack, flags): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr; when the stack is not null, Mem_DeleteArray of its buffer at +0, then Mem_Delete of the stack when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: Shape_TranslatePointLists
entries.description: (part, offset): adds the int16 triple at offset to the points of part's tree, by its class tag (vtable +0): TSPartList, TSShape, TSCellAnimPart, TSDetailPart and TSBSPPart (0x140007, 0x140008, 0x14000b, 0x14000c, 0x140015) recurse into each child (pointer array +0x12, count +0x10); TSGroup and TSBSPGroup (0x140014, 0x14000a) memset one byte per point (count +0x22) at 004a98f0 to 0, mark for each poly (pointer array +0x1c, count +0x26) whose tag is 0x140001 to 0x140003, 0x140009 or 0x14000f its point +6 and the +8 entries of the int16 index list +0x10 from its +0xa, and add offset's x, y and z to each marked point of the list at +0x14, 6 bytes each; 0x140006 calls it again with the same arguments; any other tag, 0x140005, 0x1e0003 and 0x1e0005 among them, returns. es2_xref finds calls from WeaponMount_CtorBase (0040df30) and from itself.

entries.name: WeaponMount_RenderWithDetailBias
entries.description: Vtable +0x1c of GUN_STATE (00498e44) and all ten weapon-mount classes below it, in place of CONFIG_PART's own ConfigPart_Render: pushes g_TSDetailBiasFromHercDetail into the TSDetailPart bias via TSDetailPart_SetBias, runs ConfigPart_Render on the mount -- its weapon model with its own flipbook frames -- and restores the bias to 0. The same bracket Structure_DrawWithDetailBias applies, but from the HERC DETAIL table rather than the STRUCTURE DETAIL one.

entries.name: WeaponMount_MatchGaugeNever
entries.description: GUN_STATE's vtable +0x58 gauge-match slot (00498e44), kept by POD_WPN and the five pods: returns 0 unconditionally, so WeaponMounts_SelectByGauge can never find a pod. The energy and ammunition classes (WeaponMount_EnergyMatchGauge, WeaponMount_AmmoMatchGauge) compare the argument against the mount's own gauge pointer at +0x77 instead. Together with the pod constructor clearing the selectable byte +0x4c, this is why a pod's cockpit row cannot be armed.

entries.name: WeaponMount_EnergyMatchGauge
entries.description: ENERGY_WPN and ELF_WPN vtable +0x58: returns gauge == mount+0x77, the mount's own cockpit gauge. WeaponMounts_SelectByGauge finds the mount a clicked row belongs to with it.

entries.name: WeaponMount_AmmoMatchGauge
entries.description: PROJECTILE_WPN and GRENADE_WPN vtable +0x58: returns gauge == mount+0x77, the same comparison as WeaponMount_EnergyMatchGauge.

entries.name: WeaponMount_CtorBase
entries.description: (mount, shape instance, hardpoint record, template, projectile record): with the hardpoint's byte +6 below 4 the model is WeaponMount_ShapeForMountingCode (0040fab0)(template, that byte), else 0. Stores ClassItemVtable, TSBaseVtable and TSPartBaseVtable, runs ShapeInstance_CtorCellFrames (00402fc0)(mount + 0x10, model), stores CONFIG_PARTVtable and WeaponMountBaseVtable, and keeps the hardpoint record at +0x18, the template at +0x1c and the projectile record at +0x20. +0x5b and +0x5f get ShapeInst_AddThread (00402374)(shape instance, the hardpoint's int16 +2 or +4), or 0 when that value is negative; with a model at +0x10, Shape_TranslatePointLists (0040dd4c)(model, WeaponMount_MuzzleOffset (0040f540)(mount)). Then zeroes 6 bytes at +0x24 and at +0x2a, the int16 +0x31, 8 bytes at +0x33 and at +0x3b and 0x18 bytes at +0x43, sets +0x4c to 1 and the refire scale +0x63 to 0x400. Increments *Rtl_DtorCountPtr after each base.

entries.name: WeaponMount_CtorEnergy
entries.description: Energy mount constructor (vtable 00498dcc): writes Math_Q10Multiply(820, 1200) = 960 into both the charge target (+0x7b) and the capacitor level (+0x7d), and 20 into the charge rate (+0x7f). All three are literals shared by every energy weapon. Used for weapon ids 6-12, 17, 19, 20 and 22-25, 28.

entries.name: WeaponMount_CreateEnergyGauge
entries.description: Energy mount vtable +0x64, the gauge factory WeaponMounts_BuildGauges dispatches: CockpitView_CreateEnergyWeaponGauge(CockpitViewInstance, the hardpoint record's row byte +7, mount) into +0x77, then one EnergyWeaponGauge_SetState with the gauge's own block and block[1] set to the raw charge target (+0x7b) -- not the (target << 10) / 1200 WeaponMount_PushEnergyGaugeState pushes.

entries.name: WeaponMount_CtorAmmunition
entries.description: Ammunition mount constructor (vtable 00498d54): reads the magazine size from the template's +0x3a into +0x7b and the same value shifted left 8 into +0x7d, so the mount powers up with a full magazine and its gauge prints +0x7d >> 8. Used for weapon ids 1-5, 13-16, 21 and 26.

entries.name: WeaponMount_GetDisplayName
entries.description: The name a weapon gauge prints for a mount. If the mount's resolved PROJ.DAT record (+0x20) is null or its category is non-zero, copies the template's name pointer (+0x52, written by Weapons_LoadResourceTables from the 33-entry array at 00498eb0). If the record is a Missile (category 0), copies MissileAmmoNameTable[record.subtypeId] instead -- so a launcher is named by its loaded ammunition (ARH, SARH, ...), not by its weapon id. Returns a pointer to the shared scratch buffer at 004a9954.

entries.name: WeaponMount_CreateAmmoGauge
entries.description: PROJECTILE_WPN and GRENADE_WPN vtable +0x64, the gauge factory WeaponMounts_BuildGauges dispatches: CockpitView_CreateAmmoWeaponGauge(CockpitViewInstance, the hardpoint record's row byte (+0x18)+7, mount) into +0x77. The energy counterpart is WeaponMount_CreateEnergyGauge.

entries.name: Pod_CtorBase
entries.description: (pod, shape instance, hardpoint record, template): WeaponMount_CtorBase (0040df30)(pod, shape instance, hardpoint record, template, 0), then stores the pod base vtable PodMountVtable (00498cdc), clears the selectable byte +0x4c and writes -1 to the int16 +0x77, the pods' catalog id.
entries.signature: void * __cdecl Pod_CtorBase(void *pod, int shapeInstance, int hardpoint, int weaponTemplate)

entries.name: EcmPod_Ctor
entries.description: ECM pod (catalog id 0x12, mech+0x307). Vtable 00498c64.

entries.name: TurboPod_Ctor
entries.description: Turbo Pod (catalog id 0x1f, mech+0x317). Vtable 00498bec, and the only pod whose constructor arms anything: 2000 of charge at +0x7d and the engaged flag at +0x81 clear.

entries.name: TargetingPod_Ctor
entries.description: Targeting Pod (catalog id 0x1d, mech+0x30b). Vtable 00498b74, object size 0x8a -- the extra bytes over the other pods are the component lock at +0x7d/+0x86 and its decay timer at +0x81. It writes none of them, so a pod starts with whatever its arena block holds; the cursor is always set by TargetingPod_ResetComponentLock before anything reads it.

entries.name: ShieldPod_Ctor
entries.description: Shield Pod (catalog id 0x1e, mech+0x30f). Vtable 00498afc.

entries.name: EnergyPod_Ctor
entries.description: Energy Pod (catalog id 0x20, mech+0x313). Vtable 00498a84.

entries.name: EcmPod_CreateGauge
entries.description: ECM pod vtable +0x64.

entries.name: TurboPod_CreateGauge
entries.description: Turbo Pod vtable +0x64.

entries.name: EnergyPod_CreateGauge
entries.description: Energy Pod vtable +0x64.

entries.name: ShieldPod_CreateGauge
entries.description: Shield Pod vtable +0x64.

entries.name: TargetingPod_CreateGauge
entries.description: Targeting Pod vtable +0x64.

entries.name: TargetingPod_ResetComponentLock
entries.description: Targeting Pod (mech+0x30b): the selection changed, so restart the component rotation. Sets the cursor pod+0x7d to 0 when the new target exists and its target class (obj+0x1a8) is 0, and to -1 otherwise -- which is what fences component targeting, and with it the target's vtable +0x58/+0x80/+0x84, off everything that is not a HERC. Called once per selection change by Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate, which is the only writer of the player's mech+0x1a4.

entries.name: TargetingPod_CycleComponent
entries.description: Targeting Pod: step the component lock on. Asks the target's vtable +0x80 (NextTargetableComponent) for the next component it still has, storing the new cursor in pod+0x7d and letting the slot write the resolved component id into pod+0x86. This is the manual's [Tab]: CockpitWidgets_HandleCommand's scancode 0x0f case calls it directly. TargetingPod_ResolveAimPoint calls it too, to move off a component that has since been shot away.

entries.name: TargetingPod_ResolveAimPoint
entries.description: Targeting Pod: the pod half of Player_ResolveTargetAimPoint. With a live cursor (pod+0x7d >= 0) and pod damage under 0x9b it reports the locked component's position through the target's vtable +0x58 and its id through outComponentId, advancing the lock first if vtable +0x84 says the component is gone; past 0x68 of damage it also runs a 5 s countdown at pod+0x81 that drops the lock. Otherwise it falls back to the target's vtable +0x24 aim node, or the raw origin, and reports no component. The fourth parameter -- the caller passes the target's occupancy-array pointer mech+0x20e -- is never read: [EBP+0x14] is untouched in the whole body.
entries.signature: void __cdecl TargetingPod_ResolveAimPoint(void *pod, void *target, int *outPoint, void *unused, short *outHasComponent, short *outComponentId)

entries.name: WeaponMount_RangeAllows
entries.description: (mount, range): 1 when the int32 +0x2c of the template at the mount's +0x1c is below range and range is below the template's int32 +0x30, both bounds exclusive, otherwise 0: the weapon's engagement window.

entries.name: WeaponMount_HardpointBoneId
entries.description: Returns the mount's .GL record +0, the hardpoint's bone id. The same id WeaponMount_PrepareShot resolves the firing frame from, so the drawn weapon and its shot ride one node.

entries.name: WeaponMount_GetEnergyAmmoType
entries.description: Energy mount vtable +0x60: writes 0 through its optional out pointer and returns a constant 5. The ammunition counterpart is WeaponMount_GetAmmoType. WeaponMounts_FireTrigger sets DAT_004d25ac and DAT_004d25aa, the electro-optical missile flags, when this returns 3, which an energy mount never can.

entries.name: WeaponMount_GetAmmoType
entries.description: Ammunition mount vtable +0x60 (AmmoMountVtable, GrenadeMountVtable), (mount, short *outRounds) -> subtype in AX. When the mount's projectile record (+0x20) is PROJ.DAT Type 0, a Missile, it writes the rounds remaining (+0x7b) through the optional out pointer and returns the record's subtype id (word +2); otherwise it tail-calls WeaponMount_GetEnergyAmmoType, which writes 0 through the out pointer and returns 5. WeaponMounts_RoundsByMissileType sums the out value per subtype; the readiness and fire gates exempt 5 and 3 from the per-subtype missile-lock flags at manager+0x0a (weapon-mounts.md, 'Readiness').

entries.name: Pod_TriggerHeldNever
entries.description: POD_WPN vtable +0x30 (00498cdc), kept by all five pods: returns 0, so a pod never reports its trigger held.

entries.name: ElfMount_TriggerHeld
entries.description: ElfMountVtable +0x30, a spin-up rather than the plain trigger read WeaponMount_TriggerHeld does. While the latch +0x48 is clear it returns 0 -- no shot -- and a fresh press instead sets +0x47 and resets the cell timer at +0x84; ElfMount_SpinUpAndChargeTick then walks the muzzle-flash flipbook and latches +0x48 at the last cell. Once latched it returns the input device's fire byte, and release clears +0x48 and rewinds the flipbook. ELF2 SKIPS THE SPIN-UP: the function opens by forcing both flags to 1 when template+0x56 (the record's self-index) is 22.

entries.name: GrenadeMount_TriggerHeld
entries.description: GRENADE_WPN vtable +0x30 (00499248), (mount, input): a hold-to-throw trigger. Idle (+0x46 clear), a press (input+0xd) starts it -- +0x46 = 1, +0x81 = 20000 -- and returns 0. While charging it returns 1 on release; held, it adds 1000 to +0x81 per call and returns 1 once that passes 100000, calling Input_LatchButton(1, 1) as it does.

entries.name: WeaponMount_PrepareShot
entries.description: The fire prologue both dispatchers open with. Resolves the firing hardpoint's bone (.GL +0) to its posed node transform, composes the gun convergence (mount+0x24/+0x28, gated on mount+0x5b/+0x5f) under it and the mech's own transform (mech+0x12) over it into the global shot transform at 004a98b8, transforms the muzzle offset into world space at 004a98d8, extracts the firing euler triple to 004a98e4, and arms the refire timer as Math_Q10Multiply(mount+0x63, template+0x4c). Both convergence gates read zero fleet-wide, so the rotation is live.

entries.name: Pod_FireNoOp
entries.description: POD_WPN vtable +0x28 (00498cdc), kept by all five pods: an empty fire dispatch.

entries.name: WeaponMount_FireDispatch_Missile
entries.description: Missile-capable-hardpoint fire dispatcher: checks the mount's cached PROJ.DAT Type field, Type==Missile(0) -> Rocket_Fire, else falls through to the shared Bullet fallback.

entries.name: GrenadeMount_FireDispatch
entries.description: GRENADE_WPN vtable +0x28 (00499248), (mount, a, b): WeaponMount_PrepareShot(mount, a); takes one round off +0x7b when the third argument (a short) is zero; clears the charging latch +0x46; then Grenade_FireNoOp.

entries.name: WeaponMount_FireDispatch_GunBeam
entries.description: Energy/gun mount vtable +0x28, the fire dispatch. Opens with WeaponMount_PrepareShot and sets mount+0x44 = 1 when the byte at (+0x18)->+6 is below 4. Then branches on the mount's cached PROJ.DAT Type: Type==4 (Beam) copies the muzzle world point into the shot transform's translation, spends min(template+0x38, capacitor +0x7d) and calls Bullet_FireBurst with that as the shot's power and template+0x30 as the range. Otherwise, with the capacitor below the cost template+0x38 (a charge-up gun), it fires Bullet_FirePowered at the whole charge from the prologue's muzzle point, and when template+0x3c == 3 two more rounds at x = 0 and x = -(template+0x40) of the template's muzzle offset, three in all; then, when template+0x3e == 0x13 and +0x4d is clear, arms +0x4d and sets the refire countdown +0x31 to template+0x4c >> 2, and otherwise clears +0x4d and empties the capacitor. With the capacitor at or above the cost it subtracts the cost and fires one unpowered Bullet_Fire.

entries.name: ElfMount_FireDispatch
entries.description: ElfMountVtable +0x28. WeaponMount_PrepareShot, then one branch -- an ELF is always a Beam record. Two deliberate differences from WeaponMount_FireDispatch_GunBeam's beam branch: the cost template+0x38 is subtracted UNCONDITIONALLY rather than capped at the charge, so the last partial shot takes the capacitor negative and ends the burst through ElfMount_CanFire; and the shot power handed to Bullet_FireBurst is the LITERAL 0x4b0 (1200), not the charge spent, so every shot of a burst lands at full strength however far the capacitor has drained.

entries.name: Pod_CanFireNever
entries.description: POD_WPN vtable +0x2c (00498cdc), kept by all five pods: returns 0, so WeaponMounts_FireTrigger never finds a pod ready.

entries.name: WeaponMount_EnergyCanFire
entries.description: Energy mount vtable+0x2c: not destroyed (+0x49), refire timer (+0x31) expired, and charge (+0x7d) at or above a threshold taken from the template's +0x36/+0x38 pair -- max(+0x36, +0x7b) when +0x36 < +0x38, otherwise +0x38 outright. Both shapes occur in retail data (EMP 350/10000, LAS100 80/80). NOT the test the ELFs use, despite their (400, 70) template -- they have their own class, see ElfMount_CanFire.

entries.name: WeaponMount_EnergyIsSpent
entries.description: ENERGY_WPN and ELF_WPN vtable +0x5c: returns the destroyed byte +0x49, sign-extended. Ai_ChooseWeapon passes over a mount whose +0x5c answers non-zero, and latches 'no weapons left' when every mount does.

entries.name: WeaponMount_AmmoIsSpent
entries.description: PROJECTILE_WPN and GRENADE_WPN vtable +0x5c: returns 1 when the rounds remaining (+0x7b) are zero or the mount is destroyed (+0x49), otherwise 0. Ai_ChooseWeapon passes over a spent mount.

entries.name: WeaponMount_AmmoCanFire
entries.description: Ammunition mount vtable+0x2c: not destroyed (+0x49), refire timer (+0x31) expired, and at least one round left (+0x7b != 0).

entries.name: ElfMount_CanFire
entries.description: ElfMountVtable +0x2c, AND THE REASON AN ELF CANNOT BE RE-TRIGGERED UNTIL ITS CAPACITOR IS FULL. Same two template fields as WeaponMount_EnergyCanFire with the branch between them dropped, so the threshold is ALWAYS max(template+0x36, mount+0x7b): !destroyed && (charge >= max(+0x36, chargeTarget) || (mount+0x33 && charge >= template+0x38)). Both ELFs read +0x36 = 400 against a 960 charge target, so a fresh trigger pull needs the full capacitor; the +0x33 clause is the sustain, dropping the bar to one shot's 70 while the mount is firing every tick. No refire-timer term, consistent with both ELF templates carrying a +0x4c of zero.

entries.name: WeaponMount_AutoFireDue
entries.description: Reports a mount as due for an auto-fire follow-up shot: refire timer (+0x31) expired AND the burst-continues flag (+0x4d) set. Only WeaponMount_FireDispatch_GunBeam's multi-shot branch ever sets +0x4d, and never on the beam path, so a beam weapon never reports due.

entries.name: WeaponMount_ConditionChangedBase
entries.description: Base weapon-mount vtable +0x68, the condition notification Mech_ComponentDamageWrite pushes through every mount with its component's reading before and after the write. A reading of 0x100 destroys the mount, with no roll.
entries.signature: void __cdecl WeaponMount_ConditionChangedBase(void *mount, void *mech, int before, int after)

entries.name: WeaponMount_ConditionChangedEnergy
entries.description: ENERGY_WPN and ELF_WPN vtable +0x68: WeaponMount_ConditionChangedBase, then sets the charge rate +0x7f to 20, less Math_Q10Multiply(20, ((reading - 0x80) / 0x19) * 100) when the reading (last argument) is past 0x80 -- a damaged energy mount charges more slowly. The two weapon-carrying classes' other override is WeaponMount_ConditionChanged.

entries.name: WeaponMount_ConditionChanged
entries.description: Vtable +0x68 of the ammunition classes, PROJECTILE_WPN and GRENADE_WPN (the energy classes install WeaponMount_ConditionChangedEnergy). Runs the base slot, then, while the mount is not empty (+0x7b) and the reading is past 0x80: a Missile mount rolls rand & 0x3ff < 300 for each 25 points crossed and the first success destroys it; a Bullet mount instead sets its refire scale mount+0x63 = 0x400 - steps * 0x66, which makes a damaged gun fire FASTER since WeaponMount_PrepareShot multiplies by it; a Beam mount gets neither.
entries.signature: void __cdecl WeaponMount_ConditionChanged(void *mount, void *mech, int before, int after)

entries.name: TargetingPod_ConditionChanged
entries.description: Targeting Pod vtable +0x68, and the only pod that overrides the base notification: after WeaponMount_ConditionChangedBase it caches the component reading the damage write just produced in pod+0x7f. Every degradation of the pod is a threshold on that cached value. The Shield and Energy pods take the other route and read their damage live through Component_ReadDamagePercent.
entries.signature: void __cdecl TargetingPod_ConditionChanged(void *pod, void *mech, int before, int after)

entries.name: WeaponMount_RefireTick
entries.description: Ammunition mount vtable +0x34, and the first thing WeaponMount_ChargeCapacitor does for an energy mount: counts the refire timer (+0x31) down by SimTickDelta via Math_CountdownTimerTick, and shuffles the two 8-byte muzzle-flash flag blocks at +0x33/+0x3b plus the burst frame counter at +0x44. Gated on the mount not being destroyed, so a dead mount's cooldown does not run. Consumes no energy -- an ammunition mount's whole turn at the pool is this.

entries.name: WeaponMount_ChargeCapacitor
entries.description: One energy mount's draw on the pool. Target is the mount's capacity (+0x7b), or zero when told another mount is already charging, minus its stored charge (+0x7d); takes min(chargeRate +0x7f, budget, deficit) and returns the remainder. A non-positive deficit clears the charging flag (+0x43) and bleeds charge back at up to 5/tick. PLAS (catalog id 25) is half-efficiency: its deficit counts double and only half the drawn energy is stored. Ammunition mounts override this with a no-op that consumes nothing.

entries.name: TurboPod_Engage
entries.description: Engages the Turbo Pod: if the engaged flag at pod+0x81 is clear and the charge at pod+0x7d is over 600, sets the flag and plays sound 0x2c (throtl.wav, the same servo the throttle lever uses) -- but only when the pod has a cockpit gauge at +0x79, which no AI machine's pod has. Its callers found by es2_xref are Mech_BehaviourFleeThink and Ai_DriveToPoint, which is how an AI machine engages one since its pods are never ticked; TurboPod_Tick makes the same test inline for the player's row button rather than calling this.

entries.name: TurboPod_ChargeTick
entries.description: Turbo Pod vtable +0x34, the only pod that overrides the pool turn -- every other pod inherits WeaponMount_RefireTick there and so consumes nothing. While engaged (pod+0x81) it spends 35 of the charge at pod+0x7d per tick, disengaging and zeroing the charge when it runs out; then, if the mount is not destroyed, it runs WeaponMount_RefireTick and takes min(20, budget, 2000 - charge) back out of the weapons' leftover budget, returning the remainder. 2000 is the value TurboPod_Ctor starts the charge at.

entries.name: Pod_TickBase
entries.description: Pod base vtable +0x50, inherited unchanged by the Shield, Targeting and Energy pods -- the three classes whose gauge row has no button. It is a display refresh and nothing else: it takes the gauge's 8-byte state block through PodGauge_GetStateBlock, replaces byte 1 with the mount's destroyed flag at pod+0x49, leaves byte 0 (the button) and the remaining six bytes as they were, and pushes the block back through PodGauge_SetStateBlock. It reads and writes no pod field. EcmPod_Tick and TurboPod_Tick are the overrides that do the same refresh and act on the button as well.

entries.name: EcmPod_Tick
entries.description: ECM pod vtable +0x50. Reads the pod gauge's on/off byte, mirrors it into pod+0x7d and pod+0x7f, and posts the jamming messages 0x2a and 0x2b on a change; the flag it pushes back carries the destroyed byte at +0x49.

entries.name: TurboPod_Tick
entries.description: Turbo Pod vtable +0x50. Engages when the gauge's button byte is set and the charge at pod+0x7d is over 600, playing sound 0x2c, and disengages when the charge runs out.

entries.name: WeaponMount_PushEnergyGaugeState
entries.description: Energy and ELF mount vtable +0x50: (mount, b14, b15, b16). Copies the gauge's state block (EnergyWeaponGauge_GetState on mount+0x77), fills it and hands it back through the gauge's vtable +0x10 (EnergyWeaponGauge_SetState). Block+0x00 is the capacitor level, (+0x7d << 10) / 1200, the LED bar's fill; the fixed 1200 denominator -- not the mount's own capacity -- is why a capacitor at its spawn 960 fills four-fifths of its bar. Block+0x04 is the charge bar's slider position, and byte +0x34 (byte 1 of the +0x33 flag block) decides which way it flows: set, the charge target goes out as (+0x7b << 10) / 1200; clear, the slider position comes back as the charge target, +0x7b = position * 1200 >> 10. Also fills +0x11 with the destroyed byte +0x49, +0x12 with the mid-charge byte +0x43, and +0x14/+0x15/+0x16 with its three arguments. Who sets +0x34, and what the round trip does to the power level: docs/retail/simulation/weapon-firing.md#the-charge-bar.

entries.name: WeaponMount_PushAmmoGaugeState
entries.description: Ammunition mount vtable +0x50, the sibling of WeaponMount_PushEnergyGaugeState: (mount, b14, b15, b16). Copies the gauge's state block (AmmoWeaponGauge_GetState on mount+0x77), moves +0x7d toward the rounds remaining +0x7b * 256 -- down by Math_IntegrateRateOverTick(250) while above, and straight up to it when below -- then fills block+0x00 with +0x7d >> 8, the round count the gauge prints, +0x11 with the destroyed byte +0x49 and +0x14/+0x15/+0x16 with its three arguments, and hands the block to the gauge's vtable +0x10.

entries.name: GrenadeMount_PushGaugeState
entries.description: GRENADE_WPN vtable +0x50 (00499248): passes its four arguments straight to WeaponMount_PushAmmoGaugeState.

entries.name: ElfMount_SpinUpAndChargeTick
entries.description: ElfMountVtable +0x34. While the spin-up flag +0x47 is set, counts the cell timer at +0x83 down and on expiry either advances the muzzle-flash flipbook one cell or, at the last cell, latches +0x48 and clears +0x47 -- which is what lets ElfMount_TriggerHeld start returning the trigger. Then falls through to WeaponMount_ChargeCapacitor, so an ELF's capacitor charges exactly as an energy mount's does.

entries.name: WeaponMount_AdjustPowerLevel
entries.description: Energy mount vtable +0x38, reached by WeaponMounts_HandleCommand codes 0x0c/0x0d/0x4a/0x4e ([-], [=], keypad [-], keypad [+]) with the 'up' half as a flag. Moves the charge target (+0x7b) by +/-0x50, clamped to 0..0x4b0. This is the power-level control, which the manual never mentions, and the only thing in the retail build that raises a capacitor past its idle 820. The ammunition and pod classes have a no-op in this slot.

entries.name: WeaponMount_WakeCapacitor
entries.description: Energy mount vtable +0x3c: puts the charge target (+0x7b) back to its idle 0x334 unless the mount is destroyed. Called after a chain toggle when the mount reports a zero arbitration priority, so a capacitor that had been zeroed starts asking for charge again. The ammunition and pod classes have a no-op in this slot.

entries.name: WeaponMount_DemandFullCharge
entries.description: Energy mount vtable +0x40: sets the mid-charge flag (+0x43) and raises the charge target (+0x7b) to 0x4b0, the same 1200 the cockpit bar is scaled against. NEVER INVOKED in the retail build -- its only caller, WeaponMounts_DemandFullChargeOnArmed_Dead, is itself unreferenced. What actually raises a capacitor past the idle 820 is WeaponMount_AdjustPowerLevel, the player's power-level keys.

entries.name: WeaponMount_GetEnergyPriority
entries.description: Vtable+0x48 on energy mounts: returns the mount's capacity (+0x7b), or 10000 when its charging flag (+0x43) is set so a mount already mid-charge jumps the arbitration queue and finishes charging. The ammunition mount class returns 0 from this slot.

entries.name: WeaponMount_AmmoCountsInCombatRating
entries.description: PROJECTILE_WPN and GRENADE_WPN vtable +0x54: rounds remaining (+0x7b) >= the magazine size (template+0x3a) >> 3. Mech_ComputeCombatRating adds a mount's value (template+0x4e, scaled by its condition) only when this slot answers non-zero, so a launcher or gun below an eighth of a magazine stops counting.

entries.name: WeaponMount_MuzzleOffset
entries.description: Adds the hardpoint's own mount-point offset (.GL +0x10/+0x12/+0x14) to WeaponMountTemplate_SideMuzzleOffset's result and returns the sum, in the firing bone's space. WeaponMount_PrepareShot adds the template's own muzzle triple at +0x40 on top.

entries.name: WeaponMount_Destroy
entries.description: The mount side of weapon-mount destruction, and idempotent -- its whole body sits under a test of the destroyed byte. Clears the weapon model at mount+0x10 and sets mount+0x49, then, for a visibly-mounted hardpoint, spawns the mechwpn2 shape at template+0x26 as debris on a Math_EulerToward bearing. The third argument picks the debris lifetime pair: 0 gives (2, 0x14), anything else (0xff, 0xffff). Ported except the debris.

entries.name: WeaponMount_StaticInitNoOp
entries.description: Static initialiser of the weapon-mount module (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7ab6, priority 0x20): a lone RET. It follows WeaponMount_Destroy, the last function of the block of WeaponMount_/Pod_ fire and tick routines, and precedes that module's class records (DEBRIS at 0040f78d).

entries.name: Debris_Dtor
entries.description: DEBRIS vtable +0x08 (00497ed8), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). Two RTL destructor-count decrements, installs TSObjVtable, deletes the shape instance at +0x34 through its own vtable +0x18 with flags 3, two more decrements, and Mem_Deletes this on flags bit 0. Meteor_Dtor is the same body.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 0040f7e6; class record at 0040f796

entries.name: WeaponMount_AndFlagBlocks
entries.description: dst[i] &= src[i] over 8 bytes. WeaponMount_RefireTick calls it as (mount+0x33, mount+0x3b) and then clears +0x3b, while WeaponMount_PrepareShot sets both on firing -- so +0x33 survives only while the mount fires on every tick and drops on the first tick it sits out. It is an 'is still firing' flag, not 'has ever fired', and ElfMount_CanFire is what reads it.

entries.name: WeaponMount_DrainNoOp
entries.description: GUN_STATE vtable +0x4c (00498e44), kept by POD_WPN and the five pods: an empty body. The energy classes install WeaponMount_DrainCapacitor, the ammunition classes WeaponMount_DrainAmmo.

entries.name: WeaponMount_IsSpent_Always
entries.description: GUN_STATE vtable +0x5c (00498e44), kept by POD_WPN and the five pods: returns 1 in AX. Ai_ChooseWeapon passes over a mount whose +0x5c answers non-zero, so it passes over every pod, and a pod does not keep its 'no weapons left' latch off.

entries.name: WeaponMount_TriggerHeld
entries.description: Mount vtable +0x30, shared by the energy and ammunition classes: returns the input device struct's byte at +0x0d, the fire button. This is the whole of the trigger -- it is a held state polled every frame, not a command, which is why no scancode case for [Space] exists in Sim_DispatchCommand or WeaponMounts_HandleCommand.

entries.name: WeaponMountTemplate_ReadRecord
entries.description: (record, stream): per-record reader for simvol0/dat/WEAPONS.DAT, called from Weapons_LoadResourceTables in a Total-length loop. HercPiece_ReadRecord into record+0x00 (the weapon's .DMG piece), Collision_ReadCluster into record+0x12 (its .COL hit-sphere cluster), then a raw 48-byte (0x30) read into record+0x22 through the stream's vtable +0x18, and finally stores word 0 at record+0x48 -- the middle (y) of the side-muzzle-offset vector at +0x46, which is zero in every retail record anyway. Full writeup in docs/retail/formats/weapons-dat-sim.md.

entries.name: WeaponMountTemplate_SideMuzzleOffset
entries.description: Given a template and the hardpoint's mounting code (.GL +6: 0 on top, 1 underneath, 2 left, 3 right, 4 invisible), returns a 3-vector at 004a9b74 built from the template's lateral figure at +0x46 and vertical figure at +0x4a. Only one axis is ever nonzero: top/bottom take +/-vertical, left/right take -/+lateral, invisible takes neither. Y is always zero. This is what makes a mirrored hardpoint pair fire from mirrored points off one template.

entries.name: WeaponModels_LoadShapeChunks
entries.description: Opens dts/mechwpns and reads every top-level chunk (all type 0x140008) raw into malloc'd buffers: DAT_004a9988[i] is the buffer, DAT_004a9a78[i] its length, DAT_004a9b68 the count. Retail ships 56 weapon shapes. They are kept as bytes rather than parsed once because each mount needs its own copy.

entries.name: WeaponModels_FreeShapeChunks
entries.description: Frees the DAT_004a9988 buffers WeaponModels_LoadShapeChunks allocated and nulls each slot.

entries.name: WeaponMount_ShapeForMountingCode
entries.description: Instantiates one weapon model: reads template[0x22 + mountingCode*2] as an index into the mechwpns chunk table, opens that raw chunk as a memory stream, loads the shape from it, and binds the wpntex atlas at shape+0x26. One fresh copy per mount, because the caller then translates its points and stamps a transform id into it.

entries.name: MechLoadout_FileEquipmentPods
entries.description: Walks the finished weapon-mount list and files five specific weapon ids into the five-pointer pod array at mech+0x307, keyed on the mount template's +0x56 (the SHELL0 gam/WEAPONS.DAT catalog id, written as the record index by Weapons_LoadResourceTables). Slot order is not id order: 0x12 ECM->[0], 0x1d TARG->[1], 0x1e SHLD->[2], 0x20 ENRG->[3], 0x1f TURB->[4]. Assigns rather than accumulates, so a duplicate pod contributes nothing.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_RoundsByMissileType
entries.description: Fills a 5-entry short array with rounds carried per PROJ.DAT missile subtype, by walking the mount array calling each mount's vtable +0x60 (WeaponMount_GetAmmoType) and accumulating its out-parameter (mount+0x7b) into rounds[subtype], skipping the 5 sentinel. THIS is the ammunition count; manager+0x0a is the lock state. Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate uses it to decide which lock timers run.

entries.name: GunLayout_CollectHardpointBones
entries.description: Walks a .GL hardpoint list (26-byte records) and writes one short per hardpoint: the record's bone id when its mounting code at +6 is under 4, else -1. Returns the hardpoint count. The -1 is what keeps the invisible mounting out of the hardpoint splice, which matters because that bone carries real body geometry.

entries.name: Weapons_LoadResourceTables
entries.description: Opens 'wpntex' (textures), 'mechwpn2', 'weapons' (88-byte per-hardpoint mount-template records), then 'proj' -- reads PROJ.DAT's 36-byte records into ProjDat_RecordTable. The 'weapons' resource is simvol0/dat/WEAPONS.DAT, read byte-exact: a UINT16 Total then Total records via WeaponMountTemplate_ReadRecord, consuming exactly the file's full content length with zero remainder across all 33 real records.

entries.name: WeaponMountTemplate_GetByWeaponId
entries.description: weaponId * 0x58 + WeaponMountTemplate_Table -- direct flat-array index into the loaded WeaponMountTemplate table (simvol0/dat/WEAPONS.DAT's in-memory copy, 88 bytes/record) by SHELL0/GAM/WEAPONS.DAT catalog weapon id. The sim and shell catalogs share one 33-entry order and indexing scheme.

entries.name: GunLayout_GetBySlot
entries.description: index * 6 + GunLayout_Table -- flat index into the loaded gun-layout table. Each 6-byte entry is {short count, record*}. Callers reach it through Mech_GetGunLayout, which adds the mech type's own allocation index to the base slot cached in _DAT_004a9df4.

entries.name: GunLayout_Reserve
entries.description: (n): returns GunLayout_Count (004a996c) and adds n to it -- the gun-layout twin of CollisionTable_Reserve and DmgTable_Reserve. maybe_MechTypeSlot_Allocate passes 1 for each newly allocated mech type and keeps the first result in 004a9df4, the base slot Mech_GetGunLayout adds a type's index to.

entries.name: GunLayout_AllocTable
