entries.description: GunLayout_Table = Mem_NewArray(GunLayout_Count * 6). DBSim_LoadScriptDat calls it.

entries.name: GunLayout_LoadForMechType
entries.description: Loads one gl\<HERC>.GL hardpoint list into the object pool slot for a mech type: short count, then count 26-byte records. Asserts in GUNLIST.CPP. The record's byte at +0x17 indexes the mission's loadout arrays and its byte at +7 is the cockpit weapon row the resulting mount owns.

entries.name: Proj_LookupRecordByIndex
entries.description: index * 0x24 + ProjDat_RecordTable -- direct flat-array index into PROJ.DAT's in-memory table, distinct from Proj_LookupRecord's (category,subtypeId) linear search. Called by MechLoadout_ConstructWeaponMounts with the value read from a WeaponMountTemplate's PROJ.DAT index (in-memory +0x3e), which is what resolves a real catalog weapon id to its PROJ.DAT damage record for 21 of 32 real weapons directly. Base_ArmedThinkTick and Flyer_AttackRun also call it with the literal 2, for the speed they lead by. See docs/retail/formats/weapons-dat-sim.md.

entries.name: Proj_LookupRecord
entries.description: PROJ.DAT in-memory lookup by (category, subtypeId) -- linear search against ProjDat_RecordTable, first match. Fired shots resolve their record through it again.

entries.name: MechLoadout_ConstructWeaponMounts
entries.description: Called from Mech_ConfigureLoadout (0x004175dc). Given per-hardpoint slot records (stride 0x1a) and two parallel weapon-id/secondary-key lookup tables, for each occupied slot: reads the weapon id, looks up its WeaponMountTemplate (WeaponMountTemplate_GetByWeaponId), reads that template's PROJ.DAT index (in-memory +0x3e), resolves the matching PROJ.DAT record (Proj_LookupRecordByIndex direct-index, or Proj_LookupRecord(0,secondaryKey) search for the 0x22 sentinel), then constructs a weapon-id-specific mount C++ object (one of several vtables/sizes keyed by a big switch on the weapon id) passing the resolved template/PROJ.DAT pointers. This is the mech-loadout-time mechanism that resolves a real catalog weapon id into the shot data direct-fire/beam dispatch consumes. Four live classes: WeaponMount_CtorAmmunition (ids 1-5, 13-16, 21, 26), WeaponMount_CtorEnergy (7-12, 17, 19, 20, 23-25, 28), the five pod constructors (18, 29-32), and the ELF case (6, 22) -- which is the only one that is not just a constructor call: it runs WeaponMount_CtorEnergy and then OVERWRITES the object's vtable pointer with ElfMountVtable. Id 27 (MINE) has no case at all. See docs/retail/simulation/weapon-mounts.md.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_CtorLocal
entries.description: (manager and five more, the third the int16 mount count): the locally-piloted machine's mount manager (vtable 00499238). Runs MechLoadout_ConstructWeaponMounts (0040fff8) with all six, stores PLAYER_GUNLISTVtable, runs Rtl_VectorNew(manager + 0x1f, 6, 3, 1, ARRAY_short_Ctor (00411892)) and gives each of the three fire-group arrays (+0x1f, +0x25, +0x2b) the int16 count at its +4 and Mem_NewArray(count * 2) at its +0; sets +0x1d to 0xff, then for each non-null mount takes wanted = -1 when its template's (+0x1c) int16 +0x56 is 0x12 or 0x1d-0x20 (the pods) and 0 otherwise, the first mount with 0 becoming +0x1d, and writes (array number == wanted) into the mount's entry of all three arrays, so every non-pod mount starts in group I and groups II and III start empty. Last, WeaponMounts_SetChain (00410ae4)(manager, 0), +0x16 set to 1 and one live destructor counted.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_BuildGauges
entries.description: Walks the mount array (pointer at +4, count at +8) and calls each non-null mount's own gauge factory slot, vtable +0x64. Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets calls it after building its seven top-level gauges, so the weapon rows' clickables follow theirs in the flat list; what each row registers, and why the select gadget wins where the charge bar overlaps it: docs/retail/simulation/cockpit-input.md.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_MountForHardpointSlot
entries.description: (manager, slot): the first non-null mount of the array at +4 (int16 count +8) whose .GL record (+0x18) has the slot as its byte +0x17, or null. The match is on the .GL slot, not on a position in the array.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_SelectByGauge
entries.description: (manager, gauge): the first non-null mount of the array at +4 (int16 count +8) whose vtable +0x58 slot returns nonzero for the gauge; returns 0 when none does or when that mount's byte +0x4c is clear; otherwise WeaponMounts_SetSelection(manager, index), sets the byte +0x18 and returns 1 in AX. es2_xref finds one call, from CockpitView_ArmWeaponByGauge (00432a50).

entries.name: WeaponMounts_SetSelection
entries.description: (manager, index): when index differs from the signed byte +0x1d: when that mount is linked (+0x4b) and its .GL record's (+0x18) signed partner offset +0x16 is negative, adds the offset to index, so a linked pair is armed on its first half; stores index at +0x1d and clears the word 004d25ac.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_StepSelection
entries.description: (manager, step): with the signed byte +0x1d not negative, moves an index from it by step, wrapping below 0 to the int16 count +8 less 1 and at the count to 0, until it reaches a non-null mount with +0x4c set, either unlinked (+0x4b clear) or with a positive .GL partner offset (+0x18's byte +0x16), whose int16 entry in the current fire group's array (+0x1f + the byte +0x1c * 6) is non-zero, or comes back to +0x1d; then WeaponMounts_SetSelection (00410708)(manager, index). It does not touch the single-fire flag +0x18.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_ArbitrateEnergy
entries.description: (manager, budget, selection, machine): the weapon half of the Master Energy Pool tick. The budget it hands back is the one it was given when the machine's +0xa3 is set, MissionModeFlag is 0 and UnlimitedAmmoFlag is 1. Clears ten int16 served flags, then serves up to the int16 count +8 mounts: the selection while it is not negative and not yet served, otherwise the unserved non-null mount whose vtable +0x48 answers highest, a later mount replacing the best only when strictly higher. Each served mount gets vtable +0x34(mount, budget, a word that is 1 once a mount served so far had +0x43 set), whose answer becomes the budget; then, when WeaponMount_AutoFireDue (0040ede8)(mount) answers non-zero, its vtable +0x28(mount, machine, the refund flag). Returns the budget, or the original under the refund.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_MountIsReady
entries.description: (manager, mount, mountIndex, followLink): 1 when the mount's vtable +0x2c answers non-zero, then, unless the dword +0x31 is 0, WeaponMount_RangeAllows (0040e5f8)(mount, +0x31) answers non-zero, and vtable +0x60(mount, 0)'s subtype is 5 or 3 or names a non-zero int16 at manager + 0x0a + subtype * 2; and then, when followLink is 0 and the mount is linked (+0x4b), the answer for its partner (mountIndex + the .GL record's byte +0x16) with followLink 1. Otherwise 0.
entries.signature: short __cdecl WeaponMounts_MountIsReady(void *manager, void *mount, int mountIndex, short followLink)

entries.name: WeaponMounts_ChainReady
entries.description: (manager, mount, mountIndex): 1 without asking while the single-fire byte +0x18 or the word 004d25aa is set; otherwise WeaponMounts_MountIsReady (00410970)(manager, mount, mountIndex, 0).

entries.name: WeaponMounts_AdvanceToReady
entries.description: (manager): with the signed byte +0x1d not negative and WeaponMounts_ChainReady (00410a04) refusing the armed mount, steps with WeaponMounts_StepSelection (0041074c)(manager, 1) and asks again, clearing +0x18 and returning at the first mount that passes; when the selection comes back round, or after more steps than the int16 count +8, stores the original at +0x1d and passes it to WeaponMounts_SetSelection (00410708).

entries.name: WeaponMounts_SetChain
entries.description: (manager, chain): when the chain differs from the signed byte +0x1c, stores it there, calls WeaponMounts_StepSelection (0041074c)(manager, 1) when a mount is armed (+0x1d not negative) and its int16 entry in the new chain's array (+0x1f + chain * 6) is 0, and passes the chain to ConsoleButtons_SetChainNumber (00441f68) with the panel Cockpit_GetConsoleButtons returns.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_PerFrameUpdate
entries.description: The mount manager's per-frame pass. Stores its range argument -- the distance to the selected target, measured by Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate -- into manager+0x31 BEFORE running WeaponMounts_AdvanceToReady, so the chain advance and the row lamps both see this frame's range. Then reads the weapon-panel input block, applies the chain/link commands, and walks every mount calling its vtable+0x50 gauge push with three state bytes: selected (index == manager+0x1d), in the current fire group (groups[manager+0x1c][index]), and ready (WeaponMounts_MountIsReady).

entries.name: WeaponMounts_XorChainBit
entries.description: (manager, index): XORs 1 into the index's int16 entry of the current fire group's array (+0x1f + the signed byte +0x1c * 6), so a call adds or removes the mount.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_IdleAllCapacitors
entries.description: (manager): calls vtable +0x3c, WeaponMount_WakeCapacitor (0040f4d8) on an energy mount, of each non-null mount of the array at +4 (int16 count +8).

entries.name: WeaponMounts_DemandFullChargeOnArmed_Dead
entries.description: (manager): calls vtable +0x40, WeaponMount_DemandFullCharge (0040f4f0) on an energy mount, of the armed mount (index == the signed byte +0x1d) and clears +0x43 of every other non-null mount. es2_xref finds no branch or stored pointer to it.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_FireTrigger
entries.description: (manager, trigger, machine): the weapon manager's fire entry. With the signed byte +0x1d not negative: the free-shot flag is 1 when MissionModeFlag is 0 and UnlimitedAmmoFlag is 1; the partner is the mount at the armed index + the .GL record's byte +0x16 when the armed mount is linked (+0x4b). It returns 0 unless the armed mount's vtable +0x2c answers non-zero, and the partner's, and then both vtable +0x30(mount, trigger); then the armed mount's vtable +0x28(mount, machine, free-shot flag), +0x18 cleared when its +0x2c now answers 0, the words 004d25ac and 004d25aa set to 1 when its vtable +0x60(mount, 0) answers 3, and the partner's +0x28 the same way, +0x18 cleared again when the armed mount's +0x2c answers 0. Returns 1 when it fired.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_SetTrackLatch
entries.description: (manager): stores 1 at the byte +0x14, TRACK's latch.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_ToggleLink
entries.description: (manager): with the signed byte +0x1d not negative, takes the armed mount's .GL record's (+0x18) signed partner offset +0x16; when it is not 0, the mount at the armed index + offset is not null, and the two mounts' templates (+0x1c) agree on the int16 weapon id +0x56, XORs 1 into both mounts' +0x4b.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_HandleCommand
entries.description: The weapon-mount manager's command handler (manager, code). Callers found by es2_xref: Mech_HandleCommand, and Sim_PollPlayerInput three times for the joystick's WEAPON TOGGLE, NEXT WEAPON and PREV WEAPON. 0x202-0x20b (Alt+1..0) toggle a row's fire-chain membership via WeaponMounts_ToggleChainMember; 0x11 and 0x211 (W, Alt+W) step the armed weapon +1 or -1 via WeaponMounts_StepSelection and clear the single-fire flag at manager+0x18; 0x30 advances the fire chain at +0x1c, wrapping after 2, through WeaponMounts_SetChain and sets +0x16 to 1; 0x2c calls WeaponMounts_IdleAllCapacitors; 0x0c/0x0d and 0x4a/0x4e ([-], [=], keypad [-], keypad [+]) call the armed mount's (+0x1d, when not negative) vtable +0x38, WeaponMount_AdjustPowerLevel, with whether the code was 0x0d or 0x4e. Returns 1 for those codes and 0 for any other. Its switch has no firing case: the trigger is polled, not dispatched -- see WeaponMount_TriggerHeld.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_ToggleChainMember
entries.description: (manager, row): for the first non-null mount whose .GL record's (+0x18) fire-chain byte +7 is the row and whose template's (+0x1c) int32 +0x30 is above 0 (zero for every pod): WeaponMounts_XorChainBit (00410cd0)(manager, index), then the mount's vtable +0x3c when its vtable +0x48 answers 0, and 1 returned. Returns 0 when none matches. It does not arm anything.

entries.name: Weapons_RegisterSubsystem
entries.description: Static-init registrar of the weapons module (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7abc, priority 0x20): its whole body is RegisterSubsystemLoader(Weapons_LoadResourceTables, 2).

entries.name: EnergyPod_Dtor
entries.description: ENERGY_POD vtable +0x18 (00498a84), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). The weapon-mount teardown -- one RTL destructor-count decrement per class level, HeapBlockOwner_Dtor(this+0x10, 0) on the weapon model's cell-frame holder, TSBase_Dtor(this, 0) -- then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00411174; class record at 00411120

entries.name: WeaponMount_AdjustPowerLevelNoOp
entries.description: GUN_STATE vtable +0x38 (00498e44), kept by POD_WPN, the five pods and both ammunition classes: an empty body. Only the energy classes install WeaponMount_AdjustPowerLevel.

entries.name: WeaponMount_WakeCapacitorNoOp
entries.description: GUN_STATE vtable +0x3c (00498e44), kept by POD_WPN, the five pods and both ammunition classes: an empty body. Only the energy classes install WeaponMount_WakeCapacitor.

entries.name: WeaponMount_DemandFullChargeNoOp
entries.description: GUN_STATE vtable +0x40 (00498e44), kept by POD_WPN, the five pods and both ammunition classes: an empty body. Only the energy classes install WeaponMount_DemandFullCharge.

entries.name: WeaponMount_ZeroChargeTargetNoOp
entries.description: GUN_STATE vtable +0x44 (00498e44), kept by POD_WPN, the five pods and both ammunition classes: an empty body. Only the energy classes install WeaponMount_ZeroChargeTarget.

entries.name: WeaponMount_GetEnergyPriorityZero
entries.description: GUN_STATE vtable +0x48 (00498e44), kept by POD_WPN, the five pods and both ammunition classes: returns 0. Only the energy classes install WeaponMount_GetEnergyPriority.

entries.name: WeaponMount_CountsInCombatRating_Always
entries.description: GUN_STATE vtable +0x54 (00498e44), kept by POD_WPN, the five pods, ENERGY_WPN and ELF_WPN: returns 1 in AX, so every such mount's value counts in Mech_ComputeCombatRating. The ammunition classes install WeaponMount_AmmoCountsInCombatRating.

entries.name: ShieldPod_Dtor
entries.description: SHIELD_POD vtable +0x18 (00498afc), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). The weapon-mount teardown (see EnergyPod_Dtor), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00411246; class record at 004111f2

entries.name: TargetingPod_Dtor

entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 004112f8; class record at 004112a0

entries.name: TurboPod_Dtor
entries.description: TURBO_POD vtable +0x18 (00498bec), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). The weapon-mount teardown (see EnergyPod_Dtor), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.

entries.name: EcmPod_Dtor
entries.description: ECM_POD vtable +0x18 (00498c64), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). The weapon-mount teardown (see EnergyPod_Dtor), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00411450; class record at 00411400

entries.name: Pod_DtorBase
entries.description: POD_WPN vtable +0x18 (00498cdc), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). The weapon-mount teardown (see EnergyPod_Dtor), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 004114fa; class record at 004114aa

entries.name: WeaponMount_DtorAmmunition
entries.description: (this, flags): PROJECTILE_WPN vtable +0x18 (00498d54). Returns at once for a null mount; otherwise four destructor-count decrements around HeapBlockOwner_Dtor on the mount's shape-instance block and TSBase_Dtor(this, 0), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 004115a5; class record at 0041154d

entries.name: WeaponMount_DrainAmmo
entries.description: PROJECTILE_WPN and GRENADE_WPN vtable +0x4c, the slot the energy classes fill with WeaponMount_DrainCapacitor: zeroes the rounds remaining (+0x7b).

entries.name: WeaponMount_DtorEnergy
entries.description: ENERGY_WPN vtable +0x18 (00498dcc), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). The weapon-mount teardown (see EnergyPod_Dtor), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 0041165a; class record at 00411606

entries.name: WeaponMount_ZeroChargeTarget
entries.description: Energy mount vtable +0x44 (and the ELF table's): zeroes the charge target (+0x7b) and the mid-charge flag (+0x43), and sets +0x34 and +0x3c so the next WeaponMount_PushEnergyGaugeState carries the new target out to the charge bar.

entries.name: WeaponMount_DrainCapacitor
entries.description: Energy mount vtable +0x4c (and the ELF table's): zeroes the charge (+0x7d) and the charge target (+0x7b), and sets +0x34 and +0x3c as WeaponMount_ZeroChargeTarget does.

entries.name: WeaponMount_DtorBase
entries.description: GUN_STATE vtable +0x18 (00498e44, RTTI 'GUN_STATE', 0x77 bytes, derived from CONFIG_PART), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). The weapon-mount teardown (see EnergyPod_Dtor), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00411743; class record at 004116ef

entries.name: WeaponMountTemplate_ElementCtor
entries.description: (record): returns its argument -- the per-element constructor Weapons_LoadResourceTables hands Rtl_VectorNew for the WEAPONS.DAT mount-template table (PUSH at 0040fd97: 0x58 bytes each, count WeaponMountTemplate_Count (004a9974), result stored at WeaponMountTemplate_Table (004a9970)); the LEAs of +0x12, +0x1a, +0x40 and +0x46 are inlined empty member constructors.

entries.name: GunLayoutRecord_ElementCtor
entries.description: (record): returns its argument -- the per-element constructor GunLayout_LoadForMechType hands Rtl_VectorNew for a .GL file's 26-byte hardpoint records (PUSH at 0040ff56: element size 0x1a, count the file's leading int16, array stored at the slot's +2); the LEA of +0x10 is an inlined empty member constructor.

entries.name: ARRAY_short_Ctor
entries.description: (array): ARRAY<short>'s constructor (6-byte class record at 0041bfc3, destructor ARRAY_short_Dtor): zeroes the buffer pointer at +0 and counts one live destructor (*Rtl_DtorCountPtr += 1). WeaponMounts_CtorLocal runs it through Rtl_VectorNew(manager+0x1f, 6, 3, 1, it) over the three fire-group arrays, then fills each one's buffer (+0) and count (+4).

entries.name: WeaponMounts_ArbitrateEnergyWithSelection
entries.description: (manager, budget, machine): PLAYER_GUNLIST vtable +0x00 (00499238): WeaponMounts_ArbitrateEnergy (004107e4)(manager, budget, the sign-extended byte +0x1d, machine), the pool turn that serves the selected mount first.

entries.name: GrenadeMount_Dtor
entries.description: GRENADE_WPN vtable +0x18 (00499248), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). The weapon-mount teardown (see EnergyPod_Dtor), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00411969; class record at 004118a6

entries.name: ElfMount_Dtor
entries.description: ELF_WPN vtable +0x18 (ElfMountVtable, 004992c0), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). The weapon-mount teardown (see EnergyPod_Dtor), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 004119c3; class record at 004118fa

entries.name: WeaponMounts_ArbitrateEnergyNoSelection
entries.description: (manager, budget, arg): WeaponMounts_ArbitrateEnergy(manager, budget, -1, arg), the energy pool turn with no selected mount served first. Slot 0 of the GUNLIST vtable 00499338, the base manager's; es2_xref finds one reference, that stored pointer.

entries.name: SimObject_ComponentPositionNoOp
entries.description: ACTOR and FLYER vtable +0x58: push ebp / mov ebp,esp / pop ebp / ret. Writes nothing to its out-parameter.

entries.name: SimObject_ComponentNearestAim_None
entries.description: ACTOR and FLYER vtable +0x54: returns -1 (OR EAX,-1), the 'no component' answer Mech_ComponentNearestAim gives when no slot is occupied.

entries.name: SimObject_GetShieldByHeadingZero
entries.description: Vtable +0x34 of the ACTOR base, the flyer and all five structure tables: returns 0. Only the mech overrides it (Mech_GetShieldByHeading).

entries.name: SimObject_GetSpeedZero
entries.description: Vtable +0x38 of the ACTOR base and all five structure tables: returns 0. The mech (Mech_GetSpeed) and the flyer (Flyer_GetSpeed) override it.

entries.name: SimObject_GetTorsoTwistAngleZero
entries.description: Vtable +0x3c of the ACTOR base, the flyer, BASE, RADAR_BASE and LC_BASE: returns 0. GUN_BASE and VEHICLE replace it with Base_GetTurretAngle, the mech with Mech_GetTorsoTwistAngle.

entries.name: SimObject_ReceiveSquadOrder_Refuse
entries.description: Vtable +0x28 of the ACTOR base, the flyer and all five structure tables: returns 0, where Mech_ReceiveSquadOrder returns 1 for an order it took.

entries.name: SimObject_HandleCommandNoOp
entries.description: Vtable +0x2c of the ACTOR base and all five structure tables: returns 0 and acts on nothing. The mech installs Mech_HandleCommand; the flyer has its own stub, Flyer_HandleCommandNoOp.

entries.name: SimObject_GetAimPointZero
entries.description: The shared base's vtable +0x30 (ACTOR's SimObjectBaseVtable and FlyerVtable), (this, outEye, outOffset): memsets both 6-byte out triples to zero, i.e. aim at the object's own origin with no offset. The structure tables wrap it in Base_GetAimPoint (0040351c) and the mech table installs Mech_GetAimPoint (004155c4).

entries.name: SimObject_GetAimNodeTransform_None
entries.description: Vtable +0x24 on the flyer and the SimObject base: return 0. Every caller's null branch falls back to the object's raw origin for aiming and to a literal 500 for sight height. The mech's own is Mech_GetAimNodeTransform; all five structure vtables install Base_GetAimNodeTransform (00403548) instead.

entries.name: SimObject_GetBodyRadiusZero
entries.description: ACTOR and FLYER vtable +0x5c: returns 0. The mech installs Mech_GetBodyRadius, the structures Base_GetBodyRadius.

entries.name: SimObject_GetCollisionRadiusZero
entries.description: ACTOR and FLYER vtable +0x7c: returns 0, so a flyer adds nothing to the collision gap a walking machine measures against it. The mech installs Mech_GetCollisionRadius, the structures Base_GetCollisionRadius.

entries.name: SimObject_TickNoOp
entries.description: Vtable +0x14 of the ACTOR base and all five structure tables (LC_BASE, VEHICLE, GUN_BASE, BASE, RADAR_BASE): returns 1 in AX and does nothing. The mech and flyer install their behaviour move dispatchers here (Behaviour_DispatchMove, Flyer_DispatchMove). Mech_AiTick, which calls the slot on each group member, discards what it returns. See docs/retail/simulation/ai-dispatch.md#how-the-per-tick-work-reaches-a-state.

entries.name: SimObject_CompareCombatRatingStub
entries.description: The shared base's vtable +0x4c: returns 1 in AX. es2_xref finds it in seven tables: ACTOR's, the flyer's and the five structure tables. Ai_SelectTarget (00411fa0) dispatches this slot on the ASKING object, so a structure or a flyer scores every candidate against column 1 of the four Q10 weight tables at 0049933c/42/48, whatever the ratings actually are. The mech table installs Mech_CompareCombatRating (0041cabc) in the slot.

entries.name: SimObject_BearingInSensorArc
entries.description: Vtable +0x44 of the ACTOR base, the mech and the flyer: (bearing - obj+0x10 + 0x3800) < 0x7000 unsigned, so +/-78.75 degrees about the object's heading. Callers fold the aim twist into the bearing before calling. The five structure classes install Base_BearingInSensorArc_Always instead.

entries.name: SimObject_AiOnTakingFire
entries.description: The shared base's vtable +0x50 (AiOnTakingFire), which es2_xref finds in ACTOR's SimObjectBaseVtable, the FlyerVtable and all five structure tables, (this, attacker, damage): calls Detection_ShareContact(this, attacker) and does nothing else, so a structure or aircraft that is shot passes its attacker on to its own side and has no other reaction. Mech_AiOnTakingFire, the mech's override, calls it directly with (this, attacker, 0) when the attacker's side byte differs from its own.

entries.name: SimObject_MissileLockState_Always
entries.description: Vtable +0x6c of the ACTOR base, the flyer and all five structure tables: returns 1 in AX for every missile subtype. The slot is the launcher's own lock gate and Mech_MissileLockState is the only override, so a missile launched by a flyer or a structure is always handed the launcher's selected target.

entries.name: SimObject_ComponentPresent_Always
entries.description: SimObjectBaseVtable and FlyerVtable +0x84: a bare return 1.

entries.name: SimObject_NextTargetableComponent_None
entries.description: SimObjectBaseVtable and FlyerVtable +0x80: answers -1 and writes -1, so a flyer has no components a targeting pod can single out.

entries.name: SimObject_CreditNeutralisedTargetNoOp
entries.description: An empty body (push ebp; mov ebp,esp; pop ebp; ret). es2_xref finds it in the +0x60 kill-credit slot of SimObjectBaseVtable, FlyerVtable and the five structure vtables; the mech's override is Mech_CreditNeutralisedTarget.

entries.name: SimObject_AiOnLineOfFireBlockedNoOp
entries.description: Vtable +0x64 (AiOnLineOfFireBlocked) of the ACTOR base, the flyer and all five structure tables, by es2_xref: an empty body. The mech table installs Mech_AiOnLineOfFireBlocked.

entries.name: SimObject_ApplyExplosiveDamage
entries.description: The SimObject base class's vtable +0x70, which a FLYER inherits. No roll, no component selection, no shields and no range test: applies (blastRadius - (distance - vtable +0x5c body radius)) * damage / blastRadius to component 0 through vtable +0x74, the distance taken from the hit point to the object's position. A blast inside the body radius scales by more than one, though a flyer's +0x5c is 0.
entries.signature: void __cdecl SimObject_ApplyExplosiveDamage(SimObject *this, short damage, int *hitPoint, short blastRadius, SimObject *attacker)

entries.name: SimObject_SetOutOfActionCounters
entries.description: Copies ten counter refs to obj+0x1ba and ten ops to obj+0x1ce -- the slots Mech_ReportOutOfAction runs. es2_xref.py finds three calls, all in DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects: a roster mech (record 0x42/0x56), a flyer (0x2e/0x42) and a structure (0x06/0x1a). The mech call sits on the roster side of that function's index < rosterCount test, so the player's squad does not reach it there; Mech_Constructor sets refs 0-2 to -1.

entries.name: Mech_ReportOutOfAction
entries.description: (object): with a group at +0x45, Group_ReportIfAllOutOfAction (00423f30)(group, object); then for each of ten slots, the int16 counter refs from +0x1ba and the int16 operations from +0x1ce, a non-negative ref writes that counter of DAT_004a9ef4: operation 1 zeroes it, 2 adds 1, 0xd-0x10 store the operation less 0xc, anything else writes nothing. es2_xref.py finds four calls: both of Mech_ComponentDamageWrite's branches, Flyer_ComponentDamageWrite and Base_ApplyDamage.

entries.name: Ai_KnowsObject
entries.description: The AI's knowledge test, far looser than the player's: radar-visible (+0x95) within 999999 units, or a contact this machine holds (this+0xc2 + other[0x4b]) at any range.

entries.name: Ai_TargetStateTier
entries.description: (object): with a behaviour descriptor at +0x4d, 2 when its flag byte +0xd (flag bit 5) is set, 1 when its byte +0xc (bit 4) is, otherwise 0; 0 with no descriptor.

entries.name: Mech_AiTick
entries.description: One machine's whole AI frame, calling the three behaviour dispatchers through vtable +0x1c, +0x14 and +0x18. No-ops unless a descriptor is installed at mech+0x4d. Order: reassess (vtable +0x1c) when the dwell countdown at mech+0x52 has reached 0; Timer_CountDown against that countdown unless descriptor+0x08[0] is set, which is true of every state but deciding, the five combat states, driving off en and fleeing; move (vtable +0x14); then think (vtable +0x18) unless mech+0xaf is set, in which case think is skipped and the flag cleared -- a think returning nonzero zeroes its own countdown. Ends with Behaviour_CountTick on the behaviour block at +0x4d. es2_xref finds one caller, Group_OrderTick (00423a74) at 00423af5, which ticks each member of a group that has entered the mission.

entries.name: Formation_RotateAndAddOffset
entries.description: Rotates a formation offset into world space and adds it to a position. Takes the group leader (first entry of the group's member array at group+0xc), builds its rotation matrix from its euler triple (BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14, leader+0xc -> leader+0x12) when the flag at leader+0x32 is clear and sets the flag, then rotates the offset's x/y by the matrix's first four shorts (Math_Rotate2DPoint) -- the matrix stores its XY block first, so this is the leader's XY rotation, a plain heading rotation for a level leader: worldDX = dx*cos - dy*sin, worldDY = dx*sin + dy*cos. Adds the rotated x/y and the offset's unrotated z into the point it is handed. es2_xref finds three calls, from Mech_ApplyFormationOffset, Base_ApplyFormationOffset and Flyer_ApplyFormationOffset.

entries.name: ObjectList_Add
entries.description: (list, obj): stores obj at entry int16 +6 of the array at +0, stores that index at obj's int16 +0x4b and adds 1 to +6.

entries.name: ObjectList_Init
entries.description: (list, capacity): Mem_NewArray(capacity * 4) at +0 and the int16 capacity at +4.

entries.name: ObjList_SwapRemove
entries.description: (list, obj): list->items[obj+0x4b] = list->items[count - 1], then count (the short at list+6) -= 1, where items is the pointer at list+0. It does not rewrite the moved item's own +0x4b. Callers found by es2_xref (nine call sites): the deleting destructors of VEHICLE, GUN_BASE, BASE and RADAR_BASE, which call it on maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList on flags bit 0 in place of freeing the object, SimObject_OperatorDelete, and two sites inside functions the dump bounds at 00426eac and 00406a98.

entries.name: ObjectList_Next
entries.description: (list, obj): the entry after obj in the list, wrapping: items(+0)[(obj's int16 +0x4b + 1) % the int16 count +6]. es2_xref finds two calls, from Sim_DispatchCommand.

entries.name: ObjectList_Prev
entries.description: (list, obj): the entry before obj in the list, wrapping: items(+0)[(obj's int16 +0x4b + count - 1) % the int16 count +6]. The reverse of ObjectList_Next (00411e40).

entries.name: Ai_IsTargetable
entries.description: (this, candidate, mask): whether an AI machine may target a candidate. 0 when the candidate's group's (+0x45) side byte +0x12 is this machine's, when it is destroyed (+0x99) or collapsed (+0xb4), when Ai_KnowsObject (00411c58)(this, candidate) answers 0, when it is invulnerable (+0xb7), with mask bit 0x10 when its class +0x1a8 is this machine's, and for a class-2 candidate when +0xa5, +0xa4 or +0x99 is set; then 0 when the first member of this machine's group's array +0xc is locally piloted (+0xa3), the word DAT_004a9ed8 is 3 and Group_OrderTargetObject (004238a0)(group) is the candidate, and 0 when this machine's +0x9a is set and the candidate is CockpitViewInstance's +0x210; otherwise 1.

entries.name: Ai_SelectTarget
entries.description: The AI's general target acquisition, used by mechs, flyers and armed structures: (this, mask, coneLimit) walks the live object list and returns the best-scoring candidate, or 0. Candidates pass Ai_IsTargetable; one at +0xa4 (immobilised) is skipped unless it is the designated target and this machine's side byte (group+0x12) is nonzero; then a tier bar of 2*designated+alive, where designated is Group_IsOrderTarget with a group order verb of 0 (every candidate counts as designated when mask bit 0 is clear) and the bar starts at 1, or 0 under verb 3. Range, by Math_DistanceBetweenPoints, caps at 1000000 for the designated target and 100000 otherwise. Score starts at b = 0x1000 - (bearingError >> 3) (0 error with mask 0x20), a nonzero coneLimit rejecting anything past it, as Q10(70, b), raised inside 60000 to b / max(range >> 12, 1) when that is larger, then multiplied by the Q10 weight tables at 0049933c (candidate targets this), 00499342 (candidate's behaviour descriptor +9 clear and not locally piloted), 00499348 (candidate targets something else) and 0049934e (by object class, a class-1 candidate targeting this re-indexed as 0), indexed by vtable +0x4c, and divided by one more than the candidate's other holders (+0x1a2, less this machine's own hold). A higher tier replaces the best whatever its score and raises the bar. Mask: 0x01 restrict the designated bonus, 0x02 drop the shooting-at-me weight, 0x04 drop the crowding divisor, 0x10 reject own class, 0x20 ignore bearing.

entries.name: Sim_DetectionTick
entries.description: (): three passes over maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList. First, for each object whose group's (+0x45) dword +0x14 is 0, Math_CountdownTimerTick on its LOS-cache timer +0x1e2 and its contact-decay timer +0x1e5; when the second answers 0, its counter gets 10000 + Math_RandomBelow(004d261d, 1000) and Detection_DecayContacts (0041251c) runs on the object. Second, for each object whose group's +0x14 is 0, neither immobilised (+0xa4) nor destroyed (+0x99), whose group's side byte +0x12 is 0: Detection_Sweep (004128f8), except that a locally-piloted one (+0xa3) is held back, and the last one held is swept after the walk. Third, clears every object's +0xa2.

entries.name: Detection_DecayContacts
entries.description: (object): clears its radar visibility +0x95, then for each entry whose group's (+0x45) dword +0x14 is 0, whose side byte +0x12 differs from the object's group's, and which the object holds as a contact (+0xc2 + the entry's +0x4b): unless Math_GroundDistanceBetweenPoints (004927c4)(object +0x26, entry +0x26) is at most 100000 and Detection_LineOfSight (00412608)(object, entry) answers non-zero, clears that contact byte and the entry's for the object. The range is on the ground plane, where the sweep's are 3D.

entries.name: Detection_LineOfSight
entries.description: Terrain ray (Terrain_RayHitDistance, radius 0, distance unread) between two objects' origins (+0x26), each raised by its vtable +0x24 record's +0x1c, or by 500 with no record; 1 when the ray reports no ground hit. (self, other): cached per pair in self's row table, byte self+0x132 + other[+0x4b], and the cached byte is returned. The cache gate tests OTHER's countdown at +0x1e3 and reloads SELF's -- verified in raw disassembly at 00412617 and 0041263f, so it is the original's own asymmetry and not a decompiler slip. The reload is 5000 + Math_RandomBelow(1000). Only human-side objects sweep, so Cybrid timers stay zero and those pairs are re-walked whenever asked.

entries.name: Detection_ShareContact
entries.description: (spotter, contact): when their groups' (+0x45) side bytes +0x12 differ, for each object whose group's dword +0x14 is 0 and whose side is the spotter's, the spotter included: within 100000 of the contact (Math_DistanceBetweenPoints) it sets the object's contact byte (+0xc2 + the contact's +0x4b); within 50000 it also sets the contact's +0x9e and runs Action_Activate on the object's own +0x1b2 unless that is null or the object's +0xa2 is set. Detection_Sweep (004128f8) and SimObject_AiOnTakingFire (00411aec) call it.

entries.name: SimObject_AiEnemySightedNoOp
entries.description: Vtable +0x48 (AiEnemySighted) of the ACTOR base, the flyer and all five structure tables, by es2_xref: an empty body. The mech table installs Mech_AiEnemySighted, which calls out a contact.

entries.name: Mech_AiEnemySighted
entries.description: (machine, object): mech vtable +0x48, the enemy-detected callout. Sets the byte 00499358 to 1 when it is 0. For a locally-piloted machine (+0xa3) it sets EnemySighted_CalledInLatch[object+0x4b]. Otherwise it ticks EnemySighted_CalloutRateLimit (004a9be8); then, when the object's class +0x1a8 is not 1, the machine's group is PlayerMech's, the latch is clear, the object is not radar-visible (+0x95) and neither the machine nor PlayerMech holds it as a contact (+0xc2), it sets the latch and, when the counter 004a9be9 is 0, posts squad message 1 through Ai_PostSquadMessage (00420a98)(machine, 1, 0) and stores 10000 there.

entries.name: Detection_Sweep
entries.description: (machine): one human-side object's look around, over each entry that is neither immobilised (+0xa4) nor destroyed (+0x99), whose group's (+0x45) dword +0x14 is 0 and side byte +0x12 is 1, with d = Math_DistanceBetweenPoints(machine +0x26, entry +0x26). When the two are not both radar-visible (+0x95), either has its scanner on (+0x96), d is below 200000 and Detection_LineOfSight (00412608)(machine, entry) answers non-zero: when the entry's +0x96 is set or d is below 140000, the machine's vtable +0x48(machine, entry) and the entry's +0x95 set; when the machine's +0x96 is set or d is below 140000, the machine's +0x95 set. Past 80000 it goes on to the next entry. When each holds the other as a contact (+0xc2 + the other's +0x4b): below 50000 the entry's +0x9e set, Action_Activate of the machine's +0x1b2 unless it is null or the machine's +0xa2 is set, the machine's +0x9e set and the entry's +0x1b2 the same way. Otherwise, with h = Math_HeadingToward from the machine to the entry: when the machine's vtable +0x44(machine, its vtable +0x3c + h) and the line of sight answer non-zero, its vtable +0x48(machine, entry) and then Detection_ShareContact (00412704)(machine, entry), or for a locally-piloted machine (+0xa3) its own contact byte instead; and when the entry's +0x44(entry, its +0x3c + h - 0x8000) and the line of sight answer non-zero, Detection_ShareContact(entry, machine).

entries.name: Group_OrderSubjectObject
entries.description: The object a group's current order names -- order+0x0e read as an object pointer. Valid when the order's kind discriminator (order+0x0c) is 1, 2 or 3.

entries.name: Group_OrderSubjectGroup
entries.description: The group record a group's current order names -- order+0x0e read as a group pointer. Valid when the order's kind discriminator (order+0x0c) is 0. Identical code to Group_OrderSubjectObject; the two exist as separately typed accessors.

entries.name: Group_IsWipedOut
entries.description: (group) -> AX: 1 when every member in the group's member array (+0xc, count +0x10) is out of the fight -- destroyed (+0x99), immobilised (+0xa4) or disarmed (+0xa5); 0 as soon as one member is still in it. A group with no members answers 1. es2_xref finds one caller, Group_NoRivalOrderOnSubject (00412e74), the guarding-order completion test. With the +0xa5 term a group of ordinary structures -- which Base_Construct's Plain and Radar arms spawn already disarmed -- reads as wiped out from the moment it is built.

entries.name: Group_AllMembersDisarmed
entries.description: True when every member of the mission group (member pointers at group+0x0c, count at group+0x10) is disarmed (+0xa5); an empty group answers true, since the loop returns 1 on running off the end. The group form of objective condition 7 in Mission_EvaluateObjectives.

entries.name: Group_ConditionTier
entries.description: A mission group's 0-4 condition tier: 4 when every member is immobilised (+0xa4) or destroyed (+0x99); else 3 when the lost fraction reaches 650/1024 or the mean overall damage across all members reaches 0xc1; else 2 at 250/1024 or 0x81; else 1 at mean damage 0x33; else 0. The mean includes dead members. Both the mean and the fraction divide by the member count (group+0x10) unchecked, so a group with no members divides by zero.

entries.name: Group_OrderSubjectEngaged
entries.description: Whether the group's current order (group+0x44[group+0x6c]) has had its subject engaged: for an order whose kind (+0x0c) is 0, Group_AnyMemberEngaged of the subject group; otherwise the subject object's own +0x9e byte, sign-extended. es2_xref finds no caller.

entries.name: Group_AnyMemberEngaged
entries.description: True when any member of the group has been engaged (+0x9e). The one helper of Group_StatusLineIndex that is also live: Mission_EvaluateObjectives calls it for objective condition 6.

entries.name: Group_OrderSubjectCondition
entries.description: The 0-4 condition tier of the subject a group's current order names. For an order naming an object (order+0x0c in 1..3): 4 when destroyed (+0x99) or collapsed (+0xb4), otherwise the object's vtable +0x40 overall damage banded at 0x32/0x80/0xc0. For an order naming a group (order+0x0c == 0): Group_ConditionTier over its members.

entries.name: Group_OrderSubjectDestroyed
entries.description: Whether Group_OrderSubjectCondition reports tier 4 for the group's current order subject. The completion test for order verb 0 and half of the test for verb 2.

entries.name: Group_NoRivalOrderOnSubject
entries.description: (group): 1 unless another of the 0x7a-byte mission groups has a different side byte (+0x12), a current order whose subject (+0x0e) is the same pointer as this group's current order's, and is not wiped out by Group_IsWipedOut (00412be4); 0 at the first such group.

entries.name: Group_AnyMemberObjectiveSighted
entries.description: True when any member of the group has +0x9f set. Called only from Group_StatusLineIndex, which is unreachable.

entries.name: Group_AnyMemberDataLinked
entries.description: True when any member of the group has +0xa0 set. Called only from Group_StatusLineIndex, which is unreachable.

entries.name: Group_AnyMemberScoredAKill
entries.description: True when any member of the group has +0xa6 set. Called only from Group_StatusLineIndex, which is unreachable -- so mech+0xa6, latched by Mech_CreditNeutralisedTarget, has no live reader.

entries.name: Group_StatusLineIndex
entries.description: Maps a mission group and an order verb onto a status line index -- the group report. UNREACHABLE: no relative call in the code section and the dword 00412f90 occurs nowhere in the file, so no table or vtable holds it. The six Group_AnyMember*/Group_OrderSubject* helpers below exist for it, and all but Group_AnyMemberEngaged are dead with it.

entries.name: Mission_StatusForAlert
entries.description: The wrapper both alert paths go through: calls Mission_Status with the script.dat objective selector and the publish flag, and when publish is set also records the answer in DAT_004a9ed0, the status already raised. The poll passes 0; [Q] passes 1, so reading the status yourself is enough to stop the poll announcing it. Returns the status in AX.

entries.name: Mission_PollStatus
entries.description: The objective poll, called with the player's machine from Sim_MainTick (the one call es2_xref finds), which makes the call only while that machine's +0x99 is clear. Steps MissionAlertTimer (004a9ee9) and then MissionPollTimer (004a9ee6) through Math_CountdownTimerTick, and returns -1 without evaluating while the poll counter is above 0 and SimObject_IsOutsideMissionBox is false. Otherwise it takes Mission_StatusForAlert(machine, 0). A status whose DAT_0049935c entry is set and which differs from the last raised status (DAT_004a9ed0) arms the alert delay the first time (MissionAlertArmed 004a9eec := 1, counter 004a9eea := 10000), and is stored in DAT_004a9ed0 and returned in AX once that counter is 0 or the status is 2. Every other path re-arms the poll counter (004a9ee7) to 10000 and returns -1. 10000 counts is about 4.9 s. This function never clears MissionAlertArmed.

entries.name: Mission_GroupOrderCompleteOnRoute
entries.description: Objective condition 0: finds the group's order slot whose route (+0x08) is the record's waypoint group and answers that slot's completion flag at group+0x70.

entries.name: Mission_EvaluateObjectives
entries.description: Walks the mission's objective array (script.dat block 12) and reduces it to a status: a failure condition holding, every required record holding, or neither, each split by whether the player is clear of threats (6/10, 9/10, 5/4). The first time a record's condition holds it applies its ten counter pairs to DAT_004a9ef4 (4 set, 5 clear, 6 increment, 7 decrement) and latches +0x22; the first required record not holding is published at DAT_004d1f1c as the failure text.

entries.name: Mission_Status
entries.description: The mission judgement: the player's own condition, then the mission box, then Mission_EvaluateObjectives. The second argument, the objective selector Mission_StatusForAlert passes, is not read. The third argument suppresses the hold, both box arms and the SYSTEM.STR post.

entries.name: Mission_IsOutsideBox
entries.description: (point, margin): returns 1 when the point's x and y are not strictly inside Mission_Box (004aa6c4) widened by margin on every side, 0 when they are. It reads the box and writes nothing; DBSim_LoadScriptDat builds the box inline. SimObject_IsOutsideMissionBox and SimObject_IsFarOutsideMissionBox call it for Mission_Status's two box arms.

entries.name: SimObject_IsFarOutsideMissionBox
entries.description: (obj): Mission_IsOutsideBox(obj+0x26, 110000) -- whether the object is outside Mission_Box widened by 110000 on every side. Mission_Status answers 8 on it, ahead of the plain box test.

entries.name: SimObject_IsOutsideMissionBox
entries.description: (obj): Mission_IsOutsideBox(obj+0x26, 0) -- whether the object's position is outside Mission_Box. Mission_Status answers 7 on it, and Mission_PollStatus tests it when its poll interval expires.

entries.name: Mission_IsClearOfThreats
entries.description: Whether nothing hostile is working on this object. Walks the live-object list, skipping an object whose group has not arrived (group+0x14), one on the subject's own side, and one out of the fight (+0xa5, +0xa4 or +0x99). The subject is not clear when a survivor knows it (Ai_KnowsObject) within 80000, 100000 if it is that survivor's selected target (+0x1a4); or, when the subject is not in LocalPlayerMech's group, when the survivor's group's current order names it (Group_IsOrderTarget) and either that group's route has a waypoint after its cursor (Route_WaypointAt) or the survivor knows the subject, at any range.

entries.name: Group_IsWrittenOff
entries.description: A group's condition tier against its side's threshold -- 3 for a human group, 4 for a Cybrid one.

entries.name: Group_AllMembersClearOfThreats
entries.description: False when the group is written off, or when any member that is not destroyed fails Mission_IsClearOfThreats.

entries.name: Group_OrderSubjectRouteExhausted
entries.description: Whether the current order's subject has no waypoint after its route cursor: returns Route_WaypointAt(route, cursor + 1) == 0, where the route is the subject group's own (+0x04) for an order of kind 0 and the subject object's group's (object+0x45, then +0x04) otherwise. es2_xref finds no reference to it, Group_StatusLineIndex included.

entries.name: Group_OrderSubjectArrivedAndClear
entries.description: Whether the current order's subject is deployed and clear of threats, 1 or 0: for an order of kind 0, the subject group's deployment action (+0x14) is null and Group_AllMembersClearOfThreats holds; otherwise the subject object's group (+0x45) has a null +0x14 and Mission_IsClearOfThreats holds for the object. Callers found by es2_xref: two calls in Group_StatusLineIndex, for which es2_xref finds no caller.

entries.name: Shield_Init
entries.description: Initializes the 5-field shield struct (mech+0x222) from the mech-type base capacity (typeRecord+0xc0): max fields = baseValue, current fields = baseValue>>1 (default 50/50 split).

entries.name: Shield_SetMax
entries.description: Trivial setter: writes the shield array's total capacity at shieldStruct+6 (mech+0x228). The base capacity at shieldStruct+8 is left alone. es2_xref finds one call, from Mech_ComputeShieldCapacity.

entries.name: Shield_RefillToBalance
entries.description: Fills the shield array to its max and splits it at the current balance: front = Q10(balance, max), rear = max - front. Called from Mech_ConfigureLoadout right after Shield_SetMax, so a mech spawns with full shields at whatever capacity its pods bought it.

entries.name: Shield_BalanceAdjust
entries.description: Nudges the shield balance (shield block +0x4, mech+0x226) by +0x66 (102) for a nonzero direction and -0x66 for zero, clamped to [0, 0x400]. 102 is just short of a tenth of the range, so five presses from the 0x200 centre reach 1022 or 2 and the sixth hits the clamp.

entries.name: Shield_RechargeTick
entries.description: Shield recharge primitive: clamps the request to at most 5 units/tick and to the remaining deficit, redistributes front/rear via balance using Math_RateLimitedMoveToward, returns the unclaimed portion.

entries.name: Shield_BalanceInputRead
entries.description: Per frame for the player: copies the shield gauge's 15-byte state block (UI slot +0x1e9, ShieldsGauge_GetStateBlock); if the block's byte 13 is set calls Shield_BalanceAdjust(1) and clears it, else if byte 14 is set calls Shield_BalanceAdjust(0) and clears it. Then writes (front << 10) / baseMax, (rear << 10) / baseMax (shield block +0x0, +0x2 over +0x8) and the raw balance (+0x4) into the block and hands it back through ShieldsGauge_SetStateBlock.

entries.name: Mech_ShieldAbsorb_Explosive
entries.description: Explosion path own separate shield-absorption implementation (parallel to, not shared with, Mech_ShieldAbsorb_DirectFire). scaledDamage = Math_Q10Multiply(1000, damage) comes off the chosen facing (a zero front argument selects the second short, the rear); a negative facing clamps to 0 and the function returns overflow*0x400/1000. THE TWO SCALES ARE EXACT INVERSES -- 1000/1024 in and 1024/1000 out -- so a blast overflow is its own face value and the exchange rate matches direct fire. Reading the input scale as >>8 makes this look like a 4x amplification and a retail bug; the instruction is Math_Q10Multiply and there is no bug.
entries.signature: int __cdecl Mech_ShieldAbsorb_Explosive(short *shieldPair, short front, short damage)

entries.name: Mech_ShieldAbsorb_DirectFire
entries.description: Direct-fire shield absorption: picks front/rear zone by where the muzzle sits in the mech frame, absorbed = min(incomingDamage, remainingShieldInZone), hard cap not threshold gate. Unlike Mech_ShieldAbsorb_Explosive it scales neither its input nor its output. Returns the ray's entry point into the hit cylinder, so a fully absorbed shot still stops the ray.

entries.name: Behaviour_SetState
entries.description: __cdecl(block, descriptor): installs a behaviour state in the 0x45-byte block a mech or flyer carries at +0x4d, the AI state machine's transition primitive -- its call sites are the edge list (ai-dispatch.md, Transitions). Stores the descriptor pointer at +0x00 and zeroes the int at +0x09; adds 0xd to the 16-bit global DAT_004a9bf4 and seeds the countdown at +0x05 to descriptor+0x04 plus (that word & 0xf); memsets +0x35 for 0x10, sets +0x36 to 1, and memsets +0x0d for 0x28. It does not touch the machine's selected target.

entries.name: Behaviour_CountTick
entries.description: (block): called from Mech_AiTick at 00411d58, the one call es2_xref finds. When block+0x36 (set to 1 by Behaviour_SetState) is set it clears it and counts nothing; otherwise it sets block+0x35 to 1 and increments the int block+0x09. So +0x09 counts the AI ticks a state has run, less the one it was installed in.

entries.name: Behaviour_BuildStateTable
entries.description: The C++ static initialiser that builds the 22 Mech behaviour state descriptors, 0x3e bytes each, at BehaviourStateTable (004993a4); es2_xref finds its address once, in the priority-0x20 Borland _INIT_ entry at 004a7ac2. For state N it writes +0x00 the name (BehaviourStateNames 00499c10 + offset), +0x04 a dwell immediate, +0x08 a 16-bit mask immediate expanded through Behaviour_ExpandFlagBits, +0x18/+0x24/+0x30 the think, move and reassess triples copied in that order from the 0x24-byte block at BehaviourSlotBlocks (004998f8 + 0x24*N), and +0x3c an immediate short. The per-state values are ai-dispatch.md's state table.

entries.name: Flyer_BuildStateTable
entries.description: Static initialiser for the Flyer class' own behaviour state table: seven 0x3c-byte descriptors at FlyerBehaviourStateTable (00499cf8), each taking its name from FlyerBehaviourStateNames (00499f98), a dwell immediate, a 16-bit flag mask through Behaviour_ExpandFlagBits, and its three {func,thisDelta,vtableIndex} triples copied from FlyerBehaviourSlotBlocks (00499e9c). Sits immediately after Behaviour_BuildStateTable's RET; its address is the priority-0x20 entry at 004a7ac8 in Borland's _INIT_ table, and es2_xref finds no call to it.

entries.name: Behaviour_ExpandFlagBits
entries.description: (out16, mask2): unpacks two mask bytes into 16 one-byte booleans, low bit first ((byte >> k) & 1). Callers found by es2_xref: 22 calls in Behaviour_BuildStateTable and 7 in Flyer_BuildStateTable, each on a descriptor's +0x08. The masks the mech builder passes are 0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x03, 0x05, 0x06, 0x09, 0x12 and 0x21, and the flyer builder's 0x00 and 0x01; what each bit means to its readers is ai-dispatch.md's 'The flag bits'.

entries.name: Mech_ApplySquadCondition
entries.description: Writes a player-squad machine's carried-over condition into its damage arrays at spawn; es2_xref finds one caller, DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects' squad branch (004258de), after Mech_ConfigureLoadout. Components 0-12 take the external entries one for one, entry n against component n's armour. Arguments are the damage header at mech+0x206 and the 0x7e-byte squad record's three player.mec condition spans: +0x3c external (13), +0x56 internal (10), +0x6a hardpoint (10), each 0-100. Each entry becomes damage (100 - condition) * maximum / 100: components 0-12 against the piece's armour, components 13-18 zeroed; internals 0-8 against their maxima, internal 9 (pilot) and 10-11 zeroed, so the internal span's tenth entry (overall condition) is not read; components 19-28 against the mount's armour plus the maximum of internal 12+i, and past the armour the mount is written -1 and the rest goes to that internal (-1 past its maximum). Internals 12-21 have maximum 0 in retail, so a mount simply takes its share of its own armour. Writes only through the header's two array pointers.

entries.name: Component_FillDamageReadouts
entries.description: Fills the damage-readout buffer from a component-damage object: shorts 1-19 the armour components as Q8 fractions (0x100 when destroyed), 20-31 the twelve dependents on their own, 32-41 ten combined armour+dependent readings. MfdStatusScreen_Paint scans 20-31 for its CRITICAL/INT DAMAGE condition.

entries.name: Component_ReadEntryDamage
entries.description: (header, kind, index): one damage-array entry as Q8 of its maximum, (damage << 8) / max by signed division, with no aggregation -- unlike Component_ReadDamagePercent. header is the component system at obj+0x206. Kind 0: dependent (internal) entry index at (header[0]) against the .DMG internals' maximum at (header[3])[+4]; kind 1: main entry index at (header[1]) against piece index's armour (18-byte piece records at (header[3])[+0]); kind 2: the main entry 19 places further on (+0x26 bytes) against the same piece's armour. A negative (destroyed) entry or a zero maximum reads 0x100. A kind above 2 reaches the read with neither pointer set.

entries.name: Mech_WeightedArmorRemaining
entries.description: (header): the sum of (maximum - damage) * weight / maximum over components 0-18 whose occupancy flag (header +8) is set, against their .DMG armour and the int16 weights at 00499fe0, and over internals 0-11 whose maximum is not 0, against that maximum and the weights at 0049a006; an entry below 0 or at 150 damage or more adds nothing.

entries.name: Mech_FlushDeletes
entries.description: ObjectPool_FlushDeleteQueue(g_MechDeleteQueue (004a9c02), GlobalMechList (004a9bfe, the mech pool)). Mech_RegisterSubsystem registers it as the mech module's subsystem phase-5 stub. An absolute-address search of the disassembly for 004a9c02 finds this read and one write, at 004251fe in DBSim_LoadScriptDat; accesses to the queue through a copied pointer are outside that search.

entries.name: Mech_ResetMissionGlobals
entries.description: The mech module's subsystem phase-2 stub, registered by Mech_RegisterSubsystem (PUSH 0x415464 at 0041bc6e), so run at every mission start: sets Mech_DrawEnabled (004a9c06) to 1 and loads the developer move and turn steps DevKeys_MoveStep (004a9d50)/DevKeys_TurnStep (004a9d52) from entry 3 (2000) of the step tables at DevKeys_MoveStepTable (0049a020)/DevKeys_TurnStepTable (0049a032) (words 0049a026 and 0049a038). It lies outside every Ghidra function, two bytes after Mech_FlushDeletes ends.

entries.name: Mech_GetTorsoTwistAngle
entries.description: Returns mech+0x298. Mech vtable slot +0x3c; the Center Body command (scancode 0x2b) uses it to work out the heading the legs must turn to.

entries.name: Mech_GetSpeed
entries.description: Mech vtable slot +0x38 (vtable 0049a282). Returns Q10(2000, mech+0x28e) for a walker, or mech+0x2bd, the airspeed, when the type record's flyer flag (+0x50) is set. Bullet_Fire (read) adds it to a travelling round's speed; mech-locomotion.md cites the Center Body branch's sign test and the AI's lead-the-target maths as other readers.

entries.name: Mech_GetShieldByHeading
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x34. Given a heading angle, returns the front (+0x222) or rear (+0x224) shield value by which side is within +/-90 degrees.

entries.name: Mech_GetOverallDamage
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x40. Returns Component_ReadOverallDamage over the machine's damage block at +0x206: its whole damage as a Q8 fraction, 0 pristine and 256 destroyed. Mech_AiFleeCheck uses it as the base of its fear value.

entries.name: Mech_GetBodyRadius
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x5c: returns typeRec+0x70 (.DAT offset 110, the body radius), which every retail HERC states as 750. Mech_GetCollisionRadius at 0041552c (vtable +0x7c) is a byte-identical second copy of this function, so a machine's body and collision radii are the same field. Distinct from typeRec+0x1a, the generous shot radius the direct-fire hit test rejects against, and from shape+8, the drawn model's bound.

entries.name: Mech_GetCollisionRadius
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x7c: a byte-identical copy of Mech_GetBodyRadius (00415518), returning the same typeRec+0x70 -- 750 on all 21 retail chassis, so it is never zero for a machine. Read by Mech_CollisionTest of the object being walked into, and by Mech_AiObstacleAvoidance through the same vtable slot.

entries.name: Mech_ComponentPresent
entries.description: MechVtable +0x84. One entry of the occupancy array at mech+0x20e, by component slot. The targeting pod asks it to notice that the component it had locked has been shot off. The index is not bounds-checked; the pod cannot pass a bad one because the cursor and the id it holds are written together by Mech_NextTargetableComponent.

entries.name: Mech_NextTargetableComponent
entries.description: MechVtable +0x80. Steps a targeting pod's component cursor over the seven-entry rotation TargetingPodComponentRotation, skipping any slot the machine has lost (its occupancy array at +0x20e) and wrapping at 7. Answers the new cursor and writes the component id it names through the out-parameter, both -1 when the walk comes back to where it started.

entries.name: Mech_MissileLockState
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x6c: returns manager[0x0a + subtypeId*2], the per-missile-subtype LOCK flag -- NOT an ammunition count. Written every tick for every mech by Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate, which clears all five and sets the ones whose range-derived countdown expired. Rocket_Fire will not attach a target without it; WeaponMounts_MountIsReady gates a missile row's ready box on it. The real per-subtype round count is WeaponMounts_RoundsByMissileType's separate local array.

entries.name: Mech_GetAimPoint
entries.description: The mech vtable +0x30: first triple (0, type+0x64, type+0x66), the pilot's eye; second (0, type+0x68, type+0x6a), the outside view's orbit centre.

entries.name: Mech_PlayerFireTick
entries.description: (mech, inputDevice): the player's fire path, called from Sim_PollPlayerInput (the one call es2_xref finds) with the input device struct. Calls WeaponMounts_FireTrigger(mech+0x202, inputDevice, mech). When that returns 0 it zeroes the line-of-fire count DAT_004a9d4c; otherwise it stamps the player's LINE OF FIRE into DAT_004a9c0c: (x, y) points every 0x1000 units from the machine's position along heading (+0x10) less the torso twist (vtable +0x3c), the first one step out, numbering Math_DistanceBetweenPoints to the selected target (+0x1a4) >> 12 clamped to 1..40, or 20 with no target. The other references es2_xref finds to the two globals are reads in Mech_AiObstacleAvoidance (00416709, 004167ec), which steers the player's own squadmates out of the line, and the array's construction in Mech_RegisterSubsystem.

entries.name: Mech_CreditNeutralisedTarget
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x60, told to the machine that just put victim out of the fight. Plain __cdecl on three stack arguments -- every call site pushes three and cleans 12 bytes, so the decompiler's __thiscall rendering with a leading parameter is wrong. Unless victimAlreadyImmobilised is set: when the attacker is in PlayerMech's group, is not PlayerMech and the victim's team byte (group+0x12) differs from its own, Ai_PostSquadMessage(attacker, 0x02, 0); and whenever the team bytes differ, the attacker's kill tally at mech+0x2a4 for the victim's target class (+0x1a8) goes up one and +0xa6 is set. Either way, when the victim is in PlayerMech's group and is not PlayerMech, Ai_PostSquadMessage(victim, 0x25 if +0x99 is set else 0x04, forced), and when the attacker is PlayerMech mission counter DAT_004a9f08 goes up one.

entries.name: Mech_HandleCommand
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x2c. Offers the command code to the machine's weapon-mount manager (WeaponMounts_HandleCommand) first and returns if that consumed it; otherwise handles the turret, throttle and shield commands itself. The shield commands are scancodes 0x1a/0x1b ([ and ]): it answers both with one Widget_PressChild(CockpitViewInstance+0x1e9, key != 0x1b, 1), pressing the shield gauge's rear child for [ and its front child for ] -- so a bracket key and a click on the meter are one code path from ShieldFacing_OnClick onward, click sound included. A flyer installs a stub at this slot, so the brackets do nothing in a RAZOR.

entries.name: Behaviour_DispatchMove
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x14. Reads the behaviour descriptor at *(mech+0x4d); when its +0x24 move triple {func, thisDelta, vtableIndex} is all zero it returns 0 without calling, otherwise it returns (*func)(mech + thisDelta). The third dword enters only the zero test. Mech_MovementTick, Razor_MovementTick and Mech_BehaviourRamTick are reached this way, as the move triples in BehaviourSlotBlocks, which is where es2_xref finds their addresses.

entries.name: Behaviour_DispatchThink
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x18. Behaviour_DispatchMove's shape over the descriptor's +0x18 think triple: 0 when the triple is all zero, otherwise (*func)(mech + thisDelta), whose value it returns.

entries.name: Behaviour_DispatchReassess
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x1c. Behaviour_DispatchMove's shape over the descriptor's +0x30 triple. 'Reassess' is a coined name for the slot, from what its two implementations do; the binary carries none. Behaviour_BuildStateTable points it at Mech_AiCombatReassess in attacking, flanking, facing off, attacking base, attacking flyer and fleeing, at Mech_AiSelectBehaviour in deciding and states 8-17, and leaves it zero in player, player fly, in limbo, dead and disabled, for which this returns 0.

entries.name: Mech_Constructor
entries.description: (mech, typeId): the Mech class constructor; es2_xref finds its one call, in DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects. Builds the base through SimObjectBase_ConstructWithDetailTable with the type's detail table (typeRec+0xde), sets target class +0x1a8 to -1, +0x98 and +0xa7 to 1, joins the live-object list (004a9b7c), clears both mission actions (+0x1b2, +0x1b6), writes -1 to +0x1ba/+0x1bc/+0x1be and installs MechVtable (0049a282, 34 slots). Then Component_AllocDamageArrays(+0x206, 29 components, 22 dependents), five 3-byte countdown timers at +0x258, +0x29c 0, typeTag (+0x04) 7, the type record at +0x1f2 (MECH_TYPE_DATA + index*0x21e), turret angles and rates (+0x294..+0x29a), throttle +0x290, speed +0x28e and turn rate +0x28c zeroed, the energy pool +0x292 at 10000, +0x1a8 0, Shield_Init(+0x222, typeRec+0xc0), fear +0x2aa and cruise speed +0x252 zeroed, and +0xb3 (worth no salvage) set when the salvage scale typeRec+0x54 is 0. Registers the locomotion thread on typeRec+0x12 at +0x22c, zeroing the priority (+6) of the shape's own sequences typeRec+0x12 and +0x14 (00415dbc, 00415dd5), then the twist (+0x1c) and pitch (+0x24) threads at +0x230/+0x234; a negative sequence id leaves its pointer 0. Counts typeRec+0x72's bytes up to the first negative into +0x23c and builds one flat ground shape per entry into the array at +0x238 (typeTag 9, z -100000). Installs a behaviour state on +0x4d: deciding (004993a4) when +0xa3 is clear, otherwise player fly (00499420) when typeRec+0x50 is set and player (004993e2) when not. Zeroes +0x29e and the squad order verb +0x23e; loads the .DMG (Damage_LoadMechDmgFile, +0x1fa) and the collision model (Collision_RegisterObject, +0x1f6) from the type's folder name (004a9de4[typeRec+0x6c]) and joins them with Component_LinkMaxRefData; zeroes +0x2b4..+0x2b7 and sets +0x2b8 to 1; zeroes the 0x4e-byte flight block at +0x2b9, points +0x2d9 at +0x0c, seeds +0x2dd with the inverse of the current transform, the airspeed +0x2bd with 1000 and +0x2d7 from +0x290, and zeroes +0x31c. Returns mech. DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects sets +0xa3 only after this returns, so the player's own machine is constructed in deciding (ai-dispatch.md).

entries.name: Mech_ApplyThrottleInput
entries.description: Player throttle handler. Integrates the stick axis into mech+0x290 (throttle, Q10, clamped +/-0x400) at Q8(0x91,-axis) per tick, converts it to a desired speed via Q10(maxRev or maxFwd, throttle), then calls Mech_LocomotionTick. ThrottleLeverMode (0049a06e) gates the clamp: at 0 it spans the full +/-0x400, so the axis held down runs through zero into reverse.

entries.name: Mech_AiObstacleAvoidance
entries.description: Amends a turn axis and a desired speed in place through its pointer arguments: (mech, short *turn, short *desired, flags). Returns at once when the speed (+0x28e) and *desired are both zero, or when *desired is negative and the unstick counter (+0x26e) is zero. Each side's range starts at 22000. Unless flags bit 0 is set: two body-space probes from fixed literals, the same on every chassis -- left (-1500,0,0)->(-10000,20000,0), right (1500,0,0)->(10000,20000,0) -- put through the machine's frame with both ends' Z set to one Terrain_HeightQuery under the machine; each side takes Sim_RaycastShapes' range when under 22000, then Terrain_RayWalk mode 1's hit measured by Math_GroundDistanceBetweenPoints from the probe's start when nearer. Then every live-list object other than itself whose group +0x14 is zero and whose vtable +0x7c is nonzero, at Q10(2000, Math_DistanceBetweenPoints), claims the left side for a bearing error (Math_HeadingToward minus heading) of 0 to 0x1fff and the right for -1 to -0x1fff. When the group leader (group+0x0c slot 0) has +0xa3 set, each of the DAT_004a9d4c points at DAT_004a9c0c does the same at Q10(1000, Math_GroundDistanceBetweenPoints) inside 0x3000, marking its side as a firing-line reading. While +0xae (backing out of a block) is set: both sides at 22000 takes a quarter off the side +0x254 names (left when positive, else right); both under 22000 adds +0x254 to the left. Then, if either side is under 22000, the closer (left on a tie) gives (22000 - closest) * gain / 22000, gain 1000 for a firing-line reading and 700 otherwise, added to *turn and negated when left is closer; a firing-line reading under 3000 sets *desired to typeRec+4. A reverse-mode local is zeroed at the top and has no other write in the body; set, it would rotate the bearing tests half a turn and make the override take typeRec+6 >> 1.

entries.name: Mech_ApplyTerrainSlopeToSpeed
entries.description: Adjusts desired speed by dot(terrainNormal, forwardVector)/0x960, signed by direction of travel, clamped to zero on sign flip. Uphill slows, downhill speeds up.

entries.name: Mech_LocomotionTick
entries.description: (mech, steer, desiredSpeed, avoidance arg): the HERC control law and gait state machine. An immobilised machine (+0xa4) has steer and desired speed zeroed. Otherwise, while the unstick timer at +0x26d runs, the desired speed is replaced by the type's top reverse speed when +0xae is set and its top forward speed when not; once it has expired +0xae is cleared, Mech_ApplyTerrainSlopeToSpeed adjusts the desired speed and it is clamped to the type's reverse and forward limits. A machine other than the player (004a9c08) that is not immobilised runs Mech_AiObstacleAvoidance. Leg or reactor damage scales the desired speed by Q10 400 (+0xa9/+0xab) or 750 (+0xa8/+0xaa), an engaged Turbo Pod at +0x317 adds its term, steer is clamped to +/-0x100, and the speed scalar +0x28e moves toward the desired speed by typeRec+0x08 per tick. The gait machine then compares |speed| with last tick's on the locomotion thread (+0x22c): while a transition frame is in flight (thread +4 != +8) it is skipped and the speed restored to last tick's; an immobilised machine not turning in place runs the fall to typeRec+0x46 (rate 100 then 0x78, sounds 0x1e and 0x29, latches +0xb4 and calls Mech_SpreadImpactDamage(150, 120) when the sequence has played out); every other machine requests or cuts to the walk, run, stop and turn-in-place sequences with AnimThread_SetTarget and AnimThread_SetSequence and sets the playback rate +0x2a0, per the table in docs/retail/simulation/mech-locomotion.md, 'The gait state machine'. After it a speed of 1 to 44 lifts a nonzero playback rate under 60 to 60, and the turn rate +0x28c moves by typeRec+0x0a toward Q8(Q10(1600, tent), steer), the tent over speed peaking at half top speed and zeroed when the speed is 0 or the gait machine stepped off or requested a stop this tick; the heading +0x10 takes the turn rate and +0x32 is cleared. It writes no position: all translation is animation root motion.

entries.name: Mech_Draw
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x00, the draw slot. Runs Mech_SpliceHardpointShapes over every LOD root of the type's shape -- replacing each hardpoint placeholder part with the fitted weapon's shape or a blank record -- and then calls Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel. Gated on Mech_DrawEnabled.

entries.name: Shape_StampTransformId
entries.description: (part, id): writes one transform id through a shape's part tree, switching on the part's class tag (vtable slot 0): a TSGroup (0x140014) takes it at part+4 and returns without visiting children; a TSCellAnimPart (0x14000b) takes it at part+4, and a TSBSPPart (0x140015) in every entry of its per-node transform array (+0x1c, count +0x16), and both go on to their children; a TSPartList, TSShape or TSDetailPart (0x140007, 0x140008, 0x14000c) only passes it to its children (count +0x10, array +0x12); a TSBasePart (0x140005), 0x140006 and every other tag return. Mech_ConfigureLoadout uses it to hang a weapon model on the hardpoint's bone.

entries.name: Mech_ConfigureLoadout
entries.description: (mech, ...): mech loadout configuration, called from DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects. Allocates the weapon-mount manager at mech+0x202 (0x14 or 0x35 bytes depending on the locally-simulated flag) and builds the mounts. Then, per fitted mount: the weapon template's cluster (+0x12) takes the mount's component index (.GL +0x17 + 19) and Collision_ReplaceClusters puts its spheres, moved by WeaponMount_MuzzleOffset, into the machine's .COL model (mech+0x1f6); the template's piece takes the chassis piece's parent byte and internal 12 + slot, HercPiece_ReplacePieces copies it over the mount's .DMG piece (mech+0x1fa) and HercPiece_SetInternalMaxima gives that internal the template's +0x2a. Then Collision_CollectComponentAnchors and HercPiece_BindComponentAnchors, then clears the occupancy flag (mech+0x20e) of each of the first 29 components whose piece's dependent count (+6) is 0, then MechLoadout_FileEquipmentPods, Mech_ComputeShieldCapacity, Shield_RefillToBalance and Mech_ComputeReactorRate.

entries.name: Mech_ApplyFormationOffset
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x78: adds this machine's formation slot offset to the point it is handed. No-op for slot 0 (mech+0x49 zero); otherwise Formation_GetSlotOffset(group's formation id at group+2, mech+0x49) gives three shorts, widened to ints and handed to Formation_RotateAndAddOffset. Spreads a group at spawn and gives Ai_KeepFormation each follower's post on the leader's live position.

entries.name: Mech_ApplyStartingCondition
entries.description: (mech, percent): applies a mission record's starting condition (script.dat block 7 +0x84); es2_xref finds its one call, in DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects at 004259b0. Negative or 0x50 and up: Mech_SpreadImpactDamage(mech, 0, 25), which returns at once. 0x3c-0x4f: 50. 0x28-0x3b: 80. 0x14-0x27: 120, with dependent 5 (the reactor) set to Q8(0x100, its maximum) and +0xb3 (worth no salvage) set. Below 0x14, a wreck: component 7 on an odd Math_RandomNext roll, 8 on an even one, written off with 32000 through vtable +0x74 with no attacker, and when typeRec+0x4a exceeds 2 likewise 13 on an odd roll, 14 on an even one; then +0xa4 (immobilised), +0xb3 and +0xb4 (collapsed) set; 150. Each band ends in Mech_SpreadImpactDamage(mech, n, n+0x19). Args derived from disassembly: two pushes with ADD ESP,0x8 at 004259b0; [EBP+8] mech, [EBP+0xc] word.

entries.name: Mech_SpreadImpactDamage
entries.description: Spreads one impact over the whole machine instead of aiming it. Each of the 29 live components draws its own (rand & 0xff) < odds roll; a component that is caught takes Math_Q8Multiply(rand(maxDamage) + maxDamage/2, Component_TotalArmor(i)) through vtable +0x74, so the share scales with what that component had to lose. maxDamage 0 returns immediately. es2_xref finds three calls: the collapse landing in Mech_LocomotionTick (150, 120), Mech_ApplyStartingCondition and Mech_ApplyOutnumberedDamage. Args derived from disassembly: [EBP+8] mech, [EBP+0xc] and [EBP+0x10] words, plain RET.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Mech_SpreadImpactDamage(MechObject *mech, short maxDamage, short odds)

entries.name: Mech_AttachToGroup
entries.description: Attaches a mech to its mission group: stores the group pointer at mech+0x45 and the member slot index at mech+0x49, then fills in heading and position ONLY IF still at the -0x8000 'unset' sentinel -- which is why a roster record's own position ref wins where set and the group's point is the fallback. The heading is the group's (+0x0a), with pitch and roll zeroed. Position comes from the group's coordinate pointer (group+0x18), or from Route_WaypointAt against the group's route cursor when that is null. Z is Terrain_HeightQuery at that point -- the group's, before any formation offset -- plus the mech type's foot offset (typeRecord+0x16), plus 5000 when typeRecord+0x50 is set. Then calls mech vtable +0x78 (Mech_ApplyFormationOffset) on the (x, y, z) triple and stores the result as the position.

entries.name: Mech_GetAimNodeTransform
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x24: resolves the type record's +0x0c (.DAT file offset 10, the camera node's shape part id -- the node the cockpit eye rides) through the shape's part lookup (shape vtable +0x20) and returns that node's 0x20-byte transform record at shapeInstance+0x16 + index*0x20, or the zeroed DAT_006c572c when the shape has no such part. Callers take its +0x14 translation as the point to aim at and its +0x1c as a sight height. This is what makes both guidance routines and the HUD target indicator aim at a HERC's cockpit rather than the ground point its model origin sits on.

entries.name: Mech_ComputeShieldCapacity
entries.description: Writes mech+0x228 via Shield_SetMax. Base is typeRecord+0xc0 = record offset 190, a fleet-wide 3500. The shield generator's own reading -- internal 4's damage against its maximum, 0x100 when destroyed -- scales the base by ((reading - 0x80) / 0x19) * -0x66 + 0x400 in Q10 once it is 0x80 or more, down to about half. A Shield Pod at mech+0x30f adds Q10(((podDamage / 0x33) * -0xcc + 0x400), base), the base undamaged, while podDamage -- Component_ReadDamagePercent of the pod hardpoint's component, .GL+0x17 + 19 -- is under 0xe1.

entries.name: Mech_ComputeReactorRate
entries.description: Computes the mech reactor output rate into mech+0x256. Base is a literal 0x14 (20) shared by the whole fleet -- the type record is never read. Replaced outright by Q10(200,20)=3 when mech+0xab (reactor critical) or Q10(600,20)=11 when mech+0xaa (reactor degraded). An Energy Pod in slot mech+0x313 then adds Q10(1024 - 204*(podDamage/51), 20), up to a second full 20 (it doubles output), gated off entirely at 225/256 damage. ONE reference in the whole binary, the tail of Mech_ConfigureLoadout, so the rate is sampled at spawn and never recomputed.

entries.name: Mech_ComponentDamageWrite
entries.description: (mech, component, damage, attacker): Mech vtable +0x74, the shared damage endpoint. Returns at once for the locally piloted machine (+0xa3) while Sim_DamageToPlayerDisabled answers non-zero, and for a component whose occupancy flag (+0x20e) is clear. Snapshots each mount's Component_ReadDamagePercent (.GL +0x17 + 19), and for the player internal 4's reading; sets g_DebrisAlternate to typeRec + 0x212; Component_ApplyDamageAndCascade. For the player, 0x0c when internal 4 reaches 0x100, else 0x03 when it leaves 0. Each mount's slot +0x68 with its readings before and after, 0x10 for the player when one reaches 0x100. Mech_ComputeShieldCapacity. Not for a flyer (typeRec+0x50): the leg readings of internals 0 and 1, and 10 and 11 when typeRec+0x4a is above 2; a leg at 0x100 queues its ground shape on g_FlatObjDeleteQueue; unless immobilised (+0xa4), half the legs gone, while +0x99 is clear, credits the attacker through its slot +0x60 with 0 (and posts 0x2f when the attacker is LocalPlayerMech and the mech its +0x1a4), runs Mech_ReportOutOfAction, the defeat action and the disabled state; then latches +0xa4 and releases its target (+0x1a4, the holder's +0x1a2, +0x9d); otherwise the averaged sides latch +0xa9 at 0x8d or more (0x13) or +0xa8 past 0x50 (8), each message for the player while its latch was clear. Death, while +0x99 is clear, when Component_IsFullyDestroyed answers for component 0 or 1, or internal 9 or 8 reads 0x100: +0x99 set, 30000 to component 0 through the slot, the attacker credited with the sampled +0xa4, the report and the defeat action when that was clear, the target released, the scanner +0x96 cleared, 0x2e on the 0x2f test, and the dead state for a non-flyer, or with typeRec+0x4c set +0x38 set, Z -100000, in limbo and every ground shape queued with the count zeroed. Then, while +0xaa and +0xab are clear, internal 5 latches +0xab past 0xc0 or +0xaa past 0x80, with 4 for the player. Ends with Sim_FlushDeleteQueue.

entries.name: Mech_ApplyExplosiveDamage
