entries.description: Mech vtable +0x70. Args (weaponDamage, hitPos, blastRadius, attacker). Front/rear facing classification (<0x4000 BAM) -> Mech_ShieldAbsorb_Explosive -> per-component roll at 0x802-in-0x1000 across up to 29 slots -> component world position via vtable +0x58 -> linear distance falloff (overflow * (blastRadius-distance)/blastRadius) via mech vtable +0x74. Structurally different from the direct-fire path: many random components with falloff, versus one deterministic component without.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Mech_ApplyExplosiveDamage(MechObject *this, short damage, int *hitPoint, short blastRadius, int *attacker)

entries.name: Mech_ApplyDirectFireDamage
entries.description: Splits the armor damage by the PROJ.DAT splash factor (Math_Q10Multiply(shotData+8, shotData+4)) -- NOT a per-weapon-type effectiveness scale. The remainder goes to component health via mech vtable +0x74; the split-off share, when nonzero, becomes a 500-unit secondary explosion through the struck object's OWN +0x70 (a direct call, not a sweep). Also rolls to destroy the struck weapon mount on a damage-band change.

entries.name: Mech_DirectFireHitTest
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x20, (mech, shot): the direct-fire hit test and damage application in one call. Rejects when ray[+8] (200) + ray length + typeRec+0x1a is under the muzzle-to-machine distance. For a machine not locally piloted, the shot's rocket subtype (shot+0x12) 0 or 1 turns the scanner (+0x96) on while the radar-silence timer is 0, and 2 turns it off and loads the timer with 6000. Concatenates the machine's world transform with the ray's cached world-to-muzzle transform and calls Mech_ShieldAbsorb_DirectFire with the shot's shield damage (shot+6); a zero return is a miss. On a hit it clears +0x94 and adds what the shields took to mech+0x288. Shield damage left at 0 ends there: an effect from the shot's first impact array (shot+0xa, rand & 3) at the shield's hit distance down the ray, and that distance returned. Otherwise, for the locally piloted machine with +0xb0 clear and front + rear under 500, posts 0x15 and sets +0xb0; then Mech_SelectStruckComponent on the machine's .COL model (+0x1f6) with its active flags; a miss returns 0, a hit adds the armour damage (shot+4) to +0x288 and calls Mech_ApplyDirectFireDamage(component, shot, point at that distance down the ray), returning the distance.

entries.name: Mech_SalvageValue
entries.description: What one machine is worth to the player's side at mission end. Zero when mech+0xb3 is set. Otherwise queues every hardpoint under 0x80 damage to the salvage list as {template+0x56, (0x100-damage)*100/256}, then returns Q10(Mech_WeightedArmorRemaining(mech), typeRec+0x54) with typeRec+0x54 halved when component 0 is at full damage.

entries.name: Mech_IntegrateMotion
entries.description: Sets the animation playback rate from mech+0x2a0, then advances the object by dt = Math_IntegrateRateOverTick(100) via SimObject_ApplyRootMotion.

entries.name: Mech_CollisionTest
entries.description: Returns nonzero when the position the move just produced is refused. Takes this machine's vtable +0x5c (body radius) as a short and its position, and clears mech+0x2b0. (1) Walks the live-object list at 004a9b7c (count 004a9b82), passing over itself and, before anything else is read, any object whose group (+0x45) has a non-zero +0x14. For each other object it takes the object's vtable +0x7c (collision radius) and Math_DistanceBetweenPoints from this machine's position; when the object's target class (obj+0x1a8) is 1 and its own vtable +0x5c exceeds that distance it is stored at mech+0x2b0, so the field ends holding the last such structure the loop reached, the blocking object included. A collision radius of 0 then moves on to the next object. Otherwise a distance under own +0x5c plus its +0x7c blocks: the object's vtable +0x68 (SimObject_SetRunInto) is called whatever its class, a target class 0 object also triggers the collision damage below, and the function returns 1. (2) Structure_GatherWalkCandidates(position, own +0x5c, 0) nonzero returns 1. (3) Terrain_FaceNormalAt(ActiveHeightGrid, position): a null normal (off the grid) or |normal.z| < 0x5aa is steep. A machine that is not locally piloted (+0xa3 clear) returns the steep flag, left in AX by the SETL (the decompile drops this return). For the player, steep ground while no slide is running (004a9d68 clear) and the new Z above the pre-move Z Mech_MovementTick saved at 004a9d64 returns 1; any other steep case latches 004a9d68, adds Q10(10, normal.x) and Q10(10, normal.y) to the per-tick slide displacement at 004a9d54/004a9d58 that Mech_MovementTick adds to the position, and returns 0, reading the normal through its pointer, which is null off the grid. Walkable ground with a slide running clears 004a9d68 and, when Math_FastMagnitude2D of that displacement exceeds 0xfa, writes d + Math_RandomBelow(3d) to components 7 to 12 through vtable +0x74 with attacker 0, where d = Q10(SlideDamageScaleByDifficulty[MissionDifficulty], magnitude) and the sum is 16-bit, then calls Cockpit_StartHitShake(0) and Sound_Play(0x29); the displacement is zeroed whether or not it hurt, and it returns 0. The collision damage: builds either machine's rotation matrix if its +0x32 flag is clear, writing the matrix and the flag; rotates (0, struck +0x28e, 0) by the struck machine's rotation and then by the transpose of this one's; damage = Q10(300, Q10(own typeRec+0x4e, own +0x28e) - Q10(struck typeRec+0x4e, that vector's Y)). Above 200 the point is the X/Y midpoint of the two positions with Z the lower of the two machines' camera-node (typeRec+0x0c) transform Z translations, model-space, from the shape instance's +0x16 array (the record at 006c572c when the part is missing), and vtable +0x70(damage, point, 0x4b0, other) is called on this machine and then on the struck one. Scene_SubmitFrameObjects files the machine under the mech+0x2b0 structure's draw cell (mech-locomotion.md).

entries.name: Mech_PlaceLegsOnGround
entries.description: Per-leg terrain placement over the mech animated node hierarchy. For each entry of mech+0x238 still holding a ground shape: moves the shape to the world position of the node typeRec+0x77[i] names, gives it the machine's heading (euler +0x10) and clears its +0x32 matrix-valid flag -- unconditionally. Then, within 15000 of the camera or for the player, tests the footfall for kind-0 entries (typeRec+0x72[i]) against the gait's thresholds and plays sound 0x1d on a plant.

entries.name: Razor_MovementTick
entries.description: The RAZOR's per-tick move, the counterpart of Mech_MovementTick and not an autopilot: the move triple of behaviour state 2 (player fly; slot block 2 at 00499940, +0x0c at 0049994c, the one reference es2_xref finds), reached through Behaviour_DispatchMove. Copies the airframe transform before moving and computes five probe points through the copy; unless +0xa4 is set, adds the world velocity at +0x2c5, each component through Math_IntegrateRateOverTick, to the position. Then, each probe only while its component is intact: right wing (8) and left wing (7), a ground test and a Sim_RaycastObjectList sweep the airspeed (+0x2bd) long at clearance 300, rolling the airframe away by Q10(4000, depth) or a flat 4000; left and right nacelles (4, 5), the sweep alone at clearance 150, a flat 8000 roll, both reporting at the left nacelle's point; the cockpit (0), ground test and sweep at clearance 200, a negative pitch rate zeroed and then pitched up by Q10(2000, depth) or 2000; a look-ahead ground test at (0, 15000, -1500) while 4, 5 and 0 are all intact, pitching up by Q10(20, depth); and the fuselage (6), a ground test at the moved position that puts the airframe back on the ground. Each ray probe writes its point into the copy's translation and leaves it there. A contact applies its kick to the attitude at once and damages its component through Mech_ApplyDirectFireDamage with AirframeContactShot (0049a170): Q10(airspeed, 500/1000/5000) for a wing/cockpit/fuselage ground contact, 1000 (wing) or 5000 for an object contact, shield figure 8000. Destroying the cockpit or the fuselage throws debris group 3 and latches +0xa4. For the locally piloted machine it then sets the engine hum (sound 0x2d) to Math_FastMagnitude3D(body velocity)*16+28000 clamped to 16 bits, or stops it once +0x99 is set; last, unconditionally, Mech_ConvergeGunsOnRange with the range to +0x1a4, 0 with none. Returns 1.

entries.name: Mech_MovementTick
entries.description: Per-tick mech physics step. For the locally piloted machine (+0xa3) it first saves the position at 004a9d5c/004a9d60/004a9d64, the pre-move Z Mech_CollisionTest's uphill test compares against. Then SimObject_PushTransform and Mech_IntegrateMotion; for the player with the slide flag 004a9d68 set it adds the slide displacement 004a9d54/004a9d58 to X and Y; and it sets Z to Terrain_HeightQuery(ActiveHeightGrid) plus typeRec+0x16 (ride height). When Mech_CollisionTest refuses: SimObject_PopTransform; a machine that is not locally piloted arms the unstick manoeuvre (mech+0x26e = 10000, mech+0x254 = -5000, or +5000 when Math_RandomNext's low bit is clear, mech+0xae = speed > 0), the player gets Sound_Play(0x29); throttle +0x290 = 0 and the throttle-dirty byte +0x93 = 1. If the locomotion thread's +0x50 & 2 is set (a transition frame in flight) it cuts that thread to frame 0 of the forward stop sequence (typeRec+0x12) and goes on to the legs. Otherwise it reverses: speed = -speed clamped to [typeRec+0x6e, typeRec+0x06], animation rate negated, Mech_IntegrateMotion again with no terrain clamp, and a second refusal pops the same saved transform and zeroes the speed. Mech_PlaceLegsOnGround last; returns 1. It steers nothing itself: the speed and turn it integrates are set by Mech_LocomotionTick. How it is dispatched is in docs/retail/simulation/ai-dispatch.md.

entries.name: Mech_TorsoTwistTick
entries.description: Torso/turret twist (yaw): rate at mech+0x294, angle at mech+0x298, clamped to +/- typeRec[+0x22]. Rates dt-scaled via Math_IntegrateRateOverTick. Only ACCELERATION is rate-limited -- when |Q8(axis, typeRec[+0x1e])| <= |rate| the rate snaps to it, so releasing or reversing the stick stops the turret dead. Args are (mech, axis, snapTarget, snapEnable); with snapEnable set the turret stops on the tick its angle crosses snapTarget, which is how Mech_CenterTorsoTick lands on centre. Ends by seeking the twist thread (mech+0x230) to (unsigned)angle >> 2 via AnimThread_SeekToPosition -- the turret has no rotation of its own. See docs/retail/simulation/torso-aim.md.

entries.name: Mech_TorsoTwistServoSoundTest
entries.description: Run at the end of Mech_TorsoTwistTick for the locally piloted machine only (mech+0xa3), with that tick's axis input. When |axis| exceeds 0xc0, the twist angle (mech+0x298) differs from the one recorded last call and the static byte at 0049a1c9 is clear, it tests Sound_IsPlaying(0x21) and sets the byte if that sound is not playing; it clears the byte when the axis is zero or the angle has stopped moving; it records the angle in the static word at 0049a1ca. It never starts or stops a sound, and es2_xref.py finds no other reference to either static. See docs/retail/simulation/torso-aim.md.

entries.name: Mech_ConvergeGunsOnRange
entries.description: Gun convergence, run at the tail of Mech_TorsoPitchTick with that tick's range argument -- the distance to the aim point, so the player's guns and the AI's both toe in on whatever the turret is tracking. For each mount, Math_EulerToward from WeaponMount_MuzzleOffset's result -- the mount point, without the template's barrel triple at +0x40 -- (its z less typeRec+0x66, the sight height) to (0, range, 0), stored at mount+0x24 and +0x28; a range of zero clears them. WeaponMount_PrepareShot is the consumer, composing them under the firing bone. Both gates (mount+0x5b/+0x5f, from .GL +0x02/+0x04) read zero on every retail chassis, so the convergence applies fleet-wide.

entries.name: Mech_TorsoPitchTick
entries.description: Torso/turret pitch: rate at mech+0x296, angle at mech+0x29a, clamped to the asymmetric range [typeRec+0x2c, typeRec+0x2a]. Same shape as Mech_TorsoTwistTick, on the pitch thread (mech+0x234) and typeRec[+0x24..+0x2c]. Its third argument is the range to the current target, passed straight to Mech_ConvergeGunsOnRange for gun convergence. See docs/retail/simulation/torso-aim.md.

entries.name: Mech_TorsoPitchServoSoundTest
entries.description: Run at the end of Mech_TorsoPitchTick for the locally piloted machine only (mech+0xa3), with that tick's axis input. When |axis| exceeds 0xc0, the pitch angle (mech+0x29a) differs from the one recorded last call and the static byte at 0049a1cc is clear, it tests Sound_IsPlaying(0x21) and sets the byte if that sound is not playing; it clears the byte when the axis is zero or the angle has stopped moving; it records the angle in the static word at 0049a1ce. It never starts or stops a sound, and es2_xref.py finds no other reference to either static. See docs/retail/simulation/torso-aim.md.

entries.name: Mech_IsEcmSwitchedOn
entries.description: The machine's jammer answer, stored into mech+0xa1 by Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate. Zero without an ECM pod at mech+0x307. With one, a locally piloted machine (mech+0xa3) answers with the pod's button copy at pod+0x7d and any other machine with its radar mode at mech+0x96, so an AI machine jams exactly while its radar is ACTIVE.

entries.name: Mech_GetEcmPodSwitch
entries.description: Returns the ECM pod's word at pod+0x7f, or 0 without a pod. EcmPod_Tick alone writes it, so it is zero for every machine but the player. Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate raises the engagement-action latch obj+0xa2 on the machine's selected target while it is set.

entries.name: Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate
entries.description: Per-mech, per-tick systems pass, in two halves. Energy: integrates the reactor rate into the energy pool (+0x292), hands the pool less 500 to the weapon mounts' vtable slot 0 (WeaponMounts_ArbitrateEnergy) and what they leave to Shield_RechargeTick, then stores the remainder plus 500 clamped to 0-10000. On the locally piloted machine it clears +0xb0 while shield front + rear exceeds 0x5dc. It counts down the retarget, friendly-fire-complaint, radar-silence and under-fire timers (the last expiring clears the damage-from-player-group total) and the +0x285 timer (expiry reloads 4000 and clears the damage-taken total), and runs Mech_ComputeCombatRating while +0x94 is clear. Missile lock: with a target and Mech_GetEcmPodSwitch set it raises target+0xa2; stores Mech_IsEcmSwitchedOn into the jammer flag +0xa1; counts rounds per missile subtype (WeaponMounts_RoundsByMissileType) and clears the five per-subtype lock flags at weaponMounts+0x0a and the lamp +0x9b. With a target selected: against a jamming mech target it re-rolls the spoof flag +0x9c on the ECM timer (weight 0x14, 5 with a Targeting Pod whose +0x7f is under 0x33; spoof holds 5000, a miss re-rolls after 0x5dc), clearing it otherwise; the lock reload is distance >> 2 capped at 0x7fff, or 0 for a chassis with type record +0x50 set; while +0x9d is clear, the bearing (turret twist included) is within +-0x3000 and line of sight holds, each carried subtype's timer runs and latches its flag at zero unless +0x9c stands: subtype 0 and 4 hold their timers while the own scanner (+0x96) is off or this tick's roll spoofed, subtype 1 holds on a spoof alone, subtype 2 holds while the target's scanner and jammer are both off and latches regardless of +0x9c. Failing the gate reloads timers 0, 1 and 2 and clears +0x9d at the end. On the locally piloted machine it sets the lamp from the armed mount's subtype (any lock for a non-launcher) and calls Mech_LockTonePlay.

entries.name: Mech_LockTonePlay
entries.description: Turns mech+0x9b (lock acquired) into the cockpit lock tone: Sound_Play(0x15) on a 0x40-coarse-tick blink cadence while set, 0x14 when clear but the target just changed (+0x9d), 0x16 once on loss. Called from the tail of Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate for the locally-piloted machine only.

entries.name: Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate
entries.description: The player's once-a-frame cockpit exchange; es2_xref finds calls from Sim_RenderFrame and Sim_InitMissionSession. Pushes (pool << 10) / 10000 to the energy meter (cockpit +0x1e5) and runs Shield_BalanceInputRead. Calls WeaponMounts_PerFrameUpdate with the range to the selected target (+0x1a4), measured from ViewChain_Viewed when DAT_0049ef5c is set and this is LocalPlayerMech, otherwise from the machine, 0 with none. The throttle exchange with the gauge (cockpit +0x1f1): with +0x93 clear the gauge's throttle is written to +0x290 and, when the type record's flyer flag (+0x50) is set, to +0x2d7 as well; with +0x93 set the machine's +0x290 goes to the gauge and +0x93 is cleared. The speed half it feeds the gauge is (+0x28e << 10) / top speed (typeRec+6 forward, -typeRec+4 in reverse), the walker speed scalar -- see KNOWN_ISSUES.md. Fills the gunsight (cockpit +0x1f5) with the heading and twist (left as they were while +0xa4 is set), the pitch, the cockpit's selection and +0x9b. When the cockpit's selection (cockpit +0x210) differs from +0x1a4 it clears +0x9b, moves +0x1a4 over with the +0x1a2 reference counts and sets +0x9d, resets the Targeting Pod's component lock (pod slot 1) for a non-null selection, and arms the ATT wait timer (+0x31c) at 0x1194 when nothing is selected and weaponMounts+0x14 is set. While nothing is selected and that byte is set it counts the timer (record +0x31b) down and sets g_CenterTurretMode at 0. Ends with Player_ResolveTargetAimPoint for a selected target and CockpitView_SetTargetBlock.

entries.name: Mech_ToggleRadarMode
entries.description: The manual's [R]. es2_xref finds one caller, CockpitWidgets_HandleCommand. Flips mech+0x96 between PASSIVE and ACTIVE, gated on +0xa3 so only the locally-piloted machine toggles, then withdraws and posts the radar-mode message (0x2c/0x2d) and plays the mode tone. The F4 scanner's PASS/ACTIVE buttons go through MfdButton_OnClick, which writes +0x96 directly. The player's HERC starts each mission PASSIVE in retail; es2_fieldscan finds no write of +0x96 in a machine constructor. Base_Construct latches it on for structure types 5, 6, 0x1d and 0x1e, the radar masts.

negatives.claim: The player's HERC starts each mission PASSIVE
negatives.how: the user's recollection of retail play: as far as they know, the radar always starts passive

entries.name: Mech_ReadDamageReadouts
entries.description: (machine, buffer): fills a damage readout buffer for one machine: entry 0 is the type record's (+0x1f2) +0x6c, the rest come from Component_FillDamageReadouts on the component damage at +0x206.

entries.name: Mech_ReadEntryDamage
entries.description: (mech, kind, index): Component_ReadEntryDamage(mech+0x206, kind, index), returning its AX unchanged. Callers found by es2_xref: Cockpit_PowerUpTick, which passes kind 0 and internals 0-9, and Player_DependentCondition.

entries.name: Mech_ComponentNearestAim
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x54. Walks the machine's 29 component slots, places each occupied one through vtable +0x58, and returns the index of the one whose bearing from the given pose's position (+0x1a) is nearest the pose's euler triple (+0x0), measured as the sum of the absolute differences of Euler elements 0 and 2 (-0x8000 counts as 0x7fff, first of equals wins); -1 when no slot is occupied. Rocket_Fire calls it through the locked target at launch with the round's +0xc block and stores the result in the round's lock component (+0x5a), which Rocket_HomingSteer steers at. Base_FirstLiveComponent is the structure class's counterpart.

entries.name: Mech_ComponentPosition
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x58: the world position of one of the 29 .DMG components. Indexes the piece table at *(mech+0x1fa) by componentIndex * 0x12 and reads the two RUNTIME-ONLY HercPiece fields +0x0c (shape part id) and +0x0e (pointer to a short[3] point), which the .DMG loader leaves as -1/null and Mech_ConfigureLoadout fills in from the .COL. A null point returns the MACHINE'S OWN POSITION. Otherwise the point goes through the object transform, composing the part's posed node transform first when the part id is > 0 (strictly greater, so part 0 stays in the object frame). A part the shape lacks falls back to the identity transform at 006c572c.

entries.name: Player_ResolveTargetAimPoint
entries.description: Resolves the point the HUD aims at on the selected target. With a targeting computer fitted (mech+0x30b) and the target inside 30000 units it asks the pod for a component aim point and component id; otherwise it takes the target's vtable +0x24 aim node transformed by the target's own rotation, falls back to the raw origin, and writes 0 to the component id.

entries.name: Mech_ApplyOutnumberedDamage
entries.description: (mech): returns at once when Mission_IsClearOfThreats(mech). Otherwise sums two strengths over every deployed object (group+0x14 clear) not out of weapons (+0xa5), immobilised (+0xa4) or destroyed (+0x99), split by whether its group side (+0x12) matches the mech's: each HERC within 45000 adds its type record's int16 +0x54 (the salvage scale), each flyer (pool 004a9e3d) within 50000 adds 500, and each armed structure (BASES.DAT +0x2e non-zero) within 35000 adds 500. The friendly sum loses 600, floored at 0; then Mech_SpreadImpactDamage(mech, 0x40, 0x40) runs once per 400 by which the hostile sum exceeds it. Group_ApplyOutnumberedDamage calls it.

entries.name: Mech_SquadOrderLineIndex
entries.description: The string index the F7 heads-down comm box prints on a squadmate's OBJECTIVE: line, into STRINGS0 group 40 (ATTACK/TRAVEL/PATROL/FORM UP/GUARD/FLEE/DEAD/IMMOBILE), returned in AX. Starts from the machine's behaviour descriptor +0x3c, then overrides it with the standing squad order at mech+0x23e (1->1, 2->2, 3 or 6->4), but only when the machine is neither immobilised (+0xa4) nor destroyed (+0x99), the descriptor's +0x3c is not 5, and the descriptor's +0x09 (flag bit 1, committed to a fight) is zero. es2_xref finds its one call, in HddGauge_PaintIdle. Args derived from disassembly: [EBP+8] only.

entries.name: Mech_GetDisplaySpeedKph
entries.description: The km/h figure the HUD prints for a mech. A walker: mech+0x28e * typeRec+0xc2 / typeRec+0x06, where MechType_InitOne sets typeRec+0xc2 = Math_Q10Multiply(315, raw forward speed) before rescaling +0x06, so top speed reads 315/1024 of the file's forward speed (docs/retail/simulation/mech-locomotion.md). A flyer (typeRec+0x50 != 0, the RAZOR): Math_MapRange(mech+0x2bd airspeed, 0, typeRec+0x206 (the .FM's top airspeed), 0, typeRec+0xc2), where +0xc2 is the chassis file's own value because the loader writes it for walkers alone -- 265 on the RAZOR (docs/retail/simulation/razor-flight.md#hud-speed).

entries.name: Razor_ApplyFlightInput
entries.description: The flyer's input hand-off, called by Sim_PollPlayerInput in place of Mech_ApplyThrottleInput AND both turret ticks -- which is why a RAZOR's turret never moves. Packs the four device axes, Terrain_HeightQuery at the machine's position and four wing-destroyed flags (component array at mech+0x20e, entries 7/8/4/5) into a stack record and calls FlightModel_Step with the type record's flight model at typeRec+0x1dc. The axes are remapped against the walker's: device +0x0e (steer) is the aileron, +0x10 (throttle) the elevator, +0x12 (turret twist) the rudder and +0x14 (turret pitch) the throttle. On a tick the throttle axis moved it copies mech+0x2d7 to mech+0x290 and sets the mech+0x93 dirty flag, so the cockpit gauge follows the flight model.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Razor_ApplyFlightInput(MechObject *mech, int aileron, int elevator, int throttle, int rudder)

entries.name: Mech_RegisterSubsystem
entries.description: The mech module's C++ static initialiser (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7ace): inside an Eh_InitExceptBlock frame, registers Mech_ResetMissionGlobals (00415464) through RegisterSubsystemLoader as subsystem phase 2, the once-per-mission phase, and Mech_FlushDeletes (0041544c) as phase 5, the once-a-frame phase; zeroes GlobalMechList (004a9bfe, which is the mech pool object itself) and vector-news DAT_004a9c0c as 40 elements of 8 bytes, the player's line-of-fire points. Subsystem_RunPhase is what dispatches a registered phase.

entries.name: Mech_StaticDtor
entries.description: Mech_RegisterSubsystem's _EXIT_ routine (Borland _EXIT_ entry 004a7c12): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr and Mem_Deletes GlobalMechList (the mech pool) when it is set.

entries.name: FlatObj_Destruct
entries.description: FlatObj vtable +0x08: restores TSObjVtable (004a0b98), deletes the shape instance at obj+0x34 through its own +0x18 with flag 3, and frees the object when the flag's low bit is set. ObjectPool_FlushDeleteQueue calls it with 2 and hands the node back to g_FlatObjPool itself.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_Dtor
entries.description: GUNLIST's destructor, from its class record (0041be41; GUNLIST is the 0x14-byte mount manager, table 00499338): (manager, flags). Two RTL destructor-count decrements, Mem_DeleteArray of the mount-pointer array at +4 when set, then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 0041be8d; class record at 0041be41

entries.name: WeaponMounts_DtorLocal
entries.description: PLAYER_GUNLIST's destructor, from its class record (0041bde1; table 00499238): (manager, flags). Rtl_VectorDelete(manager+0x1f, 6, 3, 1, 0041bf94) over the three 6-byte fire-group arrays WeaponMounts_CtorLocal allocates, then GUNLIST's teardown -- Mem_DeleteArray of the array at +4 -- and Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 0041bf19; class record at 0041bde1

entries.name: ARRAY_short_Dtor
entries.description: ARRAY<short>'s destructor, the dtor its class record (0x6 bytes, at 0041bfc3) names: (array, flags): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr; when the array is not null, Mem_DeleteArray of its buffer at +0 when that is set, then Mem_Delete of the array when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: ARRAY_GUN_STATE_Ptr_Dtor
entries.description: ARRAY<GUN_STATE *>'s destructor, the dtor its class record (0x6 bytes, at 0041bec9) names: (array, flags): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr; when the array is not null, Mem_DeleteArray of its buffer at +0 when that is set, then Mem_Delete of the array when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: CountdownTimer_ElementCtor
entries.description: (timer): returns its argument -- the per-element constructor Mech_Constructor hands Rtl_VectorNew(mech+0x258, 3, 5, 1, it) at 00415c82 for the first five 3-byte countdown timers of the mech's run at +0x258 (the missile-lock countdowns).

entries.name: ObjPool_MECH_Dtor
entries.description: ObjPool<MECH>'s destructor, the dtor its class record (0x8 bytes, at 0041c079) names: (pool, flags): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr; when the pool is not null, Mem_Delete of its entry buffer at +0 when that is set, then Mem_Delete of the pool when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: Mech_AiEngageOrderedTarget
entries.description: (mech, target). When target differs from mech+0x1a4 it installs it, maintaining the +0x1a2 holder counts and raising +0x9d. Then it switches on the target's class (target+0x1a8, read without a null test): 0, a HERC, sets mech+0xac and runs Mech_AiEnterCombat; 1 or 3, a structure or ground vehicle, installs attacking base (descriptor 00499518); 2, a flyer, installs attacking flyer (00499556); any other class installs nothing. Callers found by es2_xref: Mech_AiSelectBehaviour, Mech_AiOnTakingFire and five sites in Mech_ReceiveSquadOrder.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourPlayerThink
entries.description: Think slot of behaviour states 1 player and 2 player fly. Gated on the machine being its group's leader, and always returns 0. Its first arm is the player's own waypoint arrival: the waypoint after the group's route cursor, inside 10000 units of ground range and not a closed route's terminating duplicate (Route_NextWaypointClosesRoute), posts WAYPOINT REACHED and steps the shared cursor. Then it switches on DAT_004a9ed8, the script.dat objective selector, into one mission-objective arm: 0 MISSION TARGET DETECTED (one-shot, raises +0x9f), 5 a 40000-unit goal proximity (raises +0x9f), 3 and 7 the four-message data-link sequence (raises +0xa0). Any other selector, 2 included, runs no arm. None of the arms touches the route.

entries.name: Ai_UpdateWeaponsFree
entries.description: The AI's radar switch, whatever the name says: writes mech+0x96, the PASSIVE/ACTIVE scanner mode, from mech+0xb2 (the squad's radar order) when the first member of the machine's group (**(group+0xc)) has +0xa3 set, the player's group, and from mech+0x97 (the mission file's standing setting) otherwise. It does not test the radar-silence timer. Callers found by es2_xref: Ai_NavigationStep, Mech_BehaviourSleepThink and two sites in Mech_BehaviourGuardThink.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourSleepThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 13 (sleeping). Releases the target (decrementing its +0x1a2 holder count and setting +0x9d) when one is held, then Mech_LocomotionTick(0,0,0) and Ai_UpdateWeaponsFree; returns 0, so the state never ends itself.

entries.name: Ai_ClearSquadEngageOrder
entries.description: Returns 1, and clears a standing squad engage order (mech+0x23e 4 to 0) when its target mech+0x248 is the machine's current target mech+0x1a4. Callers found by es2_xref: the attacking, flanking, facing off, attacking base and attacking flyer thinks, each as the tail of its completion test.

entries.name: Ai_ShouldAbandonTarget
entries.description: Whether a combat state should drop its target, mech+0x1a4. Under squad order verb 4 (mech+0x23e) with an order target at +0x248: when Ai_TargetStateTier of the current target exceeds mech+0x250, compared signed, and nothing else is tested. For the group order's designated target (Group_IsOrderTarget): on the human side (group+0x12 zero) when the target's +0xa4 or +0x99 is set, on the Cybrid side when +0x99 is. Otherwise when it is out of action (+0xa5, +0xa4 or +0x99). Callers found by es2_xref: the attacking, flanking and facing off thinks, and a call in the bytes of Mech_BehaviourDriveOffThink that follow its unconditional jump to the epilogue.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourAttackThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 3 (attacking). Returns 0 when Ai_BeginSkirtIfBlocked starts a skirt. Builds the combat geometry. With |aspect| < 8000 it sets approach = (0x8000 - |bearing error|) >= 4000 ? 1 : -1, takes the point 18000 units from the target along its heading +-0x4000 (+0x4000 when (bearing error < 0) equals (|bearing error| > 0x4000)), reflects that point through this machine's position when approach is -1, and steers at it (bearing error = Math_HeadingToward(point, position) - heading); otherwise approach is 0, or -1 past 0x1fff of bearing error, and the steer stays on the target. Leaves the built-in 15000/30000 standoff ring. Ai_CombatMoveStep, then Ai_AimAndFire with the aspect. Returns Ai_ClearSquadEngageOrder's 1 when Ai_ShouldAbandonTarget answers nonzero or this machine is out of action (+0xa5, +0xa4 or +0x99), else 0.

entries.name: Ai_CircleStep
entries.description: (mech, geom): the circling step. While the break-off countdown at mech+0x60 (stepped through the handle +0x5f) is running it writes near standoff 0, approach -1 and bearing error 0 into the block, clears the hysteresis byte mech+0x66 and reloads the interval countdown mech+0x63 with 4000, so one break-off and its interval take 5000 counts. Otherwise it steps the interval (handle +0x62) and, when that has run out and mech+0x288 (damage in the current window) exceeds 100, sets the break-off to 1000. Threshold = 0x4000 when +0x66 is set, else 0x6000. With |aspect| (geom+0x08) under it, it circles: near standoff 0, approach 1, and the bearing error points at Math_OffsetPointByBearing(target position, bearing + 0x8000 + (bearing error >= 0 ? 6000 : -6000), 15000), clearing +0x66. Otherwise it squares up: sets +0x66, and with its own twist (vtable +0x3c) in [-2000, 2000) writes approach 0 and the word at mech+0x5d to 0, else approach -1. The squaring-up arm writes no standoff. Callers found by es2_xref: the flanking and attacking base thinks.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourAttackBaseThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 6 (attacking base). Returns 0 when Ai_BeginSkirtIfBlocked starts a skirt. Builds the combat geometry and, when the target's type record +0x2e (BASES.DAT armament class) is zero, forces the aspect and its magnitude to 32000, so Ai_CircleStep stands off instead of circling. Ai_CircleStep, then standoffs 25000 / -20536, which makes the ring mandatory; Ai_CombatMoveStep and Ai_AimAndFire with the aspect. Its completion test replaces Ai_ShouldAbandonTarget: when a squad engage order stands (+0x23e == 4 with +0x248 non-null) or Group_IsOrderTarget(group, target) holds, the target is finished only when destroyed (+0x99); otherwise when out of action (+0xa5, +0xa4 or +0x99). Returns Ai_ClearSquadEngageOrder's 1 when the target is finished or this machine is out of action, else 0.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourAttackFlyerThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 7 (attacking flyer). No skirt gate. Builds the combat geometry, then approach = -1 at 2000 BAM or more of bearing error; inside that, 1 when |aspect| > 2000 and the 3D range > 35000, 0 when only one of the two holds, -1 when neither. Standoffs 0/1000000, which leave the approach to the state at any range the think keeps. Ai_CombatMoveStep, then Ai_AimAndFire with the aspect. Returns 1 past 150000 range, before any other test; otherwise returns Ai_ClearSquadEngageOrder's 1 when the flyer's +0x99 (destroyed) is set or this machine is out of action (+0xa5, +0xa4 or +0x99), else 0. That completion test reads the flyer's +0x99 directly in place of Ai_ShouldAbandonTarget.

entries.name: Mech_CompareCombatRating
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x4c. Compares this machine's combat rating (+0x29e) with a candidate's and returns the index the AI's three target-weight tables share: 0 this machine's is higher, 1 within 400, 2 the candidate's is higher. Returns 0 for every non-HERC candidate. Both ratings are jittered by rand & 1000 (AND AX,0x3e8) where rand % 1000 was meant.

entries.name: Ai_SumAttackerRatings
entries.description: (object). Sums the signed short +0x29e (combat rating) over every machine in GlobalMechList, walked with Pool_Prev, whose +0x1a4 is the object: the combined rating of the HERCs targeting it. Callers found by es2_xref: Mech_AiFleeCheck, at two sites.

entries.name: Mech_AiFleeCheck
entries.description: Decides whether a machine breaks off; returns 1 when it has installed a state itself. Out of action (+0xa5, +0xa4 or +0x99): when its target (+0x1a4, read without a null test) is class 1 or 3 and that type's BASES.DAT +0x2e is zero it runs Mech_AiSelectBehaviour, otherwise it installs fleeing (descriptor 00499800); either way it returns 1 and leaves +0x2aa alone. Otherwise fear = Mech_GetOverallDamage (vtable +0x40) plus, band by band, the band's penalty (0049a334: 5/25/50) once for each of the six components 0049a328 lists (0, 1, 4, 5, 6, 7) whose Q8 damage ratio (damage*256/max, 256 for a negative damage word) exceeds the band's threshold (0049a33a: 60/120/180), stopping at the first band no component passes. Then against +0x1a2 holders: fear over 70 writes +0x2aa = 1000 and flees on any holder; 51-70 writes 600 and flees on three or more, or on one or two whose Ai_SumAttackerRatings beats its own +0x29e; 31-50 writes 300 and flees on three or more whose average rating beats its own; 30 or under writes nothing and returns 0.

entries.name: Mech_AiSelectAimComponent
entries.description: Chooses the component slot the AI aims at and writes it to mech+0x2a2, or -1. One rand & 0x7f, always drawn, picks a band: a collapsed target (target+0xb4) gives slot 0 alone; under 0x28, or whenever the targeting pod at mech+0x30b exists and its +0x7f is under 0xaa, slots 7-18; under 0x50 the weapon-mount slots 19..18+count, the count read from the shooter's own manager (mech+0x202 +0x08); otherwise slots 0-6. Within the band it skips slots whose word in the target's occupancy array (the pointer at target+0x20e) is zero, and for the rest takes the highest Component_ReadDamagePercent(mech+0x206, slot) + (rand & 0x3f) above 0, drawing one jitter per slot it reads. The damage read is the shooter's own components, mech+0x206, while the occupancy walked is the target's. Callers found by es2_xref: Mech_AiCombatReassess, Mech_BehaviourGuardThink and Mech_AiOnTakingFire.

entries.name: Mech_AiCombatReassess
entries.description: The reassess slot of behaviour states 3-7 and 18. Puts the machine's radar to ACTIVE unless its group is led by the local player; keeps a just-handed target (+0xac) or re-acquires with Ai_SelectTarget, the squad order verb choosing between the order's own target and a free pick; a committed machine under a movement order instead falls into Mech_AiSelectBehaviour and drops the fight. A group's first member re-enters every other live uncommitted member, so one machine's fight commits the group. Then runs Mech_AiFleeCheck and, if that did not decide, installs attacking base / attacking flyer for a structure or flyer and facing off / attacking / flanking for a HERC by Mech_CompareCombatRating; an outgunned machine flanks only with both leg-damage latches (+0xa8, +0xa9) clear and typeRec+0xc8 over 0xb9, and faces off otherwise.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourFleeThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 18 (fleeing). When mech+0x1a4 is set it stores it at mech+0x61 in the block scratch and releases it (target+0x1a2 decremented, mech+0x9d set); the geometry, the aim and the completion test then run against mech+0x61. Under 0x3000 of bearing error: approach -1 and the steer turned a half turn (+0x8000). Otherwise: when the countdown stepped by Timer_CountDown through handle mech+0x5a (the int at +0x5b) has run out, it reloads 4000 counts (about 2 s) and writes rand & 1 as a word at +0x5f; then approach 1 and the steer offset by -0x6000 when +0x5f is set, +0x6000 when clear. Standoffs 0/10000000. TurboPod_Engage on the pod at mech+0x317 when there is one, every tick. Ai_CombatMoveStep, then Ai_AimAndFire(mech, aspect, stash). Returns 1 when the stashed object is out of action (+0xa5, +0xa4 or +0x99), else 0.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourFaceOffThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 5 (facing off). Ai_BeginSkirtIfBlocked gate (returns 0 when it fires), the combat geometry, then approach 1 under 0x2000 of bearing error and -1 at 0x2000 or more, standoffs 16000/35000, and the bearing error left pointing at the target. Ai_CombatMoveStep, Ai_AimAndFire, then returns Ai_ClearSquadEngageOrder's 1 when Ai_ShouldAbandonTarget answers nonzero or this machine is out of action (+0xa5, +0xa4 or +0x99), else 0.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourFlankThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 4 (flanking). Ai_BeginSkirtIfBlocked gate (returns 0 when it fires), the combat geometry, Ai_CircleStep, Ai_CombatMoveStep, Ai_AimAndFire, then facing off's completion test: Ai_ClearSquadEngageOrder's 1 when Ai_ShouldAbandonTarget answers nonzero or this machine is out of action (+0xa5, +0xa4 or +0x99), else 0. The combat reassess installs it for an outgunned machine whose typeRec+0xc8 is over 0xb9; MechType_InitOne copies the forward speed typeRec+0x06 there, and 13 of the 21 retail chassis clear the bar.

entries.name: Ai_NavigationStep
entries.description: The movement half of the patrol and search-and-destroy thinks; callers found by es2_xref: Mech_BehaviourSearchDestroyThink, Mech_BehaviourPatrolThink and Ai_NavigationStepThunk. Under a standing squad order (mech+0x23e nonzero) Ai_DriveToPoint at mech+0x240; otherwise Ai_FollowRoute when this machine is its group's slot 0 (**(group+0x0c)) and Ai_KeepFormation when it is not, so on this path the group leader is the one machine that reads the route. Then Ai_UpdateWeaponsFree and Mech_CenterTorsoTick(mech, 0).

entries.name: Mech_AiEnterCombat
entries.description: Calls Mech_AiCombatReassess(mech) and returns. Callers found by es2_xref: Mech_AiEngageOrderedTarget, Mech_AiCombatReassess (the leader sweep), Mech_BehaviourSearchDestroyThink, Mech_BehaviourPatrolThink and Mech_AiOnTakingFire.

entries.name: Ai_NavigationStepThunk
entries.description: Calls Ai_NavigationStep(mech) and returns. No caller, stored pointer or vtable slot found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourSearchDestroyThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 12, search/destroy. Ai_NavigationStep, then releases mech+0x1a4, then returns 0 unless this machine is its group's slot 0 or mech+0xb6 (FIRE AT WILL) is set. Past that gate, when the countdown stepped by Math_CountdownTimerTick through handle mech+0x5a (the word at +0x5b) has run out, it reloads 10000 counts (about 4.9 s) and, for a machine out of action (+0xa5, +0xa4 or +0x99), installs Ai_SelectTarget(this, 0, 0) and, when that is non-null, writes -1 to mech+0x2a2 and installs fleeing (descriptor 00499800). Otherwise it takes Ai_SelectTarget(this, 1, 0) and, when that passes Group_IsOrderTarget, installs it, sets mech+0xac and runs Mech_AiEnterCombat. Always returns 0. Mech_BehaviourPatrolThink's shape, with no squad-verb term in the gate and no verb test on the acquisition.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourPatrolThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 8, patrolling. Reads the squad verb mech+0x23e, runs Ai_NavigationStep, releases mech+0x1a4, then returns 0 unless this machine is its group's slot 0, the squad verb is nonzero or mech+0xb6 (FIRE AT WILL) is set. Past that gate, when the countdown stepped by Math_CountdownTimerTick through handle mech+0x5a (the word at +0x5b) has run out, it reloads 10000 counts (about 4.9 s) and, for a machine out of action (+0xa5, +0xa4 or +0x99), installs Ai_SelectTarget(this, 0, 0) and, when that is non-null, writes -1 to mech+0x2a2 and installs fleeing (00499800). Otherwise it acquires with Ai_SelectTarget(this, 1, 0) when the squad verb is 2, or is 0 with the group's current order verb 3 (a null order entry reads as 0x0b); it installs the pick, null included, and on a non-null pick sets mech+0xac and runs Mech_AiEnterCombat. Always returns 0.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourTravelThink
entries.description: Behaviour states 9 and 11, travelling and bulldog travel. Calls Ai_FollowRoute directly rather than through Ai_NavigationStep, so every member reads the route and every member can advance the shared cursor. Releases mech+0x1a4. When the countdown stepped by Timer_CountDown through handle mech+0x5a (the int at +0x5b) has run out: Ai_SelectTarget(this, 0, 0) into mech+0x5f, a turret look-at this function keeps out of mech+0x1a4; reload 10000; radar mech+0x96 = 1 when the pick is non-null or mech+0x97 is set, else 0. While mech+0x5f is non-null, Ai_AimAndFire(this, aspect, it), the aspect built by hand: Math_HeadingToward from it to this machine, less its heading, plus its vtable +0x3c twist. Always returns 0.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourFollowThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 10, following. Mech_BehaviourTravelThink with the route replaced: the object Group_OrderTargetObject returns (read without a null test) is stood off with Mech_LocomotionTick(this, 0, 0, 0) inside a 3D Math_DistanceBetweenPoints range of 25000, and driven at with Ai_DriveToPoint beyond it. Then the travel think's release, look-at acquisition, radar write and Ai_AimAndFire. It advances no route cursor, while verb 6's completion test is a route test -- so a following order can only complete on a group whose route was empty to begin with. Always returns 0.

entries.name: Mech_AiGoalPosition
entries.description: Returns a pointer to the point a machine is working to, by squad order verb (mech+0x23e): 3, the position of the object at +0x24c; 5, the position of the object at +0x248; 6, the position of the object at +0x24c, or the stored point at +0x240 when that is null; any other verb, Group_OrderTargetPosition of the machine's group. Verbs 3 and 5 read the pointer without a null test. Callers found by es2_xref: Mech_BehaviourPlayerThink, Mech_BehaviourGuardThink, Mech_AiOnTakingFire and the second body of Mech_BehaviourDriveOffThink.

entries.name: Ai_LineOfSightBlocked
entries.description: Line of sight from this machine (+0x26) to its selected target (+0x1a4, its +0x26), each raised by its vtable +0x24 record's +0x1c or by 500 units when there is none. Runs Terrain_RayWalk mode 1 (the slope walk), then Sim_RaycastShapes, then Terrain_RayHitDistance (the thin ray, distance unread). Returns 1 when the shape probe stops on something other than the target (target+0xc); otherwise 0 when the thin ray reports no ground hit, 1 when it does and the slope walk also blocks, 2 when it does and the slope walk is clear -- so steep ground counts only where the thin ray also meets the ground. The trigger for the skirting state.

entries.name: Mech_AiOnLineOfFireBlocked
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x64. With a target at mech+0x1a4 it copies the target's position (+0x26) to mech+0x31e and sets mech+0xad, which makes the next combat think enter skirting; with none it does nothing. Found by es2_xref only as the MechVtable slot; the call through the slot is Sim_RaycastObjectList's (hit-detection.md). The other SimObject-shaped tables fill the slot with SimObject_AiOnLineOfFireBlockedNoOp.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourSkirtThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 14 (skirting). Walks at the position stashed at mech+0x31e or, while the last line-of-sight reading (mech+0x61) is 1, at a point offset from it by the stored range mech+0x67 along the bearing from it to this machine plus or minus 0x4000 (side mech+0x60, chosen on the first tick from the sign of the bearing error to the stash). The first tick (word mech+0x5e zero) sets +0x5e, arms the re-test countdown (the int at mech+0x63, handle +0x62) with 5000 counts (about 2.4 s) and sets +0x61 = 1. On each expiry it reloads 5000 and stores Ai_LineOfSightBlocked's answer at +0x61: 0 reinstalls the descriptor stashed at mech+0x5a and clears mech+0xad, nonzero writes the ground range to the stash to +0x67. A reading of 2 (ground the machine could walk) gets no offset. Steers with Mech_LocomotionTick(this, error >> 6, 0x100, 0), then Mech_CenterTorsoTick(this, 0). Always returns 0.

entries.name: Ai_BeginSkirtIfBlocked
entries.description: The skirt gate. When mech+0xad is set it keeps the current descriptor pointer (mech+0x4d), installs skirting (descriptor 0x499708, state 14), stores the kept pointer at mech+0x5a in the scratch that install just zeroed, writes the 3D range from the machine to mech+0x31e at mech+0x67, and returns 1; otherwise returns 0. It leaves +0xad set. Callers found by es2_xref: the attacking, attacking base, facing off, flanking and driving off en thinks.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourDriveOffThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 16 (driving off en). Returns 0 when Ai_BeginSkirtIfBlocked takes over; otherwise calls Mech_BehaviourFaceOffThink and returns its answer. The states differ only in their descriptors: this one holds a place and reassesses through Mech_AiSelectBehaviour. The bytes after that call's jump to the epilogue (0041df1b-0041e0d6, raw in the Ghidra listing) hold a second body: it steers relative to Mech_AiGoalPosition, stores 750 to mech+0x2aa, calls Ai_AimAndFire and Ai_ShouldAbandonTarget, and on completion zeroes mech+0x248. Searched for an entry into them with es2_xref on every instruction start: no rel32 branch found, and one stored-pointer hit that is CALL operand bytes at 00492064.

entries.name: Ai_SelectDefenceTarget
entries.description: (mech, point). Reloads mech+0x5b, the guard think's sweep countdown, with 10000. Limit is 90000, or 980000 when the group's current order record (group+0x44 indexed by group+0x6c) has a null subject at +0x0e. Walks GlobalMechList with Pool_Prev over the HERCs that Ai_IsTargetable(mech, candidate, 0) passes and whose +0xa4 is clear; score = limit - Math_GroundDistanceBetweenPoints(candidate, point), divided by holders + 1 when +0x1a2 is nonzero (this machine included when it holds the candidate), and a score that is not positive is dropped. A live candidate (+0xa5 and +0x99 clear) displaces one that is not whatever the score, and one that is not live is skipped once a live one is held; otherwise the higher score wins. Returns the best, or 0. Callers found by es2_xref: Mech_BehaviourGuardThink and Mech_AiOnTakingFire.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourGuardThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 15, guarding. Post = Mech_AiGoalPosition. Releases mech+0x1a4. A machine in a group whose slot 0 is PlayerMech with no standing squad order (mech+0x23e zero) does not hold the post; any other does. When it holds the post or mech+0xb6 is set, and the countdown at mech+0x5b (Math_CountdownTimerTick through handle +0x5a) has run out, it picks mech+0x248 under squad verb 4 when that is non-null, Ai_SelectDefenceTarget(this, post) otherwise; the think does not reload the countdown itself. With no pick, a machine not holding the post runs Ai_KeepFormation, Ai_UpdateWeaponsFree and Mech_CenterTorsoTick; one holding it runs Mech_CenterTorsoTick and Ai_UpdateWeaponsFree, then Ai_DriveToPoint at the post past 30000 ground range, else Mech_LocomotionTick(this, (bearing to post - heading + 0x8000) >> 6, range under 10000 ? 0x100 : 0, 0) -- facing away from the post, walking away inside 10000 and standing between. A pick is installed at mech+0x1a4; out of action (+0xa5, +0xa4 or +0x99) installs fleeing (00499800) and writes -1 to mech+0x2a2, otherwise driving off en (00499784), Mech_AiSelectAimComponent, and radar mech+0x96 = 1 unless the group's slot 0 has +0xa3 set and mech+0xb2 is clear. Always returns 0. It calls Ai_KeepFormation and Ai_DriveToPoint itself rather than through Ai_NavigationStep.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourRamTick
entries.description: The move slot of the ramming state (17), in place of Mech_MovementTick: Mech_IntegrateMotion, Z set to Terrain_HeightQuery(ActiveHeightGrid) plus typeRec+0x16, Mech_PlaceLegsOnGround, then Mech_CollisionTest -- with no SimObject_PushTransform/SimObject_PopTransform, so a refused step is kept. When the test refuses, or mech+0xb1 (the 'something ran into me' latch SimObject_SetRunInto raises) is set, it calls Damage_ExplosiveBlastSweep(pos, 3000, 2000, 0, self) and then writes a flat 32000 through vtable +0x74, attacker self, to each of its 29 components whose active flag (the +0x20e array) is set. Returns 1.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourInertThink
entries.description: Behaviour states 20 (dead) and 21 (disabled). Mech_LocomotionTick(mech, 0, 0, 0), then returns 0.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourRamThink
entries.description: The think slot (+0x00) of AI behaviour state block 00499b5c, the ramming attack. When the countdown stepped by Timer_CountDown through handle mech+0x5a (the int at +0x5b) has run out it installs Ai_SelectTarget(this, 6, 0) at mech+0x1a4, maintaining the +0x1a2 holder counts and +0x9d, and reloads 10000 counts (about 4.9 s). With no target, Mech_LocomotionTick(this, 0, 0, 1) and return. Otherwise it steers with Mech_LocomotionTick(turn = (bearing - heading) >> 8, throttle 0x100, avoidance flag 1) -- a quarter the >> 6 steer gain of the other states. A two-phase word flag at mech+0x5f over a countdown at mech+0x62 (Math_CountdownTimerTick through handle +0x61), each phase arming the countdown of the phase it enters: approaching (0) lasts 8000 + Math_RandomBelow(4000) counts, charging (1) 3000 + Math_RandomBelow(1500). Charging, after the first steer come Mech_BehaviourRamTick, a steer, Mech_BehaviourRamTick again and a third steer, returning early whenever the target has gone after a RamTick -- three RamTicks a tick counting the move slot's own. Both fields start zeroed by Behaviour_SetState, so the first think flips to charging and the extra RamTicks start on the next. Always returns 0.

entries.name: Ai_BuildCombatGeometry
entries.description: (mech, geom, target): fills the 0x18-byte block a combat think passes down. A null target means mech+0x1a4. +0x00 bearing to the target (Math_HeadingToward); +0x02 that less the machine's heading (+0x10); +0x06 the aspect, target vtable +0x3c (turret twist) + bearing + 0x8000 - target heading; +0x0a the 3D range (Math_DistanceBetweenPoints); +0x04 and +0x08 the magnitudes of +0x02 and +0x06, -0x8000 saturating to 0x7fff; +0x0e approach 0; +0x10 15000 and +0x14 30000, the standoff pair. Callers found by es2_xref: the attacking, attacking base, attacking flyer, fleeing, facing off and flanking thinks.

entries.name: Ai_CombatMoveStep
entries.description: (mech, geom): the combat states' walk. Range (geom+0x0a) under the near standoff sets approach to 1 when |bearing error| (geom+0x04) is 0x4000 or more, else -1; range over the far standoff sets it to 1 when the magnitude is 0x4000 or less, else -1; between them the approach already in the block stands. Then it recomputes geom+0x04 from geom+0x02, and with approach nonzero stores it as a short at mech+0x5a and takes speed +0x100 or -0x100 by its sign, speed 0 otherwise. Ends in Mech_LocomotionTick(mech, bearing error >> 6, speed, 0). Callers found by es2_xref: the attacking, attacking base, attacking flyer, fleeing, facing off and flanking thinks.

entries.name: Mech_CenterTorsoTick
entries.description: The [Backspace] 'Center Turret' command, run every tick while g_CenterTurretMode is latched. Drives each torso tick with -clamp(Q10(0xfa, angle), +/-0x100) and snapTarget 0 with the snap enabled, so the turret runs home and stops exactly on centre. Nothing clears the mode on arrival; the input path clears it the moment either turret axis is non-zero.

entries.name: Ai_AimAndFireAtMech
entries.description: (mech, aspect, target): Ai_AimAndFire's machine branch. Bearing error = Math_HeadingToward(target, mech) - mech heading (+0x10); unless (u16)(error + lim) < (u16)(2 * lim), lim being the shooter's typeRec+0x22 torso-twist limit, so the error lies in [-lim, lim), it runs Mech_CenterTorsoTick(mech, 0) and returns. With mech+0x2a2 at 0 or above and the 3D range (Math_DistanceBetweenPoints) in [5000, 20000) the point is the target's vtable +0x58 (Mech_ComponentPosition) for that slot; otherwise it is the target's aim node, Mech_GetAimNodeTransform (vtable +0x24) +0x14 put through Transform_ApplyToPoint with the target's world frame at +0x12, which it first rebuilds from the euler triple at +0x0c when the valid flag +0x32 is clear and then sets. Ends in Ai_FireAtPoint(mech, point, aspect, target). typeRec+0x22 is 14000 on 20 of the 21 chassis; PITBULL's 32767 refuses only 0x7fff and -0x8000.

entries.name: Ai_AimAndFire
entries.description: (mech, aspect, target): the aim-and-fire tail. A null target means mech+0x1a4, read without a further null test. Switches on the target's class (obj+0x1a8): 0 goes to Ai_AimAndFireAtMech; 1 aims at the structure's component that vtable +0x54 returns with a null second argument, placed by vtable +0x58; anything else aims at the object's position plus the second triple vtable +0x30 fills. The last two end in Ai_FireAtPoint(mech, point, aspect, target). Callers found by es2_xref: the attacking, flanking, facing off, attacking base, attacking flyer, fleeing, travelling and following thinks, and a call in the bytes of Mech_BehaviourDriveOffThink that follow its unconditional jump to the epilogue.

entries.name: Mech_AiSelectBehaviour
entries.description: __cdecl(mech): picks and installs the next AI behaviour state. Three mutually exclusive paths: the local player (mech+0xa3) takes 'player fly' (00499420) or 'player' (004993e2) on the type record's flyer flag typeRec+0x50; a machine in a group whose slot 0 is PlayerMech with a standing squad order (mech+0x23e) maps verbs 1/2 to 'patrolling', 4 to Mech_AiEngageOrderedTarget against the order target at mech+0x248 -- or, when that target's +0x99 is set, clears mech+0x23e and re-enters -- and 6 to 'guarding'; anything else reads its mission group's current order (mech+0x45, array at group+0x44 indexed by group+0x6c, verb = the entry's first short) and maps 0-6 to search/destroy, ramming, guarding, patrolling, sleeping, travelling-or-bulldog-travel (bulldog when typeRec+0x22 is over 0x7d00) and following. A null order entry substitutes verb 0x0b, which matches no case and installs whatever descriptor EDX held on entry. The player branch, squad verbs 1/2 and 6 and the order-verb path each release a non-null mech+0x1a4 after installing (target+0x1a2 decremented, mech+0x9d set); squad verb 4 does not, and squad verbs 3, 5 and above 6 install nothing and leave the target. Returns 1 on every path.

entries.name: Mech_ComputeCombatRating
entries.description: Writes the combat rating at mech+0x29e and sets mech+0x94, the flag that marks it current. Rating = (typeRec+0x44 + for each non-null mount whose damage reading (Mech_ReadDamageReadouts) is not negative and whose vtable +0x54 answers non-zero, Q8(template+0x4e, 0x100 - reading), the template being mount+0x1c + for each of 19 components with a non-negative reading, Q8(component maximum, 0x100 - reading) - typeRec+0x7e[i] for each of the first 10 systems whose reading is above 0xb4) >> 4. Returns the rating. See docs/retail/simulation/ai-targeting.md.

entries.name: Cockpit_TargetAnglesFromCameraBone
entries.description: Transforms a world point into the pilot eye's frame and returns its azimuth/elevation. The camera part id (typeRec+0x0c) is a shape PART id: the shape find-by-id vtable slot (+0x20) returns the part, its TSBasePart.Transform (+4) is a transform id, and that indexes the per-node transform array at shapeInst+0x16 (0x20 bytes per entry). Composes the inverse of the mech transform (mech+0xc) then the inverse of that node transform, and subtracts typeRec+0x66. The cockpit eye rides the same node, which is where the retail cockpit bob comes from -- no dedicated bob code exists. Chain is uniform across the fleet: part 5 -> transform 11 -> 4 -> 1 for 16 of 18 HERCs, node 1 being the one the walk cycle animates.

entries.name: Ai_ChooseWeapon
entries.description: (mech, aspect, range, target). Scores every mount and returns the best above a floor of Math_MapRange(mech+0x2aa, 0, 0x400, 150, -100), or 0, in which case the machine aims and does not shoot. It asks the target's vtable +0x34 for the shield with the boolean (u16)(aspect + 0x4000) < 0x8000 in place of a heading, and sets the jitter bound to 35 for a class-0 target and 30 otherwise. It also compares the machine's group with PlayerMech's and discards the result. Per mount: a null slot or one whose vtable +0x5c answers nonzero (spent) is passed over; any other clears the all-spent flag. kind = vtable +0x60; a kind-0 (SARH) mount that WeaponMount_RangeAllows passes turns mech+0x96 on when it is off and the radar-silence counter +0x26b is zero. It is scored only when in range and either kind 5 or 3 or the manager's lock word at +0x0a + 2*kind is set, and then only when vtable +0x2c (can fire) answers nonzero. Credit from the mount's PROJ.DAT record at mount+0x20: its armor damage (+6) with no shield, its shield damage (+4) when that does not exceed the shield, and armor damage + 10000 when it does. Score = Q10(100, credit) - Q10(1000, template+0x34) + rand(bound) * rand(bound), the best held as a short. When every mount was absent or spent and mech+0xa5 is clear it sets +0xa5, activates the object's +0x1b6 action, and raises MissionPollTimer_Count (004a9ee7) to at least 1000.

entries.name: Ai_FireAtPoint
entries.description: (mech, point, aspect, target): the AI's fire decision. Range is the ground distance to the point. It keeps the latched mount at mech+0x2ac when one is latched, its vtable +0x2c answers nonzero and WeaponMount_RangeAllows passes. Failing that: with mech+0xb5 set it clears it and the weapon is 0 for this call; without, it runs Ai_ChooseWeapon and zeroes +0x2ac. Weapon 0: Cockpit_TargetAnglesFromCameraBone(mech, point) and return. With one: when the PROJ.DAT speed (mount+0x20 +0x0a) is positive and the target's vtable +0x38 speed is nonzero, the point is moved along the target's heading by (short)((short)(range >> 2) * speed * 4 / projectile speed); for a group whose side byte (group+0x12) is nonzero, a nonzero scatter from 0049a30c indexed by the difficulty at 004a9ee0 adds Math_RandomBelow(scatter) to x, y and z. Then it aims through Cockpit_TargetAnglesFromCameraBone, and fires (vtable +0x28) when the mount's vtable +0x60 kind is not 5, or when both residual angles are in [-1000, 1000). After a shot it latches the mount into +0x2ac when its template's +0x56 is 6 or 0x16, ELF or ELF2. Callers found by es2_xref: Ai_AimAndFireAtMech and Ai_AimAndFire.

entries.name: Mech_AiFriendlyFireComplaint
entries.description: When the countdown at mech+0x278 is zero, reloads it with 40000 (about 19.5 s) and posts squad message 8 through Ai_PostSquadMessage(mech, 8, 0); otherwise does nothing. It tests nothing about the shooter: callers found by es2_xref, Mech_AiOnTakingFire (the player hitting a member of its own group) and Sim_RaycastObjectList (the player's shot hitting its own side outside its group), make that decision.

entries.name: Mech_AiOnTakingFire
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x50, called with (attacker, damage) when something hits this machine; it applies no damage itself. In order: when the attacker is PlayerMech and this machine's group (+0x45) is PlayerMech's, Mech_AiFriendlyFireComplaint. Returns when the attacker is out of action (+0xa5, +0xa4 or +0x99) or its group's side byte (+0x12) equals this machine's. SimObject_AiOnTakingFire(this, attacker, 0), which runs Detection_ShareContact, and the under-fire countdown at +0x27d set to 30000 (about 14.6 s). In PlayerMech's group it adds the damage to +0x281 and returns while the total is under 8000. Returns for the local player (+0xa3), while the retarget cooldown at +0x273 runs, or when the attacker is mech+0x1a4 and the state's flag bit 1 (descriptor+0x09) is set. Sets +0x273 to 10000 (about 4.9 s). With flag bit 1 clear in a group whose slot 0 has +0xa3 set: squad message 3 through Ai_PostSquadMessage when the attacker is a HERC (+0x1a8 zero), and +0x9a cleared when the attacker is that slot-0 machine's target. Flag bit 2 (descriptor+0x0a; guarding, driving off en): pick = Ai_SelectDefenceTarget(this, Mech_AiGoalPosition(this)), replaced by mech+0x248 under squad verb 4 unless the pick's +0x1a4 is this machine; a non-null pick replaces the attacker, which is installed at +0x1a4; a HERC gets driving off en (00499784) and Mech_AiSelectAimComponent, anything else Mech_AiEngageOrderedTarget. Flag bit 3 (descriptor+0x0b; sleeping, ramming, bulldog travel): returns. Otherwise pick = Ai_SelectTarget(this, 0x24, 0); under squad verb 4, unless the pick's +0x1a4 is this machine, mech+0x248 replaces it when non-null with +0xa4 and +0x99 clear, and the verb is cleared to 0 when not. The pick is installed; non-null sets +0xac and runs Mech_AiEnterCombat, null with a target held on entry runs Mech_AiSelectBehaviour.

entries.name: Ai_DriveToPoint
entries.description: The AI's one steering primitive: Mech_LocomotionTick(mech, (Math_HeadingToward(point, mech) - mech.heading) >> 6, speed, 0) with speed = mech+0x252 or 0xaa when that is zero, and a Turbo Pod sprint at 0x100 past 30000 units that only a standing squad order can reach. Returns whether the GROUND-PLANE range is under 10000 -- arrival, which is what Ai_FollowRoute steps the route cursor on.

entries.name: Ai_FollowRoute
entries.description: Drives at the waypoint after the group's route cursor (Route_WaypointAt(group+0x04, index + 1)), stepping the cursor with Route_AdvanceCursor(group+0x04) when Ai_DriveToPoint reports arrival, and calling Mech_LocomotionTick(mech, 0, 0, 0) -- standing with the throttle at zero -- when there is no such waypoint. Callers of Route_AdvanceCursor found by es2_xref: this, Mech_BehaviourPlayerThink, Flyer_LeadRouteStep and GroundVehicle_LeaderSteer.

entries.name: Ai_KeepFormation
entries.description: Holds this machine's formation slot on the group leader (group+0x0c slot 0): the post is the leader's position through this machine's vtable +0x78 (Mech_ApplyFormationOffset), so the formation rotates with the leader, and dist is Math_GroundDistanceBetweenPoints to it. Under 2000: turn -((heading - leader heading) >> 6), speed 0. Otherwise, at or under 25000 with the leader's +0x28e outside [-25, 24] (unsigned +0x19 > 0x31): when |heading - leader heading| is under 0x2000 it takes the delta from the post into the leader's frame (the leader's Q14 matrix at +0x12, built from +0x0c when +0x32 is clear, first four shorts through Math_TransposeRotation2D and Math_Rotate2DPoint) and drives turn -((headingError >> 6) + (-lateral >> 5)), speed leader +0x28e + (-longitudinal >> 5); at 0x2000 or more it turns +-0x100 (0x100 when the error is under 1) at speed -0x100. Every other case steers (bearing to the post - heading) >> 6 at dist >> 7, or 0x100 from 25000.

entries.name: MechAi_StaticInitNoOp
entries.description: Static initialiser of the mech AI behaviour module (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7ad4, priority 0x20): a lone RET. It follows Ai_KeepFormation, the last of that module's Mech_Behaviour*/Ai_* functions, and precedes Mech_LoadResources (mechsys.cpp).

entries.name: Mech_LoadResources
entries.description: mechsys.cpp's resource-load sequence for the mech subsystem -- the mech-side twin of Base_LoadResources (00405fac). Resets the mech-type-slot table (memset &DAT_004a9d8c, 0xff, 0x55), then streams dat\mforms (string 'mforms' at 0049a46b, joined with the shared 'dat' folder-prefix helper ResourcePath_BuildFolderName): reads a 2-byte record count into DAT_004a9dec, allocates that many 28-byte vector elements (Rtl_VectorNew(..., 0x1c, count, ...) -- 7 (x,y) int16 pairs/formation, matching Formation_GetSlotOffset's stride), stores the vector pointer into g_MechFormationTable (g_MechFormationTable), then reads count*28 bytes straight from the file into the buffer. Afterwards loads the 7 mech texture groups (g_MechTextureGroupNames/g_MechTextureGroupSlots) via Resource_Load/BitmapArray_PackToAtlas, unrelated to formations. Auto-analysis does not disassemble it on its own: it sits directly after another function's RET with no call-graph edge, so it is found only by scanning for the 'mforms' string's address as a PUSH-immediate operand. Registered into DBSIM's subsystem-loader table via a thunk at 00420654 (RegisterSubsystemLoader(Mech_LoadResources, 2)), so the game runs it.

entries.name: maybe_MechTypeSlot_GetIndex
entries.description: Trivial accessor, returns (&DAT_004a9d8c)[param_1] -- a per-slot byte, 0xff sentinel meaning 'unused', otherwise the allocated dense index used by MechType_InitOne. Not independently cross-checked beyond its two callers (Mechs_InitAllTypes, MechTypeSlot_Allocate).

entries.name: maybe_MechTypeSlot_Allocate
entries.description: Assigns the next dense allocation index (DAT_004a9d8a, post-incremented) to slot param_1's (&DAT_004a9d8c)[param_1] entry the first time it's requested; on the very first allocation overall, also caches GunLayout_Reserve(1)'s result, the first gun-layout table slot, into _DAT_004a9df4. Not independently cross-checked beyond call-site usage.

entries.name: Shape_RemapTransformId
entries.description: (idRef, map): when the int16 at idRef is non-negative, replaces it with the signed byte map[*idRef] -- which is -1 for an id the map leaves unset. Shape_RemapTransformIds' per-field step.

entries.name: Shape_RemapTransformIds
entries.description: (part, map, nodeCount): rewrites the transform ids in a shape's part tree through a byte map, the remapping counterpart of Shape_StampTransformId with the same class-tag switch on vtable +0 (tags from the GetClassTag bodies). TSGroup (0x140014): Shape_RemapTransformId on part+4 and returns without visiting children. TSCellAnimPart (0x14000b): Shape_RemapTransformId on part+4, then the children. TSBSPPart (0x140015): each int16 of the per-node array at +0x1c (count ushort +0x16) that is above 0, below nodeCount and maps to a non-negative byte is remapped; then the children. TSPartList (0x140007), TSShape (0x140008), TSDetailPart (0x14000c) and ANShape (0x1e0003): the children. Children are the part-pointer array at +0x12, count ushort +0x10, recursed with the same map and count. TSPartBase (0x140005/0x140006) and any other tag: returns. MechType_RemapDetailRootTransforms calls it once per root after the first.

entries.name: MechType_RemapDetailRootTransforms
entries.description: (detailSet, partIds): renumbers every LOD root after the first into root 0's transform numbering. detailSet is the type record's root set at typeRec+0xde (root array +0, root count int16 +0xc); partIds is typeRec+0x30, bytes 46-65 of the mech .DAT. With more than one root: fills a 400-byte stack table (eight 50-byte rows, one per root 1-8) with 0xff; for each part id, up to 50 or the first negative byte, finds the part in root 0 through the root's vtable +0x20 (TSPartList_FindPart) and takes its transform id (part+4, read without a null check), then for each root L >= 1 finds the same part id and, when found, sets row L[that part's transform id] = root 0's transform id. Then Shape_RemapTransformIds(root L, row L, int16 +0x10 of root 0's +0x2a record) for each L >= 1, so a transform id whose row entry is still 0xff becomes -1 at a TSGroup or TSCellAnimPart. MechType_InitOne calls it at 004202b6, right after Shape_LoadAllRoots and the CONNECT_INFO allocation. Retail .DAT lists: 1,2,3,4,5,12-17 on most chassis; HEADHUNT adds 44, MONGOOSE 10,88,99, PITBULL 18-25, SPIDER 1-4,12,14,15,18-23, RAZOR 12; each -1-terminated within the 20 bytes.

entries.name: MechType_InitOne
entries.description: (type): loads one chassis into its slot's 0x21e-byte MECH_TYPE_DATA record in 004a9de8, the name from 004a9de4 and the slot from maybe_MechTypeSlot_GetIndex. Ovl_ReadFile reads 0xd8 bytes of dat\<name> into +2; the slot goes to +0 and the type to +0x6c. Shape_LoadAllRoots loads dts\<name> (tag 0x1e0003, skip 0) into +0xde, the count to +0xea, g_ShapeDetailThresholds to +0xe2 and an Rtl_VectorNew of count CONNECT_INFO_Ctor pairs to +0xe6; then MechType_RemapDetailRootTransforms(+0xde, +0x30). It copies +6 to +0xc8 and, when +0x50 is 0, stores Q10(0x13b, +6) at +0xc2 and multiplies +4, +6, +0x2e and +0x6e by Q16Divide(+0xc6 * 400, +0xc4). GunLayout_LoadForMechType(gl\<name>, slot + 004a9df4) and GunLayout_CollectHardpointBones, then per root MechType_BindHardpointSlots and root+0x26 = &g_MechTextureGroupSlots + (+0x96) * 8. PaperDoll_Load(name, slot) goes to +0xda. When +0x50 is set it reads 0x36 bytes of <name> in the folder at 0049a47e into +0x1dc and stores Q16Divide(+0x1fe - +0x202, +0x206 - +0x20a) at +0x1ea; when the name at +0xce is not empty, Debris_LoadDatabase(+0x212, +0xce, that texture slot).

entries.name: Mechs_InitAllTypes
entries.description: Creates the 'mechs' object pool (string xref confirmed) sized DAT_004a9d8a*0x21e (the MECH_TYPE_DATA record size), then loops mech-type slot 0..0x54 calling MechType_InitOne (004201a8) for every slot MechTypeSlot_GetIndex (0041ff00) reports as in-use (!= 0xff).

entries.name: Mechs_FreeAllTypes
entries.description: Tears down the mech-type table: Rtl_VectorDeleteCounted(004a9de8, 0x29, 0x21e, 0, 0x19, MECH_TYPE_DATA_Dtor) -- the exception-aware wrapper over Rtl_VectorDelete, mode 0x19 taking the count from the array's prefix -- then resets the 0x55-byte slot-index map 004a9d8c to 0xff and the allocated-type count 004a9d8a to 0, the same two resets Mech_LoadResources opens with. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Formation_GetSlotOffset
entries.description: Returns a static 3-short {x, y, 0} formation offset: table[formationId * 0x1c + slot * 4 - 4] and the short after it. So a formation is 28 bytes = seven (x, y) short pairs, covering follower slots 1-7. The table pointer g_MechFormationTable is written by Mech_LoadResources (0041fdb0), which reads dat\MFORMS.DAT -- 142 content bytes = count + five 28-byte formations, byte-exact.

entries.name: Mech_GetGunLayout
entries.description: GunLayout_GetBySlot(mechTypeRecord[0] + _DAT_004a9df4) -- this machine's hardpoint list. Its return value is what Mech_ConfigureLoadout hands MechLoadout_ConstructWeaponMounts as the record array and count.

entries.name: Mech_RegisterLoader
entries.description: Thunk that registers Mech_LoadResources (0041fdb0) into DBSIM's subsystem-loader table via RegisterSubsystemLoader(Mech_LoadResources, 2), then vector-constructs the mech-texture-group vector, 8 slots of 8 bytes (Rtl_VectorNew(&g_MechTextureGroupSlots, 8, 8, 1, ...)), of which Mech_LoadResources fills 7. Found by raw dword-scanning DBSIM.EXE for Mech_LoadResources' address used as a PUSH-immediate operand (68 B0 FD 41 00).

entries.name: ConfigPart_Ctor
entries.description: (part): CONFIG_PART's constructor: stamps the ClassItem, TSBase, TSPartBase and CONFIG_PART (0049a494) vtables in turn, counting three live destructors, and runs ShapeInstance_CtorCellFrames(part+0x10, 0) on the SHAPE_INST member; returns part. MECH_TYPE_DATA_Ctor runs it over the ten 0x18-byte config parts at typeRec+0xec, the blank records Mech_SpliceHardpointShapes falls back on.

entries.name: ConfigPart_GetClassTagZero
entries.description: CONFIG_PART vtable +0x00 (0049a494), kept by GUN_STATE and every weapon-mount class: returns 0, where TSPartBase answers a real class tag.

entries.name: ConfigPart_Dtor
entries.description: CONFIG_PART vtable +0x18 (0049a494, RTTI 'CONFIG_PART', 0x18 bytes; bases TSPartBase and SHAPE_INST at +0x10), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). HeapBlockOwner_Dtor(this+0x10, 0) on the SHAPE_INST, TSBase_Dtor(this, 0), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00420730; class record at 004206c9

entries.name: MechFormation_ElementCtor
entries.description: (formation): Rtl_VectorNew(formation, 4, 7, 1, Rtl_ReturnArgCopy) over its seven 4-byte (x, y) slot offsets, returning formation -- the per-element constructor Mech_LoadResources hands Rtl_VectorNew for the MFORMS.DAT table (PUSH at 0041fe43: 0x1c bytes each, count 004a9dec, stored to g_MechFormationTable).

entries.name: CONNECT_INFO_Ctor
entries.description: (info): CONNECT_INFO's constructor (6-byte class record at 004208e3, destructor CONNECT_INFO_Dtor, which decrements twice): zeroes the slot-array pointer at +0 and counts two live destructors. MechType_InitOne runs it through Rtl_VectorNew(buffer, 6, rootCount, 0x211, it) at 00420286 for the per-root {slots, count} pairs it stores at typeRec+0xe6 and MechType_BindHardpointSlots fills.

entries.name: MECH_TYPE_DATA_Ctor
entries.description: (data): MECH_TYPE_DATA's constructor: Rtl_VectorNew(data+0xec, 0x18, 10, 1, ConfigPart_Ctor), counts one live destructor, returns data. Mechs_InitAllTypes hands it to Rtl_VectorNew (PUSH at 004204f1) for the 0x21e-byte type records, count 004a9d8a, mode 0x211.

entries.name: MECH_TYPE_DATA_Dtor
entries.description: MECH_TYPE_DATA's destructor, the dtor its class record (0x21e bytes, at 00420937) names: (data, flags): when data is not null, decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr, Rtl_VectorDelete of the ten 0x18-byte config parts at +0xec with ConfigPart_Dtor, then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: CONNECT_INFO_Dtor
entries.description: CONNECT_INFO's destructor, the dtor its class record (0x6 bytes, at 004208e3) names: (info, flags): when info is not null, decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr twice, Mem_DeleteArray of the buffer at +0 when that is set, then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: ARRAY_TSPartBase_PtrPtr_Dtor
entries.description: ARRAY<TSPartBase * *>'s destructor, the dtor its class record (0x6 bytes, at 004209e3) names: (array, flags): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr; when the array is not null, Mem_DeleteArray of its buffer at +0 when that is set, then Mem_Delete of the array when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: Computer_PostMessage
entries.description: Posts a SYSTEM.STR message id to the cockpit computer's ticker -- the port at CockpitView+0x20b -- through its vtable slot 0, as a {short id, int subject} record with a null subject. The sibling for the pilot and squad channel is Ai_PostSquadMessage (00420a98).

entries.name: Ai_PostSquadMessage
entries.description: (machine, id, force): unless the machine's byte +0x99 is set and force is 0, posts {int16 id, machine} to the pilot-and-squad message port CockpitView_GetSquadMessagePort returns, through its vtable slot 0.

entries.name: Mech_ReceiveSquadOrder
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x28. One machine receiving one transmitted squad order: switches on the record's verb (STRINGS0 group 0, 0-0x11) over twelve jump-table arms covering sixteen verbs (6, 9 and anything above 0x11 take the default) and installs the standing order at mech+0x23e, its destination at +0x240, its target at +0x248, its guard subject at +0x24c and its abandon tier at +0x250. Verbs 0xd/0xe write patrol and move, 0/2/0xb write engage, 0xc writes guard; 3/0xa/0xf clear the order and reinstall patrolling; 4/0x10 and 7/0x11 are the radar pair, writing mech+0xb2 and mech+0x96; 5 and 8 are the FIRE AT WILL / HOLD YOUR FIRE pair, writing mech+0xb6; 1 sets the ignore-the-player's-selection latch at mech+0x9a, which 0, 5 and 0xb clear. Returns 1 when the order was taken. Each case picks a reply id for Ai_PostSquadMessage, posted only when priorReply is 0, or 1 with an accepted order. Args derived from disassembly: [EBP+8], [EBP+0xc], [EBP+0x10]; the vtable call site at 0043164d pushes three and does ADD ESP,0xc.

entries.name: Flyer_GetSpeed
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x38: Q10(1000, flyer+0x233), where +0x233 is the type record's +0x04 forward speed, copied in by Flyer_Constructor and never written again. A chassis constant, not anything the aircraft is doing.

entries.name: Flyer_FlushDeletes
entries.description: ObjectPool_FlushDeleteQueue(g_FlyerDeleteQueue (004a9e41), g_FlyerPool (004a9e3d)). Flyer_RegisterSubsystem registers it as the flyer module's subsystem phase-5 stub (PUSH 0x4215a8 at 00421fc2). It lies outside every Ghidra function.

entries.name: Flyer_HandleCommandNoOp
entries.description: FLYER vtable +0x2c: loads its second argument into AX, then XOR EAX,EAX and returns 0 without acting on it -- which is why the shield bracket keys do nothing in a RAZOR.

entries.name: Flyer_Draw
entries.description: (flyer): TSDetailPart_SetBias (004768ac)(the dword 004a9e48), Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel (004033e4)(flyer), TSDetailPart_SetBias(0). es2_xref finds its address in one vtable slot.

entries.name: Flyer_Constructor
entries.description: Flyer class constructor (flyer, FLYERS.NAM index). SimObjectBase_ConstructStatic with the type record's +0x36, then the block every ACTOR constructor writes: SimObjectBaseVtable, +0x1a8 = 0xffff, +0x98 = 1, +0xa7 = 1, ObjectList_Add, +0x1b2 and +0x1b6 = 0, +0x1ba, +0x1bc and +0x1be = 0xffff. Installs FlyerVtable (0049a5e0) and allocates the component-damage header at flyer+0x200 with literal counts of 1 and 1 (one main component, one dependent -- exactly what SKIMMER.DMG ships). Stores the type record at flyer+0x1fa, sets +0x1a8 = 2, zeroes +0x231 and +0x235, copies the record's +0x04 into +0x233, and links the record's .DMG and .COL pointers (+0x2e, +0x32) via Component_LinkMaxRefData. Installs the deciding state, Behaviour_SetState(flyer+0x4d, 00499cf8).
