Seeds the flight block at +0x243: zeroes its 0x4e bytes, points +0x263 at the euler angles (+0x0c), builds the object's rotation matrix if +0x32 is clear, copies it to +0x267 and transposes it, rotates the negated position through it into +0x27b, and sets +0x247 = 1000 (airspeed) and +0x261 = 0x200 (throttle). Steps the RTL constructor counter at [006cbf74] twice. The stores it makes are the ones listed; its own body writes none of +0x1f4, +0x1f8, +0x21c or +0x23c.

entries.name: Flyer_DispatchMove
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x14, the one reference es2_xref finds (FlyerVtable). Reads the behaviour descriptor at flyer+0x4d and calls its +0x24 move triple as (*func)(flyer + thisDelta), returning that call's EAX; when all three dwords of the triple are zero it returns 0 without calling. It also copies the flyer's position (+0x26, 12 bytes) to the stack first, a leftover the dispatch ignores. The flyer twin of Behaviour_DispatchMove.

entries.name: Flyer_DispatchThink
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x18; es2_xref finds that slot as its one reference. Reads the behaviour descriptor pointer at flyer+0x4d and its think triple at descriptor+0x18/+0x1c/+0x20. When all three dwords are zero it returns 0; otherwise it calls the +0x18 function with flyer plus the +0x1c this-adjustment and returns the callee's EAX, with the OR of the three dwords still in ECX.

entries.name: Flyer_DispatchReassess
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x1c; es2_xref finds that slot as its one reference. Reads the behaviour descriptor pointer at flyer+0x4d and its reassess triple at descriptor+0x30/+0x34/+0x38. When all three dwords are zero it returns 0; otherwise it calls the +0x30 function with flyer plus the +0x34 this-adjustment and returns the callee's EAX. The OR of the three dwords is left in ECX across the call; every flyer state that has a reassess carries {Flyer_AiSelectBehaviour (00422d00), 0, 0}, so ECX holds 00422d00, which Flyer_AiSelectBehaviour's no-case path hands Behaviour_SetState as its descriptor.

entries.name: Flyer_MovementTick
entries.description: The flyer's per-tick move, the +0x24 slot of the four behaviour states that have one. Rebuilds the rotation matrix at +0x12 from the euler triple at +0x0c (BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14) when the flag at +0x32 is clear, and sets the flag. Adds the world velocity at flyer+0x24f to the position at +0x26 RAW -- three plain ADDs at 0042190a, with no Math_IntegrateRateOverTick, so a flyer's world velocity is a per-tick step where Razor_MovementTick's is a rate. Then four probes, each a body-frame point placed by Transform_ApplyToPoint through the transform at +0x12, which is not rebuilt between them, and compared with Terrain_HeightQuery; where the ground is above the point by d: the wingtip (1000,-420,-300) subtracts Q10(4000,d) from the roll rate +0x25d and the wingtip (-1000,-420,-300) adds it, then roll +0x0e += roll rate; the nose (0,1000,0) and the look-ahead (0,15000,-1500) first zero a negative pitch rate +0x25b, add Q10(2000,d) and Q10(20,d) to it respectively, then pitch +0x0c += pitch rate; each contact clears +0x32. Then sets the origin's Z to terrain + 500 when it is lower. While the airspeed +0x247 is positive it measures Math_FastMagnitude3D to ViewObjectPtr's position: under 30000 with the latch +0x06 clear it calls Sound_Play(0x31), flyby1.wav, whose loop count is 1, and sets the latch; at 30000 or more it clears the latch. Returns 1 in AX. It reads +0x1fa into a local it never uses, does no damage, sweeps no objects and tests no wrecked flag.

entries.name: Flyer_ComponentDamageWrite
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x74, (flyer, component, damage, attacker). Points DAT_004a96e4 at the flight block's world velocity for the length of the call, so debris the cascade throws inherits it, then Component_ApplyDamageAndCascade on the header at flyer+0x200. When that cascaded and the component is 0: with an attacker, posts 0x2e if the attacker is LocalPlayerMech and the flyer its +0x1a4 target, and credits the attacker through its +0x60; then sets +0x99, clears the scanner, sets +0x38, writes -100000 to the world Z (+0x2e), runs Mech_ReportOutOfAction, activates the defeat action, installs behaviour state 00499e60, and stops sound 0x31 when +6 says it is playing, clearing +6. Nothing in it tests +0x99 first.

entries.name: Flyer_DirectFireHitTest
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x20. Returns 0 at once while the spectator flag DAT_0049ef5c is set and this flyer is ViewChain_Viewed. Coarse reject on vtable +0x10 shape radius + ray[+8] + ray length, then Mech_SelectStruckComponent against the type's .COL model (flyerTypeRec+0x32) with the active flags at +0x208. On a hit: draws an effect from the shot's third impact array (shot+0xa entries 8-11, rand & 3) before anything else, calls vtable +0x74(component, armour damage, shot owner), then if +0x99 is now set swaps in effect 10 and debris group 3 for the ordinary group 1. Spawns the effect with no owner and throws the debris group from the point at distance + 1 down the ray, and returns that distance. No shields and no collision volume.

entries.name: Flyer_GetOverallDamage
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x40: Component_ReadOverallDamage on the health header at flyer+0x200.

entries.name: Flyer_ApplyFormationOffset
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x78; es2_xref finds that slot as its one reference. (flyer, point): no-ops when the word at flyer+0x49, the member's formation slot, is 0 (the flight leader); otherwise takes the three int16 FlyerFormation_GetSlotOffset (00423044) resolves out of dat/FFORMS.DAT for (group+0x02 formation id, that slot), sign-extends them to ints and hands them to Formation_RotateAndAddOffset (00411d64), which rotates them by the GROUP LEADER's rotation and adds them to the point. Unlike a mech's or a base's, the offset carries a Z, which is what stacks a flight vertically.

entries.name: Flyer_AttachToGroup
entries.description: Attaches a flyer to its mission group: stores the group at flyer+0x45 and the member index at +0x49; with flyer+0x0c holding the -0x8000 sentinel takes the group's heading and zeroes pitch and roll; with the Z position holding the sentinel takes the group's own point (the one group+0x18 points at, else Route_WaypointAt on the group's route at its cursor, group+4), applies the formation offset through vtable +0x78, and finally substitutes 5000 for a Z that came out zero.

entries.name: Flyer_RegisterSubsystem
entries.description: Static-init registrar of the flyer module (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7ae0, priority 0x20): registers Flyer_FlushDeletes at subsystem phase 5, nulls g_FlyerPool (004a9e3d) and counts one live destructor. Flyer_StaticDtor is its _EXIT_ counterpart.

entries.name: Flyer_StaticDtor
entries.description: Flyer_RegisterSubsystem's _EXIT_ routine (Borland _EXIT_ entry 004a7c18): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr and Mem_Deletes g_FlyerPool when it is set.

entries.name: SimObject_SetRunInto
entries.description: Vtable +0x68 in eight SimObject-shaped tables -- base, mech, flyer and the five structure classes; es2_xref finds those eight slots and no branch to it. Two instructions: obj+0xb1 = 1, "something ran into me", written as ADD EAX,0x92 then byte [EAX+0x1f], so a scalar search for 0xb1 misses it. A grep of the disassembly for indirect CALL [reg+0x68] finds two calls on sim objects, both collision sweeps calling it on whatever object blocked the move, whatever its class: Mech_CollisionTest (0041903a) and GroundVehicle_CollisionTest (0046a581), the sweep inside the ground vehicle tick; the grep's third hit (00417fdf) is Mech_ComponentDamageWrite calling a component's vtable. es2_fieldscan b1 finds one reader on a sim object, Mech_BehaviourRamTick (0041e500, rebased the same way), and no write besides this one (ai-combat-states.md, The charge).

entries.name: ObjPool_FLYER_Dtor
entries.description: ObjPool<FLYER>'s destructor, the dtor its class record (0x8 bytes, at 0042201d) names: (pool, flags): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr; when the pool is not null, Mem_Delete of its entry buffer at +0 when that is set, then Mem_Delete of the pool when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: Flyer_PitchCommand
entries.description: (flyer, desiredPitch): the elevator command that holds a pitch attitude. Q16(desiredPitch - pitch +0x0c, 1500), put through Math_Q14Multiply with Math_CosBam(roll +0x0e) and sign-extended from 16 bits, less Q16(pitch rate +0x25b, 8000); returns the 32-bit difference in EAX. es2_xref finds two callers, Flyer_PitchToAltitude and Flyer_AttackRun.

entries.name: Flyer_PitchToAltitude
entries.description: Elevator command that flies the aircraft to a world Z: Math_Atan2Guarded(10000, targetZ - flyer.z) into Flyer_PitchCommand. The 10000 is a fixed horizontal run, so the demanded angle depends on the height error alone. When the base object's +0xae is set it asks instead for the current pitch (+0x0c) plus Math_Q8Multiply(flyer+0x23c, 4000), ignoring the target Z. +0xae is a walking machine's unstick-reverse flag; es2_fieldscan finds it written only by Mech_LocomotionTick and Mech_MovementTick. flyer+0x23c is a Flyer field (a mech's +0x23c is a different field of another class); es2_fieldscan and a raw disp32 sweep of the code section find this read and no write of it in flyer code.

entries.name: Flyer_CommandRoll
entries.description: Fills the command array's aileron element with Q16(desiredRoll - flyer.roll, 2500) + Q16(rollRate, -5000) and runs Flyer_ApplyFlightCommand. The arm Flyer_SteerAndFly takes whenever it is holding or limiting a bank rather than commanding one.

entries.name: Flyer_ApplyFlightCommand
entries.description: Hand-off into FlightModel_Step (00466a54). Squares the aileron and elevator elements with their sign kept ((v*v)>>8) and clamps them to +/-0x100, then calls the model with the flyer's flight block at +0x243, the .FM record at typeRecord+0x3a, and a stack array of four zeros as the wing-damage argument, which is why a Flyer never takes the model's lost-wing or lost-nacelle arms.

entries.name: Flyer_FormationThrottle
entries.description: A wingman's speed correction: (flyer, leader, stationDistance, steeringCommand, slack). Adds (Q14(stationDistance, cos(steeringCommand + own heading - leader heading)) - slack) >> 1 and (leader+0x233 - flyer+0x233) * 8 to flyer+0x21c, clamps the sum to [0x8c,0x100] and stores it back. Flyer_FormationStep passes the bearing to the station less own heading as the steering command and 0x2000 as the slack, so unless it mirrored the command the Q14 product is how far the station lies ahead of the wingman along the leader's heading. +0x233 is the type record's forward speed, copied in by Flyer_Constructor. Leaves the unclamped sum in AX. es2_fieldscan and a raw disp32 sweep of the code section find no reader of flyer+0x21c in flyer code but this one.

entries.name: Flyer_SteerAndFly
entries.description: (flyer, turn, elevator, leader): the flyer's steering channel, and the function es2_xref finds called by every movement step (Flyer_LeadRouteStep, Flyer_FormationStep, Flyer_AttackRun). The bank command is a 16-bit sum Q16(-turn, 2500) + Q16(r, 32000) + Q16(roll rate +0x25d, -5000), where r is the bank heading rate at flyer+0x287, less Q16(Math_Q14Multiply(leader+0x1f8, Math_CosBam(own heading +0x10 - leader heading +0x10)), 200) when a leader is passed. It fills a five-int command array: [1] the elevator argument, [2] rudder 0, [3] throttle 0, [4] Terrain_HeightQuery under the aircraft, FlightModel_Step's ceiling reference. With maxBank the type record's +0x0e (record pointer at +0x1fa): roll +0x0e at or above maxBank - 1500 with a positive bank command calls Flyer_CommandRoll(maxBank); at or below -(maxBank - 1500) with a negative one, Flyer_CommandRoll(-maxBank). Otherwise a turn whose magnitude (0x7fff for -0x8000) is under 2000 sets the rudder to Q16(-turn, 4000) when the roll is under 800, signed, and calls Flyer_CommandRoll(0) either way; anything larger puts the bank command in [0], zeroes the rudder and calls Flyer_ApplyFlightCommand. es2_fieldscan, a decompile grep and a raw disp32 sweep of the code section find no writer of +0x1f8, and the flyer pool is zero-filled (ai-flyers.md, Open).

entries.name: Flyer_LeadRouteStep
entries.description: The flight leader's route step. Takes Route_WaypointAt(group+0x04 cursor, index + 1); when there is one it steers at it and calls Route_AdvanceCursor when Math_GroundDistanceBetweenPoints puts it within 15000; when there is none it steers at Route_WaypointAt(cursor, index) without advancing, and when that is null too the null point goes to Math_HeadingToward. Elevator Flyer_PitchToAltitude(30000); steering Q16(Math_HeadingToward(waypoint, position) - heading +0x10, 28000), through Flyer_SteerAndFly with no leader; then writes 0xb4 to the formation throttle word flyer+0x21c.

entries.name: Flyer_FormationStep
entries.description: A wingman's station-keeping. The leader is the group's first member; the station is the leader's position offset 0x2000 along the leader's heading, plus the formation offset the flyer's vtable +0x78 adds. The steering command is the bearing to the station less own heading, mirrored (-0x8000 - err) rather than reversed when the wingman is ahead of its station (command outside +/-0x4000) while its heading is within 0x4000 of the leader's and the station is inside 10000. Holds altitude 30000 through Flyer_PitchToAltitude, then Flyer_SteerAndFly with the leader as its fourth argument. With the station inside 15000 it calls Flyer_FormationThrottle(flyer, leader, distance, steering command, 0x2000) and ignores its return; farther out it writes 0x100 to flyer+0x21c.

entries.name: Flyer_AttackRun
entries.description: The attack run, and the only place a Cybrid flyer shoots. A two-phase circuit on flyer+0x1fe: phase 0 extends AWAY from the target holding targetZ+10000 until the range passes 90000, phase 1 runs in and inside 65000 aims at the target itself, breaking off again when the bearing leaves +/-0x2000, the height over the target drops under 3000, or the range closes inside 10000. The aim is led along the target's heading by (range>>3)*(targetSpeed*8)/shotSpeed, where shotSpeed becomes PROJ.DAT row 2's speed once the run is close enough to shoot. While running in, a set base-object +0xae swaps the pitch onto the target for Flyer_PitchToAltitude(0). Firing needs phase 1 inside 65000, bearing error and pitch error (elevation to the aim point less flyer+0x0c) both in [-1000, 999], the short at flyer+0x1f4 in [-10, 9] -- the same (ushort)(x + k) < 2k test as the two angle errors -- and Math_CountdownTimerTick on the CountdownTimer record at flyer+0x21e returning 0. The record's counter is the short at flyer+0x21f; the tick is the last test of the && chain, so the countdown steps only on ticks that pass the other gates. While the flyer+0x5a flag is clear and the range is inside 30000 the shot is Rocket_Fire(0) off the (500,200,-100) muzzle and sets the flag, otherwise it is a pair of Bullet_Fire(2) off that point and its mirror; either stores 1500 into the counter at flyer+0x21f. While flyer+0x1fe is under 2, which both values this function stores are, the call ends by reloading flyer+0x21c with 0xb4 and handing the bearing error and the pitch command to Flyer_SteerAndFly.

entries.name: Flyer_ClearFormationThrottle
entries.description: Takes one argument, the flyer, zeroes its +0x21c (the accumulator Flyer_FormationThrottle folds into) and returns 0: the shape of a behaviour think that reports not finished. es2_xref finds no rel32 branch, stored pointer or vtable slot holding its address; the same sweep finds the sibling think Flyer_BehaviourScoutThink through its slot block at 00499f50. Its PUSH EBP follows Flyer_AttackRun's RET and two NOP fill bytes, so its entry is not late.

entries.name: Flyer_FollowStep
entries.description: The movement step the three non-combat flyer thinks (search and destroy, patrolling, scouting) open with: Flyer_LeadRouteStep when the flyer is the group's first member (group+0x0c [0]), Flyer_FormationStep otherwise, then flyer+0x96 (the radar mode) = 0.

entries.name: Flyer_BehaviourSearchDestroyThink
entries.description: search and destroy's think. Flyer_FollowStep; then, for the group's first member only, Math_CountdownTimerTick on the record at flyer+0x5a (the 16-bit count at +0x5b). When that reads 0 it stores 10000 there and sweeps: Ai_SelectTarget mask 0x11 (restrict the designated bonus, reject own class), cone 0. A non-null result that Group_IsOrderTarget accepts becomes the target -- obj+0x1a4, decrementing the old target's +0x1a2 holder count and incrementing the new one's, and setting +0x9d, when it differs -- and Flyer_EngageWithFlight runs. Returns 0. Behaviour_SetState zeroes +0x5a..+0x81 at every state change, so the count is 0 on the state's first tick (ai-flyers.md, The thinks).

entries.name: Flyer_BehaviourPatrolThink
entries.description: patrolling's think. The same shape as Flyer_BehaviourSearchDestroyThink with mask 0x10 (reject own class) and no Group_IsOrderTarget test: the sweep's result, null included, becomes the target with the same holder-count and +0x9d bookkeeping, and Flyer_EngageWithFlight runs when the target is non-null afterwards. Returns 0.

entries.name: Flyer_BehaviourScoutThink
entries.description: scouting's think: Flyer_FollowStep, then returns 0.

entries.name: Flyer_EngageWithFlight
entries.description: Puts the whole flight onto the leader's target. Installs the attacking descriptor (00499d34) on itself with Behaviour_SetState; then, when it is the group's first member, walks the member array group+0x0c up to the count at group+0x10, stopping at the first null entry, and for every other member whose +0x99 is clear copies its own target into the member's +0x1a4 when they differ (decrementing the old target's +0x1a2 holder count, incrementing the new one's, setting the member's +0x9d) and recurses into the member. The recursion ends there because a member that is not the first does not take the loop.

entries.name: Flyer_BehaviourAttackThink
entries.description: attacking's think. Returns finished as soon as the target is immobilised (+0xa4) or destroyed (+0x99), which zeroes the dwell and sends the aircraft back through the reassess; otherwise Flyer_AttackRun for the flight leader and Flyer_FormationStep for everyone else.

entries.name: Flyer_AiSelectBehaviour
entries.description: The reassess slot of the five flyer states that have one (sleeping and dead carry a null triple): maps the group's current order verb onto a descriptor. The order is group+0x44 + 4 * group+0x6c; a null slot reads as verb 0xb. 0 -> search and destroy (00499dac), 3 -> patrolling (00499d70), 4 -> sleeping (00499de8), 5 -> scouting (00499e24); 4 and 5 also latch flyer+0xa5, the out-of-the-fight byte. Any other verb -- 1, 2, 6, or the 0xb of an empty slot -- matches no case and leaves ECX unwritten, so Behaviour_SetState is handed ECX as Flyer_DispatchReassess left it: the OR of the reassess triple, which is 00422d00, this function's own address. Returns 1 in AX.

entries.name: Flyer_LoadResources
entries.description: The flyer subsystem's loader (flyersys.cpp). Resets the 0x22-entry type-slot table at 004a9e50 to 0xff, then opens dat/fforms, reads a 2-byte record count into DAT_004a9e7c and count*0x12 bytes of formation records into the vector at DAT_004a9e80.

entries.name: FlyerType_RecordIndex
entries.description: Maps a FLYERS.NAM index to its slot in the loaded type-record array, out of the 0x22-entry table at DAT_004a9e50. 0xff means the type is not loaded.

entries.name: FlyerType_Register
entries.description: Claims a type-record slot for a FLYERS.NAM index the mission needs, if it has none yet, bumping the loaded-type count at DAT_004a9e4e.

entries.name: FlyerType_LoadResources
entries.description: Per-flyer-type resource load into a 0x70-byte type record: the dat/<NAME>.DAT stats over the record's first 0x2e bytes, the shape, the .dmg component file (+0x2e), the col/<NAME>.COL hit-sphere model via Collision_RegisterObject (+0x32, which is what the flyer's own vtable +0x20 Flyer_DirectFireHitTest passes to Mech_SelectStruckComponent), and the fm/<NAME>.FM flight model (+0x3a, 0x36 bytes) whose ceiling slope it derives into +0x48. It also binds the shape's texture bank by writing the LITERAL slot address 0x004a9e0e into TSShapeInstance+0x26 -- g_MechTextureGroupSlots + 3*8, texture group 3 (ENEMY) -- so every flyer type shares one bank rather than choosing per chassis the way MechType_InitOne does.

entries.name: FlyerTypes_LoadAll
entries.description: When the flyer type count 004a9e4e is non-zero: 004a9e74 = LoadNameList('flyers', 0x22), 004a9e78 = Rtl_VectorNew of that many 0x70-byte records (element ctor 00423098), then FlyerType_LoadResources for each of the 0x22 name indices whose FlyerType_RecordIndex is not 0xff. DBSim_LoadScriptDat calls it.

entries.name: FlyerFormation_GetSlotOffset
entries.description: dat/FFORMS.DAT slot lookup: DAT_004a9e80 + formationId*0x12 + slot*6 - 6. Three follower slots per formation, three int16 each (x, y, z), and the slot index is one-based: the flight leader takes no offset.

entries.name: FlyerSys_RegisterSubsystem
entries.description: Static-init registrar of flyersys.cpp (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7ae6, priority 0x20): its whole body is RegisterSubsystemLoader(Flyer_LoadResources, 2).

entries.name: FlyerFormation_ElementCtor
entries.description: (formation): Rtl_VectorNew(formation, 6, 3, 1, maybe_Point3S_Ctor) over its three 6-byte (x, y, z) slot offsets, returning formation -- the per-element constructor Flyer_LoadResources hands Rtl_VectorNew for the FFORMS.DAT records (0x12 bytes each; PUSH at 00422e21).

entries.name: FlyerType_ElementCtor
entries.description: (record): returns its argument -- the per-element constructor FlyerTypes_LoadAll hands Rtl_VectorNew for the 0x70-byte flyer type records (PUSH at 00422fdd, count 004a9e4e); the LEA of +0x3a is an inlined empty member constructor.

entries.name: ActionTimer_Tick
entries.description: One script.dat block-6 action timer per frame -- the second of the four ways a mission action activates. Counts the countdown at timer+0x2c down through Timer_CountDown, in the simulation's timer unit, but only while the primary action at timer+0x00 is null or has activated (its +0x0a set), so a timer naming none runs from mission start. When the countdown reads 0 it calls Action_Activate on each non-null one of the ten action pointers at timer+0x04..+0x28 and re-arms the countdown through ActionTimer_SetDelay with 30000, which is 30,000 seconds, about 8.3 hours -- so a timer effectively activates once. This is why an action carrying no trigger area of its own is ordinary rather than dead.

entries.name: DBSim_BuildActionTimerRecord
entries.description: (record, primary, refs, delay): builds one in-memory block-6 action timer from pointers already resolved into the block-5 array: the primary action at +0x00, the ten fired actions copied from refs to +0x04..+0x28, and the delay short stored at +0x2c through ActionTimer_SetDelay.

entries.name: Route_AdvanceCursor
entries.description: (cursor): steps a route cursor -- a {short index; waypoint-group ptr} pair such as a group's at group+0x04 -- by one, and wraps the index back to zero when the route closes on itself (more than one waypoint, the new index is the last, and the last waypoint's point pointer is the same object as the first's). It writes the index only; the waypoint-group pointer at cursor+0x02 is read. A closed route is a patrol that never ends.

entries.name: Route_NextWaypointClosesRoute
entries.description: Answers 1 when the waypoint after a route cursor is both the route's last and the same point object as its first -- the duplicate a closed patrol circuit ends on, and the one Route_AdvanceCursor would wrap straight off. The one caller es2_xref finds is Mech_BehaviourPlayerThink (0041c1ee); it is what stops a circuit announcing its start point over and over.

entries.name: Squad_BroadcastOrder
entries.description: The MFD FLASH COMM page's transmit: sends one order to the whole of the player's group, best-suited machine first. Each pass scores every member not yet told -- verbs 0/2/5 prefer a machine whose behaviour descriptor +0x09 (committed) is clear, 1/8/0xf one where it is set, 4 and 7 one not already in the radar mode being asked for -- keeps the highest score and breaks ties on range to the issuer, then calls that machine's vtable +0x28 with the reply so far, so only the first recipient or the first to accept says anything. Verbs 0 and 2 stop at the first acceptance; the rest go round until everyone has been told. The score local is not initialised, so for a verb with no case every member carries the same leftover stack value ([EBP-0x1c]): range order when it is -1 or more, nobody told when it is below. Args derived from disassembly: [EBP+8], [EBP+0xc].

entries.name: TriggerArea_Resolve
entries.description: Load-time resolve of one script.dat block-4 (row #9) record into the 10-byte trigger-area record TriggerArea_ContainsPoint reads: the record's first word, the type flag, at +0; a pointer to the block-1 coordinate its second word indexes at +2; and at +6 either a pointer to the coordinate its third word indexes (type 0) or that word sign-extended (MOVSX) and multiplied by 10 (any other type), the radius.

entries.name: TriggerArea_ContainsPoint
entries.description: Tests a position against one resolved block-4 trigger area; returns 1 inside, 0 outside. Type flag 0: axis-aligned XY box strictly between the two block-1 coordinates the record points at (+0x02 and +0x06), taking the smaller and the larger of the two on each axis, so either corner order works; Z ignored. Non-zero type flag: Math_GroundDistanceBetweenPoints from the coordinate at +0x02 less than the int at +0x06, the radius (TriggerArea_Resolve stores the file literal times 10 there).

entries.name: Action_Activate
entries.description: Activates one block-5 mission action, once: sets the action runtime activation flag at +0x0a (zeroed at load), then walks ten (counter ref, operation) pairs at +0x0c/+0x20, skipping a pair whose ref is negative and otherwise bumping (op 6) or clearing (op 5) the mission counter array DAT_004a9ef4. The queue of the mission message at +0x34 is INSIDE that loop, so an action naming five counters posts its line five times and one naming none posts it not at all.

entries.name: Action_TestTrigger
entries.description: Tests a position against one action's trigger areas. Returns 1 immediately if the action has already activated (+0x0a set); otherwise offers the position to each resolved block-4 area (count at +0x04, pointer array at +0x06) via TriggerArea_ContainsPoint and calls Action_Activate on the first hit.

entries.name: Action_TestTriggerForGroup
entries.description: Action_TestTrigger applied to every member of a group in turn (member array at group+0x0c, count at group+0x10), stopping at the first that activates it, and returning that member's answer, else the last member's 0. The answer is kept at [EBP-2], the high half of the ECX pushed at entry as the local's slot, which only the loop writes, so a group with no members returns whatever ECX held.

entries.name: Deployment_PickPointNearPlayer
entries.description: Picks a clear arrival point for a deploying group or drop pod. Starts from LocalPlayerMech's position, Z included, so the point carries the player's height rather than the ground's, and adds (0, distance) rotated by (player heading +0x10 + bearing); each failed try adds 2000 to the distance and tries again along the same ray. A point must clear three tests in order. (1) Already-deployed objects on the live-object list, within their own vtable +0x7c collision radius plus 5000 by Math_DistanceBetweenPoints, skipping an object whose group +0x14 is set or whose radius is 0 -- APPLIED ONLY WHEN avoidDeployedObjects IS NONZERO; Group_DeploymentCheck, read this session, passes 1 for the two walk-on verbs and 0 for a drop pod, so a pod may come down on top of a machine. (2) Structure_GatherWalkCandidates at the point, radius 5000. (3) Terrain_FaceBlocksAt with a zero direction, which reduces to the steepness of the face under the point. The loop is unbounded. Terrain_FaceBlocksAt finds the cell by flat index, so a point past the grid's west or east edge reads a cell of the neighbouring row and can clear, which puts the arrival off the heightmap, past the end of the drawn terrain, while a point past the north or south end falls outside the array and blocks; since the player stands on the grid, every later try lies further out on the same ray, and a search that has run off the north or south end does not return.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Deployment_PickPointNearPlayer(int *outPoint, int distance, short bearing, int avoidDeployedObjects)

entries.name: Group_DeploymentCheck
entries.description: Per-frame arrival check for a mission group that has not entered the world yet; Sim_MainTick (0045f6d0) calls it instead of Group_OrderTick for a group whose +0x14 action pointer is non-null. No-ops until that action's runtime activation flag (action+0x0a) is set. Then the action verb (action+0x02) picks the arrival. 2 or 3: once only, latched by group+0x13 whether or not the pod is built, a METEOR drop pod (Pool_Alloc from g_MeteorPool, Meteor_Construct with the group) aimed 150000 units from the player at bearing 0x4000 - (rand & 0x7fff) for 2 (+-90 deg) or 0x1000 - (rand & 0x1fff) for 3 (+-22.5 deg), leaving +0x14 set for the pod to clear on landing. 4 or 5: the group leader goes to a point 90000 units away at bearing 0x9000 - (rand & 0x1fff) (behind, +-22.5 deg) for 4, or 150000 at 0x2000 - (rand & 0x3fff) (ahead, +-45 deg) for 5, with heading bearing - 0x8000 and its matrix flag +0x32 cleared; every other member gets a copy of the point through its own vtable +0x78 formation offset as its position, its heading untouched; +0x14 is cleared. Any other verb just clears +0x14, so the group goes live where it stands. The bearings are relative to the player's heading in Deployment_PickPointNearPlayer, which the pod passes 0 and the walk-on verbs 1 as its avoid-deployed-objects flag; draws use Math_RandomNext(0x4d261d).

entries.name: Group_OrderTargetObject
entries.description: The object the group's current order names -- the first member of the group it holds (+0xc == 0), read without checking that group has a member, or the object directly (1-3); 0 for no current order or another subject kind.

entries.name: Group_OrderTargetPosition
entries.description: The position the group's current order works to: the order object's +0x26 origin, falling back to the first waypoint of the group's route (**(*(group+6)+2)), read with no null check, when the slot is empty or names no subject.

entries.name: Group_IsOrderTarget
entries.description: Whether an object is what the group's current order names: for the order's +0xc == 0 the order holds a group and the test is group identity, for 1-3 it holds the object itself.

entries.name: Group_OrderSubjectPtr
entries.description: (group): the current order's +0x0e subject pointer -- the row-15 link at group+0x44 indexed by group+0x6c -- read without testing the slot for null. es2_xref finds no rel32 branch or stored pointer to it.

entries.name: Group_NearestLiveMember
entries.description: (group, obj): the member of group (array +0xc, count +0x10) nearest obj by Math_DistanceBetweenPoints, skipping obj itself and any member with destroyed (+0x99) or immobilised (+0xa4) set; 0 when none is nearer than 100000.

entries.name: Group_IsOrderComplete
entries.description: Whether a mission group's current order is finished, switched on the order's verb (order+0x00). Verb 0: the order subject's condition tier is 4 (destroyed). Verb 2: the order names a subject and either its tier is 4 or Group_NoRivalOrderOnSubject reports nothing hostile still assigned to it. Verbs 3, 5 and 6: the group's route cursor has no waypoint after the current index. Verbs 1 and 4 never complete and can only be ended by the order's action firing.

entries.name: Group_OrderTick
entries.description: Per-frame tick for a group that has entered the mission (the branch Sim_MainTick takes when group+0x14 is null). Runs the group's current order -- the row-15 link at group+0x44 indexed by the current-order index at group+0x6c -- and advances to the next when Group_IsOrderComplete reports it complete or its own action has activated, flagging the finished order in the byte array at group+0x70 and clearing each member's +0x52. Then ticks every member via Mech_AiTick.

entries.name: Route_WaypointAt
entries.description: Reads one waypoint out of a route cursor: null when the cursor has no waypoint group or the index is past its count, otherwise the resolved block-1 point at that index. Every 'is there a waypoint after this one' test in the AI is a call to this with index+1.

entries.name: DBSim_BuildGroupRecord
entries.description: Builds one script.dat block-11 record (arg 2, the 156-byte record as read) into a 0x7a-byte in-memory group record (arg 1). From the record: discriminator +0x28 to group+0, formation id +0x2a to group+2, side byte +0x6e to group+0x12, and the ten out-of-action (counter, operation) pairs from +0x72/+0x86 to group+0x1c/+0x30. From the other arguments: heading (arg 5) to group+0xa, resolved row-10 action pointer (arg 3) to group+0x14, resolved block-1 point pointer (arg 6) to group+0x18, and the ten resolved order pointers (arg 4) to group+0x44; when the first is non-null, the route cursor gets index 0 at group+4 and slot 0's route pointer (order+8) at group+6. Zeroes group+0x13, +0x6c and the ten bytes at +0x70. Counts the non-negative entries of the 20 member refs at +0x32 into group+0x10, allocates that many pointers at group+0xc, and fills them in order by discriminator through Pool_Nth -- 0 from GlobalMechList (004a9bfe) with Mech_AttachToGroup, 1 from g_FlyerPool (004a9e3d) with Flyer_AttachToGroup, 2 from g_StructurePool (004a9624) with Base_AttachToGroup, which also gets the record's +0x00 paints-ground flag -- passing each the member's slot index among the 20, not its packed index. No other record field is read, record +0x02 (.MSN row 16 +0x08) among them.

entries.name: MissionGroups_Allocate
entries.description: (array, count): array+4 = int16 count; array+0 = Rtl_VectorNew(0, 0x7a, count, 1, 004240e4), count 0x7a-byte group records. es2_xref finds one call, in DBSim_LoadScriptDat (00424dec), on MissionGroups (004a9e84) with block 11's record count.

entries.name: Group_WriteStatusBlocks
entries.description: (group, stream) Per member in group order: Mech_ReadDamageReadouts into a 42-short buffer, then entries 1-13, 20-29 and 32-41 each written as ((0x100 - r) * 100) SAR 8, then the 6 bytes at mech+0x2a4 -- the member's Herc, Structure and Flyer kill tallies. 72 bytes a member; VSHELL reads the 66 over the machine's status block and the 6 as the pilot's mission counters.

entries.name: Mission_TotalSalvage
entries.description: Sums Mech_SalvageValue over every object on the other side from the player's that is destroyed (+0x99) or immobilised (+0xa4). The second argument, the objective selector Mission_WriteResults passes, is not read. Called once as the mission writes its results; the total is scaled by Q10(2500) into the campaign salvage pool.

entries.name: Group_ApplyOutnumberedDamage
entries.description: (group): Mech_ApplyOutnumberedDamage on each member of the group's member array (+0xc, int16 count +0x10). Sim_MainTick runs it on the player's group (player+0x45) when Mission_PollStatus answers 3, and raises status 18 instead when the player is destroyed (+0x99) afterwards.

entries.name: Group_ReportIfAllOutOfAction
entries.description: Walks a mission group's member list (group+0xc, count group+0x10) skipping one nominated member; if every other member is immobilised (+0xa4) or destroyed (+0x99) it runs the group's own 10 mission-variable slots (indices at group+0x1c, opcodes at group+0x30) against DAT_004a9ef4 with the opcode set Mech_ReportOutOfAction uses: 1 zeroes the slot, 2 adds one, 0xd to 0x10 store the opcode less 0xc. It does NOT remove the member from the group: a dead machine stays in the roster and keeps being ticked, which is why the inert behaviour states exist.

entries.name: Meteor_Dtor
entries.description: METEOR vtable +0x08 (004982b8), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). Debris_Dtor's body: installs TSObjVtable, deletes the shape instance at +0x34 through its own vtable +0x18 with flags 3, and Mem_Deletes this on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00424034; class record at 00423fe4

entries.name: MissionGroup_ElementCtor
entries.description: Rtl_VectorNew's per-element constructor for MissionGroups_Allocate's 0x7a-byte group records (es2_xref finds one reference, the operand at 00423d4c of the PUSH at 00423d4b): zeroes the route cursor's index word at group+0x04 and nothing else.

entries.name: Sim_DamageToPlayerDisabled
entries.description: Two-global predicate gating the very first line of Mech_ComponentDamageWrite for the locally piloted machine: when MissionModeFlag is 0 the answer is PlayerInvulnerableFlag == 1, otherwise MissionDifficulty == 0. Which arm is live is docs/retail/simulation/difficulty.md's.

entries.name: Mission_WriteResults
entries.description: (player) Writes data\results.dat -- int16 (Mission_EvaluateObjectives(player) == 9), int32 Q10(2500, Mission_TotalSalvage) + counter 20 * 25000, int16 count and that many {int16 weapon, int16 condition} salvage pairs from DAT_004a9ef0, then Group_WriteStatusBlocks over the player's group -- and then the 2000 bytes of mission counters DAT_004a9ef4 back over data\mission.var. Asserts at severity 5 (WORLD.CPP lines 0x6f and 0x84) when either file does not open. es2_xref finds one call, from Sim_Shutdown (00461f25).

entries.name: DBSim_LoadScriptDat
entries.description: Pass 1 of DBSIM's two reads of the mission handoff. Opens data\mission.var (0049a9cb), data\player.mec (0049a9f2), data\mission.str (0049aa17) and data\script (0049aa28, extension appended) in that order; a failed open of the first, second or fourth raises a severity-5 Assert_Report (WORLD.CPP lines 0xa5, 0xb2, 0xdc). mission.var: 2000 bytes into the counter array DAT_004a9ef4, then slots 10, 20 and 21-42 zeroed. player.mec: the player's entry index into DAT_004aaae8, the entry count into DAT_004aaae2, then each entry into a 0x7e-byte record at DAT_004aaae4 (pilot +0, type +4, fit +8, ammunition +0x20, the three condition spans after); PilotingRazor is set when entry 0's type is 8. mission.str: StringTable_LoadGroup of up to 0x32 lines into g_MissionStringLines, a trailing newline stripped from each. script.dat: the 20-byte header into ScriptDatHeader (004a9ed2), MissionModeFlag zeroed, World_LoadTheater(&header); block 1 coordinates into DAT_004a9e90 with their XY extent accumulated into Mission_Box; block 2 headings times 0xb6 into DAT_004a9e94; block 3 waypoint groups into 6-byte records at DAT_004a9e9c, refs resolved to block-1 pointers; block 4 areas through TriggerArea_Resolve into DAT_004a9ea4; block 5 actions into 0x3a-byte records at DAT_004a9eac (type, verb, the area count up to the first negative ref and their pointers, counter refs and operations, message minus 1, target; the five text refs read and dropped; activation flag zeroed); block 6 timers through DBSim_BuildActionTimerRecord; blocks 7, 8 and 9 keep just each record's type (+0x28, +0x2c, +0x00); block 10 read and dropped; each block-11 record past the first marks the slots its 20 member refs name live in the mech, flyer or base flag array (004aa7ae, 004aa8da, 004aa93e and 004aaa56) by its discriminator 0, 1 or 2, and record 0 is kept on the stack; block 12 read and dropped; block 13's count and refs into DAT_004a9ec8 / DAT_004a9ecc. Then the slot-to-pool maps: live flyer and base slots numbered in slot order into DAT_004aa90c / DAT_004aa9ca; live mech slots numbered in slot order into DAT_004aa812, then the slot record 0 names at member position k mapped to (live mech count + k), then each player.mec entry k marked live at slot (block-7 count + k) and mapped to (live mech count + k). Registers each live type (maybe_MechTypeSlot_Allocate, FlyerType_Register, BaseType_LoadShape), sizes GlobalMechList (0x36a-byte elements), the flyer pool g_FlyerPool (0x291), Structure_InitPool and the live object list to the live counts, allocates the gun-layout, damage and collision tables, loads every mech and flyer type, calls Terrain_LoadZone(header+2) and copies the training mission number into TrainingMissionNumber. See docs/retail/formats/script-dat.md.

entries.name: Sim_ShutdownNoOp2
entries.description: Empty body, a lone RET. es2_xref finds one call, from Sim_Shutdown (00461f8f), after its Sim_ShutdownNoOp1 call. ES1's Sim_ShutdownNoOp2 (ES1DBSIM 0001e634) is the same.

entries.name: Mission_ResolveRefByKind
entries.description: Resolves a script.dat ref to a runtime pointer by kind: 0 gives the mission group record at MissionGroups + ref*0x7a; 1, 2 and 3 give Pool_Nth of the mech, flyer or structure pool at the index the slot-to-pool map (DAT_004aa812, DAT_004aa90c, DAT_004aa9ca, signed bytes) holds for that roster slot; any other kind gives 0. The ref is used as an index without a range test. DBSim_LoadScriptDat's mech map sends the slots block 11 record 0 names to the player's squad. DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects, read this session, calls it for each order's subject, each objective's subject and each type 7-10 action's target.

entries.name: DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects
entries.description: Pass 2 of DBSIM's two reads of the handoff, and the pass that builds the mission's objects. Re-opens data\script (string 0049aa3e plus extension), sets the announced mission status DAT_004a9ed0 to 0xffff, skips the header and blocks 1-6 and reads blocks 7-12. Block 7, then the player.mec entries, between WeaponModels_LoadShapeChunks and WeaponModels_FreeShapeChunks: for each slot DBSim_LoadScriptDat marked live it allocates from GlobalMechList and runs Mech_Constructor with the type. A roster record supplies the position ref at +0x3e (Terrain_HeightQuery plus typeRec+0x16, plus 5000 when typeRec+0x50 is set; an unset ref leaves the position sentinel), heading +0x40, fit +0x2a and ammunition +0x6a to Mech_ConfigureLoadout, radar +0x00, cruise speed +0x02 when non-negative, engaged and defeated actions +0x80/+0x82, out-of-action counters +0x42/+0x56 and starting condition +0x84 to Mech_ApplyStartingCondition. A player.mec entry gets the sentinel position and heading, its fit (+8, +0x20), Mech_ApplySquadCondition from its three condition spans and its pilot index at mech+0x29c, and the entry at DAT_004aaae8 becomes PlayerMech with locallyPiloted set. Block 8: Flyer_Constructor with type +0x2c, position +0x28 taken without a height query, heading +0x2a, actions +0x56/+0x58, counters +0x2e/+0x42. Block 9: Base_Construct on the record, position +0x02 registered with Terrain_MarkStructureFootprint and then Terrain_HeightQuery, heading +0x04, actions +0x2e/+0x30, counters +0x06/+0x1a. Block 10 into 0x16-byte order records at DAT_004a9eb4, the subject through Mission_ResolveRefByKind. Block 11 into MissionGroups (stride 0x7a) through DBSim_BuildGroupRecord: record 0's members become the player.mec machines (map entries at block-7 count + k), every other record's refs are remapped through its kind's slot-to-pool map; a group with no heading ref takes Math_HeadingToward from its slot-0 route's second waypoint to its first when that route has two or more; a base group whose paints-ground flag is 1 calls Base_ApplyFormationTerrain on its first member. Block 12 into 0x4c-byte objective records at DAT_004a9ec4: the subject through Mission_ResolveRefByKind, three mission.str line pointers from g_MissionStringLines and the empty string 0049a870. Then Terrain_FlattenStructureFootprints, every structure's height re-queried, and each action's target resolved: types 0-6 cleared, 7, 8 and 9 as mech, flyer and base slots, 10 as a group, any other type left as stored.

entries.name: Sim_ShutdownNoOp1
entries.description: Empty body, a lone RET. es2_xref finds one call, from Sim_Shutdown (00461f8a), the call before its Sim_ShutdownNoOp2 call. ES1's Sim_ShutdownNoOp1 (ES1DBSIM 0001f1bc) is the same.

entries.name: Sim_RaycastObjectList
entries.description: (shot): the ray-versus-live-object sweep of docs/retail/simulation/hit-detection.md. When the shot has an owner (+0xe) it scales the shot's +6 and +4 with Damage_ScaleByDifficulty by the owner's group's side (+0x45, +0x12); it caches the world-to-ray transform at the ray record's +0xa; it cuts the ray to Sim_RaycastTerrain's ground hit, between two RaycastShapeMinDistance_Clear calls. It walks the live object list, skipping the owner, the second excluded object at +0x14 and any object whose group's +0x14 action is set, and calls each candidate's slot +0x20 hit test, cutting the ray to each hit and going on while the hit distance is 500 or more. A hit on the owner's own target (+0x1a4) sets the owner's +0x9e and passes the target's engaged action +0x1b2 to Action_Activate unless its +0xa2 is set; any other struck object becomes the blocker (its +0xc). Unless the object is destroyed (+0x99), or of the other side with +0xa4 or +0xa5 set, it calls the object's slot +0x50 with the owner and the shot's +4, after Mech_AiFriendlyFireComplaint for the nearest live member of the owner's group within 30000 when the owner is locally piloted (+0xa3) and the object is of its side in another group. A strike with no object struck spawns an impact effect from the shot's effect table (+0xa). With a blocker and an owner target, a Math_GroundDistanceBetweenPoints to the ray's end below the range to the target and a bearing difference, each less the owner's heading, below 0x2000 as a signed int16, taken without an absolute value by the JGE at 004269eb, lead to the owner's slot +0x64 with the blocker. Returns the length + 1 after a strike, else 0. es2_xref finds nine calls in four functions: Rocket_TickUpdate (1), Bullet_TickUpdate (2), Bullet_FireBurst (1) and Razor_MovementTick (5).

entries.name: Damage_ExplosiveBlastSweep
entries.description: (hitPoint, blastRadius, damage, attacker, excluded): the radius-based splash-damage sweep. Walks the live-object list, skipping an object whose mission group still carries an action (group +0x14) and the excluded object, and for each whose Math_DistanceBetweenPoints from hitPoint less its slot +0x5c body radius is below blastRadius calls its slot +0x70(object, damage, hitPoint, blastRadius as a short, attacker) and sets the result to 1. So it returns 1 when anything was in range, whatever the +0x70 call did with it. es2_xref finds three calls, from Meteor_Tick (the drop-pod landing), Bullet_TickUpdate (the plasma round) and Mech_BehaviourRamTick. See docs/retail/simulation/damage-system.md.
entries.signature: short __cdecl Damage_ExplosiveBlastSweep(int *hitPoint, int blastRadius, short damage, int *attacker, int *excluded)

entries.name: Salvage_QueueWeapon
entries.description: (pair): appends the dword its argument points at, an {int16 weapon id, int16 condition} pair of the salvage list Mission_WriteResults writes as results.dat's salvage pairs, to the list at DAT_004a9ef0 at index DAT_004a9eee, then adds 1 to the count. The list is 200 bytes from DBSim_LoadScriptDat, room for 50, and the append has no bound. es2_xref finds two calls, from Mech_ApplyDirectFireDamage (00418ad6) and Mech_SalvageValue (00418ede).

entries.name: Detection_ContactScanRange
entries.description: Returns 30000 when DAT_004a9ee2, script.dat header word 8, the scan-range setting, is 1 and 60000 otherwise: the range within which a held contact can still be selected. es2_xref finds one call, from TargetSelect_CanTarget (004331b7). See docs/retail/simulation/target-selection.md.

entries.name: Damage_ScaleByDifficulty
entries.description: Scales a damage figure in place by a Q10 factor from one of two four-entry tables selected by the firing side -- 0049a73c {3500, 2800, 2100, 1400} for side 0, 0049a744 {300, 600, 800, 1000} for anything else -- indexed by the mission difficulty at MissionDifficulty. So difficulty moves the two sides' damage in opposite directions (3.42x down to 1.37x, versus 0.29x up to 0.98x).

entries.name: ActionTimers_Tick
entries.description: Walks the whole resolved block-6 array at ActionTimer_Array (count ActionTimer_Count, stride 0x31) calling ActionTimer_Tick on each. Sim_MainTick calls it immediately before Actions_EvaluateTriggers and both AFTER the per-group Group_OrderTick/Group_DeploymentCheck pass, so a group waiting on an action arrives on the tick after it activates.

entries.name: Actions_EvaluateTriggers
entries.description: (mech): walks the whole block-5 action array (DAT_004a9eac, count DAT_004a9ea8, stride 0x3a) and offers Action_TestTrigger positions by the action's type +0: 0 the mech's (+0x26); 1 each member of its group (+0x45) through Action_TestTriggerForGroup; 2 and 3 each member of each mission group (stride 0x7a) of side +0x12 0 or 1, and 4, 5 and 6 of kind +0 0, 1 or 2, each of those skipping a group whose action +0x14 is set (an undeployed group cannot trip a trigger) and stopping at the first group that answers; 7, 8 and 9 the action's resolved target object +0x36's position; 10 the target group +0x36; any other type tests nothing. Neither 7-9 nor 10 tests +0x36 for null. A non-zero answer goes to Action_Activate. es2_xref finds one call, from Sim_MainTick (0045f760).

entries.name: World_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser of WORLD.CPP (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7aec, priority 0x20): StringTable_Ctor on g_MissionStrings (004aa6d4), the table DBSim_LoadScriptDat loads data\mission.str into. World_StaticDtor is its _EXIT_ counterpart.

entries.name: World_StaticDtor
entries.description: World_StaticInit's _EXIT_ routine (Borland _EXIT_ entry 004a7c1e): OwnedArray_Dtor(g_MissionStrings (004aa6d4), 2).

entries.name: DetAnimObj_Dtor
entries.description: DET_ANIM_OBJ vtable +0x08 (004973cc): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). One RTL destructor-count decrement, AnimObj_Dtor(this, 0), then Mem_Delete(this) on flags bit 0.

entries.name: SimObject_Dtor
entries.description: ACTOR vtable +0x08 (0049a54c): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). Two RTL destructor-count decrements (ACTOR, DET_ANIM_OBJ), AnimObj_Dtor(this, 0), then on flags bit 0 ObjList_SwapRemove(&maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList, this) instead of a Mem_Delete.

entries.name: SimObject_OperatorDelete
entries.description: (obj): ObjList_SwapRemove(&maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList, obj). The class-specific operator delete in the +0x14 field of the ACTOR, MECH, FLYER, BASE, RADAR_BASE, GUN_BASE, VEHICLE and LC_BASE class records; their deleting destructors inline the same call.

entries.name: Mech_Dtor
entries.description: MECH vtable +0x08 (0049a282): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). Three RTL destructor-count decrements (MECH, ACTOR, DET_ANIM_OBJ), AnimObj_Dtor(this, 0), then on flags bit 0 ObjList_SwapRemove(&maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList, this).

entries.name: Flyer_Dtor
entries.description: FLYER vtable +0x08 (0049a5e0): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). Three RTL destructor-count decrements (FLYER, ACTOR, DET_ANIM_OBJ), AnimObj_Dtor(this, 0), then on flags bit 0 ObjList_SwapRemove(&maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList, this).

entries.name: ActionTimer_ElementCtor
entries.description: (timer): returns its argument -- the per-element constructor DBSim_LoadScriptDat hands Rtl_VectorNew for the script.dat block-6 action timers (PUSH at 00424b76: 0x31 bytes each, count ActionTimer_Count (004a9eb8), stored to ActionTimer_Array (004a9ebc)).

entries.name: GridShape_HeightAround
entries.description: Column height under a point of a shape's collision height field, the point already shifted by the grid origin. When (1 << (cellShift - 1)) < radius it returns the tallest cell within radius; below that it samples the single cell. Off-grid is 0, which is what makes the volume end at its own edges. Cells hold a byte code into the 256-entry int32 height table at grid+0x34.

entries.name: GridShape_HeightAt
entries.description: GridShape_HeightAround with the grid-origin shift added to the point first (origin column and row << cellShift, 16-bit: world units rather than cells). Returns 0 for a shape with no collision volume (no columns).

entries.name: GridShape_Raycast
entries.description: Marches a ray, in shape space, through a shape's collision height field. Rejects an empty grid and a ray with BOTH ends at or above grid+0x430 (the height table's last entry, its ceiling). Shifts both ends by the origin << cellShift; the step length is (1 << cellShift) + clearance, to which Math_NormalizeVec3ToLength rescales the direction, and the step count is the segment's Math_FastMagnitude3D over the step, plus 1. Hits when GridShape_HeightAround returns nonzero above the ray's current Z; reports the hit point with the grid origin offset removed.

entries.name: GridShape_Construct
entries.description: ClassItem registry loadFn for classId 0x02bc0001 (dgs\bases/bhulks shape records): allocates a 0x438-byte GridShape (RTTI name, vtable 0049aaa0, base TSShape), installs the vtable, then calls vtable+0xc (GridShape_ReadFromStream). See dgs-hd0-notes.md.

entries.name: GridShape_GetClassTag
entries.description: GridShape vtable 0049aaa0 slot 0: returns 0x2bc0001, GridShape_Construct's class id.

entries.name: GridShape_GetStreamSize
entries.description: GridShape vtable 0049aaa0 slot +4 (shape): TSShape's stream size (00490cdc) plus columns +0x2a times rows +0x2c plus 0x40a -- the five int16 grid scalars and the 1024-byte height table GridShape_ReadFromStream reads after TSShape's fields, then one byte per cell.

entries.name: GridShape_GetMemorySize
entries.description: GridShape vtable 0049aaa0 slot +8: returns 0. It does not call TSShape's slot +8 (00490d08).

entries.name: GridShape_ReadFromStream
entries.description: Field reader for a dgs\bases/bhulks shape record (vtable+0xc for classId 0x02bc0001), on top of the generic ClassItem base-class chain (TSShape_ReadFromStream). Its tail is the shape's COLLISION VOLUME, a coarse height field: int16 columns (+0x2a), rows (+0x2c), origin column (+0x2e), origin row (+0x30), cell shift (+0x32), a 256-entry int32 height table (+0x34, 1024 bytes, last entry addressed as the ceiling at +0x430), then, when rows is not 0, rows pointers allocated with Arena_AllocDup at +0x434, each to a row of columns height codes read from the stream. The obvious reading, five undecoded scalars and an opaque block followed by sub-record count * sub-record size raw records, spans the same bytes and parses every retail record, but it is not the layout. See docs/retail/simulation/hit-detection.md.

entries.name: GridShape_WriteToStream
entries.description: GridShape vtable 0049aaa0 slot +0x10 (shape, stream): TSShape's write (00490e34), then the stream's +0x14 write of what GridShape_ReadFromStream reads, in the same order: the int16 columns +0x2a, rows +0x2c, origin column +0x2e, origin row +0x30 and cell shift +0x32, the 0x400-byte height table at +0x34, then one columns-byte row per row through the row-pointer array at +0x434.

entries.name: GridShape_RegisterClassItem
entries.description: Static initialiser of the GridShape module (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7af2, priority 0x20): ClassItem_RegisterBucket(GridShape_ClassItemEntry (0049aa7c), 1), the one-entry bucket {0x02bc0001, GridShape_Construct, 'GridShape'} that lets ClassItem_FindHandler load a GridShape.

entries.name: GridShape_Dtor
entries.description: GridShape vtable 0049aaa0 slot +0x18 (shape, flags): when shape is set, lowers the destructor count at *Rtl_DtorCountPtr, runs TSShape_Dtor (00490958) with flags 0, then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: Terrain_LoadZone
entries.description: terrain.cpp zone/grid loader. Builds a 'zoneNNNN' filename, reads a grid header, allocates a HeightGrid, installs it as ActiveHeightGrid.

entries.name: maybe_SimObject_TransformPointPairToWorld
entries.description: (obj, out): returns 0 when the pointer at obj+0x41 is null. Otherwise builds the object's Q14 rotation (BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14 from obj+0xc into obj+0x12) while the frame-valid word obj+0x32 is 0 (setting it to 1), and Transform_ApplyToPoint's the two Point3I at *(obj+0x41) and *(obj+0x41)+0xc through the object transform at obj+0x12 into out and out+0xc; returns out. What a pair of points at obj+0x41 is has not been read; maybe_SimObject_TransformPointPairToWorldStatic is the caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: maybe_SimObject_TransformPointPairToWorldStatic
entries.description: (obj): sets the static-local guard byte 0049ab6e on first use and returns maybe_SimObject_TransformPointPairToWorld(obj, 004aab3c), a static two-point buffer (EAX passes through). No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Structure_WalkCollisionTest
entries.description: The walking-collision half of the structure volume test, called from Structure_GatherWalkCandidates's gather. Per candidate: 2D distance from the point to the structure against shape+8 (the shape read through the model instance, obj+0x34 -> +4), then the offset rotated into shape space by the transposed XY block of the object's rotation, then GridShape_HeightAt(shape, point, 0), which applies the same origin << cellShift GridShape_Raycast applies, so a walker meets the footprint a shot meets. Returns the first nonzero height; the radius argument is not read.
entries.signature: int __cdecl Structure_WalkCollisionTest(int *point, unsigned short radius, int *candidates, short count)

entries.name: Terrain_HeightQueryActive
entries.description: (point): Terrain_HeightQuery(ActiveHeightGrid, point). Debris_TickUpdate calls it.

entries.name: RaycastShapeMinDistance_Clear
entries.description: Sets RaycastShapeMinDistance (004aab54) to 0. es2_xref finds two calls, both from Sim_RaycastObjectList (00426650, 00426694), around its Sim_RaycastTerrain call.

entries.name: RaycastShapeMinDistance_Get
entries.description: Returns RaycastShapeMinDistance (004aab54) in EAX (the decompile drops the return).

entries.name: Sim_RaycastShapeVolume
entries.description: (result, ray, objects, count): ray versus the collision height fields of count objects in a pointer array. The ray record: +0 frame pointer, +4 length, +8 int16 clearance, +0x0a world-to-ray transform. Per object, its shape being its model instance (obj+0x34) +4 (0 without one) and reach = shape+8 + clearance: the distance from the ray's start (frame +0x14) to the object's position (+0x26) replaces RaycastShapeMinDistance (004aab54) when it is less; when it is at most reach + length, RaycastShapeMinDistance becomes 0, Transform_ApplyToPoint takes the position through the ray's +0x0a, and with |x| < reach and -reach < y < length + reach (Z is not tested) the object's rotation (BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14 from its angles +0x12 first when +0x32 is 0), inverted by Transform_TransposeRotation and Transform_RotatePoint of the negated translation, takes the ray's start and its end (0, length, 0) into shape space for GridShape_Raycast with the clearance. On a hit the ray's +0x04 becomes Math_DistanceBetweenPoints from the start to the hit point, result +4 the object's +0xc (0 for a null object) and result +0 the distance, and the walk ends for a distance under 500. Returns the hit flag in AX. es2_xref finds two calls, at 00404c80 in Sim_RaycastShapeList and at 004050b9 in Base_DirectFireHitTest.

entries.name: Sim_RaycastTerrain
entries.description: (&result{distance, object}, rayRecord) -> bool. The ray-versus-terrain query Sim_RaycastObjectList runs before it tests any object. The origin is the ray transform's translation (transform+0x14) and the far end Transform_ApplyToPoint(transform, (0, rayRecord+4, 0)); calls Terrain_RayWalk(ActiveHeightGrid, origin, end, rayRecord+8 -- the literal 200, as a radius, &hitPoint (a stack local), mode 0). On a hit it stores Math_DistanceBetweenPoints(origin, hitPoint) and &g_TerrainHitPseudoObject in the result, copies hitPoint to 004aab72/76/7a, and returns 1. Its one caller found by es2_xref, Sim_RaycastObjectList (call at 0042665d), cuts the ray to the distance when it is shorter. In v1.0 a hit whose plane solve found no point leaves hitPoint unwritten, so the distance is measured to whatever the stack slot held. This is what stops a shot passing through a hillside. Its companion RaycastShapeMinDistance_Clear is only a counter reset (RaycastShapeMinDistance), not part of the query.

entries.name: Terrain_RayHitDistance
entries.description: (&distance, from, to, short radius): Terrain_RayWalk mode 0 on ActiveHeightGrid from from to to, the radius passed through as its fourth argument and the hit point into a stack local; when it reports a hit, stores Math_DistanceBetweenPoints(from, hitPoint) in distance and returns 1 in AX, else 0. Callers found by es2_xref: Detection_LineOfSight and Ai_LineOfSightBlocked, both of which pass radius 0 and read only the return value, never the distance.

entries.name: Scene_DrawTerrain
entries.description: (view): Raster_SetModelTransform(&DAT_004aab08); sets the render context's clip mode +0x208 to 1 while its clip block (+4) holds one region whose first dword is 0; Terrain_DrawVisibleCells(g_TerrainDrawGrid, view); restores +0x208. Called from Scene_DrawTerrainPass in the frame draw and from the heads-down map's terrain pass.

entries.name: Terrain_StaticInitNoOp
entries.description: Static initialiser of the terrain module (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7af8, priority 0x20): a lone RET. It follows Scene_DrawTerrain and precedes the HeightGrid class record (004281a1).

entries.name: ObjList_DrawTableIndex
entries.description: (a, b): returns the index recorded for the pair in the draw table at 004cf574 (three int16 per entry: a, b, index; count 004cf8f8); a new pair is appended with the next index, asserting 'ObjList::drawTable full' in objlist.cpp once 0x96 entries exist. ObjList_AddToDrawTable and ObjList_DrawCellObjects call it.

entries.name: ObjList_LoadResources
entries.description: The object list's subsystem phase-2 loader, registered by ObjList_RegisterSubsystem: allocates three 0x800-byte pointer arrays to 004cf8fc, 004cf900 and 004cf90c, 512 render entries of 0x36 bytes with ObjList_DrawEntryConstruct to 004cf908, 512 sort-tree nodes through ObjList_AllocSortNodes, and zeroes 0x249f0 bytes at 004aab84 (which ObjList_DrawCellObjects indexes in 1000-byte rows). It lies outside every Ghidra function; es2_xref reports it as the end of ObjList_DrawTableIndex's extent (+0x80).

entries.name: ObjPick_Arm
entries.description: (point): copies the {x, y} pair to 004cf9b5/004cf9b9 and sets the pending flag 004cf9b4, arming the pixel pick. A grep of the disassembly for 004cf9b4 by address finds this store of 1, a store of 0 at 00428945 and four tests (ObjPick_IsIdle, 004287dd, 004288c5, 00428928); es2_xref finds no reference to the function.

entries.name: ObjPick_GetObject
entries.description: Returns 004cf9c0: the object ObjList_DrawEntryRender stores there (00428802) when an entry's draw changes the pick's pixel; ObjList_DrawAfterTerrain also stores to it (0042891c). es2_xref finds one call, at 0043d79c in Gunsight_UpdateAndPaint.

entries.name: ObjPick_IsIdle
entries.description: Returns 004cf9b4 == 0 (SETZ): no pick is pending. es2_xref finds one call, at 0043d793 in Gunsight_UpdateAndPaint.

entries.name: Scene_SubmitObject
entries.description: (obj): Scene_SubmitObjectWithRadius(obj, obj->vtable[+0x10]()) -- files one object into ObjList::drawTable under the terrain cell its position and its own shape radius pick. Scene_SubmitFrameObjects' submit for ground shapes (FlatObj), projectiles, ownerless explosions, debris, the 004a96f2 pool and drop pods.

entries.name: ObjList_AddToDrawTable
entries.description: Files one object into ObjList::drawTable at DAT_004aab80 (rows of 1000 bytes, row index interned per cell by ObjList_InternCellRow) or, when it resolves to no cell, into the flat DAT_004cf910 bucket that ObjList_DrawAfterTerrain draws after the terrain walk with no depth fade of its own. Asserts carry the objlist.cpp strings 'ObjList::drawTable entry full' and 'ObjList::drawTable full'.

entries.name: Scene_SubmitObjectWithRadius
entries.description: (obj, radius): HeightGrid_PickDrawCell(ActiveHeightGrid, obj->vtable[+0x04](), radius), then ObjList_AddToDrawTable(obj, cell); returns the cell record, which Scene_SubmitFrameObjects' machine walks cache at obj+0x7a/+0x1ea (0xffff when null).

entries.name: Scene_SubmitObjectAtCell
entries.description: (obj, cellXY): HeightGrid_ClaimDrawCell(ActiveHeightGrid, cellXY), then ObjList_AddToDrawTable(obj, cell); returns the cell record. Used where the cell is already known: a machine with a cached cell at +0x1e8, an explosion filed under its owner's cell (Explosion_GetOwnerDrawCell), and every fire.

entries.name: ObjList_RemoveListedObject
entries.description: (obj): searches the pointer array at 004cf8fc (count int16 0049abba) for obj and, at the first match, decrements the count and moves the last entry into the match's slot. No caller found by es2_xref; an absolute-address search of the disassembly finds 004cf8fc read here and written by ObjList_LoadResources, and 0049abba read here and at 00461798 in Sim_InitMissionSession.

entries.name: Scene_SubmitFrameObjects
entries.description: Per-frame scene assembly. Clears DAT_004cf8f8 and calls HeightGrid_ClearCellScratch(ActiveHeightGrid), clears DAT_004cf9b0 after the first walk, and walks the object pools and lists in a fixed order and files each drawable object into ObjList::drawTable by terrain cell: g_FlatObjPool first (only shapes within 30000 of the view object, by Math_DistanceBetweenPoints, through Scene_SubmitObject), then the 004a9624 structure list, GlobalMechList and the 004a9e3d flyer list by body radius (vtable +0x5c), a machine whose mech+0x2b0 names a structure under that structure's cached cell instead (Scene_SubmitObjectAtCell); each skips an object whose group's +0x14 deployment gate is set and caches the cell it filed at obj+0x1e8/+0x1ea (0xffff for the no-cell bucket); then the projectile pool 004a9746, g_ExplosionPool (Explosion_IsHiddenFromOwnerCockpit, then the owner's cell or its own), g_DebrisPool, the smoke-ball pool 004a96f2, g_FirePool (Scene_SubmitObjectAtCell) and g_MeteorPool. It decides no visibility beyond the flat-shape range and the two gates.

entries.name: ObjList_DrawEntryRender
entries.description: Slot 0 of the depth-sorted render entry's vtable (stamped as PTR_FUN_0049ac38 by ObjList_DrawEntryConstruct). Reads the entry's cached position (+4/+8/+0xc) and radius (+0x10), runs LightManager_SelectLightsForObject with them, WorldShades_ApplyForObject with the object (+0x32), the entry's distance (+0x12) and the byte 004cfa08, Raster_SetDepthFadeFromDistance with that distance, then the object's vtable slot 0 -- Bullet_Draw for a projectile. After the draw it runs Light_ReregisterPersistent while 004cfa08 is set; while the pick flag 004cf9b4 is set, a pick pixel no longer reading 1 records the object at 004cf9c0 and is reset to 1; and while 0049abbc is set and the object is the probed one (004cf9f8), ObjProbe_MarkCorners.

entries.name: ObjList_DrawAfterTerrain
entries.description: (view): runs after the terrain walk in Sim_RenderFrame. Calls slot 0 of every object in the no-cell bucket DAT_004cf910 (count DAT_004cf9b0) that ObjList_AddToDrawTable fills. Then, when LocalPlayerMech's type record (+0x1f2) has the flyer flag +0x50 set (the RAZOR) and Cam_IsAttachedTo(view, player) is 0, Terrain_DrawCellObjects for the player's cached cell (+0x1e8/+0x1ea). Then, while the pick flag 004cf9b4 is set, points the display's source page +0x38 at +0x8c, saves the pixel under the pick point (004cf9b5) at 004cfa00, writes 1 there and clears ObjPick_GetObject's 004cf9c0; ObjList_SetViewObject(view); restores the saved pixel and clears 004cf9b4. Last, ObjProbe_TestCorners when DAT_0049abbc is set.

entries.name: ObjProbe_Arm
entries.description: (obj): projects obj's position (vtable +4) to the screen (Raster_SetModelTransform(0), Raster_ModelToView, Raster_PerspectiveDivide, Raster_ProjectToScreen) and sizes a square from its radius r (vtable +0x10): e = Math_FastMagnitude3D(g_EyeInModelSpace) - r, 1 only when it is 0, and half-size h = (r << 006c60ac) / e, 1 when that is 0, so with the eye inside r the half-size is negative. Stores the four corners {x-h, y-h}, {x+h, y-h}, {x+h, y+h}, {x-h, y+h} from 004cf9c4, the object at 004cf9f8, and sets 0049abbc. Each corner's flag 004cf9f4[i] is set when the first corner lies outside the rect at +0x210..+0x21c of the block 006c5ff4 points at: the loop never advances its point pointer, so all four take the first corner's answer. es2_xref finds no reference to it.

entries.name: ObjProbe_IsHidden
entries.description: Returns whether all four of ObjProbe_Arm's corner flags 004cf9f4[0..3] are set. es2_xref finds no reference to it.

entries.name: ObjProbe_MarkCorners
entries.description: Records the display (006c5f54) at 004cf9fc; for each probe corner whose flag 004cf9f4[i] is clear, saves the pixel there (g_RasterRoutines_GetPixel) at 004cf9e4[i] and writes 2 (g_RasterRoutines_PutPixel). es2_xref finds one call, at 00428831 in ObjList_DrawEntryRender.

entries.name: ObjProbe_TestCorners
entries.description: Records the display (006c5f54) at 004cf9fc and points its source page +0x38 at its +0x8c, storing that at 004a369e and passing it to maybe_g_RasterRoutines_SetSourcePage when it is still the current display; for each corner with its flag clear, restores the saved pixel when it still reads 2, otherwise sets the flag -- something drawn after the probed object covered it. Clears 0049abbc. es2_xref finds one call, at 00428955 in ObjList_DrawAfterTerrain.

entries.name: ObjList_SetDrawDistances
entries.description: (radius): the five object draw distances at DAT_004cfa0c, each Math_Q10Multiply(radius, factor) over the int16 table at 0049abb0 = {800, 900, 1000, 800, 1200}. Its one caller, Terrain_SetupVisibleRegion, passes the terrain draw radius in world units (grid+0x10c << cellShift), once a frame. ObjList_IsBeyondDrawDistance reads the result.

entries.name: ObjList_IsBeyondDrawDistance
entries.description: (obj, dist): picks a draw distance from DAT_004cfa0c by the object's type tag at +4 -- tag 0 entry 1, tag 8 entry 2, tag 5 entry 3, or entry 4 when SimObject_GetShapeRadius (vtable +0x10) is 7000 or more, anything else entry 0 -- and returns whether dist exceeds it. Called only by ObjList_DrawCellObjects (00428d92), which drops the object's render entry when it does.

entries.name: ObjList_DrawCellObjects
entries.description: The per-terrain-cell object draw hook (installed at HeightGrid+0x125, invoked by Terrain_DrawCellObjects). Walks the cell's ObjList::drawTable row and branches on each object's type tag at +4: tag 9 (a ground shape) is drawn immediately, in filing order, with the ramp row count DAT_004a5b1c zeroed around the draw and no fade of its own -- its solid faces fog with the one the cell's quad installed; everything else (a Bullet is tag 3, written by Bullet_Construct) is turned into a 0x36-byte render entry carrying its position, LOD short and distance, appended to the list ObjList_DrawSorted then walks. See docs/retail/rendering/terrain-drawing.md, 'Objects in the walk'.

entries.name: ObjList_RegisterSubsystem
entries.description: Static-init registrar of objlist.cpp (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7afe, priority 0x20): registers ObjList_LoadResources (00428230) at subsystem phase 2, then Rtl_VectorNew(004cf9c4, 8, 4, 1, Rtl_ReturnArg).

entries.name: ObjList_DrawEntryConstruct
entries.description: Constructor for the depth-sorted render entry: three successive vtable stamps (base, derived, most-derived), the last being PTR_FUN_0049ac38 whose slot 0 is ObjList_DrawEntryRender.

entries.name: ObjList_SetViewObject
entries.description: (obj): stores its argument at DAT_0049ac3c. ObjList_DrawCellObjects and ObjList_DrawAfterTerrain pass the view object.

entries.name: ObjList_AllocSortNodes
entries.description: (count): ObjList_SortNodes (0049ac40) = Rtl_VectorNew(0, 0x1d, count, 1, ObjListSortNode_ElementCtor) -- the 0x1d-byte depth-sort tree nodes ObjList_SortTreeAddKind12 and ObjList_SortTreeAddOthers hand out. ObjList_LoadResources passes 0x200.

entries.name: ObjList_PointNearSegment
entries.description: (entry, point): whether Point3I_DistanceBetween(entry+4, point) is less than half of Point3I_DistanceBetween(entry+0x18, entry+0x24) -- the point lies inside the sphere on the render entry's position whose diameter is its segment's length. ObjList_SortCompareSegment and ObjList_SegmentEndpointNear (0042933c) call it.

entries.name: ObjList_PointNearSegmentAxis
entries.description: (entry, point): 0 when ObjList_PointNearSegment(entry, point) answers non-zero or the entry's int16 +0x30 is 0. Otherwise builds the rotation facing along the segment (Math_EulerToward between +0x18 and +0x24, BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14, Transform_TransposeRotation), rotates point by it untranslated (Transform_RotatePoint) and returns 1 when both the x and z components are less than +0x30 in magnitude. es2_xref finds no reference to it.

entries.name: ObjList_SortCompareSegment
entries.description: (node, newNode): ObjList_SortCompare's case where exactly one render entry carries a segment (entry +0x16 of 1 or 2, endpoints at +0x18 and +0x24). When the segment entry is the nearer (+0x12) the answer is plain distance order, and also when 00428f38 accepts neither the camera (0049ac3c + 4) nor the other entry's position (+4) against it. Otherwise it builds, once per entry (flag +0xc), the normal of the plane that contains the segment and faces the camera -- Vec3I_Cross(segment, Vec3I_Cross(segment, camera - start)), each vector halved until Math_FastMagnitude3D is at most 32000 -- at +0x11 with the camera's side of it (Vec3I_DotSign) at +0xd, and returns whether the other entry's position lies on the camera's side.

entries.name: ObjList_SegmentEndpointNear
entries.description: (entryA, entryB): returns entryA+0x18 when ObjList_PointNearSegment(entryB, entryA+0x18), else entryA+0x24 when ObjList_PointNearSegment(entryB, entryA+0x24), else 0 -- the first of A's segment endpoints inside B's segment sphere. ObjList_SortCompareSegments asks it each way round.

entries.name: ObjList_SortCompareSegments
entries.description: (node, newNode): ObjList_SortCompare's case where both render entries carry segments. Asks 0042933c for a point of one against the other, each way round; with none, plain distance order (+0x12). Otherwise it moves that entry's position (+4) to the point and its type (+0x16) to 0 for the call, compares through ObjList_SortCompareSegment with the other entry as the segment, restores both fields, and inverts the answer when the moved entry was node.

entries.name: ObjList_SortCompare
entries.description: (node, newNode): which side of node newNode's render entry (+8) goes on; non-zero is right, drawn later. When both entries' int16 +0x16 is 1 or 2 the answer is 0042937c's; when both are 0 it is whether newNode's distance (+0x12) is less than node's; otherwise 0042900c's.

entries.name: ObjList_SortTreeInsert
entries.description: (node, newNode): descends right (+4) when ObjList_SortCompare(node, newNode) is non-zero and left (+0) otherwise, recursing until it finds the empty child to link newNode into.

entries.name: ObjList_SortTreeAddKind12
entries.description: (entries, count): for each entry whose int16 +0x16 is 1 or 2, fills the next 0x1d-byte node from 0049ac40 (entry at +8, children and byte +0xc cleared) and inserts it under the root with ObjList_SortTreeInsert (the first node is the root). Returns the next free node; the decompile drops it (MOV EAX,ESI).

entries.name: ObjList_SortTreeAddOthers
entries.description: (entries, count, node): ObjList_SortTreeAddKind12's complement: every entry whose int16 +0x16 is neither 1 nor 2 gets the next node from node onwards and is inserted under the root at 0049ac40 with ObjList_SortTreeInsert, unless it is the root itself.

entries.name: ObjList_SortTreeDraw
entries.description: (node): in-order walk of the sort tree: the left subtree, then slot 0 of the render entry at +8 (ObjList_DrawEntryRender), then the right subtree.

entries.name: ObjList_DrawSorted
entries.description: (entries, count): nothing for count 0. Builds a binary tree of the render entries in the 0x1d-byte node pool at 0049ac40 ({+0 left, +4 right, +8 entry}, the first node the root): ObjList_SortTreeAddKind12 adds the entries whose int16 +0x16 is 1 or 2, ObjList_SortTreeAddOthers the rest from the node it returns, both through ObjList_SortTreeInsert; then ObjList_SortTreeDraw walks it from the root. es2_xref finds one call, from ObjList_DrawCellObjects at the end of a cell with the entries it built, each of which it gave +0x16 = 0, so they order by distance alone: farthest first.

entries.name: ObjListSortNode_ElementCtor
entries.description: (node): returns its argument -- the per-element constructor ObjList_AllocSortNodes hands Rtl_VectorNew for the 0x1d-byte depth-sort tree nodes; the LEA of +0x11 is an inlined empty member constructor.

entries.name: CockpitViewManager_Ctor
entries.description: (manager, machine), MECHVIEW.CPP: sets +0x14 to -1. While CockpitPaletteSingleton is 0 it loads dpl\cockpit into it with Palette_LoadDpl (ResourcePath_BuildFolderName) and sets ExternalView_DefaultRect to {0, 0, (0x140 << VideoMode_XCoordShift) - 1, (0xc3 << VideoMode_YCoordShift) - 1, -0xa0 << the x shift, -0x5a << the y shift}, copied to ExternalView_Rect. Takes the scheme word +0x27 from the machine's type record +0x1f2's +0x6c and the 8-character name +0x2d (+0x35 = 0) from the name table DAT_004a9de4 at that index, or from CockpitOverride_Index and CockpitOverride_Name when that name is set; stores the machine at +0x29; CockpitViewManager_LoadViews(manager, name); +0x18 = -1, +0x1c = 0 and the word +0x1d = 0; shifts the rect 0049ac54..0049ac60 by the coordinate shifts; gives 004cfb18 Mem_NewArray(Region_PixelCount(004cfb02)) bytes; +0x36 = 0. The 0x37-byte manager holds the current view at +0x14, the pending command at +0x18 and the CockpitView widget tree at +0x1f. es2_xref finds one call, from Sim_InitMissionSession.

entries.name: CockpitViewManager_Publish
entries.description: Stores its argument in CockpitViewManagerPublished (004cfa20). One call site: the tail of CockpitViewManager_LoadViews, passing the manager itself.

entries.name: CockpitViewManager_Published
entries.description: Returns CockpitViewManagerPublished (004cfa20) -- the cockpit view manager, or null before the cockpit is built. Sim_PollPlayerInput's HDD VIEW case tests the pointer itself rather than any field of it, which is the retail bug recorded in KNOWN_ISSUES.

entries.name: CockpitViewManager_GetCockpitView
entries.description: (manager): returns manager+0x1f, the CockpitView widget tree (CockpitViewInstance). Sim_DispatchCommand calls it on CockpitViewManagerInstance twice, in the auto-track paths, and discards the result.

entries.name: CockpitViewManager_LoadViews
