entries.name: MfdRadarScreen_Ctor
entries.description: (screen, rect): the SCANNER screen's constructor. MFDisplay_Ctor, then MFDRadarVtable at +0, a 100-entry vector of 0xc-byte contacts at +0x68 (Rtl_VectorNew with MfdRadarContact_ElementCtor), MFD bank (0049cbcc) frames 14 and 15 at +0x10 and +0x14, the plot radius 0x19 at +0x28, the plot centre at the rect's top-left + (0x41 << XCoordShift, 0x1c << YCoordShift) at +0x20, the dish top-left at the rect's top-left + (0x26 << XCoordShift, 1 << YCoordShift) at +0x18, +0x2c = 1 and +0x30 = 0. Four 0x21-byte labels, Label_Ctor(label, DAT_0049b0e0, 1) placed by Label_SetRect with zero margins and the fill +0x1d = 0x11, rects the rect's top-left plus a shifted offset and size: +0x38 (0x26, 0x33) + (0xc, 5) flags 1, +0x3c (0x4f, 1) + (0x10, 5) flags 4, +0x40 (0x26, 1) + (0xc, 5) flags 1, +0x44 (0x4f, 0x33) + (0x10, 5) flags 4. The dish rect +0x48 runs from +0x18 to +0x18 plus frame 14's width and height (+6, +4), each shifted by the coordinate shift in panel mode 3 without hi-res banks; +0x58 = the rect's top-left + (0x40 << XCoordShift, 3 << YCoordShift); +0x60 = the centre less (3 << XCoordShift, 0); +0x34 = 1. See docs/retail/simulation/mfd-scanner.md.

entries.name: MfdRadarScreen_Update
entries.description: Rebuilds the SCANNER screen's contact list: clears the count +0x518 and the selection entry +0x51c, copies the range (+0xc of the block at +8) to +0x30, and sets the mirror +0x34 to 1 when the byte +0x96 of CockpitViewInstance's +0x203 machine is 0; when that differs from the old +0x34 it presses MFD child 0xb (PASS) or 0xc (ACTIVE) through Widget_PressChild(Cockpit_GetMfd_Thunk(), child, 1). Walks the live object list, skipping the machine itself, an object with +0xa4 or +0x99 set, one whose group (+0x45) has a non-zero +0x14, and a class-1 object (+0x1a8) whose type record (+0x1f2) has +0x1e set. The position is +0x26/+0x2a when +0x95 is set or the group's side byte +0x12 is not 1; otherwise, while Time_GetCoarseTicks has bit 0x20 clear and +0xa7 is clear, the point at +0x1aa, else the object is skipped. The offset from the machine's +0x26/+0x2a with Math_FastMagnitude2D distance d (1 for 0) is kept when d < +0x30: rotated with Math_BuildRotation2D(-(machine +0x10)) and Math_Rotate2DPoint and stored as {x, -y, colour} at +0x68 + 0xc * count, the colour by class and side: class 0 DAT_004d3c20 (side 0) or DAT_004d3c12, class 2 DAT_004d3c22 or DAT_004d3c1e, classes 1 and 3 DAT_004d3c0c or DAT_004d3c18, any other DAT_004d3c24. For CockpitViewInstance's selection +0x210 it stores the entry at +0x51c and Hud_WorldUnitsToMetres(d) at +0x520. See docs/retail/simulation/mfd-scanner.md.

entries.name: MfdRadarScreen_UpdateAndPaint
entries.description: MFDRadar vtable +0x04 (0049c328), the MFD screen's per-frame slot: MfdRadarScreen_Update, then the screen's own slot +0x00, MfdRadarScreen_Paint.

entries.name: MfdRadarScreen_Paint
entries.description: Paints the SCANNER screen: floods the dish rect (+0x48) with raw palette index 0x11, takes the range from the display (+0x30) and sets the plot scale +0x2c = range / +0x28 >> XCoordShift, blits MFD frame 15 rotated about its own corner at the plot centre (+0x20/+0x24) by the torso twist - 0x6000, covers it with frame 14, and draws the passive-range ring only when +0x34 is 1 (passive) and 140000 < range: Raster_DrawEllipse in outline mode over centre +/- 140000 / scale, in DAT_004d3c16's colour. Then frame 17 (reference line), frame 18 (player marker), each contact ({x, y, colour} from +0x68, count +0x518) at centre + offset / scale -- one pixel through Gfx_PlotPixel with XCoordShift 0, otherwise a 2x2 Raster_FillRect -- frame 16 over the selected contact (+0x51c) offset -(2 << XCoordShift), and the RNG:/TRG: labels with the range in metres (Hud_WorldUnitsToMetres) and +0x520, each right-aligned and zero-padded to four characters. See docs/retail/simulation/mfd-scanner.md.

entries.name: HudScanner_Paint
entries.description: The front window's floating scanner repeater. Belongs to the GUNSIGHT complex, not the MFD: Gunsight_Paint and Gunsight_UpdateAndPaint reach it through the one-line Gunsight_PaintHudScanner after the child loop. Takes the SCANNER screen object (CockpitView+0x1ed's +0xd9) and the widget's own point at +0x10b (.GAU offset 1196). Does nothing when that screen is the display's current one, so it and the F4 screen are never on screen together; otherwise runs MfdRadarScreen_Update to rebuild the contact list. With the brush in outline mode (4) in DAT_004d3c12's colour, Raster_DrawEllipse over the square 0x2e << shift from the point; with the pen in the same colour, the turret arc as two Raster_DrawLine lines from the centre to (0, -half) rotated by the torso twist (vtable +0x3c of the machine at CockpitView+0x203) -/+ 0x2000; MFD bank frame 18 at centre - (3 << XCoordShift, 0). Sets the plot scale +0x2c = the range +0x30 / the half-height, so a contact at the range lands on the rim. Each contact ({x, y, colour} from +0x68, count +0x518) lands at centre + offset / scale: with XCoordShift 0 it is one pixel through Gfx_PlotPixel with the pen in its colour; otherwise, with the brush in fill mode (0), Raster_DrawEllipse over contact +/- 2 in DAT_004d3c26's colour and then over contact +/- 1 in its own. MFD frame 16 over the selected contact (+0x51c), offset -(2 << XCoordShift) on both axes.

entries.name: MfdRadarContact_ElementCtor
entries.description: (contact): returns its argument. The per-element constructor MfdRadarScreen_Ctor hands Rtl_VectorNew for the scanner's 100 12-byte contact entries at +0x68 (PUSH 0x43f5cd at 0043e744; element size 0xc, count 0x64).

entries.name: MfdFlashCommScreen_Ctor
entries.description: (screen, rect, display): the FLASH COMM screen's constructor. MFDisplay_Ctor, then MFDFlashCommVtable at +0 and the display at +0x10. The row block +0x39-+0x45 is the rect's top-left + (2 << XCoordShift, 0xd << YCoordShift) to + (0x60 << XCoordShift, 0x3a << YCoordShift), both corners then moved in by 1 << XCoordShift on both axes. Six 0x25-byte rows at +0x14, each Label_CtorWithAltFont(label, ColorSchemePanels[1] DAT_0049b0b0, 1) placed by Label_SetRect with flags 1 and the x margin 2 << XCoordShift over the block's width from top to top + (7 << YCoordShift), top stepping by that amount, with the hotkey font +0x21 = ColorSchemePanels[2] (DAT_0049b0b4) and the fill +0x1d = 0x11; clears the six state bytes from +0x2c and the byte +0x36, and sets the int16 +0x37 to -1. See docs/retail/simulation/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdFlashCommScreen_Paint
entries.description: MFDFlashComm vtable +0x00 (0049c36c): floods the row block (+0x39) with Raster_FillRect under the brush {0, 0x11} at the render context's +0x22c, copies the current selection (the first dword of the block at +8) into +0x32, then for each of the six rows sets its label's font -- 0049b0c4 when the row's state byte (+0x2c+i) has bit 0, 0049b0b8 for the selected row, 0049b0b0 otherwise -- and its text and hotkey index from the tables at 004d132c/004d1374 (index +3 when the state byte has bit 1) through Label_SetTextWithHotkey, and draws the selected row's plate with MfdFlashCommScreen_DrawRowPlate.

entries.name: MfdFlashCommScreen_Update
entries.description: MFDFlashComm vtable +0x04 (0049c36c): when the selection (the first dword of the block at +8) differs from +0x32, the force byte +0x36 is set, or the int16 +0x37 is not -1: repaints the old row (+0x37 when not -1, else +0x32) in ColorSchemePanels[1] (0049b0b0) with MfdFlashCommScreen_DrawRowPlate(screen, row, 1) and Label_SetTextWithHotkey, then makes the selection current at +0x32 and repaints it in [3] (0049b0b8) with its text and MfdFlashCommScreen_DrawRowPlate(screen, row, 0), each followed by Widget_DrawToCockpit(1, the label's rect, 0), and clears +0x36. Sets +0x37 to -1 in every case.

entries.name: MfdFlashComm_SelectedVerb
entries.description: The STRINGS0 group 0 verb the FLASH COMM page's selected row names: the row index at screen+0x32, plus 3 when that row's own state byte at screen+0x2c+row has bit 1 set. Only rows 4 and 5 ever have that bit set (MfdFlashComm_ToggleRowVariant refuses any other row), so the page sends verbs 0-5, 7 and 8. Args derived from disassembly: [EBP+8] only.

entries.name: MfdFlashComm_SetScreenRow
entries.description: (screen, row) copies screen +0x32 into the previous-row word +0x37, then stores row at +0x32. Seven calls from MfdFlashComm_HandleAltKey.

entries.name: MfdFlashComm_ToggleRowVariant
entries.description: (screen): for selected row (+0x32) 4 or 5 only, flips bit 1 of that row's state byte at screen+0x2c+row and sets +0x36; any other row is left alone. MfdFlashComm_SelectedVerb adds 3 to the verb of a row with that bit set.

entries.name: MfdFlashComm_ResetRow
entries.description: (screen, row) ANDs the row state byte +0x2c+row with 1 (clears the second-verb bit 1, keeps bit 0) and restores the row label's hotkey font +0x21 to ColorSchemePanels[2] CPRED (0049b0b4). No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: MfdFlashComm_DisableRow
entries.description: (screen, row) ORs bit 0 into the row state byte +0x2c+row and sets the row label's hotkey font +0x21 to ColorSchemePanels[6] CPOFF (0049b0c4). No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: MfdFlashCommScreen_DrawRowPlate
entries.description: (screen, row, erase): blits the selected-row plate at the top-left of row label row (rows past 6 map to row - 3) from the MFD bitmap bank at 0049cbcc, through VideoMode_BlitBitmap: frame 13 when erase is set, otherwise 11 plus the press byte (+0x1b) of the widget at the MFD's +0x40, XMIT. Callers found by es2_xref: MfdFlashCommScreen_Paint, MfdFlashCommScreen_Update (twice) and MfdButton_SetCaption.

entries.name: MfdMissileViewScreen_Ctor
entries.description: (screen, rect): the MISSILE CAM screen's constructor. MFDisplay_Ctor, then MFDMissileViewVtable at +0, the rect copied to 004d1ac8-004d1ad4. +0x10 = a 0x239-byte GLViewport (GLViewport_Ctor) whose rect +0x210-+0x21c is the rect with +0x218 less 1 and whose origin +0x220/+0x224 is -(w >> 1), -(h >> 1); the clip block 004d18ac gets the count 1, the region pointer 004d1ab4 and at 004d1ab8-004d1ac4 the viewport's rect, the viewport's +0x208 = 2, the block's 0x81 dwords are copied over the viewport's +4 and its +0x20c cleared. +0x14 = a 0x4e-byte camera: View_Ctor(camera, the viewport, 7, 0x80, two zero triples), CAMVtable at +0, and +0x32, +0x4a, +0x36, +0x48, +0x46 and +0x44 cleared. Four 0x21-byte labels at +0x33-+0x3f, Label_Ctor(label, DAT_0049b0b4, 1) placed by Label_SetRect with flags 2 and zero margins over the rect's top-left plus the x and y of the int16 tables 0049c374 and 0049c37c to that point plus the width and height of 0049c384 and 0049c38c, each shifted by VideoMode_XCoordShift or VideoMode_YCoordShift; label 2 (+0x3b) then takes DAT_0049b0b8 and the fill DAT_004d3c0a, and the byte +0x45 is cleared. See docs/retail/simulation/mfd.md, 'MFDMissileView -- mode 5'.

entries.name: MfdMissileViewScreen_Paint
entries.description: The MISSILE CAM screen's draw: the code pointer stored first in the vtable at 0049c449 that MfdMissileViewScreen_Ctor installs. A nonzero DAT_0049c398 starts a flash: when it differs from the screen's copy at +0x45 it stamps a deadline 0x1e coarse ticks ahead at +0x46, and until then each paint toggles the byte at +0x20 and fills the screen rect (DAT_004d1ac8) with COLORS.DAT id 16 (DAT_004d3c20) or id 19 (DAT_004d3c26) alternately and returns; at the deadline it clears the copy and DAT_0049c398. With DAT_0049c394 set it walks the effect pool (Pool_Prev) for that round: gone, it clears DAT_0049c394; found, the camera takes the round's position (+0x26/+0x2a/+0x2e) plus Q14(500, cos h) in x and Q14(500, cos(h - 0x4000)) in y, h being the heading at +0x10 -- 500 units along the round's own X axis, to its right, not along its heading -- and the round's euler triple (+0xc/+0x10), and the world is drawn from there into the screen's own render context, installed with Raster_InstallRenderContext, through the screen's view (+0x14), installed with Raster_InstallViewProjection so that the pass projects and picks every level of detail at that view's perspective shift from the camera: fill id 16 one column short of the rect's right edge, Scene_SubmitFrameObjects with ViewObjectPtr swapped to the camera, Terrain_SetupVisibleRegion and Scene_DrawTerrain with TerrainTexturingEnabled forced 0 and shade mode 004aab30 forced 1, then two Raster_DrawLine calls through the centre (full width, full height) and a ring-mode Raster_DrawEllipse of radius half the centre's y, all in id 19, with the cockpit shake offset taken out of the context rect for the pass. With DAT_0049c394 clear it fills the rect with palette index 0x11 and sets the labels from STRINGS0 group 35: NONE in label 1 when CockpitView_SumLauncherCounts is 0, else READY TO and LAUNCH in labels 0 and 1; LOCK in label 3, in ColorSchemePanels[0] on id 4 while the gunsight's +0xd6 (mech+0x9b, lock) is clear, else in [3] on id 19 or id 9 by coarse-tick bit 0x20. See docs/retail/simulation/mfd.md, 'MFDMissileView -- mode 5'.

entries.name: MfdMissileViewScreen_Update
entries.description: MFDMissileView vtable +0x04 (0049c449): raises the repaint counter +0x43 to 2 when DAT_0049c394, +0x1c, or the cockpit view's +0x1f5 object's +0xd6 byte is set; at 2 runs the screen's own slot +0x00 (MfdMissileViewScreen_Paint), at 1 Widget_DrawToCockpit(0, 004d1ac8), decrementing the counter either way.

entries.name: CockpitView_SumLauncherCounts
entries.description: Calls _strlen(DAT_004d16e8) and discards the result, then over CockpitViewInstance's weapon gauges (+0x70 array, count +0x98) calls slot +0x60 of each set gauge's set mount (gauge+0xbd) with (mount, the address of an int16 n) and adds n when the call returns other than 5; returns the sum.

entries.name: MfdMissileViewScreen_BlinkLockLabel
entries.description: (screen): flips the MISSILE CAM screen's +0x44 with coarse-tick bit 0x20 and, on each flip, re-fonts label 3 (+0x3f) in ColorSchemePanels[3] on a plate of COLORS.DAT id 9 (bit set) or id 19 (bit clear), returning 1; 0 when nothing changed. The same blink MfdMissileViewScreen_Paint applies to the LOCK label, latched in a byte. es2_xref.py finds no branch to it and no stored pointer.

entries.name: MfdMissileView_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser of the MFD missile-cam module (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7b3a, priority 0x20): constructs the global GLRectangleRegion at maybe_MfdMissileView_ClipRegion (004d1ab0) in place -- vptr through 004a6a08, 004a3380, 004a33a8 to GLRectangleRegion's 004a327c, with the RTL destructor count incremented three times and +4 set to 0. MfdMissileViewScreen_Ctor writes its rect at +8..+0x14 and stores 004d1ab4 at 004d18b0. MfdMissileView_StaticDtor undoes the count.

entries.name: MfdMissileView_StaticDtor
entries.description: MfdMissileView_StaticInit's _EXIT_ routine (Borland _EXIT_ entry 004a7c36): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr three times, the inlined destructor chain of the region at maybe_MfdMissileView_ClipRegion (004d1ab0).

entries.name: MfdMapScreen_Ctor
entries.description: (screen, insetRect): the NAV MAP screen's constructor (mode 2). MFDisplay_Ctor, then MFDNavMapVtable (0049c4be) at +0; saves the installed render context (006c5ff4); a 0x239-byte GLViewport (Mem_New, GLViewport_Ctor) at +0x10; the rect's four dwords at +0x18..+0x24; the viewport's +0x220/+0x224 = -((x1 - x0) >> 1), -((y1 - y0) >> 1) and +0x208 = 1; a 0x22-byte view at +0x14, View_Ctor(view, the viewport, 8, 0x100, position (0, 0, 0), MfdMapScreen_ViewAngles (0049c454)); reinstalls the saved context with Raster_InstallRenderContext. No labels.

entries.name: MfdMapScreen_PaintNoOp
entries.description: MFDNavMap vtable +0x00 (0049c4be): an empty body. The map draws from its per-frame slot +0x04, MfdMapScreen_Paint.

entries.name: MfdMapScreen_Paint
entries.description: NAV MAP update slot, MFDNavMap vtable +0x04: returns at once while CockpitViewManagerPublished's byte +0x1c (the view-change flag) is set. Floods the rect +4 with the brush {0, COLORS.DAT id 19 (004d3c26)} at the installed context's +0x22c (Raster_FillRect); sets the viewport (+0x10) rect +0x210 to +0x18..+0x24 less the installed context's +0x220/+0x224, copies the context's 0x81 dwords from +4 and its +0x208 over the viewport's, and installs it. Calls View_GetActiveObject and drops the result. The view (+0x14) gets position (the cockpit machine's +0x26, +0x2a, 200000) and angles (MfdMapScreen_ViewAngles' first int16, 0, 0); the viewport's +0x20c = 0; Raster_InstallViewProjection(view); HddMap_DrawTerrain(the machine's int16 heading +0x10). Then +0x20c = 1, the pen {0, COLORS.DAT id 16 (004d3c20)} at the viewport's +0x228, and Raster_DrawLine from (-(1 << VideoMode_XCoordShift), 0) to (1 << it, 0) and from (0, -(1 << VideoMode_YCoordShift)) to (0, 1 << it); reinstalls the saved context and calls Widget_DrawToCockpit(1, rect, 0).

entries.name: MfdMapScreen_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser of the MFD nav-map module (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7b40, priority 0x20): writes the int16 triple {0xc000, 0, 0} to MfdMapScreen_ViewAngles (0049c454).

entries.name: WeaponGauge_Ctor
entries.description: (gauge, block, cockpit, mount): the weapon row gauge's base constructor. PanelGauge_Ctor(gauge, block, cockpit), WeaponGaugeVtable at +0; loads the pweapons bank into 0049c4d0 and the wpn_dmg bank into 0049c4d4 when each is 0 (folder by VideoMode_UseHiResBanks, ResourcePath_BuildFolderName, Resource_Load), and with wpn_dmg builds once the two-sequence frame table from the start frames WeaponGauge_WipeFirstFrames and the end frames at 0049c4cc, each frame held 1, at 004d1ad8/004d1adc; stores the mount at +0xbd and 0 in the bytes +0xb1 and +0xc1; a 0x2a-byte SpriteSequence_Init over wpn_dmg and that table at +0x6c; the int16 +0x74 = 0; the dropout ranges +0x7c..+0x88 = 120, 360, 180, 1800; the byte +0x8e = 0.

entries.name: WeaponGauge_MountProjectileType
entries.description: (gauge): the int16 +0 (the type) of the PROJ.DAT record the gauge's mount (+0xbd) holds at +0x20, or -1 with no mount or no record.

entries.name: WeaponGauge_MountProjectileSubtype
entries.description: (gauge): the int16 +2 (the subtype id) of the PROJ.DAT record the gauge's mount (+0xbd) holds at +0x20, or -1 with no mount or no record.

entries.name: EnergyWeaponGauge_Ctor
entries.description: (gauge, block, cockpit, row, mount): the energy row's constructor. WeaponGauge_Ctor(gauge, block, cockpit, mount); ChainedWeaponGaugeVtable (0049c93c), the int16 row at +0xd9, EnergyWeaponGaugeVtable (0049c91c). Child 0, a 0x67-byte ChainedWeaponSelectGadget_Ctor(child, block, gauge, row, bit row of the block's byte +0x40), at +0x18, registered with Widget_RegisterClickable in the root widget at +0 of CockpitViewInstance; strncpy of 12 bytes of WeaponMount_GetDisplayName(mount) to +0xb1; child 1, a 0x7e-byte WeaponSliderGadget_Ctor(child, the value field x0 + (0x24 .. 0x35 << VideoMode_XCoordShift), y0 .. y0 + (5 << VideoMode_YCoordShift), mirrored from x1 when the flag is set, gauge, the block's dword +0x3c), at +0x1c, registered; +0x68 = 2; +0xc6 = 0x400; _memset(+0xc2, 0, 0x17), which clears the 0x400.

entries.name: EnergyWeaponGauge_Paint
entries.description: EnergyWeaponGauge vtable +0x04 (0049c91c): while +0x8c is set, paints the row's two children (+0x18, +0x1c) through slot +0x00 of their tables at +0x17. AmmoWeaponGauge_Paint is the ammunition row's.

entries.name: EnergyWeaponGauge_Update
entries.description: The energy row's per-frame update, vtable +0x08. Returns unless CockpitView_RectCornerVisible(+4) passes or CockpitViewManagerPublished's +0x1c is set, and the row is armed (+0x8c). Before the power-up is done (+0x8d) it runs EnergyWeaponGauge_PowerUpFill; once done, with +0x8e clear and the rect on screen, it calls its own slot +0x04, sets +0x8e and returns. Then Player_DependentCondition(2) into +0x74 and PanelGauge_TickDropout when nonzero; when +0x76 has just turned 0 (differs from +0x77), both children's slot +0x04; and both children's slot +0x0c.

entries.name: EnergyWeaponGauge_SetState
entries.description: EnergyWeaponGauge vtable +0x10 (gauge, block), the write-back twin of EnergyWeaponGauge_GetState over the 0x17-byte state block at +0xc2. Block+0x04, the charge bar's slider position, when it differs from +0xc6: stored there and passed to the slider (child +0x1c) through slot +0x14 of its table at +0x17. Block+0x00, the bar's fill, when it differs from +0xc2: stored there and at the slider's +0x7a (what WeaponSliderGadget_Paint fills the bar to), and at +0xdb, the live value EnergyWeaponGauge_PowerUpFill ramps toward, while the power-up is not done (+0x8d clear). The destroyed byte (+0x11) puts both children's state (+0x1b) to 2 or back to 0, deferred through +0xc1 while CockpitView_GetShakeOffset's +4 is non-zero. Bytes +0x14..+0x16 go to +0xd6..+0xd8. Repaints (slot +0x04) whichever children changed.

entries.name: EnergyWeaponGauge_GetState
entries.description: Returns gauge+0xc2, the 0x17-byte display state block that WeaponMount_PushEnergyGaugeState and 0040e0e0 copy into a local.

entries.name: EnergyWeaponGauge_PowerUpFill
entries.description: An energy weapon row's power-up fill: the charge bar shows min(elapsed * 0x19, live) against the coarse ticks since the row was armed, then the live value (+0xdb) and done from elapsed >= 0x33. Repaints both children.

entries.name: EnergyWeaponGauge_OnChildClick
entries.description: (gauge, child, value): the energy row's vtable +0x00. Finds the child among the +0x68 children from +0x18. Child 0: with bit 1 of value set, WeaponMounts_ToggleChainMember(the cockpit machine's (CockpitViewInstance +0x203) manager +0x202, the int16 row +0xd9); otherwise CockpitView_ArmWeaponByGauge(+0x14, gauge). Child 1, the charge bar: stores value, clamped to 0..0x400, at +0xc6.
entries.signature: void __cdecl EnergyWeaponGauge_OnChildClick(int gauge, int child, uint value)

entries.name: AmmoWeaponGauge_Ctor
entries.description: (gauge, block, cockpit, row, mount): the ammunition row's constructor. WeaponGauge_Ctor(gauge, block, cockpit, mount); ChainedWeaponGaugeVtable, the int16 row at +0xd9, ProjectileWeaponGaugeVtable (0049c8fc). The mirror flag is bit row of the block's byte +0x30. The value rect +0xdf..+0xeb is x0 + (0x24 << VideoMode_XCoordShift) .. x0 + (0x35 << it), y0 .. y0 + (5 << VideoMode_YCoordShift), or with the flag x1 - (0x35 << it) .. x1 - (0x24 << it). Child 0, a 0x67-byte ChainedWeaponSelectGadget_Ctor(child, block, gauge, row, flag), at +0x18, registered with Widget_RegisterClickable in the root widget of CockpitViewInstance; strncpy of 12 bytes of WeaponMount_GetDisplayName(mount) to +0xb1; a 0x21-byte label, Label_Ctor(label, ColorSchemePanels[11] (0049b0d8), 1), placed by Label_SetRect over +0xdf with zero margins and flags 1, or 4 with the flag, fill +0x1d = 0x2e, at +0xdb; +0x68 = 1; _memset(+0xc2, 0, 0x17).

entries.name: AmmoWeaponGauge_Paint
entries.description: Ammunition row's paint, while the row is armed (+0x8c): paints the select gadget (+0x18) through its slot +0x00, then, unless the row is dark (+0x76) or mid-wipe (+0x6c sequencer not idle), its value label (+0xdb) is off screen, the select gadget's state +0x1b is 2 or the destroyed byte +0xd3 is set, itoa's the round count at +0xc2 into the label in ColorSchemePanels[10] WHITE when +0xd6 is set and [11] GRAY otherwise.

entries.name: AmmoWeaponGauge_Update
entries.description: The ammunition row's per-frame update, vtable +0x08. Returns unless CockpitView_RectCornerVisible(+4) passes or CockpitViewManagerPublished's +0x1c is set, and the row is armed (+0x8c). Sets +0x8d to 1 and +0xb0 to 2. With +0x8e clear and the rect on screen, calls its own slot +0x04, sets +0x8e and returns. Then Player_DependentCondition(2) into +0x74 and PanelGauge_TickDropout when nonzero; when +0x76 has just turned 0, child 0's slot +0x04 and +0xb0 = 2; child 0's slot +0x0c. Unless +0x76 is set or the +0x6c sequencer is busy (SpriteSequence_State): +0xb0 = 2 when child 0's byte +0x1f is set; at +0xb0 = 1, Widget_DrawToCockpit(0, the label +0xdb's rect +4, 0) unless +0xd3 is set, and +0xb0 lowered; at 2 with the label's rect on screen, unless +0xd3 is set, _itoa(+0xc2, 10) into the label (Label_SetText) in ColorSchemePanels[10] when +0xd6 is set and [11] otherwise, and +0xb0 lowered.

entries.name: AmmoWeaponGauge_SetState
entries.description: ProjectileWeaponGauge vtable +0x10 (0049c8fc), (gauge, block): EnergyWeaponGauge_SetState's ammunition twin. A new dword 0 (the round count) goes to +0xc2 and marks the row dirty (+0xb0 = 2). A new byte +0x11 goes to +0xd3 and sets the select gadget's (+0x18) state +0x1b to 2 or 0. New bytes +0x14/+0x15/+0x16 go to +0xd6/+0xd7/+0xd8. Any of the byte changes also invalidates the select gadget (its slot +0x04) and marks the row dirty.

entries.name: AmmoWeaponGauge_GetState
entries.description: Returns gauge+0xc2, the display state block WeaponMount_PushAmmoGaugeState copies into a local from the mount's +0x77 gauge. The ammunition twin of EnergyWeaponGauge_GetState.

entries.name: AmmoWeaponGauge_OnChildClick
entries.description: (gauge, child, value): the ammunition row's vtable +0x00. Finds the child among the +0x68 children from +0x18; for a later child returns its index less 1. Child 0: with bit 1 of value set, WeaponMounts_ToggleChainMember(the cockpit machine's manager +0x202, the int16 row +0xd9); otherwise CockpitView_ArmWeaponByGauge(+0x14, gauge); then +0xb0 = 2.
entries.signature: uint __cdecl AmmoWeaponGauge_OnChildClick(int gauge, int child, uint value)

entries.name: PodGauge_Ctor
entries.description: The weapon-row gauge class for equipment pods (vtable 0049c8d0), built via CockpitView_CreatePodGauge. Builds its click target as the plain WeaponSelectGadget (WeaponSelectGadget_Ctor), not the chained class, so it has no plate, no state box and no value field: its name label spans x0+11..x0+53 of the .GAU hardpoint rect, left-aligned (right-aligned when the slot-mask bit mirrors it), and its 11-char name buffer is seeded with a literal space, then the mount name, then STRINGS0.STR group 3 (' POD') appended into whatever room is left -- 'SHIELD' becomes ' SHIELD POD'.

entries.name: PodGauge_Paint
entries.description: PodGauge vtable +4, shared by all three pod gauge classes. While armed (+0x8c) it first runs the select gadget's (+0x18) paint slot, which for this plain class is WeaponSelectGadget_PaintUnderlay -- so a pod row has no PWEAPONS plate. Then, unless dark or mid-wipe and when the name label (+0xca) is on screen, picks the label's font and ink from the two state bytes: the destroyed byte at +0xc3 wins and prints the offline text centred across the label from x0+11 to the gauge's edge, and sets the select gadget's state +0x1b to 2 (after that gadget has painted), and failing that the button byte at +0xc2 selects the gray font 0049b0d8 with ink 0x2e when off and the dark font 0049b0dc with HudColorTable id 12 when on. That re-fonting is the only feedback a pod row gives, since it has no state box.

entries.name: PodGauge_Update
entries.description: Pod row's per-frame update: the power-up slot, then the sensor dropout, then the name label's repaint, held back while the row is dark or mid-wipe.

entries.name: PodGauge_SetStateBlock
entries.description: PodGauge vtable +0x14. Writes the caller's 8 bytes over gauge+0xc2 and marks the widget dirty, but only when the destroyed byte at +0xc3 has changed -- the button byte at +0xc2 cannot make this class repaint. TogglePodGauge_SetStateBlock compares both bytes.

entries.name: PodGauge_GetStateBlock
entries.description: PodGauge vtable +0x18, shared by every pod gauge class: returns gauge+0xc2, an 8-byte block whose byte 0 is the button and byte 1 the mount's destroyed flag.

entries.name: PodGauge_OnClick
entries.description: PodGauge vtable slot 0 (0049c8d0), reached the usual way -- the row's WeaponSelectGadget child forwards its click to the owner's slot 0, after sounding Widget_ClickSound. It sets the repaint byte at +0xb0 and returns. A Shield, Targeting or Energy pod row therefore clicks and sounds but holds no on/off state; TogglePodGauge_OnClick is the ECM/Turbo override that does.

entries.name: TogglePodGauge_Ctor
entries.description: PodGauge_Ctor followed by the vtable 0049c8a4 -- the pod gauge row that carries an on/off state. Built for the ECM pod directly and for the Turbo pod through TurboPodGauge_Ctor; no other pod gets it.
entries.signature: void * __cdecl TogglePodGauge_Ctor(void *gauge, int *rect, int cockpitView, short hardpoint, void *pod)

entries.name: TogglePodGauge_SetStateBlock
entries.description: TogglePodGauge vtable +0x14: PodGauge_SetStateBlock's override, repainting when either the button byte at +0xc2 or the destroyed byte at +0xc3 has changed rather than the destroyed byte alone.

entries.name: TogglePodGauge_OnClick
entries.description: TogglePodGauge vtable slot 0 -- structurally identical to ShieldsGauge_OnClick: searches its own child table at +0x18 (count at +0x68) for the widget that was clicked and, for child 0, XORs the button byte at +0xc2 and marks the row dirty. This is the whole of a pod's on/off toggle, and only the ECM and Turbo rows have it.

entries.name: TurboPodGauge_Ctor
entries.description: TogglePodGauge_Ctor followed by the vtable 0049c878 and one extra child widget -- the Turbo pod's charge bar over pod+0x7d.
entries.signature: void * __cdecl TurboPodGauge_Ctor(void *gauge, int *rect, int cockpitView, short hardpoint, void *pod)

entries.name: TurboPodGauge_SetStateBlock
entries.description: EnergyPodGauge (the Turbo Pod row, TurboPodGauge_Ctor) vtable +0x14, (gauge, block): when the button byte, the destroyed byte or the charge dword (block+4) differs from +0xc2/+0xc3/+0xc6, copies the block's first two dwords to +0xc2/+0xc6, also stores the charge in +0xe2 while the power-up fill is not done (+0x8d clear), and marks the row dirty (+0xb0 = 2).

entries.name: TurboPodGauge_OnClick
entries.description: EnergyPodGauge vtable +0x00, (gauge, child): when child is the row's first child (+0x18), XORs the button byte +0xc2 and marks the row dirty -- TogglePodGauge_OnClick's toggle.

entries.name: TurboPodGauge_Paint
entries.description: EnergyPodGauge vtable +0x04: while +0x8c is set, paints the select gadget (+0x18) and, unless +0x76 is set, the sprite sequence at +0x6c is running (SpriteSequence_State), the label's rect is off screen or the gadget is hidden (+0x1b == 2), sets the label (+0xca): a destroyed pod (+0xc3) gets the text at DAT_004d13c8 and hides the gadget; otherwise the frame and colour for the button's state (+0xc2). A live pod also paints its charge bar (+0xde) to +0xc6.

entries.name: TurboPodGauge_Update
entries.description: EnergyPodGauge vtable +0x08: PodGauge_Update(gauge).

entries.name: TurboPodGauge_PowerUpFill
entries.description: The Turbo Pod row's power-up fill, the same ramp as EnergyWeaponGauge_PowerUpFill over the pod's raw charge (+0xe2 into +0xc6): min(elapsed * 0x19, live) until elapsed > 0x32, then the live value and done. On a 2500-unit bar it climbs to 1250 and then jumps.

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_Ctor
entries.description: (panel, gauBlock, owner): the console button panel under the weapon rows, from .GAU offset 468. Installs WeaponRangeGaugeVtable and builds FOUR WeaponRangeSelectGadget children from the rects at 484/500/516/532, each offset by the block's first pair, registering each with Widget_RegisterClickable in index order -- the chain selector, LINK, TRACK, and a fourth whose rect is zero in every retail .GAU -- with a centred Label over its rect at child +0x2c and its index at child +0x28. Sets the child count +0x68 to 4 and clears the auto-track latch +0xb3. When the piloted machine's type record sets the flyer flag (+0x50), puts child 2 (TRACK, panel +0x20) in widget state 2 (+0x1b), which hit-testing passes over, ConsoleButton_Paint skips, and ConsoleButtons_ToggleAutoTrack refuses.

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_SetChainNumber
entries.description: (panel, chain): stores the int16 chain number at panel+0xb1 and does nothing else; the caption is repainted elsewhere. WeaponMounts_SetChain, Gau_WeaponButtonsWidget, ConsoleButtons_SetStateBlock and ConsoleButtons_OnChildClick call it.

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_ToggleAutoTrack
entries.description: The console buttons manager's auto-track toggle, reached from ConsoleButtons_SetStateBlock, ConsoleButtons_OnChildClick's child 2, and Sim_DispatchCommand's command 0x14 (and command 0xe while the latch is set). Refuses when the TRACK widget (+0x20) is in state 2 (+0x1b), returning 0. Otherwise flips the manager's +0xb3, copies the new state into the TRACK widget's +0x40 and repaints it through its vtable, withdraws both 0x26 AUTO TRACKING ENGAGED and 0x27 AUTO TRACKING DISABLED from the computer's message port, posts the one the mode just became -- the same shape as Mech_ToggleRadarMode -- and returns 1 in the low byte.

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_SetLinkLatch
entries.description: Stores the LINK button's latch byte at panel+0xb4 and calls WeaponMounts_ToggleLink. Called from the button's own click handler and again from ConsoleButtons_SetStateBlock when the manager writes the byte back cleared -- two of the three toggles one press produces.

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_Paint
entries.description: WeaponRangeGauge vtable +0x04 (0049c85c), the console-button row: paints its four children (+0x18..+0x24) through slot +0x00 of each child's table at +0x17.

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_Update
entries.description: WeaponRangeGauge vtable +0x08 (0049c85c): runs each of its four children's slot +0x0c (FlushDeferredPaint).

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_SetStateBlock
entries.description: The write-back half of ConsoleButtons_GetStateBlock: applies each of the three fields that differs from the panel's own copy. The manager clears the LINK byte before writing back, so this sees a change and calls ConsoleButtons_SetLinkLatch again -- the third of the three toggles one LINK press produces.

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_GetStateBlock
entries.description: Copies the console panel's three live fields -- chain number (+0xb1, short), auto-track latch (+0xb3) and LINK latch (+0xb4) -- into the scratch block at 004d1ae0 for WeaponMounts_PerFrameUpdate to read.

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_OnChildClick
entries.description: The console button panel's child-click slot, switching on the child index: 0 advances the chain number at panel+0xb1 (wrapping at 3) and repaints the caption, 1 calls ConsoleButtons_SetLinkLatch, 2 toggles auto-track. Reached identically by a mouse click and by a key, since ConsoleButtons_HandleCommand presses the same children.

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_HandleCommand
entries.description: The console button panel's command slot: scancode 0x26 (L) presses child 1, the LINK button; 0x29 (backquote) presses child 0, the chain button. The pair of literals is what identifies the whole command-code space as PC set-1 scancodes.

entries.name: WeaponSelectGadget_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for WeaponSelectGadget, the weapon-row leaf without chain membership: Widget_CtorRect on the .GAU rect, the PanelSelectGadget then WeaponSelectGadget vtables at +0x17 with their PanelGadget mixins at +0x20, param_3 at +0x24, the slot at +0x28, and +0x1b and +0x1d zeroed. Builds the slot-number Label at +0x40 in font DAT_0049b0d4, its rect 2 to 5 GAU units (each shifted by VideoMode_XCoordShift) in from the gadget's left edge, or from its right edge when param_5 is set, and 0 to 5 down, centred (Label_SetRect flag 2). Writes the slot's digit, (slot + 1) % 10 + '0', to +0x44 and 0 to +0x46, so row 10 prints 0. Callers found by es2_xref: PodGauge_Ctor, and ChainedWeaponSelectGadget_Ctor as its base constructor. Class name from the descriptor record at 00443283.

entries.name: WeaponSelectGadget_PaintUnderlay
entries.description: Paints a weapon row's underlay and slot number, when CockpitView_RectCornerVisible passes the gadget. Does nothing while the owning gauge (+0x4) is dark (+0x76) or its sprite sequence at +0x6c is running (the wipe), or while the gauge's armed byte +0x8c is clear. Otherwise blits the first frame of the bitmap DAT_0049c4d4 holds (WPN_DMG frame 0, the row background) at the gadget's rect, sets the slot Label's (+0x40) colour to ColorSchemePanels[10], or [11] when +0x1b is 0, and sets its text to the digit buffer at +0x44.

entries.name: WeaponSelectGadget_FlushDeferredPaint
entries.description: WeaponSelectGadgetVtable +0x0c: the same body as MFDStateGadget_FlushDeferredPaint -- at pending-paint count +0x1f 1, Widget_DrawToCockpit(0, gadget, 0); at 2, slot 0 of the vtable at +0x17; decrementing it either way.

entries.name: WeaponSelectGadget_OnClick
entries.description: WeaponSelectGadgetVtable +0x08 (gadget, flags): unconditionally calls the owner's (+0x24) vtable slot 0 with (owner, gadget, flags), then slot 1 of the vtable at +0x17 and slot 2 of the PanelGadget mixin at +0x20, which is Widget_ClickSound (00438e2c) -- so every press of a pod row clicks, by mouse or by number key through Widget_PressChild.

entries.name: ChainedWeaponSelectGadget_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for ChainedWeaponSelectGadget (object size 0x67), the clickable weapon row EnergyWeaponGauge_Ctor and AmmoWeaponGauge_Ctor build. Derives from WeaponSelectGadget, whose constructor it calls first; the extra level is what carries fire-chain membership, which is why PodGauge_Ctor builds the plain base class instead. Also builds the row's hardpoint state box and weapon-name label. Class name from the descriptor record at 0044333b.

entries.name: WeaponSelectGadget_Paint
entries.description: ChainedWeaponSelectGadgetVtable +0x00: paints one energy or ammunition row, when CockpitView_RectCornerVisible passes the gadget and the owning gauge (+0x4) is armed (+0x8c). Unless the gauge is dark (+0x76) or its wipe sequence (+0x6c) runs: WeaponSelectGadget_PaintUnderlay; the name label (+0x2c) from the gauge's 12-char buffer (+0xb1) in ColorSchemePanels[10] when the selected byte +0xd6 is set and [11] otherwise, or, with the destroyed byte +0xd3 set, the OFFLINE text (DAT_004d13c8) in [11], centred in the label widened to the gauge's own edge; the slot number (+0x40) again in [13] when selected and [11] otherwise; then the state box at +0x46 -- PWEAPONS frame 6 destroyed, frame 4 ready (+0xd8) or 5 not when selected or in the group (+0xd7), else a fill of palette 0x2e. Always, last: PWEAPONS frame 0 selected / 1 not at the gadget's rect less 1 << VideoMode_XCoordShift on both axes, the row plate's bezel.

entries.name: ChainedWeaponSelectGadget_FlushDeferredPaint
entries.description: ChainedWeaponSelectGadget's FlushDeferredPaint slot +0xc (vtable 0049c7dc), also reached by the jump at 004433ea. Counter +0x1f at 1: Widget_DrawToCockpit(0) on the gadget and on its second rect at +0x56; at 2: WeaponSelectGadget_PaintUnderlay and the Paint slot. Either way it decrements the counter.

entries.name: ChainedWeaponSelectGadget_OnClick
entries.description: ChainedWeaponSelectGadgetVtable +0x08: the same body as WeaponSelectGadget_OnClick, ending in the mixin's Widget_ClickSound -- so every press of a weapon row clicks, by mouse or by number key through Widget_PressChild.

entries.name: WeaponSliderGadget_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for WeaponSliderGadget (object size 0x7e; class name from the descriptor record at 004432df), a PanelHSliderGadget leaf: the energy weapon row's charge bar, child 1 of EnergyWeaponGauge_Ctor's gauge. Its last vtable stores are WeaponSliderGadgetVtable at +0x17 and WeaponSliderGadget_PanelSliderGadgetVtable at +0x3e. Built on SliderWidget_CtorBase, so it is a horizontal slider over 0..0x400 carrying the +0x1d drag flag, but no press reaches it: the row's ChainedWeaponSelectGadget is registered first and its hit rect, the whole .GAU hardpoint rect, contains the bar in every retail file. Drops the value field's top edge by one GAU unit, builds an LEDBarGraph over range 0x400 at +0x46, and then, when the byte it is handed is zero (as it is in every retail .GAU, where it lands in confirmed-zero padding), overwrites its three colour fields with raw palette indices 0x20 (even columns), 0x22 (odd) and 0x2e (remainder) -- not COLORS.DAT ids, which is why a capacitor bar is blue where the Master Energy Pool's meter is grey.

entries.name: WeaponSliderGadget_Paint
entries.description: WeaponSliderGadgetVtable +0x00, the energy row charge bar's paint: when the bar's rect is on screen, its state +0x1b is not 2 (destroyed), the owning gauge (+0x42) is neither dark (+0x76) nor mid-wipe (its +0x6c sequencer not idle) and is armed (+0x8c), it calls the LEDBarGraph at +0x46's slot +0x00 with the value at +0x7a -- the capacitor level EnergyWeaponGauge_SetState stores there -- then copies +0x7a to +0x4a and refreshes its cached span fields (+0x2e, +0x36, +0x6e).

entries.name: WeaponSliderGadget_FlushDeferredPaint
entries.description: WeaponSliderGadgetVtable +0x0c: calls slot 0 of the vtable at +0x17 when the pending-paint count +0x1f is 2, and does nothing at 1 and never decrements it.

entries.name: WeaponRangeSelectGadget_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for WeaponRangeSelectGadget (object size 0x41), the weapon-range gauge's button; derives from PanelStateGadget, so it latches. Built by ConsoleButtons_Ctor. Class name from the descriptor record at 00443223.

entries.name: ConsoleButton_Paint
entries.description: Paints one chain/link/auto-track console button, nothing when CockpitView_RectCornerVisible fails or the widget is in state 2 (+0x1b). By the kind field +0x28 (0 chain, 1 LINK, 2 TRACK): plate from frame 2 + n of the bank at 0049c4d0 (PWEAPONS; frame 2 unlit, solid palette index 34 = the retail blue at RGB (77,77,182); frame 3 lit, index 14 green), n being the state byte +0x1b for chain and LINK and the latch +0x40 for TRACK, blitted at the widget's own rect, then the caption into the label at +0x2c in ColorSchemePanels[10] WHITE when n is 0 and [12] DARK otherwise. The chain button's caption comes from the three-entry Roman-numeral table at 0049c71c ('I', 'II', 'III') indexed by the panel's chain number +0xb1, a literal .rdata table unrelated to the string file. LINK and TRACK read ConsoleButtonCaptions (004d13d0) indexed by the kind field, which SimStrings_LoadAll fills from STRINGS0.STR group 4.

entries.name: WeaponRangeSelectGadget_FlushDeferredPaint
entries.description: WeaponRangeSelectGadgetVtable +0x0c: the same body as WeaponSelectGadget_FlushDeferredPaint.

entries.name: WeaponRangeSelectGadget_OnClick
entries.description: WeaponRangeSelectGadgetVtable +0x08 (gadget, flags): when flags bit 0 is set, slot 2 of the sub-object at +0x20, then the owner's (+0x24) slot 0 with (owner, gadget, flags). No +0x17 repaint call and no state toggle.

entries.name: Gau_ShiftRects2
entries.description: (rects): VideoMode_ShiftRect on the first rect, then shifts the next 16-byte rect by VideoMode_XCoordShift / VideoMode_YCoordShift -- the same body as GauEnergyMeter_ApplyCoordShift. Gau_ShiftRects3, Gau_ShiftRects3Point and Gau_ShiftRects5 start with it.

entries.name: Gau_ShiftRects3
entries.description: (rects): Gau_ShiftRects2, then shifts the third rect (+0x20). Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets runs it on CockpitGauRecord+0x2d.

entries.name: Gau_ShiftRects3Point
entries.description: (rects): Gau_ShiftRects2, then shifts the third rect (+0x20) and the x0/y0 pair at +0x30. Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets runs it on CockpitGauRecord+0x41.

entries.name: Gau_ShiftRects5
entries.description: (rects): Gau_ShiftRects2, then shifts the three rects after it (+0x20, +0x30, +0x40). Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets runs it on CockpitGauRecord+0x59.

entries.name: GauWeaponButtons_ApplyCoordShift
entries.description: (rects): VideoMode_ShiftRect on the first rect, then shifts the four 16-byte rects after it left by VideoMode_XCoordShift (x) and VideoMode_YCoordShift (y). Gau_WeaponButtonsWidget runs it on the .GAU block at +0x1d4 (the panel and its four buttons).

entries.name: WeaponRangeSelectGadget_OnClickThunk
entries.description: The this-adjusting thunk at primary vtable +0x30 of WeaponRangeSelectGadget's vtable block, in the table for its PanelGadget subobject at +0x20: subtracts 0x20 from this and jumps to WeaponRangeSelectGadget_OnClick.

entries.name: WeaponRangeSelectGadget_FlushDeferredPaintThunk
entries.description: The this-adjusting thunk at primary vtable +0x28 of WeaponRangeSelectGadget's vtable block, in the table for its PanelGadget subobject at +0x20: subtracts 0x20 from this and jumps to WeaponRangeSelectGadget_FlushDeferredPaint.

entries.name: WeaponRangeSelectGadget_PaintThunk
entries.description: The this-adjusting thunk at primary vtable +0x24 of WeaponRangeSelectGadget's vtable block, in the table for its PanelGadget subobject at +0x20: subtracts 0x20 from this and jumps to ConsoleButton_Paint.

entries.name: WeaponSliderGadget_OnClickThunk
entries.description: The this-adjusting thunk at primary vtable +0x34 of WeaponSliderGadget's vtable block, in the table for its PanelSliderGadget subobject at +0x3e: subtracts 0x3e from this and jumps to HSliderGadget_OnClick.

entries.name: WeaponSliderGadget_FlushDeferredPaintThunk
entries.description: The this-adjusting thunk at primary vtable +0x2c of WeaponSliderGadget's vtable block, in the table for its PanelSliderGadget subobject at +0x3e: subtracts 0x3e from this and jumps to WeaponSliderGadget_FlushDeferredPaint.

entries.name: WeaponSliderGadget_PaintThunk
entries.description: The this-adjusting thunk at primary vtable +0x28 of WeaponSliderGadget's vtable block, in the table for its PanelSliderGadget subobject at +0x3e: subtracts 0x3e from this and jumps to WeaponSliderGadget_Paint.

entries.name: ChainedWeaponSelectGadget_OnClickThunk
entries.description: The this-adjusting thunk at primary vtable +0x30 of ChainedWeaponSelectGadget's vtable block, in the table for its PanelGadget subobject at +0x20: subtracts 0x20 from this and jumps to ChainedWeaponSelectGadget_OnClick.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_Ctor
entries.description: The real shield meter, called only by Gau_ShieldDisplayWidget (00432454) with .GAU offset 0x268=616. NOT an LED bar -- it loads no sprite bank and instead builds a 0x40-byte child per shield facing via ShieldsGauge_FacingCtor plus a text label via Label_Ctor/Label_SetRect (the same generic label constructors the .DFN font consumers use). That matches retail: nested green concentric boxes with a numeric readout above and below. The .GAU block at 616 is a zero header rect followed by four 16-byte rects at 632/648/664/680, all shifted by VideoMode_X/YCoordShift in ShieldsGauge_ApplyCoordShift. Distinct from EnergyPoolGauge_Ctor (00444d5c), which the earlier maybe_ShieldsGauge_Ctor name wrongly claimed was this widget.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_Paint
entries.description: ShieldsGauge's vtable+4 slot. Unconditionally calls ShieldsGauge_UpdateRingPalette and ShieldsGauge_UpdateReadouts.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_Update
entries.description: ShieldsGauge's per-frame update slot (vtable+8, called from the general HUD paint pass, not the click pipeline). Gated on visibility and a 'shields present' flag; when the dirty flag ShieldsGauge_SetStateBlock set (+0xb0==2) is pending, refreshes the ring palette and readouts and clears it. This is the bridge between Shield_BalanceInputRead's once-per-frame gameplay update and the HUD paint pass -- the click sets a flag, the gameplay tick consumes it into real sim state and a dirty bit, and this slot is what actually repaints from that bit.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_PowerUpFill
entries.description: The shield meter's power-up fill, called by ShieldsGauge_Update while armed and not done: each displayed facing (+0xb5, +0xb9) is the lesser of the coarse ticks since arming and the live value ShieldsGauge_SetStateBlock parked at +0xcc/+0xd0; sets done (+0x8d) once both match, and marks the gauge dirty.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_OnClick
entries.description: ShieldsGauge's own vtable slot 0 (per the same *param_1=&PTR_thisFunction ctor-assignment evidence used for MfdButton_OnClick). Searches its own +0x18/+0x68 child-pointer table (populated identically to MfdDisplay's, by ShieldsGauge_Ctor) for the clicked facing widget; index 0 (front) sets state byte +0xc2=1 clearing +0xc3, index 1 (rear) the reverse. Consumed once per frame by Shield_BalanceInputRead, not painted directly.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_SetStateBlock
entries.description: (gauge, block): write-back counterpart to ShieldsGauge_GetStateBlock (004438e0). Copies the 15-byte block over the gauge's +0xb5 (three dwords, a word and a byte); while the widget's power-up-done byte +0x8d is clear it moves the two reading dwords +0xb5 and +0xb9 to +0xcc and +0xd0 and zeroes them; and it sets +0xb0 to 2 when the block's first three dwords differ from those the gauge held.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_GetStateBlock
entries.description: (gauge): returns gauge + 0xb5, the start of ShieldsGauge's 15-byte state block: front reading, rear reading, balance, then the two click flags at block +0xd and +0xe.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_UpdateRingPalette
entries.description: Computes the shield meter's six ring colours and installs them at palette index 0x42 (66-71). Per facing (charge at +0xb5 and +0xb9) three rings light in turn: ring 1 from 0, ring 2 from 0x100 at twice the rate, ring 3 from 0x180 at four times, each as base * t >> 10 in Q10. Above 0x400 the same three tracks run again over base + (bright - base) * t. Colour immediates at 0049c9cb..0049c9d0: base RGB6 (25,59,23), bright (59,59,23). Install order is the stack layout, so 66-68 are the first facing outermost-first and 69-71 the second. At the nominal half charge all six resolve to RGB (48,116,44), matching the retail screenshot's meter.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_UpdateReadouts
entries.description: Fills ShieldsGauge's two numeric labels (object +0xc4 and +0xc8) from the fore/aft balance at +0xbd: itoa(balance * 200 >> 10), truncating, and itoa(200 - that). An even split reads 100 and 100; one forward press (614) reads 119/81 and one rear press (410) 80/120.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_FacingCtor
entries.description: Builds one 0x40-byte shield-facing child for ShieldsGauge_Ctor, one per facing, over the .GAU rects at 632 and 648. Draws no geometry: its paint slot (ShieldFacing_Paint) only tests visibility. The nested concentric rings the retail meter shows are painted into the herc's own canopy art in palette indices 66-71; the gauge animates them by rewriting those six palette slots (ShieldsGauge_UpdateRingPalette).

entries.name: ShieldFacing_Paint
entries.description: A shield-facing child's Paint slot. Its whole body is a CockpitView_RectCornerVisible call whose result it discards: it draws nothing, because the concentric rings retail shows are palette-animated into the herc's own canopy art, not drawn by this widget (see ShieldsGauge_UpdateRingPalette in docs/retail/simulation/cockpit-hud-widgets.md).

entries.name: ShieldFacing_FlushDeferredPaint
entries.description: The shield facing's vtable slot +0xc, the per-frame deferred-paint flush every cockpit widget class implements. Counter at +0x1f: 2 decrements without repainting (a facing has no content to rebuild, its rings being palette-animated), 1 calls Widget_DrawToCockpit and decrements. The counter is set to 2 by Widget_InvalidateDeferred, which Widget_Repaint calls on every press and release.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_ApplyCoordShift
entries.description: (rects): VideoMode_ShiftRect on the first rect, then shifts the four 16-byte rects after it left by VideoMode_XCoordShift (x) and VideoMode_YCoordShift (y). Gau_ShieldDisplayWidget runs it on the .GAU block at +0x268 before ShieldsGauge_Ctor.

entries.name: EnergyPoolGauge_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for EnergyPoolGauge, the Master Energy Pool meter (reactor charge), not the shield meter; Gau_EnergyMeterWidget (read) calls it on .GAU offset 548 already shifted to device pixels. PanelGauge_Ctor, vtable EnergyPoolGaugeVtable, a GLViewport stored at DAT_004d1aec. Copies the child rect's corners at block +0x10..+0x1c (.GAU 564, x0, y0, x1, y1) offset by the panel rect's origin (+0, +4) into +4..+0x10, sets block +0x20 to 0, and builds an LED bar over that rect at +0xb5 (LedBarGraph_Ctor, range 0x400), its even and odd pinstripe colours (+0x2c, +0x30) HudColorTable ids 6 and 5 and its remainder colour (+0x24) DAT_004d3c26's. The binary's class-name table pairs 'EnergyPoolGauge' with 'LEDBarGraphV' (file offset 280429) and 'ShieldsGauge' with 'ShieldsSelectGadget' (279148).

entries.name: EnergyPoolGauge_Paint
entries.description: EnergyPoolGauge vtable +0x04 (0049cabc): when the bar's (+0xb5) rect is on screen, installs the gauge's own render context (+0xbf, given the current one's clip and origin) when it has one, paints the bar to the value at +0xb1 through its slot +0x00, and reinstalls the previous context.

entries.name: EnergyPoolGauge_Update
entries.description: EnergyPoolGauge vtable +0x08: EnergyPoolGauge_Paint's body gated on the dirty byte +0xb0 == 2, followed by Widget_DrawToCockpit(1, gauge+4) and +0xb0 = 0.

entries.name: EnergyMeter_SetValue
entries.description: (meter, &value): stores value at meter+0xb1 and, when it differs from the previous one, sets the paint count +0xb0 to 2. Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate passes CockpitViewInstance+0x1e5 and energyPool << 10 / 10000 (0..0x400, the range of the LEDBarGraphV 00444edc builds).

entries.name: EnergyPoolGauge_ReturnZero
entries.description: Returns 0 (push ebp / mov ebp,esp / xor eax,eax / pop ebp / ret), between EnergyMeter_SetValue and EnergyPoolGauge_OnChildClickNoOp. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: EnergyPoolGauge_OnChildClickNoOp

entries.name: GauEnergyMeter_ApplyCoordShift
entries.description: (rects): VideoMode_ShiftRect on the first rect, then shifts the one rect after it by VideoMode_XCoordShift / VideoMode_YCoordShift. Gau_EnergyMeterWidget runs it on the .GAU block at +0x224 (the panel and its one child).

entries.name: MFDisplay_Ctor
entries.description: MFDisplay constructor (vtable 0049cfbc, RTTI name 'MFDisplay', 0x10 bytes), the base of the MFD's screens, (screen, rect): stores the vtable at +0, the rect pointer at +4 and 0 at +0xc.

entries.name: Cockpit_GetMfd_Thunk
entries.description: Calls Cockpit_GetMfd and returns its result (the decompile drops it). MfdRadarScreen_Update and MfdFlashCommScreen_DrawRowPlate use it.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the multi-function display. Lazily loads three sprite banks -- `mfd` (DAT_0049cbcc), `mfd_dmg` (DAT_0049cbd4) and `radar` -- each selecting folder "hba"/"dba" off VideoMode_UseHiResBanks.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_Repaint
entries.description: Full MFD repaint, in order: mode buttons 0-5, the screen background, all visible buttons 0-12, the current screen's paint slot, then the title from MfdCaptionTable[mode]. Background frame is a bare switch on the mode over the `mfd` bank's frame-pointer array: modes 0/1/4 take element 1, mode 3 element 2, modes 2/5 take literal 0 and skip the blit. Frame 0 is never used as a background. See docs/retail/simulation/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_Update
entries.description: MFD per-frame update. Returns at once when the published cockpit view's +0x14 is 4, when the inset rect (+0xeb) has no visible corner, or while the power-up is not armed (+0x8c). While armed and not done (+0x8d) on the scanner (mode 3) it starts, then steps, the dish animation's SpriteSequence at +0x331 and returns; the pass after it ends sets done, and the next frees the sequencer and the radar bank. On another screen done comes once the coarse tick passes +0x345. Then runs the sensor dropout (Player_DependentCondition(2)) and returns while it hides the display, updates the buttons the mode's MfdButtonVisibility row shows, and swaps the display's own 0x204-byte clip block (+0x104, the inset rect via MfdDisplay_StaticRegion) into the live render context until it returns. Under it: when g_MfdMissileCamMode is -1 and the HDD roster's transmission block (+0x766, valid flag +0x782) is up, floods the inset with palette 0x11, blits the speaking pilot's frames at inset+(0x14,0) plus the raw .OFS pair, writes the name to the message label at +0x329 while the box state is 2, and skips the screen; otherwise runs the queued repaint (+0xb0), dispatches the current screen's update slot via +0xcd + mode*4 when its dirty byte is set (modes 0 and 4 on a 0x1e-tick refresh), and refreshes the title for modes 2 and 5. See docs/retail/simulation/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_NoOp
entries.description: Empty body (push ebp / mov ebp,esp / pop ebp / ret) after MfdDisplay_Update. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_ReturnZero
entries.description: Returns 0, between MfdDisplay_NoOp and MfdButton_OnClick. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: MfdButton_OnClick
entries.description: MFD button dispatch, the display's slot 0, (display, button): finds the clicked button's index in the +0x18 array (count +0x68) and returns if it is not there, then switches on it. Indices 0-5 call MfdDisplay_SetMode(i) -- this is what makes mode index = F-key - 1. 7 (SELECT) and 9 (TARGET) are one case: MfdDisplay_StepStatusSubject on mode 0, Cockpit_CycleTarget on any other, then the mode's repaint byte (+0xe5 + mode) and 100 into the current screen's +0xc. 8 (RANGE) calls MfdDisplay_CycleScannerRange and sets the repaint byte. 10 (XMIT) returns while CockpitMouse_DoubleClick is set, and otherwise calls MfdFlashComm_Transmit and sets the repaint byte. 11 (PASS) and 12 (ACTIVE) store 0/1 to CockpitViewInstance+0x203's +0x96, light their own button's +0x40 and clear the other's, invalidating both. 6 has no case. See docs/retail/simulation/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_KeyDispatch
entries.description: MFDGauge vtable +0x0c (0049cfa0), (display, key): returns 0 while CockpitView_RectCornerVisible says the display's rect (+0xeb) is off screen. 0x20 (D), 0x2d (X) and 0x214 (Alt+T) press children 7, 10 and 9 when the current mode's (+0xc1) row of the button-visibility table shows them (0049cbdf, 0049cbe2, 0049cbe1, 13 bytes a mode); 0x213 (Alt+R) presses child 8 where the row shows it and runs MfdDisplay_CycleScannerRange where it does not. 0x34 and 0x33 (. and ,) run MfdFlashComm_NextAvailableRow or _PrevAvailableRow and set the byte at +0xe5 + mode, on mode 1 only. Those six codes return 1 on any mode. On mode 1, 0x1e, 0x22, 0x23, 0x18, 0x12 or 0x2e, and 0x21 run MfdFlashComm_SelectRow(display, +0xfb, row) for rows 0-5 and return 1. Anything else returns 0.

entries.name: MfdFlashComm_HandleAltKey
entries.description: (mfd, code): FLASH COMM's [Alt] order keys, offered every code before the MFD's own command slot. For 0x21e, 0x222, 0x223, 0x218, 0x221 ([Alt]+A G H O F) it selects row 0, 1, 2, 3 or 5 through 0043f9b8 on the comm screen (+0xd1), transmits (MfdFlashComm_Transmit) and selects the row again (MfdFlashComm_SelectRow); 0x22e and 0x212 ([Alt]+C, E) select row 4 and transmit only when MfdFlashComm_SelectedVerb is 4 or 7 respectively. Returns 1 for those seven codes, 0 for any other. See docs/retail/simulation/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_SetDropoutRanges
entries.description: Picks the MFD's sensor-dropout set by condition ([0,1,2,2,2] at 0049cb34): sequencer 004d1d0c[set], sequences set*2 and set*2+1, and the spell ranges from 0049cb94/cba0/cbac/cbb8. Each sequencer's set holds one sequence, so SpriteSequence_Select refuses both numbers for sets 1 and 2 and the sequencer plays the one it was built with both ways.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_CycleMode
entries.description: (mfd): MfdDisplay_SetMode(mfd, (+0xc1 + 1) wrapped at 6). Sim_PollPlayerInput's command 0xe calls it on CockpitViewInstance+0x1ed.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_SetMode
entries.description: (display, mode): switches the MFD to a screen (0-5, = F-key - 1). Returns at once if mode is already the one at +0xc1. Sets the new mode button's +0x40 flag if clear and invalidates it; clears the previous one's (unless the previous mode is -1) and invalidates it; stores the mode; if g_MfdMissileCamMode is not -1, clears g_MfdMissileCamArmed and sets it to -1. For buttons 6-12 it reads the mode's row of the visibility table (0049cbde + mode*13): a button the row hides goes to state 2 only while its state is 0, and one the row shows goes to state 0 only while its state is 2, each invalidated when changed. Then sets the dirty byte +0xb0 to 2; on mode 0 copies the roster entry +0x308[+0x318] to +0xb9, on mode 4 copies the cockpit's selection (CockpitViewInstance+0x210) to +0xb9, and on mode 3 presses PASS (11) or ACTIVE (12) with Widget_PressChild by the cockpit machine's radar byte +0x96. Among the callers found by es2_xref, Gau_MfdPanelWidget passes 3 (SCANNER) at build time, which is what a cockpit powers up on. See docs/retail/simulation/mfd.md.

entries.name: Cockpit_CycleTarget
entries.description: TargetSelect_Cycle(CockpitViewInstance). MfdButton_OnClick's SELECT/TARGET case calls it in every mode but 0.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_StepStatusSubject
entries.description: (mfd): increments the status screen's subject cursor +0x318, wrapping to 0 at the count +0x31c. MfdButton_OnClick's SELECT/TARGET case calls it in mode 0.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_NoOp2
entries.description: Empty body (push ebp / mov ebp,esp / pop ebp / ret) between MfdDisplay_StepStatusSubject and MfdDisplay_CycleScannerRange. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_CycleScannerRange
entries.description: The SCANNER screen's RANGE button: steps MfdDisplay+0xc5 and wraps at 3, then MfdDisplay_SetScannerRange installs MfdScannerRanges[index] at MfdDisplay+0xbd. Stepping outwards from the default index 2 means the first press goes from 1200 m to 300 m.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_SetScannerRange
entries.description: (mfd, index): when index differs from +0xc5, stores it there and MfdScannerRanges[index] at +0xbd. MfdDisplay_CycleScannerRange calls it.

entries.name: MfdFlashComm_NextAvailableRow
entries.description: (display) steps display+0xb1 forward with wrap 5->0, skipping rows whose state byte has bit 0, then MfdDisplay_SetSharedRow. The . key (0x34) via MfdDisplay_KeyDispatch.

entries.name: MfdFlashComm_PrevAvailableRow
entries.description: (display) as MfdFlashComm_NextAvailableRow but backwards, wrapping 0->5. The , key (0x33) via MfdDisplay_KeyDispatch.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_SetSharedRow
entries.description: (display, row): stores row at display+0xb1, the first int of the screen-shared state block, when it differs from what is there. Direct callers: MfdFlashComm_SelectRow, MfdFlashComm_HandleListClick, 00447014 and 00447048.

entries.name: MfdFlashComm_HandleListClick
entries.description: (display, gadget, point): resolves a click on the MFD's screen area to a FLASH COMM row. Returns at once unless the display is on mode 1 (+0xc1), then walks the six row label rects in index order -- inclusive on all four edges -- and stops at the first hit. Rows are built top..top+14 and stepped by 14, so adjacent rows share a line and the first-match walk gives it to the upper one. When CockpitMouse_DoubleClick is set and the hit row is the display's shared row (+0xb1), it presses child 10, XMIT, through Widget_PressChild(display, 10, 1), calls MfdFlashComm_Transmit and sets the mode's repaint byte (+0xe5 + mode); any other hit stores the row through MfdDisplay_SetSharedRow and sets +0xe6. A point on no row does nothing.

entries.name: MfdFlashComm_SelectRow
entries.description: (display, widget, row): only when widget is the display's base panel widget (+0xfb) and the current mode (+0xc1) is 1, FLASH COMM, stores row as the display's shared selected row through MfdDisplay_SetSharedRow and sets the byte at +0xe6, FLASH COMM's entry in the per-screen byte array at +0xe5 + mode. Both keyboard handlers pass the display's own +0xfb, so the mode test is the one that can refuse: 004469c0 for the plain hotkeys and 00446c10 for the [Alt] ones after it has transmitted. See docs/retail/simulation/mfd.md#keyboard.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile and disassembly at 00447130; docs/retail/simulation/mfd.md#keyboard

entries.name: MfdDisplay_SyncMissileCamMode
entries.description: (mfd): switches the MFD to mode 5 (MISSILE CAM) and back while an electro-optical launcher is armed: the condition is that CockpitView_FindArmedMountGauge(CockpitViewInstance) returns a gauge for which WeaponGauge_MountProjectileType is 0 (Rocket) and WeaponGauge_MountProjectileSubtype is 3. When it holds and g_MfdMissileCamMode is -1: with g_MfdMissileCamArmed set it saves the current mode (+0xc1) in g_MfdMissileCamSavedMode and MfdDisplay_SetMode(5); either way g_MfdMissileCamMode becomes 5 and the flag is set. When it no longer holds and g_MfdMissileCamMode is not -1, MfdDisplay_SetMode(saved mode) and the flag is set. MfdDisplay_SetMode clears both whenever it changes the mode with g_MfdMissileCamMode not -1, so a mode chosen by hand while the condition holds stays until the condition ends, when the saved mode is restored over it; a saved mode equal to the current one changes nothing and leaves the switch held. MfdDisplay_Update calls it, and while g_MfdMissileCamMode is not -1 draws no transmission. See docs/retail/simulation/mfd.md, 'Modes'.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00447164 and MfdDisplay_SetMode's writes at 00446e8e-00446e98

entries.name: MfdFlashComm_Transmit
entries.description: (mfdDisplay): the FLASH COMM transmit, which XMIT and the list's double-click reach. Resolves the screen's (+0xd1) selected row to a verb through MfdFlashComm_SelectedVerb, writes it into the shared order record at DAT_004d0458 and broadcasts it through Squad_BroadcastOrderFromCockpit with the display's +0x14; when that returns nonzero, calls MfdFlashComm_ToggleRowVariant on the screen.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_InScannerRange
entries.description: (mfd, object): Math_DistanceBetweenPoints from the piloted machine's position (CockpitViewInstance+0x203, +0x26) to object+0x26, returning 1 when that is less than the scanner range at mfd+0xbd (MfdDisplay_SetScannerRange's MfdScannerRanges entry), else 0. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_SetStatusRoster
entries.description: (mfd): fills the status screen's squad roster, MfdDisplay_StepStatusSubject's array: entry 0 (+0x308) is the cockpit's own machine (CockpitViewInstance+0x203), entries 1..count (+0x30c) the first count machines of g_SquadmateMachines, and +0x31c becomes count + 1. Cockpit_LoadSquadmatePilots calls it with the squadmates it seated.

entries.name: MFDSelectGadget_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for MFDSelectGadget, the MFD's momentary leaf button (object size 0x40, indices 7-10). Three levels over Widget_CtorRect ending at vtable 0049cf60, whose slot 0 is MfdButton_SetCaption; leaves slot +8 as the inherited Widget_ForwardClickToOwner, so it has no lit flag and shows only the shared press state. The class name is its own, from the descriptor record at 00447a6f. See docs/retail/simulation/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdButton_SetCaption
entries.description: The momentary MFD buttons' repaint (buttons 7-10). Blits the frame indexed by the press byte +0x1b, then sets the caption from the index at +0x28: for index < 6 it composes "F1"-"F6" on the stack from the two-byte literal at 0049cea3 ("Fx") with '1'+index written over the second byte -- the six mode captions are not stored as strings; for index >= 6 it takes MfdCaptionTable[index], STRINGS0.STR group 5. For index 10 (XMIT) it then redraws the FLASH COMM selected-row plate with MfdFlashCommScreen_DrawRowPlate(screen, MfdFlashComm_SelectedVerb(screen), 0), the screen being the owner's +0xd1. See docs/retail/simulation/mfd.md.

entries.name: MFDSelectGadget_FlushDeferredPaint
entries.description: MFDSelectGadgetVtable +0x0c: the same body as MFDStateGadget_FlushDeferredPaint.

entries.name: MFDStateGadget_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for MFDStateGadget, the MFD's latching leaf button (object size 0x41, indices 0-5, 11 and 12, plus 6 by falling through the ctor switch). Four levels over Widget_CtorRect ending at vtable 0049cf20, whose slot 0 is MfdButton_Repaint; overrides slot +8 with 004474a8, which refuses a press while the +0x40 lit flag is already set, sets it, forwards to the owner, repaints and sounds the click. The class name is its own, from the descriptor record at 00447a17. See docs/retail/simulation/mfd.md.

entries.name: MFDStateGadget_OnClick
entries.description: MFDStateGadgetVtable +0x08 (gadget, flags): PanelStateGadget_OnClick's body, but only while the state byte +0x40 is 0, so a click latches it on and never off.

entries.name: MfdButton_Repaint
entries.description: The latching MFD button classes' repaint (buttons 0-5 and 11-12). Inside a pushed canvas context it blits the frame indexed by the +0x40 lit flag, never by the press byte +0x1b; buttons 0-5 and 11-12 then take ColorSchemePanels[12] DARK when +0x40 is set and [10] WHITE when clear, which is why the selected F-key reads dark-on-green. Caption text is resolved the same way as MfdButton_SetCaption. See docs/retail/simulation/mfd.md.

entries.name: MFDStateGadget_FlushDeferredPaint
entries.description: MFDStateGadgetVtable +0x0c: steps the pending-paint count at +0x1f -- at 1, Widget_DrawToCockpit(0, gadget, 0); at 2, slot 0 of the vtable at +0x17 -- decrementing it either way.

entries.name: MFDListGadget_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for MFDListGadget (object size 0x28), the MFD's screen-content click region, registered by MfdDisplay_Ctor after the 13 buttons. Derives from PanelListGadget. Class name from the descriptor record at 004479d3.

entries.name: MFDListGadget_OnClick
entries.description: The MFD screen-area gadget's (MFDListGadget) vtable +8, (gadget, buttonFlags). Left button only; calls MfdFlashComm_HandleListClick(owner, self, &DAT_004d1e67), the owner taken from the gadget's own +0x24. It makes no other call, its PanelGadget mixin's click slot included, so the click makes no sound of its own; a double-click on the selected row sounds XMIT's, through the press MfdFlashComm_HandleListClick makes. The mirror of HDDListGadget_OnClick.
entries.signature: void __cdecl MFDListGadget_OnClick(int gadget, unsigned char buttonFlags)

entries.name: MfdGau_ApplyCoordShift
entries.description: Coordinate-shifts the MFD's .GAU block at offset 728 in place before MfdDisplay_Ctor reads it: 13 consecutive rects from int index 4 (file offset 744), then the panel rect at int index 0x38 (file offset 952). The 13 rects are zero in all nine retail .GAU files and no constructor reads them; only the panel rect is live. See docs/retail/simulation/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_StaticDtor
entries.description: _EXIT_ routine (Borland _EXIT_ entry 004a7c3c, priority 0x20): when MfdDisplay_StaticRegionBuilt (0049cc26) is set, decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr three times -- the count MfdDisplay_Ctor adds when it first constructs its function-local static GLRectangleRegion MfdDisplay_StaticRegion (004d1d34) and sets that byte. The routine runs the count down without calling a destructor.

entries.name: ThrottleGauge_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the throttle slider gauge. Lazily loads the `throttle` sprite bank into DAT_0049cfc4, folder selected by VideoMode_PanelMode == 3 choosing "hba" over "dba". Reads CockpitViewInstance and its own .GAU track rect. Bank frame 0 is a 2px tick, frame 1 the knob.

entries.name: ThrottleGauge_Paint
entries.description: ThrottleGauge vtable +0x04 (0049d1e0): paints its child (+0x18, the slider) through slot +0x00 of its table at +0x17, then Bitmap_Blit(**(DAT_0049cfc4+8), gauge+0xc2, 0).

entries.name: ThrottleGauge_Update
entries.description: ThrottleGauge vtable +0x08 (0049d1e0): runs its child's slot +0x0c (FlushDeferredPaint).

entries.name: ThrottleGauge_SetValues
entries.description: Writes the gauge's live value pair at +0xb1 from a caller struct of two ints: [0] speed as a Q10 fraction of max, [1] throttle Q10 +/-0x400. Pushes the throttle down to the slider child's set-value slot (+0x14) when it changed, and marks the child dirty (+0x1f = 2) when the speed fraction changed. Called once a frame by Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate.

entries.name: ThrottleGauge_GetValues
entries.description: Returns gauge + 0xb1, the speedFraction/throttle int pair. Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate reads [1] (gauge+0xb5) into mech+0x290 unless the mech+0x93 dirty flag says input moved the throttle this frame, in which case it pushes the other way. That arbitration is the whole of the two-way binding between the slider and the keyboard.

entries.name: ThrottleGauge_OnChildValue
entries.description: Gauge slot 0: a child reporting a value. Finds the child in the gauge's array (+0x18, count +0x68); index 0 is the slider, and its value is negated when the gauge's +0xc1 is 0 (the vertical variant) before being stored to +0xb5. That negation cancels SliderWidget_GetValueV's own inversion, leaving positive = forward = knob up.

entries.name: ThrottleSlider_CtorV
entries.description: The throttle's vertical slider child, built when .GAU offset 1064 (SLIDE_DIR) == 1 -- the case all 9 retail .GAU files use. Knob spans the track's full width with its height from throttle bank frame 1 (28x12), limits +/-0x400 at +0x24/+0x26, and an initial position centred on the track (knobBottom = trackBottom - (trackHeight - knobHeight)/2), which is the manual's centred-is-stopped detent. Also constructs the two LED fill bars from .GAU ints [8..11] and [12..15] into private fields +0x7e and +0x82 -- it never registers them as children, and nothing ever paints them (see LedBarGraph_CtorV).

entries.name: ThrottleSlider_DrawKnobV
entries.description: ThrottleVSliderGadget vtable +0x00 (0049d12c): when the slider is on screen, places the knob rect from the knob position (+0x28/+0x2c), points the raster source page at the draw page, saves the screen under the knob (offset by the canvas origin) into +0x52 with Region_Save, blits the knob bitmap (+0x4e) mirrored (flag 2) when the knob sits right of 160 << XCoordShift, and records the knob rect at +0x6e/+0x72. ThrottleSlider_PaintV is the table's +0x0c.

entries.name: ThrottleSlider_PaintV
entries.description: Vertical throttle slider paint. Copies the gauge's +0xb1 speed fraction into +0x7a/+0x4a and does nothing further with it, reads the two LED fill bars' rects only to widen the invalidated region handed to Widget_DrawToCockpit, then blits the knob at its current height. It never draws either bar -- see LedBarGraph_CtorV.

entries.name: ThrottleSlider_OnValue
entries.description: Throttle slider commit slot (vtable +8). Notifies the parent gauge via VSliderGadget_OnClick (which dispatches the owner's slot 0 = ThrottleGauge_OnChildValue, then repaints), then sets ThrottleLeverMode (0049a06e) from the sign of the committed value -- but gated on a joystick throttle control being configured AND assigned to THROTTLE in preferences, so it is inert on a keyboard/mouse setup.

entries.name: ThrottleSlider_CtorFixed
entries.description: The SLIDE_DIR != 1 throttle slider variant: a fixed 12px-wide knob centred horizontally and spanning the track's full height. No retail .GAU selects it (all 9 hold 1 at offset 1064), so this branch is never exercised by retail data and its behaviour is unverified.

entries.name: ThrottleSlider_PaintH
entries.description: Slot 0 (Paint) of ThrottleHSliderGadgetVtable, the class ThrottleSlider_CtorFixed builds and no retail .GAU selects. When CockpitView_RectCornerVisible passes: sets the knob's x span +0x2e/+0x36 from the int16 position +0x28 and width +0x2c, points the current display's draw page (+0x38) at its visible page (+0x3c), records the knob rect offset by the render context's +0x220/+0x224 in the region at +0x5a and saves the pixels under it into +0x52 (Region_Save), Bitmap_Blit's the knob bitmap +0x4e at +0x2e and keeps that position at +0x6e/+0x72.

entries.name: ThrottleSlider_FlushPaintH
entries.description: Slot 0xc (FlushDeferredPaint) of ThrottleHSliderGadgetVtable. At +0x1f == 2 and when CockpitView_RectCornerVisible passes: Region_Restore's the pixels saved under the knob's previous position (+0x6e), copies the gauge's +0xb1 into +0x7a/+0x4a, repaints the knob as ThrottleSlider_PaintH does, then Widget_DrawToCockpit(1, rect) over the union of the knob's old and new rects and the two LED bars' rects (+0x7e, +0x82), and clears +0x1f.

entries.name: GauThrottle_ApplyCoordShift
entries.description: (rects): VideoMode_ShiftRect on the first rect, then shifts the three 16-byte rects after it by VideoMode_XCoordShift / VideoMode_YCoordShift. Gau_ThrottleWidget runs it on the .GAU block at +1000.

entries.name: VSliderGadget_InvalidateDeferred
entries.description: PanelVSliderGadget vtable +0x04 (0049d19c), kept by ThrottleVSliderGadget: this->[0x1f] = 2, the vertical slider's copy of Widget_InvalidateDeferred. HSliderGadget_InvalidateDeferred is the horizontal one.

entries.name: HDDisplay_Ctor
entries.description: HDDisplay constructor (vtable 0049d668, RTTI name 'HDDisplay', 0x10 bytes): stores its two arguments at +4 and +8. HddCommandScreen_Ctor and HddDamageScreen_Ctor run it first.

entries.name: HddDisplay_Ctor
entries.description: HDDisplay constructor, .GAU offset 1212 (PHDD.CPP). Reads the block's origin, four region rects (+0xc1 screen, +0xe1 order column, +0xd1 damage column, +0xf1 title indicator), 15 widget rects and 3 comm-box marker rects; loads the 'static' and 'hdd' sprite banks and the 'hddclip' clip region; builds both page objects (+0x101 command display, +0x105 damage detail), the title label (+0x51b) and three 0x14e-byte comm gauges; ends with HddDisplay_SetPage(obj, 0).

entries.name: HddDisplay_Repaint
entries.description: Whole-display paint, only when the display's rect corner is visible (CockpitView_RectCornerVisible on +0xc1): calls paint slot 0 on every child widget (+0x18, count +0x68), each of which applies its own state gate; then the current page object's slot +0xc and HddDisplay_RepaintPage; then the title indicator rect +0xf1, filled with 004d3c1a's colour, or 004d3c1e's while +0x51f is set; then HddDisplay_SetTitle; then, for each of the three comm boxes, copies widget 10+i's rect into its gauge and either fills the rect inset one pixel with 004d3c26's colour, when the gauge's +0x137 is 0, or calls HddGauge_PaintIdle.

entries.name: HddDisplay_Update
entries.description: Heads-Down Display per-frame update: records the selected target for the damage page, runs HddDisplay_HandleWidgetPress, then (outside the external view) the sensor dropout with the PanelGauge_Ctor default ranges and no sequencer, flagging the current page for a full repaint when +0x76 changes, then the widgets' and the page's updates. It also sets the comms-out latch (gauge +0x147) of every destroyed squadmate while the view manager's transition flag +0x1c is set and its view +0x14 is 4, and forces every destroyed, latched comm box to state 1.

entries.name: HddDisplay_RepaintPage
entries.description: (display): saves the render context, sets the current page object's +0xc to the signed byte display+0xb0, runs the page's slot 0 (its Repaint -- HddCommandScreen_Repaint on the command page), decrements display+0xb0 and restores the context. HddDisplay_Repaint runs it after the page's Show, and HddDisplay_Update before HddDisplay_SetTitle.

entries.name: HddDisplay_PaintCurrentScreen
