The subtraction is 32-bit but the offset is taken in 16 bits, so the aim point is always within 32768 of the destination along the leg: from 9000 out to 41767 it sits short of the destination back down the incoming line, inside 9000 it swings past, and further out it cycles every 65536 units of range. And its gain is four times a HERC's: (Math_HeadingToward(aim, this) - heading) >> 4, not >> 6. The shift is encoded SAR EDX, 0x64, which x86 masks to 4. A speed argument of zero means none stated and takes 0xaa, the same default Ai_DriveToPoint uses. Pushes a fourth argument, 0, to the three-argument GroundVehicle_LocomotionTick.
entries.signature: int __cdecl GroundVehicle_DriveToPoint(void *vehicle, int *point, short legBearing, int speed)

entries.name: GroundVehicle_LeaderSteer
entries.description: The group leader's route follow for a ground vehicle. No waypoint after the cursor means GroundVehicle_LocomotionTick(this, 0, 0) -- steer and speed both zero; otherwise it drives at that waypoint with GroundVehicle_DriveToPoint on the bearing between it and the cursor's own, passing speed 0 so the drive takes its own 0xaa default, and advances the route cursor when the drive reports arrival.

entries.name: GroundVehicle_FollowerSteer
entries.description: A non-leader ground vehicle's formation keeping. Takes Group_FirstAbleMember's position, asks its own vtable +0x78 for the formation slot -- note that Formation_RotateAndAddOffset rotates the offset by the group's member array SLOT 0, not by the able leader it is anchored on -- and branches on heading agreement. Inside 0x4000 it matches speed (the leader's own +0x220 minus the along-track error in the leader's frame >> 5, clamped +0x100 / -0x96) and drives at a point 20000 ahead of the post along the leader's heading, with no lateral steering term at all. Outside 0x4000 it abandons the leader's heading and turns straight at the post at (distance >> 5) capped the same way.

entries.name: Raster_SpanTextured
entries.description: Mode 0 span routine: fetch atlasPage[v][u] via a packed page<<16|v<<8|u index into maybe_g_BitmapAtlasCache, store that palette byte to the framebuffer, step the fixed-point u/v, repeat. Two halves selected by DAT_004a09ac: zero is an opaque copy, non-zero skips texels of palette index 0. No shade level, no colour lookup, no blending -- which is why a beam ignores BEAM.DAT's colour index.

entries.name: Raster_SpanTexturedShaded
entries.description: Mode 1 span routine of Raster_DrawPolygon: as Raster_SpanTextured, but each texel goes through one ramp row, ShadeRampTable + (DAT_004a09c4 >> 16) * 0x100, fixed for the span. Two halves selected by DAT_004a09ac: zero stores every texel, non-zero skips a raw texel of palette index 0.

entries.name: Raster_SpanTexturedGouraud
entries.description: Mode 2 span routine of Raster_DrawPolygon: as Raster_SpanTexturedShaded, but the ramp row is per pixel, DAT_004a09c4 stepped by DAT_004a09c8, and there is only an opaque half (no DAT_004a09ac test).

entries.name: maybe_Raster_SpanTexturedShadedQuadratic
entries.description: Frameless span routine (PUSH EBP/ESI/EDI/EBX); Raster_SpanTexturedShadedQuadraticClipped calls it (0048b664). Fills DAT_004a0984 pixels from DAT_004a0980 with atlas texels (page DAT_004a09b4) through the ShadeRampTable row (DAT_004a09c4 >> 16), writing every pixel. u and v start from 004a098e/004a0992 and 004a0996/004a099a and step by 004a099e/004a09a2 and 004a09a6/004a09aa, and those steps change by 004a09bc and 004a09c0 each pixel: second-order stepping.

entries.name: maybe_Raster_SpanTexturedGouraudQuadratic
entries.description: Frameless span routine; Raster_SpanTexturedGouraudQuadraticClipped calls it (0048b72c). The second-order u/v stepping of maybe_Raster_SpanTexturedShadedQuadratic with the ramp row per pixel (DAT_004a09c4 stepped by DAT_004a09c8), and ESP as the destination pointer (ESP saved at 004a09e4, SS loaded from DS for the loop).

entries.name: FireEffect_PerFrameReset
entries.description: The burning-object pool's phase-5 subsystem hook, registered by FireEffect_RegisterSubsystem and driven once a frame from Sim_RenderFrame. Returns the pool's dead entries (ObjectPool_FlushDeleteQueue over DAT_006b4fb8/g_FirePool) and resets DAT_006b4fc0 to 0x7fffffff -- the running nearest-fire distance FireEffect_TickUpdate tests before it calls Sound_UpdatePosition(0x33), which is what keeps the one shared burning loop on the fire nearest the camera. No prologue; it is the tail of the 0046b0xx block, ending at 0046b0a3 where FireEffect_LoadResources begins.

entries.name: FireEffect_LoadResources
entries.description: Loader for the BURNING-OBJECT effect, not the muzzle flash. Reads dts/fire.dts (fire2.dts when CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand is set) into g_FireShapes, allocates the ten-entry g_FirePool and its free list, loads the two banks fire0/fire1 (fire0s/fire1s on demand), then reads dat/FIRE.DAT -- a 4-byte count header plus one byte per shape -- and points each shape's +0x26 at the bank that byte names. Retail: 4 shapes, banks [0, 0, 0, 1]. Carries the fire.cpp assert string.

entries.name: FireEffect_AcquireSlot
entries.description: Takes a free entry from g_FirePool, or when none is free walks the live ones and returns the one with the lowest +0x59 -- the loop count FireEffect_TickUpdate decrements each time the flipbook wraps. So a full pool never refuses a new fire; the one nearest going out pays for it.

entries.name: FireEffect_Ctor
entries.description: Builds one burning-object effect on a FIRE.DTS shape index: owner at +0x4a, attach cluster id at +0x4e (negative uses the raw local point, 0xffff is the structures' 'no cluster'), attach point at +0x50, frame timer +0x57 = 0x40, and the loop count at +0x59 (30, or 5 in theater 4, the Moon, the script.dat header's theater index). On the Moon only shapes 1 and 3 are built; the others go straight back on the free list. The first live instance starts sound 0x33 and FireEffect_Dtor stops it on the last, counted by DAT_006b4fbc. Two spawn sites: Component_DestroyAndCascade, whose .DMG destruction flags' bit 1 releases the machine's other fires and lights shape 0 in their place while bit 3 adds shape 2, and Base_DeathSequenceTick's last stage.

entries.name: FireEffect_Dtor
entries.description: Destroys one burning-object effect and decrements DAT_006b4fbc, stopping sound 0x33 when it reaches zero.

entries.name: FireEffect_ReleaseForOwner
entries.description: Walks the effect pool and returns every entry whose owner pointer at +0x4a matches the argument to the free list -- an object's fires going out when it is destroyed.

entries.name: FireEffect_TickUpdate
entries.description: Burning-object vtable +0x14. Counts the frame timer at +0x57 down, reloads it to 0x40 and steps the shape's cell animation, decrementing the loop count at +0x59 each time the frame wraps to zero -- so a fire LOOPS its flipbook where an impact effect plays it once, and ends when that count reaches zero. Then re-places itself from wherever the owner has carried it to, and keeps the shared burning sound on whichever live fire is nearest the camera: isqrt(Math_ISqrt) of the squared offset to ViewObjectPtr, tested against the running minimum DAT_006b4fc0 that FireEffect_PerFrameReset clears each frame, and Sound_UpdatePosition(0x33) on a win. That test sits above the loops-remaining test, so a fire counts on the tick it goes out. The three squares are 32-bit IMULs and the sum wraps past about 46341 units, which is what makes a distant fire able to read as the nearest one.

entries.name: Fire_GetOwnerDrawCell
entries.description: (fire): returns the address of the cached draw cell (+0x1e8) of the object at fire+0x4a. Scene_SubmitFrameObjects files every fire under it with Scene_SubmitObjectAtCell.

entries.name: FireEffect_RegisterSubsystem
entries.description: Registers FireEffect_LoadResources as a phase-2 subsystem loader and FireEffect_PerFrameReset as phase 5, and nulls the effect pool pointer.

entries.name: FireEffect_StaticDtor
entries.description: _EXIT_ entry 004a7c66 (pointer at 004a7c68): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr and Mem_Delete(g_FirePool) when it is set. The module's _INIT_ is FireEffect_RegisterSubsystem (entry 004a7ba6).

entries.name: TSObj_Draw
entries.description: TS_OBJ vtable +0x00 (004a0b98), inherited unchanged by ANIM_OBJ, EXPLOSION, SMOKE_BALL and FIRE: SimObject_InstallModelTransform(this), then draws the shape instance at +0x34 through its own vtable +0x1c. DET_ANIM_OBJ replaces it with Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel.

entries.name: SimObject_GetPosition
entries.description: Returns obj+0x26, the object's position (the translation of the transform at obj+0x12). Vtable +0x04 of every simulation-object, projectile, effect and FlatObj table; Scene_SubmitObjectWithRadius and ObjList_DrawCellObjects call it for the position.

entries.name: SimObject_GetShapeRadius
entries.description: SimObject vtable +0x10: the current LOD shape's bounding radius, shape+8 via the shape instance at obj+0x34. Every hit test's coarse reject uses it, as does the LOD selector Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel. shape+8 is the third of the three int16 head fields TSPartBase_ReadFromStream reads -- a radius, not an id.

entries.name: TSObj_Dtor
entries.description: TS_OBJ vtable +0x08 (TSObjVtable, 004a0b98, RTTI 'TS_OBJ', 0x41 bytes): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). Reinstalls TSObjVtable at 0046b8b0, deletes the shape instance at +0x34 through its own vtable +0x18 with flags 3, and Mem_Deletes this on flags bit 0. TS_OBJ is the base of every shaped simulation object -- projectiles, effects, FlatObj and, through ANIM_OBJ, the ACTOR hierarchy -- and its destructor is the level all of their destructors reinstall last.

entries.name: MatObj_Dtor
entries.description: MAT_OBJ vtable +0x08 (00497289): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). Two RTL destructor-count decrements (MAT_OBJ, DRAWABLE), then Mem_Delete(this) on flags bit 0.

entries.name: maybe_TextureBankSlot_ElementCtor
entries.description: (slot): returns slot. Per-element constructor of three Rtl_VectorNew arrays of 8-byte records, each a set of bitmap-bank slots: 0xf in Explosion_LoadResources (00407c09, into DAT_004a96bc, whose entries name the banks it loads), 8 into g_MechTextureGroupSlots in Mech_RegisterLoader (00420663), and 2 in FireEffect_LoadResources (0046b249) for the fire0/fire1 banks.

entries.name: ObjPool_FIRE_Dtor
entries.description: ObjPool<FIRE>'s destructor, the dtor its class record (0x8 bytes, at 0046bac5) names: (pool, flags): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr; when the pool is not null, Mem_Delete of its entry buffer at +0 when that is set, then Mem_Delete of the pool when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: Terrain_FillCellUntextured
entries.description: (points, count, shades): Terrain_DrawCellQuad's fill for a cell when terrain texturing is off. Installs the points as the current face (DAT_006c6970, count DAT_006c6968, index list 006c60ec, state bytes cleared), projects them (Poly_ProjectViewVertices) and clips them to the near plane (Poly_ClipRingToNearPlane) when that reports one behind it. With shade mode DAT_004aab30 == 2 it installs a mode-1 brush on ramp 2 with the per-vertex shades (carried through the clip by Poly_ClipRingToNearPlaneWithShade), which Raster_FillContourPolygon bands; otherwise a mode-0 brush of the one colour Raster_ShadeRampRow(0x4b)[Palette_ShadeRampLookup(2, shades[0])]. Then 0042e8e8 on a stack object (vtable 004a0cb8) and PolyFill_Fill.

entries.name: Terrain_BindTextureBank
entries.description: Binds the terrain texture bank. Takes a bare base name, joins it with the 'dba' folder pointer (PTR_DAT_004a0a28), loads that resource, and stores its 20-byte-stride frame descriptor table into _DAT_006b4fc4 for Terrain_ResolveCellTexture to index. Called from World_LoadTheater with the 4th of the five NUL-terminated strings at the end of the world<N>.wld descriptor -- so the terrain bank is named in DATA, not in code, which is exactly why neither DBSIM.EXE nor VSHELL.EXE contains the strings 'ice'/'bsnow'/'volcan'/'moon' despite those .DBA files shipping. Retail mapping: WORLD0/1 urban, 2/3 bsnow, 4/5 volcan, 6/7 ice, 8/9 moon.

entries.name: Terrain_ResolveCellTexture
entries.description: Terrain texture selection and tiling. Takes an 8-byte dat\mat0 record, the cell's X and Y, and a UV-rect output of four (u, v) pairs -- pair i belongs to vertex i of Terrain_DrawCellQuad's quad, in its corner order (cellX,cellY), (cellX,cellY+1), (cellX+1,cellY+1), (cellX+1,cellY), so u rises with cellX and the negated v FALLS with cellY. Indexes the active terrain bitmap descriptor table (_DAT_006b4fc4, 20-byte stride -- the SAME per-frame descriptor structure the mech texture path uses, see dts-texture-binding.md) by mat0 field 0, i.e. mat0's first field IS a DBA frame index. Then branches on mat0 field 1 (BlockShift): if 0, the frame's own F0..F3 UV corners are used verbatim (texture stretched across the quad); otherwise shift = cellShift + BlockShift - 13 and the rect becomes u0 = (cellX << shift) & 0xff, v0 = (cellY << shift) & 0xff, spanning 2^shift texels, with V negated. The & 0xff wrap is a 256-texel tiling space -- which is why the terrain banks are 256x256 and must be edge-tileable. Returns descriptor field 4 (bytes 16-19) as a short: the bitmap handle handed to the polygon draw. Retail: mat0 record 0 = {frame 0, BlockShift 6}, record 1 = {frame 1, BlockShift 6}; that is shift = cellShift - 7, so 128 texels per cell at cellShift 14 and 64 at 13 -- 128 world units per texel either way.
entries.signature: int __cdecl Terrain_ResolveCellTexture(int *materialRecord, int cellX, int cellY, int *uvOut)

entries.name: Terrain_FaceVisibilityTest
entries.description: Per-triangle backface test in Terrain_DrawCellQuad: dot(faceNormal, viewerPos - facePoint) > 0, with the viewer position read from g_TerrainViewerPos, DAT_006b4fcc, DAT_006b4fd0. Takes the cell's three-short normal (cell+0x1 for the near triangle, cell+0x7 for the far) and a world point on that triangle. Purely a visibility gate -- it computes no light term; the shade the triangle draws at was baked at zone load, see Terrain_BuildCellSurfaceAndShade.

entries.name: HeightGrid_Constructor
entries.description: Zero-initializes a freshly-allocated 0x129-byte HeightGrid (fields +0x3d/+0x3e/+0x3f=0, +0x42=10, +0x43=8 defaults), assigns its vtable. Called once per zone load, right after the Mem_New(0x129) allocation in Terrain_LoadZone.

entries.name: HeightGrid_Dtor
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's HeightGrid_Dtor (0042878b).
entries.source: es2_naming.py diff DBSIM 0046be78 VSHELL 0042878b: differs only in callee labels and decompiler typing; RTTI HeightGrid vtable slot

entries.name: Terrain_BuildCellSurface
entries.description: Writes one height-grid cell's diagonal selector (cell+0xf bits [0:1]) and both face normals (cell+0x1 and cell+0x7, three shorts each) from its four corner heights. Selector 1 = coplanar quad (h00+h11 == h01+h10, both normals identical), 2 = split along the (0,0)-(1,1) diagonal, 0 = along the anti-diagonal. Normals are in raw height units -- horizontal components are corner differences, vertical is the cell size over the height scale -- doubled, then rescaled to length 0x800 by Math_NormalizeVec3ShortToLength. This is the writer of the selector bits; neither zone loader touches them.

entries.name: Math_NormalizeVec3ShortToLength
entries.description: Rescales a three-short vector in place to a requested length (param_2). Halves all three components until Math_FastMagnitude3D fits under 0x7d01, then multiplies each by Math_Q16Divide(length, magnitude). Called by Terrain_BuildCellSurfaceAndShade with 0x800 for both of a cell's face normals -- which is the constant that makes Light_ComputeShadeForNormal's >> 22 come out as a saturating 512*cos.

entries.name: Terrain_BuildSurface
entries.description: Runs Terrain_BuildCellSurfaceAndShade (0046c2ec) over every cell of a height grid, row by row. The last row and column have no east/north neighbour to difference against and keep a flat (0,0,0x800) normal and selector 0. Two callers: TerrainZone_LoadHeightmap's zone load, and the tail of Terrain_FlattenStructureFootprints (00471190), which has just changed raw heights and so needs every normal, selector and baked shade rebuilt over them.

entries.name: Terrain_BuildCellSurfaceAndShade
entries.description: Terrain_BuildSurface's per-cell body, and THE ANSWER TO WHERE TERRAIN LIGHT COMES FROM. For an interior cell it runs Terrain_BuildCellSurface then normalises both face normals (cell+0x1 near, cell+0x7 far) to length 0x800 via Math_NormalizeVec3ShortToLength; edge cells get a flat (0,0,0x800) instead. Then, unconditionally, it BAKES A SHADE BYTE PER TRIANGLE: cell[+0xd] = Light_ComputeShadeForNormal(cell+0x1), cell[+0xe] = Light_ComputeShadeForNormal(cell+0x7). Terrain_DrawCellQuad reads those two bytes straight back out as the ramp row -- so terrain lighting is computed ONCE at zone load and never per frame, and cell bytes +0xd/+0xe are not dead as the engine's HeightGrid assumed.

entries.name: Terrain_CellSecondPassNoOp
entries.description: Empty body. Terrain_BuildSurface's second pass over every cell calls it once per cell.

entries.name: TerrainZone_PopulateFromBitmap
entries.description: (grid, bitmap, bias): the retail zone heightmap loader; TerrainZone_LoadHeightmap calls it for a .dba path. Treats the Dynamix bitmap's 8-bit pixel grid as the heightmap: the width and height shifts (+0x100, +0x104) are the log2 of the bitmap's width (+6) and height (+4), the 16-byte cell array (+0xec) and the per-cell scratch byte array (+0xf0) are allocated, and rows are read bottom-up from the pixel pointer at bitmap+0xe. Each pixel less the bias byte becomes the cell's raw height (+0), the scratch byte is zeroed through HeightGrid_SetCellScratchByte, and +0x114 keeps the largest raw height seen. The +0xf material bits are set with the selector bit 1 kept (& 2): a cell on a block boundary rolls Math_RandomNext() & 0xfff < 0x4ce (about 30%) for material 1 against 0 -- the roll's upper bound is the literal 2 (CMP EBX,0x2 at 0046c5ca), not the mat0 count -- and every other cell copies its block's base cell, the block mask being (1 << (0x15 - mat0[0]+4 - cellShift)) - 1. Afterwards +0x110 (height base) is 0, +0x114 is multiplied by the height scale +0x118 into the zone's highest world height, and HeightOffsetTable_SetScale(grid+0xd0, base, scale) and HeightOffsetTable_Reset run. Every retail ZONE*.DBA is 128x128 (16418 bytes) or 256x256 (65570 bytes), the pixel count plus a 34-byte bitmap header.

entries.name: TerrainZone_LoadHeightmap
entries.description: terrain.cpp. Called by Terrain_LoadZone with the zone's built 'dba\zoneNNNN' path. Also separately loads the shared 'dat\mat0' material/detail-type table (count-prefixed array of 8-byte records, ZONES_MaterialTable) into HeightGrid+0x121. Branches on the path's extension: '.dba' (real retail data, ZONES.VOL\DBA\ZONE*.DBA) goes through ClassItem_LoadResource -> TerrainZone_PopulateFromBitmap; any other extension falls back to an ASCII fopen/fscanf format ('%d %d %d %d' header = width shift, height shift, max raw height, min raw height, then one '%d' per cell) -- almost certainly a level-design/debug-only path, no such loose files found in retail data.

entries.name: Terrain_SetupVisibleRegion
entries.description: Per-frame terrain visibility setup, called twice per frame from the frame function 0045fb9c with ActiveHeightGrid passed AS A PARAMETER (which is why a search for readers of the ActiveHeightGrid global missed the terrain render path entirely). WRITES the LOD field: grid[+0x10c] = (short)DAT_004a0bcc[DAT_004d1fc3], then >>= (cellShift - 14) when cellShift > 14. DAT_004a0bcc is three int16s -- 6, 10, 14 cells -- indexed by the terrain-detail option DAT_004d1fc3, so the draw radius is a player setting; the >> only ever fires on the two shift-15 zones and nothing compensates below shift 14. Passes grid[0x10c] << cellShift to 00428bc0 (which derives 5 distance bands), builds the visible cell-space region into grid+0x28 with count grid+0xc8 / pointer grid+0xcc / visible flag grid+0x11c, and installs the grid origin in view space at grid+0x1c and the view-space step of one cell along X at grid+4 and along Y at grid+0x10. The region: Terrain_BuildDrawRegionQuad's square clipped by ViewFrustum_ClipGroundPolygon against a ViewFrustum_Build frustum loosened by 1.5 cells, points shifted down by the cell shift; when nothing is left grid+0x11c goes 0 and the previous polygon stays. Also copies the view's position to g_TerrainViewerPos.

entries.name: Terrain_DrawVisibleCells
entries.description: (grid, view): the terrain draw. Nothing while grid+0x11c is clear. Installs the identity model transform, points the render context's +0x22c at a zero dword for the duration, puts the view's cell (position >> cellShift) in g_TerrainViewerCellX/fd8 and that cell's pending-object count in g_TerrainViewerCellPending, then walks the visible region (grid+0xc8) about that cell: by column (CellWalk_PolygonByColumn, Terrain_DrawCellColumnRun) when the view's heading (+0x14) has magnitude 0x2001..0x5fff (-0x8000 read as 0x7fff), by row (CellWalk_Polygon, Terrain_DrawCellRowRun) otherwise. Ends with Terrain_DrawCellObjects for the viewer's cell when g_TerrainViewerCellPending is still set.

entries.name: Terrain_BuildDrawRegionQuad
entries.description: Builds the terrain draw region as a square of radius (grid[+0x10c] << cellShift) world units centred on the viewer (g_TerrainViewerPos / DAT_006b4fcc), clamped to the grid's own extent ((1 << widthShift) - 2 << cellShift, plus origin at grid+0xf4/+0xf8), and emits it as a 4-corner quad at constant Z (grid+0xfc); writes count 0 instead when the clamped region is empty. Confirms the LOD field is literally a terrain draw radius in cells.

entries.name: Terrain_DrawCellQuad
entries.description: Draws one terrain cell. The caller (Terrain_DrawCellRowRun / Terrain_DrawCellColumnRun) hands it a vertex block already carrying the quad's four camera-space corner positions, in the order (cellX,cellY), (cellX,cellY+1), (cellX+1,cellY+1), (cellX+1,cellY); this fetches the matching four cells at grid[0xec] + index*0x10 (16 bytes/cell) and adds each corner's projected raw height byte (cell[0], via 00495240 against the grid+0xd0 projection state). It re-derives the diagonal split here from the projected corners rather than reading cell[+0xf]: z0+z2 == z1+z3 emits one 4-vertex quad, < 0 splits along corner 0-2, > 0 along corner 1-3. Texture comes from Terrain_ResolveCellTexture(&mat0[cell[0xf] >> 2], cellX, cellY, uvOut), whose four UV pairs are handed to the vertices by index in all three branches -- the fact that pins the corner-to-UV mapping. Each triangle's shade byte is cell[+0xd] (near) / cell[+0xe] (far) and its backface test uses the normals at cell[+0x1] / cell[+0x7] via Terrain_FaceVisibilityTest. Fog: installs the visibility range grid[0x10c] << grid[0x108] via Raster_SetVisibilityRange, then Raster_SetDepthFadeFromDistance(min of the four corners' component 1) -- component 1 is the view-space DEPTH (Raster_PerspectiveDivide divides by it), so a whole cell is fogged from its NEAREST corner's depth, not per pixel and not from a radial distance. Ends by calling Terrain_DrawCellObjects for the cell.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Terrain_DrawCellQuad(int cellX, int cellY, void *grid, int *vertexBlock)

entries.name: Terrain_DrawCellRowRun
entries.description: (ctx, row, xFrom, xTo): CellWalk_Polygon's callback in the terrain draw. The grid is ctx+0x18. Builds the four view-space corners of cell (xFrom, row) from the grid origin at grid+0x1c and the per-cell steps at grid+4 (X) and grid+0x10 (Y), then calls Terrain_DrawCellQuad(cellX, row) for cellX from xFrom to xTo by ctx+0xc, adding the X step to the corners each time. Clears g_TerrainViewerCellPending when row is the viewer's (g_TerrainViewerCellY) and the run covered the viewer's column (g_TerrainViewerCellX).

entries.name: Terrain_DrawCellColumnRun
entries.description: (ctx, column, yFrom, yTo): CellWalk_PolygonByColumn's callback in the terrain draw, Terrain_DrawCellRowRun with the axes exchanged: Terrain_DrawCellQuad(column, cellY) for cellY from yFrom to yTo by ctx+0x10, stepping the corners by the Y step at grid+0x10. Clears g_TerrainViewerCellPending when column is the viewer's and the run covered the viewer's row.

entries.name: Terrain_HeightQuery
entries.description: Converts world (x,y) to a grid cell, fetches 4 corner texels from a 16-byte-per-cell heightmap, does proper barycentric/bilinear interpolation across a per-cell-selectable diagonal (2-bit flag per cell).

entries.name: Terrain_FaceNormalAt
entries.description: (grid, point{x, y}): the normal of the terrain triangle under a point. Shifts the point right by the cell size shift (+0x108) to a cell, returning 0 outside the 1 << +0x100 by 1 << +0x104 grid. Otherwise takes the 16-byte cell record at +0xec and returns a pointer to one of its two int16 face normals, +1 or +7, by which side of the cell's diagonal the point lies on: the diagonal runs one way when the cell's +0xf & 3 is 2 and the other way otherwise. Cam_Update, Mech_ApplyTerrainSlopeToSpeed and Mech_CollisionTest call it.

entries.name: Terrain_DrawCellObjects
entries.description: Draws the objects registered against one terrain cell: bounds-checks the cell index, fetches the cell's pending-object count, and if nonzero calls the hook at HeightGrid+0x125 (ObjList_DrawCellObjects) with (cellX, cellY, count), then clears the cell's scratch. Called from Terrain_DrawCellQuad for every cell the walk draws, from Terrain_DrawVisibleCells for the viewer's cell when the walk missed it, and from ObjList_DrawAfterTerrain for the player's cached cell.

entries.name: HeightGrid_PickDrawCell
entries.description: (grid, pos, radius): the terrain cell an object is drawn with. Starts from the cell holding pos (x, y >> grid+0x108). By the quadrant the viewer's cell (g_TerrainViewerPos/cc, same shift) lies in, when pos is within radius of that cell's viewer-side edge it moves one cell toward the viewer on that axis -- reverted when Terrain_FaceNormalAt gives a face and Terrain_FaceVisibilityTest says it faces away, and per axis when the move lands one cell outside the visible region (the cell list at grid+0xcc, count grid+0xc8). Returns HeightGrid_ClaimDrawCell's record, or 0 off the grid.

entries.name: HeightGrid_ClaimDrawCell
entries.description: (grid, cellXY): the 16-byte cell at grid+0xec + (y << grid+0x100 | x) * 16, or 0 off the grid. For a real cell writes x, y and Terrain_IncrementCellObjectCount's new count into the static 3-byte record at 006b50dc and returns it.

entries.name: HeightGrid_ClearCellScratch
entries.description: Single-statement function: memsets the HeightGrid's +0xf0 per-cell scratch byte array to 0, sized (1 << grid[+0x100]) * (1 << grid[+0x104]) -- exactly one byte per cell. Called first thing in Scene_SubmitFrameObjects (0042841c), so it runs once per frame. That reset is what lets one array serve two unrelated uses: the structure-footprint pass's marked/counted/written bits at mission spawn, and from the first frame onward a per-cell pending-object count, incremented by 00470cac and consumed and re-cleared per cell by Terrain_DrawCellObjects (0046e4a0). Without it the first frame would read a flattened base's footprint marks as object counts.

entries.name: Terrain_RayWalk
entries.description: Ray-versus-terrain traversal, 5129 bytes. (grid, start, end, radius, out, mode). Halves the segment delta until every component fits +/-32000, derives four Q16 slopes via Math_Q16Divide (dy/dx, dz/dx, dx/dy, dz/dy, each 0x10000 on a zero divisor), classifies the ground-plane delta into an octant 0-7, then walks the height grid cell by cell with a two-phase step (a minor-axis crossing stashes the major-axis exit and replays it next iteration). A start cell, or any later cell, outside the grid returns 0. param_6 selects the per-step surface test, and the two ask different questions. Mode 0, the thin ray (es2_xref finds Sim_RaycastTerrain and Terrain_RayHitDistance), reports the ground wherever the segment is at or below it: each non-final step yields an exit point and an edge code 0=W/1=E/2=N/3=S tested by Terrain_EdgeCrossingTest; the final step height-queries its endpoint and, when it is also the first, the start; a crossing calls Terrain_CellSurfaceIntersect when out is non-null, copies its point only when it finds one, and returns 1 either way. Mode 1, the slope walk (es2_xref finds Mech_AiObstacleAvoidance's two probes and Ai_LineOfSightBlocked), packs the delta into three shorts normalised to 0x800 by Math_NormalizeVec3ShortToLength and asks whether the face being crossed is too steep: Terrain_FaceBlocksAt at the start on the first step (a hit reports the start), Terrain_FaceBlocksAt at the endpoint on the last (clear returns 0, a hit reports Terrain_FindDiagonalCrossing), Terrain_EdgeFaceBlocks on every other step (2 reports Terrain_FindDiagonalCrossing, any other nonzero the exit point). A hit returns 1 in AL. The segment has no width in either mode, and the radius argument is only forwarded to Terrain_CellSurfaceIntersect. Six multiplies in the octant-2/3 arms are 32-bit truncating imul/sar rather than Math_Q16Multiply.

entries.name: Terrain_FindDiagonalCrossing
entries.description: (grid, a, b, cellX, cellY, out): where the step a-b inside cell (cellX, cellY) entered the triangle b lies in. Works in cell-local x and y (less the cell origin, (cellX, cellY) << grid+0x108), mirroring x across the cell when the cell's split bits (cell+0xf & 3) are 0, so y < x tells the side for both diagonals. When a and b lie on the same side out = a (z included); otherwise it bisects between them at most eight times, stopping when the midpoint's y equals its x, and out = the last midpoint back in grid coordinates with z = 0. The cell is grid+0xec + (cellY << grid+0x100 | cellX) * 0x10; an index outside 1 << (grid+0x100 + grid+0x104) makes the cell pointer 0, and the split bits are then read from address 0xf. Terrain_RayWalk's mode 1 calls it for a blocking face on the last step's endpoint and for Terrain_EdgeFaceBlocks' answer 2.

entries.name: Terrain_FaceBlocksMovement
entries.description: (unused, direction, normal): whether one terrain triangle stops a moving body, from the UPWARD COMPONENT OF ITS NORMAL: normal.z under 0x60e at the 0x800 normal scale -- about 41 degrees of slope -- is a wall and returns 1 in AL; above 0x60e it returns 0. On 0x60e exactly it returns DotProductVec3Short(normal, direction) < -8000000. es2_xref finds two callers, Terrain_FaceBlocksAt and Terrain_EdgeFaceBlocks, which hand on the direction they are given and a face normal from the cell record, built at length 0x800; Terrain_RayWalk gives them its direction normalised to 0x800 by the same Math_NormalizeVec3ShortToLength. Math_FastMagnitude3D reads at most ~8% low, so each vector is at most ~0x8b4 long, the dot product is never below about -4950000, and the boundary arm returns 0; Deployment_PickPointNearPlayer's zero direction gives 0 too. This is the face test under Terrain_RayWalk's mode 1.

entries.name: Terrain_FaceBlocksAt
entries.description: (grid, dir, point): Terrain_FaceBlocksMovement applied at a world point. Finds the cell by flat index ((y >> cellShift) << widthShift) + (x >> cellShift); an index outside the whole array returns 1 (blocks) at once, so a point just past the grid's west or east edge reads the cell at the far end of the neighbouring row. Otherwise it picks one of the cell's two face normals by the diagonal selector (+0x0f & 3), the split the height query uses: selector 0 the far normal (+0x07) when cellSize < fx + fy, selector 1 the near (+0x01), selector 2 the far when fy <= fx, else the near; selector 3 matches no arm and passes an uninitialised local as the normal pointer. It returns Terrain_FaceBlocksMovement(grid, dir, normal). Callers found by es2_xref: two calls in Terrain_RayWalk and one in Deployment_PickPointNearPlayer, which passes a zero direction.

entries.name: Terrain_EdgeFaceBlocks
entries.description: (grid, cellX, cellY, dir, edge): the mode-1 test for a step leaving a cell across a named edge (0=W/1=E/2=N/3=S): asks this cell's triangle bordering the edge first and the neighbouring cell's second. A cell's near triangle (+1) borders its west edge and its far one (+7) its east edge under either diagonal; north and south depend on the split bits. Returns 0 clear, 2 when this cell's own face stops the segment (Terrain_RayWalk reports Terrain_FindDiagonalCrossing), 1 when the neighbour's does or either cell's flat index is outside the array (Terrain_RayWalk reports the exit point). The neighbour is found by flat index, so across the grid's west or east edge it is the adjacent row's far cell.

entries.name: Terrain_EdgeCrossingTest
entries.description: Terrain_RayWalk's per-step test: (grid, cellX, cellY, exitPoint, edgeCode) -> is the terrain along that cell edge at or above the exit point. Takes the edge's two corner heights (rawByte * grid+0x118 + grid+0x110); below both = clear, at or above both = hit, straddling = interpolate the edge height at the exit point (fraction along Y for edges 0/1, along X for 2/3). Bounds-checks only the flat corner index, so an edge in the last column reads the next row's first cell -- the same wrap Terrain_HeightQuery has.

entries.name: Terrain_CellSurfaceIntersect
entries.description: Solves exactly where a segment meets the ground inside one cell, once Terrain_EdgeCrossingTest has reported a crossing. Builds a plane from each of the cell's two face normals (cell+0x1 and cell+0x7) through a corner that triangle contains, and intersects via Math_PlaneSegmentIntersect; works in cell-local X/Y with world Z and adds the cell origin back on the way out. Returns a pointer to the point, held in the statics at DAT_006b50e0, or null. Near plane first, through corner (x,y); its point is accepted when it lies in the near triangle by cell+0xf&3 (selector 0: x+y <= cellSize; 1: always; 2: x < y), the same split Terrain_HeightQuery uses. Otherwise null for selector 1, else the far plane, whose point is accepted without a triangle test; null when it misses the segment or the cell (or, for selector 0, the cell east) is off the grid by flat index. Its fourth parameter -- Terrain_RayWalk's walk radius, the literal 200 the weapon ray record carries -- is never read. Two quirks: selector 0's far triangle has no corner in this cell, so it shifts one cell east and uses corner (x+1,y); selector 2's (and 3's) far plane keeps the near plane's constant -h00*nzNear rather than -h00*nzFar, so it sits h00*(nzNear-nzFar)/nzFar above the true far plane, which moves the point along the segment and can carry it off either end, giving null.

entries.name: Terrain_ProjectFarEdgeAhead
entries.description: (grid, view, out): projects to the screen the point the terrain draw radius (grid+0x10c << cellShift) straight ahead of the viewer along its heading (+0x14), at the grid's lowest height (+0x110); the distance is a literal 1000 instead when the viewer's cell is within the radius of any grid edge. Builds the 2D transform with Math_BuildRotation2D and the viewer's x/y, applies it with Transform2D_ApplyToPoint, then Transform_ApplyToPoint by the world-to-view transform at 006c6078, Raster_PerspectiveDivide and Raster_ProjectToScreen; the screen x/y go to out[0]/out[1]. Its one caller, Scene_DrawTerrainPass, passes +0x72 of g_TheaterHzline. Only Hzline_FillGround's rolled branch reads it, into polygon vertices it overwrites before drawing, so the point never reaches the frame.

entries.name: HGrid_SpanAddCell
entries.description: (grid, cx, cy): for a cell with 0 <= cx < (1 << grid+0x100) - 1 and 0 <= cy < (1 << grid+0x104) - 1, widens row cy's span in HGrid_RowSpans to include cx and the range HGrid_SpanFirstRow..HGrid_SpanLastRow to include cy. HGrid_SpanAddOctants calls it. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's HGrid_SpanAddCell (0042b8d3), with the grid's shift fields 4 bytes further on.

entries.name: HGrid_SpanAddOctants
entries.description: (grid, centre, a, b): HGrid_SpanAddCell on the eight points centre +/- (a, b) and centre +/- (b, a), each shifted down to a cell by grid+0x108. es2_xref finds no reference to it. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's HGrid_SpanAddOctants (0042b965).

entries.name: HGrid_SpanMeanHeight
entries.description: (grid): averages byte 0 (the height Terrain_HeightQuery reads) of the 16-byte cells at grid+0xec over HGrid_RowSpans: rows HGrid_SpanFirstRow to HGrid_SpanLastRow + 1, the extra row reusing the last row's span, columns from each span's minX to maxX + 1. A cell index outside 0 .. (1 << (grid+0x100 + grid+0x104)) - 1 yields a null cell pointer that the loop still reads through. Returns sum / count. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: HeightGrid_SetCellScratchByte
entries.description: Writes the HeightGrid's parallel per-cell scratch byte array at +0xf0, addressing it by cell pointer -- ((cell - grid[+0xec]) >> 4) -- where Terrain_SetCellScratch (00470cd0) addresses the same array by cell coordinates. Called once per cell by TerrainZone_PopulateFromBitmap with 0, zeroing the array at load; the ASCII fallback loader writes it inline instead. The array's consumers are the structure-footprint pass (Terrain_MarkStructureFootprint / Terrain_FlattenStructureFootprints) and then, at runtime, Terrain_DrawCellObjects' per-cell pending-object count.
entries.signature: void __cdecl HeightGrid_SetCellScratchByte(void *grid, void *cell, unsigned char value)

entries.name: HeightGrid_GetCellScratchByte
entries.description: Reads the +0xf0 scratch byte for the cell a 16-byte cell pointer names -- the by-pointer counterpart of Terrain_GetCellScratch (00470cf4), and the read half of HeightGrid_SetCellScratchByte (00470c68).

entries.name: Terrain_IncrementCellObjectCount
entries.description: Increments the +0xf0 scratch byte of the cell a 16-byte cell pointer names and returns the new value -- the per-frame writer of the pending-object count Terrain_DrawCellObjects (0046e4a0) reads back and clears. Addresses by cell pointer, like HeightGrid_SetCellScratchByte (00470c68), rather than by coordinates like Terrain_SetCellScratch (00470cd0). The count is only meaningful after HeightGrid_ClearCellScratch (0046e840) has reset the array for the frame.

entries.name: Terrain_SetCellScratch
entries.description: Stores one byte in the height grid's +0xf0 per-cell scratch array at (cellY << widthShift) + cellX. Coordinate-addressed counterpart to HeightGrid_SetCellScratchByte (00470c68), which addresses the same array by cell pointer. No bounds check.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Terrain_SetCellScratch(void *grid, int cellX, int cellY, unsigned char value)

entries.name: Terrain_GetCellScratch
entries.description: Reads one byte of the height grid's +0xf0 per-cell scratch array at (cellY << widthShift) + cellX. Getter for Terrain_SetCellScratch. No bounds check.
entries.signature: unsigned char __cdecl Terrain_GetCellScratch(void *grid, int cellX, int cellY)

entries.name: HGrid_SpanMarkCells
entries.description: (grid): HeightGrid_SetCellScratchByte(grid, cell, 1) over the cells HGrid_SpanMeanHeight walks (HGrid_RowSpans rows HGrid_SpanFirstRow to HGrid_SpanLastRow + 1, columns minX to maxX + 1). No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Terrain_MarkStructureFootprint
entries.description: Registers one structure's footprint in the height grid's +0xf0 scratch array, ready for Terrain_FlattenStructureFootprints to level it. Sets the scratch byte to 1 for the cell the structure stands in unconditionally, then walks the cells in the position's radius-sized bounding box and, for each whose corner (cellX << cellShift, cellY << cellShift, position.z) is within radius by Math_FastMagnitude3D -- the z terms cancel, so the test is planar -- marks that cell plus the three west, south and south-west of it, covering all four quads meeting that corner. radius is the caller's SimObject_GetShapeRadius (vtable +0x10). Callers: Base_AttachToGroup (00405c3c) and DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects' own base branch, each immediately before that structure's height query. No bounds checking beyond refusing to step to a negative index.

entries.name: Terrain_AccumulateFootprint
entries.description: Terrain_FlattenStructureFootprints' measuring half: an eight-way recursive flood fill over cells whose +0xf0 scratch byte has bit 0 set and bit 1 clear. Sets bit 1, then adds the cell's raw height byte to DAT_006b54f4 and increments the cell count DAT_006b54f8, which the caller divides to get the region's average height.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Terrain_AccumulateFootprint(void *grid, int cellX, int cellY)

entries.name: Terrain_WriteFootprintHeight
entries.description: Terrain_FlattenStructureFootprints' writing half, and the part that produces the FLAT TOP rather than a flat set of corner samples. Eight-way recursive like Terrain_AccumulateFootprint but over bit 2 of the +0xf0 scratch byte; the force argument makes a cell take the height whether or not it is part of the footprint, and it is passed 1 only for the neighbours east, north and north-east. Those three are therefore written but not recursed through, being unmarked, so a region gains one sample on each of those two sides -- which turns a single marked cell into a 2x2 block of equal samples, i.e. one flat quad centred on the structure with the four surrounding quads sloping down to the plain.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Terrain_WriteFootprintHeight(void *grid, int cellX, int cellY, int height, int force)

entries.name: Terrain_FlattenStructureFootprints
entries.description: THE REASON A TURRET STANDS ON A FLAT-TOPPED MOUND. A zone heightmap marks each ground vehicle with a single raised sample (ZONE555: one cell of 120 in a plain of 97 under each turret), which as a corner sample is the apex of a four-quad pyramid at the cell's CORNER while the structure stands near its centre. This levels it instead: walk every cell, and where the scratch byte is marked (bit 0) but not yet counted (bit 1), flood-fill the connected region with Terrain_AccumulateFootprint to get its raw-height sum and count, then write sum/count back over it with Terrain_WriteFootprintHeight. Finishes with Terrain_BuildSurface, since every normal, diagonal selector and baked shade is now stale. Called once by DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects (at 004263d9) after the whole roster is placed, which then re-queries every base's ground height. Walks both axes to 1 << widthShift, which would half-cover a taller-than-wide zone; every retail zone is square.

entries.name: Terrain_PaintFormationPad
entries.description: Stamps one base formation's material over the terrain tile a world point falls in, and marks that formation's occupied cells for the flattening pass. The only writer of cell +0xf bits [2:7] outside the two zone loaders, and the only path by which materials 2-12 reach shipped terrain -- TerrainZone_PopulateFromBitmap's roll is capped at 2. The tile is 1 << (0x15 - mat0[material].BlockShift) world units square, independent of the zone's cell shift, and dimension x dimension map entries span it exactly; a cell takes 1 << (cellShift - 13) entries per axis. Every cell of the tile is painted; only cells whose map byte is nonzero also get Terrain_SetCellScratch(1), which is the second input to Terrain_FlattenStructureFootprints (00471190) alongside the per-object radius marks of Terrain_MarkStructureFootprint (00470dc8), and is why a base's whole pad levels as one region. Map row 0 indexes the tile's HIGH-y edge and counts down. The material write is skipped entirely when CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand is set (the low-memory mode: -l, or under 12 MB physical), leaving the ground flat but unpainted.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Terrain_PaintFormationPad(void *grid, int *worldPoint, int materialIndex, unsigned char **mapRows, int dimension)

entries.name: Terrain_StaticInit
entries.description: _INIT_ entry 004a7bac (pointer at 004a7bae): Rtl_VectorNew with Rtl_ReturnArg over 8-byte arrays of 4, 4 and 3 at 006b5000, 006b5020 and 006b5040, and with maybe_Point3I_Ctor over 0xc-byte arrays of 4, 4 and 3 at Terrain_CellCorners (006b5058), 006b5088 and 006b50b8 -- the terrain draw's per-cell scratch vertices. The 'HeightGrid' and 'DummyDrawable' class records follow it.

entries.name: HeightGridCell_ElementCtor
entries.description: (cell): returns cell; the LEAs of +1 and +7 are left over from inlined empty member constructors. Per-element constructor of the HeightGrid's 16-byte cell array at grid+0xec: TerrainZone_PopulateFromBitmap (0046c413) and TerrainZone_LoadHeightmap (0046c8ac) build it with Rtl_VectorNew(0, 0x10, (1 << grid+0x100) * (1 << grid+0x104), 1, this).

entries.name: DummyDrawable_Dtor
entries.description: DummyDrawable vtable +0x08 (004a0cb8, RTTI 'DummyDrawable', 0xc bytes, derived from DRAWABLE), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). Two RTL destructor-count decrements, then Mem_Delete(this) on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 004714e3; class record at 0047147d

entries.name: DummyDrawable_DrawNoOp
entries.description: DummyDrawable vtable +0x00 (004a0cb8): an empty body. Terrain_FillCellUntextured installs the table.

entries.name: DummyDrawable_GetPositionNull
entries.description: DummyDrawable vtable +0x04 (004a0cb8): returns 0 -- a null position pointer.

entries.name: Vfw_ICDecompressEx
entries.description: vfw.h's ICDecompressEx compiled out of line: (hic, dwFlags, lpbiSrc, lpSrc, xSrc, ySrc, dxSrc, dySrc, lpbiDst, lpDst, xDst, yDst, dxDst, dyDst) packed into a 0x34-byte ICDECOMPRESSEX and sent with ICSendMessage(hic, 0x403e = ICM_DECOMPRESSEX, &block, 0x34). No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Vfw_ICDecompressExBegin
entries.description: vfw.h's ICDecompressExBegin compiled out of line: Vfw_ICDecompressEx's packing sent as 0x403c = ICM_DECOMPRESSEX_BEGIN. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Vfw_ICDecompressExQuery
entries.description: vfw.h's ICDecompressExQuery compiled out of line: Vfw_ICDecompressEx's packing sent as 0x403d = ICM_DECOMPRESSEX_QUERY. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Vfw_ICDrawSuggestFormat
entries.description: vfw.h's inline ICDrawSuggestFormat compiled out of line in the AVI module, __stdcall with 8 arguments (RET 0x20): (hic, lpbiIn, lpbiOut, dxSrc, dySrc, dxDst, dyDst, hicDecomp) copies the seven after hic into a 0x1c-byte ICDRAWSUGGEST block and returns ICSendMessage(hic, 0x4032 ICM_DRAW_SUGGESTFORMAT, &block, 0x1c). No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Vfw_ICSetStatusProc
entries.description: vfw.h's inline ICSetStatusProc compiled out of line, __stdcall with 4 arguments (RET 0x10): (hic, dwFlags, lParam, fpfnStatus) packs the last three into a 0xc-byte ICSETSTATUSPROC block and returns ICSendMessage(hic, 0x4048 ICM_SET_STATUS_PROC, &block, 0xc). No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Avi_OpenDevice
entries.description: Frameless, in bytes Ghidra left undefined after Vfw_ICSetStatusProc (es2_xref reports the address as Vfw_ICSetStatusProc+0x34). mciSendCommandA(0, 0x803 MCI_OPEN, 0x2000 MCI_OPEN_TYPE, parms) with lpstrDeviceType = 'avivideo' (004a0cdc); returns 1 when MCI answers 0, else 0. The device id MCI writes into the parms block is discarded. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Avi_CloseDevice
entries.description: Frameless. mciSendCommandA(mciGetDeviceIDA('avivideo' at 004a0ce5), 0x804 MCI_CLOSE, 0, &parms), mciGetDeviceIDA through its import thunk (0049699c). No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Avi_MoveWindow
entries.description: (window, rect): GetClientRect(window); with rect, moves to its {left, top, width, height}, else to (0, 0) at the client size. The window moved is the MCI movie window 004717ec stores at 006b5504, not the argument. VSHELL's Avi_MoveWindow (0041dfd6) moves its argument and is otherwise the same code.

entries.name: Avi_CloseMovie
entries.description: (deviceId): when deviceId is non-zero, mciSendCommandA(deviceId, 0x804 MCI_CLOSE, 0, &parms). Avi_Play passes Avi_MciDeviceId (004a0cd0) after playback; es2_xref finds that one call.

entries.name: Avi_NotifyHook
entries.description: The WndProcHook filter Avi_Play registers for the length of a movie: (hwnd, msg, wParam, lParam) sets Avi_PlaybackDone (004a0ccc) to 1 on msg 0x3b9 MM_MCINOTIFY with wParam 1 MCI_NOTIFY_SUCCESSFUL, and returns 0 so MainWndProc goes on handling the message. Stored pointers at 00471821 (WndProcHook_Register) and 00471930 (WndProcHook_Unregister), both in Avi_Play.

entries.name: Avi_Play
entries.description: (path, rect): plays one AVI through MCI command messages. WndProcHook_Register(Avi_NotifyHook); MCI_OPEN (0x803) with flags 0x30200 (MCI_OPEN_ELEMENT | MCI_DGV_OPEN_WS | MCI_DGV_OPEN_PARENT), element path, style 0x40000000 (WS_CHILD) and parent MainWindow_Handle. On success keeps the device id in Avi_MciDeviceId (004a0cd0), sends MCI_WINDOW (0x841) MCI_DGV_WINDOW_STATE SW_SHOW and MCI_STATUS (0x814) item 0x4001 MCI_DGV_STATUS_HWND into Avi_MovieWindow (006b5504), runs Avi_MoveWindow(main window, rect), clears Avi_PlaybackDone and sends MCI_PLAY (0x806) with MCI_NOTIFY to the main window. Then Win_PumpMessages, Keyboard_FlushKeys on the claimed keyboard (006c5f3c), and Keyboard_PopKey / Win_PumpMessages until Avi_PlaybackDone is set, a code whose low byte is 1 (Esc) or 0x39 (Space) setting it itself; then Avi_CloseMovie. WndProcHook_Unregister(Avi_NotifyHook) on both paths. Returns 1 when a key ended the movie, else 0 (also when MCI_OPEN fails). No caller found by es2_xref. VSHELL's Avi_Play (0041e01c) is a different implementation, through MCI command strings.

entries.name: Pool_LinkFreeList
entries.description: (pool, buffer, count, elementSize): writes the pool header -- free count +0 = count, in-use count +2 = 0, element size +4, buffer +6, free-list head +0xa = buffer, in-use head +0xe = 0 -- then chains the count nodes of elementSize + 8 bytes in buffer, each node's next at +0 and previous at +4, the last next 0. Pool_Init calls it on the zeroed allocation. Ghidra's fastcall prototype is wrong; all four arguments are on the stack.

entries.name: Pool_Init
entries.description: (pool, count, elementSize): allocates count * (elementSize + 8) bytes with Mem_NewArray, zeroes them and links them into the pool's free list (Pool_LinkFreeList). Returns the pool.

entries.name: Pool_Alloc
entries.description: Pops a node off a free-list pool and returns node + 8, or 0 when the pool is empty; the node's two link words are rewritten and the rest is not zeroed. Pool header as it reads it: int16 free count +0, int16 in-use count +2, free-list head +0xa, in-use list head +0xe; a node links next at +0 and prev at +4. The node moves to the head of the in-use list. Pool_Free is its inverse and Pool_Init builds the pool.

entries.name: maybe_Pool_OperatorNew
entries.description: (size, pool): returns Pool_Alloc(pool); the first argument is not read. The name assumes the shape of a class operator new(size_t, Pool*), as VSHELL's maybe_Memory_OperatorNew is read. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: maybe_Pool_AllocZeroed
entries.description: Pool_Alloc followed by a memset of the node to its element size -- the zeroing allocator. UNREFERENCED: no E8 call, no E9 tail jump, no Ghidra reference, and the literal address appears as a raw dword nowhere in the image (control: SimObject_SetRunInto's address appears in its 8 vtable slots under the same scan). Every pool allocation in DBSIM therefore goes through the non-zeroing 00471a24, which is why a recycled node keeps stale field values.

entries.name: Pool_Free
entries.description: Returns one node to a free-list pool: decrements the in-use count, unlinks the node from the in-use list through the prev pointer at node-4, pushes it onto the free list and clears its prev. Takes node+8 (what the allocator handed out) and steps back to the header. It does NOT zero the node, so a reissued slot carries the previous tenant's bytes. Exactly one caller in the image, ObjectPool_FlushDeleteQueue -- so a deferred-delete queue is the only route back into any pool.

entries.name: Pool_Next
entries.description: (pool, node): the in-use node after node (link at node-8), or the first in-use node (+0xe) when node is null; returns it as node + 8, or 0 at the end. For a node address below 0x100000 it sprintfs a diagnostic ('array ptr ...') into a local buffer it never uses.

entries.name: Pool_Prev
entries.description: (pool, node): the in-use node before node (link at node-4), returned as node + 8 or 0; with a null node, walks Pool_Next to the last in-use node.

entries.name: Pool_Nth
entries.description: (pool, n): walks the pool with Pool_Prev from 0 and returns, in EAX, the element reached after n + 1 steps (the n-th, counting from 0), or 0 when the walk ends first. DBSim_BuildGroupRecord and Mission_ResolveRefByKind resolve mission indices to mechs, vehicles and structures with it.

entries.name: Int64_AddInPlace
entries.description: (lo*, hi*, addLo, addHi): adds {addHi:addLo} to the 64-bit value in the two dwords, carrying from the low half. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Int64_AddInPlace (0045c110). Raster_BuildEdgeTables and Raster_DrawTexturedPolyNear step their 64-bit accumulators with it.

entries.name: Int64_SubInPlace
entries.description: (lo*, hi*, subLo, subHi): subtracts {subHi:subLo} from the 64-bit value in the two dwords, borrowing from the low half. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Int64_SubInPlace (0045c128).

entries.name: Int64Pair_Q16Divide
entries.description: (out, in): when the int32 divisor in[4] is non-zero, out[0] = ({in[1]:in[0]} << 16) / in[4] and out[1] = ({in[3]:in[2]} << 16) / in[4]; otherwise out is left unchanged. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Int64Pair_Q16Divide (0045c15e).

entries.name: Raster_ScaleRunStep
entries.description: (out, delta, length, shift): the DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Raster_ScaleRunStep (0045c193): divides the two 64-bit and one 32-bit deltas by length, scaled by 2^shift. Raster_DrawTexturedPolyNear calls it once per row.

entries.name: SpriteSequence_Init
entries.description: Initialises a 0x2a-byte sprite sequencer over a bank (+0x1e) and a sequence set {count, sequences} (+0x16): state 0, sequence 0 selected (+0x12 = set's first sequence), start tick and frame index zero. Sequences are {count, frames}; a frame entry is {bank frame, hold in coarse ticks}.

entries.name: SpriteSequence_Select
entries.description: Selects sequence n of the sequencer's set (+0x12, index at +0x02) if n is within the set's count; returns whether it did.

entries.name: SpriteSequence_Start
entries.description: Starts the selected sequence at a position: stamps +0x06 with Time_GetCoarseTicks, frame index 0, holds-so-far +0x0a = frame 0's hold, end of hold +0x0e = start + that, position +0x22, state 1, and blits frame 0.

entries.name: SpriteSequence_SetIdle
entries.description: (seq): writes 0 to the sequencer's state short at +0, the value SpriteSequence_State reports as idle. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: SpriteSequence_Step
entries.description: Steps a playing sequencer on the coarse clock: once the current hold has ended it advances past every frame whose hold has run out, and reaching the last frame sets state 2; blits the frame it lands on (or whenever the second argument is set). A call in state 2 drops it to 0 and returns 0; otherwise returns 1 while playing.

entries.name: SpriteSequence_State
entries.description: Returns the sequencer's state short at +0: 0 idle, 1 playing, 2 just ended.

entries.name: CellWalk_SetCallback
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's CellWalk_SetCallback (0042f3b0): (ctx, callback, value) stores the callback at ctx+0x14 and its value at ctx+0x18. Terrain_DrawVisibleCells passes the height grid as the value.

entries.name: CellWalk_Polygon
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's CellWalk_Polygon (0042f3c4), read in its own decompile: (ctx, centre, polygon) cuts the polygon into four quadrants about the centre cell with Poly_ClipToHalfPlane, scan-converts each with Poly_BuildSpanList and calls callback(ctx, row, xFrom, xTo) per run, far to near when maybe_g_DepthBufferEnabled == 0 && DAT_0049aad4 != 0 (0 and 1 in the image) and near to far otherwise. Terrain_DrawVisibleCells walks the terrain by row with it, callback Terrain_DrawCellRowRun.

entries.name: Point_RotateQuarterAbout
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Point_RotateQuarterAbout (0042f968): (&x, &y, centre) x' = cx + (y - cy), y' = cy - (x - cx), in place.

entries.name: Point_UnrotateQuarterAbout
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Point_UnrotateQuarterAbout (0042f990): (&x, &y, centre) x = cx + cy - y', y = cy + (x' - cx), in place, the inverse of Point_RotateQuarterAbout.

entries.name: CellWalk_PolygonByColumn
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's CellWalk_PolygonByColumn (0042f9b8): turns the polygon a quarter about the centre with Point_RotateQuarterAbout, runs CellWalk_Polygon's far-to-near branch with no flag test, turns each run's ends back with Point_UnrotateQuarterAbout and calls callback(ctx, column, yFrom, yTo), then turns the points back. Terrain_DrawVisibleCells walks the terrain by column with it, callback Terrain_DrawCellColumnRun. Ghidra's decompile shows the context as Rtl_VectorNew's return, as it does for the VSHELL copy.

entries.name: CellWalk_Rect
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's CellWalk_Rect (0042fe5a), identical after normalisation: (ctx, centre, rect{x0, y0, x1, y1}) walks the rectangle's cells far to near without scan conversion, setting the direction fields ctx+8, +0xc and +0x10 per quadrant and calling the ctx+0x14 callback(ctx, row, xFrom, xTo) row by row, each half running its first quadrant's rows before its second's. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Poly_BuildSpanList
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Poly_BuildSpanList (0043000d): (poly, spans, header), translating the points so their minimum x and y are 0, scan-converting with Poly_ScanConvertEitherWinding, adding the minimum x back to every span and filling header = {top row, bottom row, row count, pointer to the first {x0, x1} pair}. Called after Poly_ClipToHalfPlane by 00471e38 and 004723f8.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile and disassembly at 00472a08, compared with VSHELL 0043000d

entries.name: Poly_ClipToHalfPlane
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Poly_ClipToHalfPlane (004300c7), the same code in a frame 8 bytes larger (0x50 against 0x48). (keepHigh, alongX, value, in, out): one Sutherland-Hodgman pass keeping the part of polygon in ({count, points*}) with x (alongX) or y at >= value (keepHigh) or <= value, writing the points through out's point pointer (out+4, filled in before the call) and the count to out+0, and returning the count's low byte; a polygon of no points gives 0. Each point is classed -1, 0 or +1 by the sign of its coordinate minus value, the first edge running from the last point to the first. The 19-byte table at 00472bdd (the same bytes as VSHELL's at 004301da), indexed by (keepHigh ? 0 : 10) + 3*previous + current + 4, picks a case through the five-dword table at 00472bf0: 0 or 1 emits nothing, 2 the current point, 3 the crossing then the current point, 4 the crossing alone. So a current point on the kept side is emitted, preceded by the crossing when the previous one was on the dropped side; a current point on the line is emitted alone, whatever the previous one; and a current point on the dropped side emits the crossing when the previous one was on the kept side and nothing otherwise. A crossing takes value on the cut axis and prev + (cur - prev) * (value - prevCut) / (curCut - prevCut) on the other, measured from the previous point, the product in 32 bits and the division truncating.

entries.name: VolRStream_Ctor
entries.description: VolRStream() constructor (vtable 004a0e28): Stream_BaseCtor, clears the filter pointers +0x27/+0x2b and position fields +0xa, +0xe, +0x16, handle -1, status 5. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolRStream_Ctor without its g_VolumeGroup assert.

entries.name: VolRStream_CtorFromHandle
entries.description: VolRStream(handle) constructor (vtable 004a0e28): as VolRStream_Ctor, but adopts an open handle without owning it (+0x26 = 0) and probes it with _lseek(h, 0, SEEK_CUR); failure goes to VolRStream_SetIoError. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolRStream_CtorFromHandle.

entries.name: VolRStream_CtorFromPath
entries.description: VolRStream(path) constructor (vtable 004a0e28, RTTI name 'VolRStream', 0x2f bytes): Stream_BaseCtor, clears the entry fields and filter pointers, handle -1, then VolRStream_Open(path). The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolRStream_CtorFromPath, without the volume-group assert; layout as described there.

entries.name: VolRStream_Dtor
entries.description: VolRStream destructor: deletes the RLERStream at +0x27 and the LZHRStream at +0x2b through their virtual destructors, VolRStream_Close, Stream_BaseDtor, frees when flag & 1. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolRStream_Dtor.

entries.name: VolRStream_SetFile
entries.description: (stream, handle): VolRStream_Close, adopt the handle without owning it (+0x26 = 0), probe it with _lseek(h, 0, SEEK_CUR); status 0 on success, else VolRStream_SetIoError. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolRStream_SetFile.

entries.name: VolRStream_Close
entries.description: _close on the handle at +8 when the stream owns it (+0x26), releases the filters at +0x27 (0047b4c0) and +0x2b (0047b8c0), zeroes +0xa, +0xe and +0x16, handle -1, status 5. Returns 0 with status 3 if _close fails. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolRStream_Close.

entries.name: VolRStream_Open
entries.description: VolRStream::open(path), the DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolRStream_Open with the asserts compiled out: tries _open(path, O_BINARY|O_RDONLY) first, then VolumeGroup_FindEntry on g_VolumeGroup (004a0d30), and switches on the entry's compression type: 2 reads the volume stream directly, 7 attaches the RLERStream at +0x27, 9 the LZHRStream at +0x2b (each created on first use). Any other type returns 1 with status 0 and no source at +0xe. Returns 0 with status 1 when neither source has the file.

entries.name: VolRStream_SetGroup
entries.description: (a, b, c, d): creates g_VolumeGroup (004a0d30, 0x79 bytes, 00467a98) on first use, otherwise passes the same arguments to VolumeGroup_SetGroup on the existing group. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolRStream_SetGroup without its allocation assert.

entries.name: VolRStream_DeleteGroup
entries.description: (): when g_VolumeGroup (004a0d30) is set, VolumeGroup_Dtor(g_VolumeGroup, 3) and clears g_VolumeGroup. Frameless, between VolRStream_SetGroup and VolRStream_LoadVolume. No reference found by es2_xref. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolRStream_DeleteGroup (004030a5).

entries.name: VolRStream_LoadVolume
entries.description: (path): passes path to VolumeGroup_LoadVolume on g_VolumeGroup (004a0d30). The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolRStream_LoadVolume without its assert.

entries.name: VolRStream_GetSize
entries.description: Returns a VolRStream's length: _filelength of the handle for a plain file, the entry size at +0x22 for an open volume entry, else 0. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolRStream_GetSize.

entries.name: VolRStream_GetPosition
entries.description: VolRStream vtable slot +4: _lseek(h, 0, SEEK_CUR) for a file handle, else the position within the volume entry (+0x16), or 0 when no entry is open. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolRStream_GetPosition.

entries.name: VolRStream_SetPosition
entries.description: VolRStream vtable slot +8: (stream, pos). The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolRStream_SetPosition without its assert.

entries.name: VolRStream_GetCapabilities
entries.description: VolRStream vtable slot +0xc: answers capability queries 0-4 as VSHELL's VolRStream_GetCapabilities does, without its assert.

entries.name: VolRStream_Flush
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolRStream_Flush (00403396).
entries.source: es2_naming.py diff DBSIM 0047346c VSHELL 00403396: identical after normalisation; RTTI VolRStream vtable slot

entries.name: VolRStream_SetIoError
entries.description: Sets the stream status at +4 to 1 when the dword at 004966ea is nonzero, else 3, and returns 0. That dword is the cw3220 _errno import thunk's own code bytes (FF 25 10 C3), not errno, so it always stores 1, as in VSHELL's VolRStream_SetIoError.

entries.name: VolRStream_Write
entries.description: VolRStream vtable slot +0x14: sets status 4 and returns 0. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolRStream_Write without its assert.

entries.name: VolRStream_Read
entries.description: VolRStream::read, the DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolRStream_Read, including its end clamp: a read that runs past the entry size copies size - position + 1 bytes from the volume stream at +0xa, the rest of the entry plus the one-byte trailer after it, and sets status 2.

entries.name: Sos_InitBackend
entries.description: (window, config): SFX backend bring-up. Keeps window at Music_NotifyWindow and binds the SOS library; then copies config words 0, 1 and 2 (rate, the fixed 1, width) to 004a0e5c, 004a0e5e and 004a0e60, word 6 (buffers) to 004a0e64 and word 7 (0x200) to 004a0e62, and calls Sos_OpenDrivers(config word 3, the Driver id, 0xffff, window, window) -- MIDI id 0xffff, so no MIDI driver -- and on failure Sos_OpenDrivers(1, 0xffff, window, window), unbinding the library when that fails too. Returns true on success.

entries.name: Sos_Shutdown
entries.description: Sos_ShutdownDrivers, then Sos_UnbindLibrary. SfxManager_Dtor's first call.

entries.name: Sos_AcquireDigiDriver
entries.description: Returns whether Sos_AcquireDriver(Sos_GetDriverHandle()) returns 0.

entries.name: Sos_ReleaseDigiDriver
entries.description: Sos_ReleaseDriver(Sos_GetDriverHandle(), 0x1000).

entries.name: Sos_Service
entries.description: (hwnd, msg, wParam, lParam): Sos_UserService(Sos_GetDriverHandle()); then, when hwnd is non-zero, passes the window message on to 00474994. Returns 0.

entries.name: maybe_Sfx_FillDefaults
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's maybe_Sfx_FillDefaults (0042d8ea), byte-identical: (out) writes out+0 = 0x78, +4 = 0x20, +8 = 1. maybe_Sfx_FillDefaultsThunk (00463870) calls it after testing its address for null (MOV EDX,0x473700 at 00463876), and zeroes the three dwords itself when the address is null. What the three values mean is not established.

entries.name: Sos_LoadOrFreeSample
entries.description: (resourceName, slotIndex, load, isMidiSong). Loads or frees one resource's backend object at record+0x214. isMidiSong picks the .hmp song path (00474550 / 004745fc) over the digital sample path (00474254 / 004743fc).

entries.name: Sos_StartVoice
entries.description: (resourceRecord+4, voiceRecord+4). Starts one voice on the backend. Branches three ways on the voice flags: bit 0 = MIDI song, bit 12 = the streamed-by-name path (Sos_StartStream), otherwise a SOS digital sample -- packing volume into both 16-bit halves, translating loop count 0 to -1 (infinite) and n to n-1, and copying pan and callback into the sample object. The sample path zeroes voiceRecord+0x20 and passes it to sosDIGIStartSample as the out-handle, so each call yields a fresh SOS handle and the previous one is dropped without being stopped.

entries.name: Sos_StopVoice
entries.description: Stops one voice on whichever of the three backend paths its flags select.

entries.name: Sos_PauseVoice
entries.description: (voice): for a MIDI song (flags +4 bit 0) returns whether Sos_MidiPauseSong(+0x20, 0) answers 0; for a digital sample it returns 0 without a call. No caller found by es2_xref. Identical after normalisation to VSHELL's 0042dae6.

entries.name: Sos_ResumeVoice
entries.description: (voice): for a MIDI song (flags +4 bit 0) returns whether Sos_MidiResumeSong(+0x20) answers 0; for a digital sample it returns 0 without a call. No caller found by es2_xref. Identical after normalisation to VSHELL's 0042db0f.

entries.name: Sos_VoiceIsDone
entries.description: (voice): Sos_MidiSongDone(+0x20) for a MIDI song (flags +4 bit 0), otherwise Sos_SampleDone(Sos_GetDriverHandle(), +0x20); returns the answer (the decompile drops it). Sfx_IsDone asks it.

entries.name: Sos_GetVoiceBytesProcessed
entries.description: (voice): for a digital sample (flags +4 bit 0 clear) returns Sos_GetBytesProcessed(Sos_GetDriverHandle(), +0x20); for a MIDI song returns 0. No caller found by es2_xref. Identical after normalisation to VSHELL's 0042db63.

entries.name: Sos_SetMasterVolume
entries.description: Writes Sos_MasterVolume from the passed voice record's +0x10. es2_xref.py finds no branch, stored pointer or vtable slot referencing it.

entries.name: Sos_ApplyMidiMasterVolume
entries.description: (voice): Sos_MidiSetMasterVolume(+0x10 * 0x7f / 100), Sos_ApplyVolume's MIDI branch on its own, without the digital path. No caller found by es2_xref. Identical after normalisation to VSHELL's 0042db99.

entries.name: Sos_ApplyVolume
entries.description: Converts a voice's 0-100 volume to the backend's range: volume * Sos_MasterVolume * 0x7fff / 10000 duplicated into both 16-bit halves for left and right, or volume * 0x7f / 100 for a MIDI song.

entries.name: Sos_ApplyVoicePitch
entries.description: (voice): for a digital sample (flags +4 bit 0 clear), Sos_SetSampleRate(Sos_GetDriverHandle(), +0x20, (+0x1c * 11025) >> 16) -- the Q16 pitch at +0x1c scales 11025 Hz. Nothing for a MIDI song. Sfx_SetPitch calls it.

entries.name: Sos_ApplyVoicePan
entries.description: (voice): for a digital sample (flags +4 bit 0 clear), Sos_SetPanLocation(Sos_GetDriverHandle(), +0x20, +0x18). Nothing for a MIDI song. Sfx_SetPan calls it.

entries.name: Sfx_ApplyLoopingNoOp
entries.description: Empty body. Sfx_SetLooping calls it when the voice is playing. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Sfx_ApplyLoopingNoOp.

entries.name: Sos_StubNoOp1
entries.description: Empty body (PUSH EBP; MOV EBP,ESP; POP EBP; RET), number 1 of the ten that follow Sfx_ApplyLoopingNoOp (00473a9c) in the SOS backend block. No caller found by es2_xref. VSHELL has the same run of ten empty bodies after its Sfx_ApplyLoopingNoOp; this one sits at the position of 0042dc73, identical after normalisation.
