entries.name: Point3S_ChebyshevMagnitude
entries.description: (p int16[3]): returns Math_ChebyshevMagnitude3D_Thunk(x, y, z) of the sign-extended components, the largest absolute component (the Chebyshev length). Caller found by es2_xref: Point3S_ChebyshevDistanceBetween (0047d514).

entries.name: Vec2_ExactMagnitude
entries.description: (p): Math_ISqrt of x*x + y*y, summed in 32 bits; the two-component form of Point3I_ExactMagnitude. Vec2_ExactDistanceBetween calls it.

entries.name: Vec2_ChebyshevMagnitude
entries.description: (p int32[2]): returns Math_ChebyshevMagnitude2D_Thunk(x, y). Caller found by es2_xref: Vec2_ChebyshevDistanceBetween (0047d5bc), on the difference of two points (Vec2_Subtract of a local copy).

entries.name: Point3I_ChebyshevMagnitude
entries.description: (p int32[3]): returns Math_ChebyshevMagnitude3D_Thunk(x, y, z). Caller found by es2_xref: Point3I_ChebyshevDistanceBetween (0047d660), on the difference of two points (Vec3_Subtract of a local copy).

entries.name: Math_ChebyshevMagnitude2D_Thunk
entries.description: (a, b): forwards to Math_ChebyshevMagnitude2D and returns its result in EAX. Callers found by es2_xref: Point2C_ChebyshevMagnitude (0047d6f5) and Point2S_ChebyshevMagnitude (0047d807) (an int8 and an int16 pair, sign-extended) and Vec2_ChebyshevMagnitude.

entries.name: Math_ChebyshevMagnitude3D_Thunk
entries.description: (a, b, c): forwards to Math_ChebyshevMagnitude3D and returns its result in EAX. Callers found by es2_xref: Point3C_ChebyshevMagnitude (0047d78c) (an int8 triple, sign-extended), Point3S_ChebyshevMagnitude and Point3I_ChebyshevMagnitude.

entries.name: Math_AsinBam
entries.description: Arcsine of a Q14 sine as a binary angle. Takes the magnitude (restoring the sign at the end), rounds it to a multiple of 4, and below 0xe00 * 4 (about 0.875) reads the coarse table at 004a1e54 at a further 8x step; above it reads the fine table at 004a05d4 (entry 0x1000, for 1.0, is 0x4000, a quarter turn).

entries.name: Vec3I_Cross
entries.description: (a, b, out): out = a x b on int32 triples (x = a.y*b.z - a.z*b.y, y = a.z*b.x - a.x*b.z, z = a.x*b.y - a.y*b.x), 32-bit products; returns out. Callers found by es2_xref: ObjList_SortCompareSegment, twice, for its plane normal.

entries.name: Math_Dot2S
entries.description: (a, b): a.x*b.x + a.y*b.y on int16 pairs, as an int. Mech_ApplyTerrainSlopeToSpeed calls it.

entries.name: DotProductVec3Short
entries.description: Literal 3-component dot product on two three-short vector pointers: a.x*b.x+a.y*b.y+a.z*b.z, no scaling/clamping. Called (via the Light_ComputeShadeForFace accessor wrapper DotProductVec3Short_Thunk) with the poly's Normal-index point and a directional light's own direction vector -- confirms the type-1 (directional) lighting term in Light_ComputeShadeForFace is a plain dot product, i.e. the poly's 'Normal' auxiliary point genuinely holds a normal-like vector (not a position), consistent with TSPoly_FrontBackVisibilityTest's use of them: the normal and centre are auxiliary vertex-index fields used for facing math, not literal mesh geometry.

entries.name: DotProductVec3Int
entries.description: Same as DotProductVec3Short but on int (not short) components -- used by Light_ComputeShadeForFace's type-2 (point light) branch after converting the light-to-face displacement into ints.

entries.name: Vec3I_DotSign
entries.description: (a, b): the sign of the dot product of two int32 triples, summed in 64 bits: 1 when it is zero or more, -1 when negative. Callers found by es2_xref: ObjList_SortCompareSegment, twice, for plane sides.

entries.name: Math_DivMod64
entries.description: (out{quotient, remainder}, int64 *n, d): stores n / d and n % d as two int32s and returns out.

entries.name: Math_FastMagnitude2D
entries.description: Sqrt-free 2D magnitude approximation: max(|dx|,|dy|) + min(|dx|,|dy|)/2 -- the octagonal estimate, exact on axis and up to ~11.8% high on a diagonal. The 2D counterpart of Math_FastMagnitude3D. This is the distance both HUD distance readouts display, so the original's own on-screen ranges carry that error.

entries.name: Math_FastMagnitude3D
entries.description: Sqrt-free 3D magnitude approximation: L + M*0.34375 + S*0.25 (sorted |dx|,|dy|,|dz|). Verified via raw disassembly (three CMP/XCHG sort pairs, SAR+ADD coefficient chains). Direction-dependent error: about 8% low on the body diagonal, up to about 8.7% high elsewhere. Reused for collision bounding-sphere radius, sound placement, LOD size and the rocket's proximity beep (round to camera, not a fuze).

entries.name: Math_ChebyshevMagnitude2D
entries.description: (a, b): returns max(|a|, |b|), each absolute value by CDQ/XOR/SUB; ENTER-framed like Math_FastMagnitude2D beside it. Caller found by es2_xref: Math_ChebyshevMagnitude2D_Thunk.

entries.name: Math_ChebyshevMagnitude3D
entries.description: (a, b, c): returns max(|a|, |b|, |c|), each absolute value by CDQ/XOR/SUB. Caller found by es2_xref: Math_ChebyshevMagnitude3D_Thunk.

entries.name: Math_TransposeRotation2D
entries.description: Swaps the two off-diagonal shorts of a Q14 2D rotation matrix, which for a rotation is its inverse. Ai_KeepFormation uses it to take the delta from a formation post into the group leader's own frame.

entries.name: Transform_TransposeRotation
entries.description: Transposes a transform's rotation in place (swaps +2/+4, +8/+0xc, +0xa/+0xe), which inverts a pure rotation; the rank byte is left alone.

entries.name: Math_MapRange
entries.description: Five-argument linear remap of a value from one range onto another, with a rounding bias of one less than the input span, signed to match the output's direction. Callers found by es2_xref: the flyer branch of Mech_GetDisplaySpeedKph (airspeed onto the HUD's km/h) and Ai_ChooseWeapon (fear onto a score floor).

entries.name: Math_Mul32To64
entries.description: (out int64, a, b): stores the 64-bit product a * b and returns out.

entries.name: Math_ISqrt
entries.description: (n) -> floor(sqrt(n)) for unsigned n, bit by bit: BSR for the top bit, then trial additions of halving powers of two against the running square. 0 for 0.

entries.name: Math_CosBam
entries.description: Cosine of a 16-bit binary angle in Q14: rounds the angle to a 16-BAM step ((a >> 4) + bit 3), takes its magnitude, and reads the quarter-turn table at 004a25dc (indices 0-0x400, 16384 at 0, 11585 at 0x200, 0 at 0x400) directly below a quarter turn and negated as table[0x800 - i] above it.

entries.name: Math_Q16Divide
entries.description: Q16 fixed-point divide: ((int64)a << 16) / b.

entries.name: Math_Q16Multiply2
entries.description: Q16 fixed-point multiply, (int64)a*b >> 16: a second copy of Math_Q16Multiply with an identical body.

entries.name: Math_Q16Multiply
entries.description: Q16 fixed-point multiply: (int64)a*b >> 16. Used by MechType_InitOne to rescale a mech type's speed fields by a Q16 ratio built with Math_Q16Divide.

entries.name: Math_Q8Multiply
entries.description: Q8 fixed-point multiply: (int64)a*b >> 8. Verified via raw disassembly (SHRD EAX,EDX,0x8) matching the decompiler's >>8 exactly.

entries.name: Math_Q10Multiply
entries.description: Q10 fixed-point multiply: (int64)a*b >> 10. Used in the shield-balance code; also builds the HUD's speed-display scale factor in MechType_InitOne.

entries.name: Math_Q14Multiply
entries.description: (int a, int16 b): Q14 fixed-point multiply, (int64)a*b >> 14. The scale of the Q14 sine/cosine table at 004a25dc.

entries.name: PlaneS_FromPointNormalS
entries.description: (plane, point int16[3], normal int16[3]): sign-extends normal into an int32[3] local (maybe_Point3I_Ctor) and calls PlaneS_FromPointNormal(plane, point, local). No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: PlaneS_FromPointNormal
entries.description: (plane, point int16[3], normal int32[3]): Plane_FromPointNormal's body for a 10-byte plane of three int16 normal components and an int32 d at +6. Scales normal to length 0x800 component by component through Math_Mul32To64_Thunk and Math_DivMod64_Thunk by its magnitude (Point3I_ExactMagnitude when every component lies strictly within +/-0x3a99, Point3I_Magnitude otherwise), stores the quotients as int16 at +0/+2/+4 and sets +6 = -(point . normal'). Callers found by es2_xref: PlaneS_FromPointNormalS and PlaneS_FromTriangle.

entries.name: PlaneS_FromTriangle
entries.description: (plane, a, b, c int16[3]): normal = (a - b) x (c - b) computed in int32, then PlaneS_FromPointNormal(plane, b, normal). No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: PlaneS_SegmentIntersect
entries.description: (plane {int16 nx, ny, nz; int32 d at +6}, segment int16 {start[3], end[3]}, out int16[3]) -> bool: Math_PlaneSegmentIntersect's body over int16 data. Denominator = n . (end - start), numerator = -(n . start + d); returns 0 when the denominator is 0 or the numerator lies outside [0, denominator] taken with the denominator's sign; otherwise writes out = start + (end - start) * numerator / denominator per component through Math_Mul32To64_Thunk and Math_DivMod64_Thunk and returns 1. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Plane_FromPointNormal
entries.description: (plane, point, normal): scales normal to length 0x800 component by component through Math_Mul32To64 and Math_DivMod64 by its magnitude -- Point3I_ExactMagnitude when every component lies strictly within +/-15001 (0x3a99), Point3I_Magnitude otherwise -- and sets plane.d = -(point . normal').

entries.name: Plane_FromTriangle
entries.description: (plane, a, b, c int32[3]): normal = (a - b) x (c - b), then Plane_FromPointNormal(plane, b, normal). The int32 twin of PlaneS_FromTriangle. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Math_PlaneSegmentIntersect
entries.description: (plane{nx,ny,nz,d}, segment{start[3],end[3]}, out[3]) -> bool in AL. Denominator = dot(n, end-start), numerator = -(dot(n, start) + d), both with 32-bit IMUL. Returns 0 with out unwritten for a zero denominator (segment parallel to the plane) or a parameter outside [0, 1], decided by comparing the pair with the sign of the denominator rather than dividing first; otherwise out = start + run * numerator / denominator per component, through Math_Mul32To64_Thunk (0047e995) and Math_DivMod64_Thunk (0047e9b2), and returns 1.

entries.name: Poly_SplitByPlane
entries.description: (plane, poly, front, back) -> bool, each polygon {count, int32 {x, y, z} points*} with the output point buffers supplied by the caller. Walks the edges from the last vertex, classifying each with Plane_ClassifyPoint: a front vertex (1) goes to front, a back vertex (-1) to back, one on the plane (0) to both, and an edge that crosses from one side to the other adds its Math_PlaneSegmentIntersect point to both before the vertex. A side left with fewer than 3 points is emptied. When each side either ends that way or received no vertex strictly on its own side (a polygon lying in the plane), front becomes a copy of the whole input. Returns 1 only when both sides are non-empty, and empties both for an input of fewer than 3 points. Its two callers, 00494ba8 and 00494d4c, each call it at six sites, keeping front each time and swapping the in and out lists with Dword_Swap.

entries.name: Point3I_ExactMagnitude
entries.description: (p): Math_ISqrt of x*x + y*y + z*z, summed in 32 bits.

entries.name: Math_ISqrt_Thunk
entries.description: One-line forwarder to Math_ISqrt.

entries.name: Math_Mul32To64_Thunk
entries.description: Forwarder to Math_Mul32To64 that returns its out pointer.

entries.name: Math_DivMod64_Thunk
entries.description: Forwarder to Math_DivMod64 that returns its out pointer.

entries.name: Point3IPair_Ctor
entries.description: (p): runs maybe_Point3I_Ctor on p and p+0xc. Poly_SplitByPlane calls it on a local. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Point3IPair_Ctor (004514ab).

entries.name: Plane_ClassifyPoint
entries.description: (plane{nx,ny,nz,d}, point[3]) -> int: 1 when dot(n, point) > -d, 0 when equal, -1 when less, the dot product through DotProductVec3Int_Thunk. Poly_SplitByPlane sorts vertices with it.

entries.name: Math_BuildRotation2D
entries.description: Builds a 2x2 Q14 rotation matrix for a binary angle into a short[4] -- {cos, sin, -sin, cos}, both looked up in the quarter-turn table at 004a25dc.

entries.name: BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14
entries.description: Builds a 3x3 rotation matrix (9 Q14 fixed-point shorts + 1 mode byte, 10 shorts total output) from three short Euler angles (param_1), using a sin/cos lookup table at DAT_004a25dc (1024-entry quarter-wave table, angle unit = 0x10000 per full circle, i.e. raw/65536*360 = degrees). Has a fast-path when the X and Y angle components are both zero (2-axis-only case, cos/sin of Z alone); otherwise builds the general 3-axis matrix via the standard trig-table-driven approach (the same trig-table technique as the simulation's other rotation math). Called by Light_CreateMissionSun with angles (-6000, 0, 21000) -- confirms the sun's direction is computed, not stored as a literal vector.

entries.name: Rotation_Concat
entries.description: (a, b, out): composes two 20-byte rotations (nine Q14 int16 entries, rank byte at +0x12) into out, with +0x2000 rounding and the rank fast paths of Transform_Concat but no translation. A rank below 1 on either side copies the other; two rank-1 (Z-only) operands give a rank-1 result with entries 4-7 zeroed and entry 8 = 0x4000; any other mix gives rank 2. Debris_Throw composes a piece's yaw onto the spawn attitude with it; FlightModel_Step also calls it.

entries.name: Transform_ConcatRotation
entries.description: (a, b, out): copies b's three int32 translations (+0x14/+0x18/+0x1c) into out, then composes a's and b's rotations (nine Q14 int16 entries, rank byte at +0x12) into out with Rotation_Concat's body; a diff against Rotation_Concat shows those three stores as the whole difference. A rank below 1 on a copies b's rotation, on b copies a's; two rank-1 operands give rank 1 (entries 4-7 zeroed, entry 8 0x4000); any other mix rank 2, each entry rounded with +0x2000 >> 14. Returns out. WeaponMount_PrepareShot passes the convergence rotation it builds with BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14 as a and the firing bone's transform as b, so the convergence goes on under the bone and the bone's translation is kept.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0047f3e8; es2_naming diff against 0047ef4c

entries.name: Transform_RotationToEuler
entries.description: (rotation short[9] Q14, out ushort[3]): out[0] = Math_AsinBam(m[5]). At a quarter turn either way (gimbal lock) out[1] = 0 and out[2] = Math_Atan2Bam(m[0], m[1]); otherwise out[1] = Math_Atan2Bam(m[8], -m[4]) and out[2] = Math_Atan2Bam(m[3], -m[2]). Returns out.

entries.name: Transform_Concat
entries.description: Composes two 32-byte transforms (9 Q14 int16 matrix entries, a rank byte at +0x12, three int32 translations at +0x14/+0x18/+0x1c) into a third. Branches on both operands' rank bytes -- translation only, Z-rotation only, or full 3x3 -- as an optimisation, not a behavioural difference. Every hit test builds its object-to-muzzle frame with this.

entries.name: Transform_RotateVector2D
entries.description: (vec2, transform, out): rotates an int16 2D vector by the transform's XY block alone (terms +0..+6), Q14 with +0x2000 rounding, into int16 out.

entries.name: Math_Rotate2DPoint
entries.description: Rotates an {int x, int y} point by a Math_BuildRotation2D matrix, rounding at Q14.

entries.name: Transform2D_ApplyToPoint
entries.description: (point int[2], xf, out int[2]): out = the point through the 2x2 Q14 matrix at xf (Math_BuildRotation2D's short[4] layout, rounded by +0x2000 >> 14) plus the int translation at xf+8/+0xc.

entries.name: RotateVectorByMatrixQ14
entries.description: Matrix-vector multiply: rotates param_1 (three shorts) by the 3x3 Q14 matrix param_2 (as built by BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14), writing the result to param_3. Has fast-paths for the matrix's degenerate mode byte (param_2[9]) similar to the matrix builder's own fast path. Called by Light_CreateMissionSun as rotate((0,0x1000,0), sunRotationMatrix) -- i.e. the sun's direction is 'straight up' rotated by the fixed Euler angles, not an arbitrary hand-authored vector.

entries.name: Transform_ApplyToShortPoint
entries.description: Transforms an int16 point by a 32-byte transform into an int32 result, Q14 with round-to-nearest (+0x2000 before the >>14). Same math as Transform_ApplyToPoint, narrower input; used for collision sphere centres.

entries.name: Transform_RotatePoint
entries.description: (point, transform, out): Transform_ApplyToPoint without the translation -- the rotation alone on an int32 point, Q14 with +0x2000 rounding and 64-bit intermediates, with the rank-byte fast paths. The rigid-inverse idiom rotates the negated translation through a transposed copy with it.

entries.name: Transform_ApplyToPoint
entries.description: (point, transform, out): transforms an int32 point by a 32-byte transform, rotation then translation, Q14 with +0x2000 rounding and 64-bit intermediates. Rank byte (+0x12) below 1: translation only; 1: rotates x and y only and passes z through; otherwise the full 3x3. The int-width counterpart of Transform_ApplyToShortPoint.

entries.name: GL_ClaimGlobal
entries.description: (this, index, instance): clears this+0 and stores instance at GL global index (006c5f38 + index*4, the table GL_GetGlobal reads) when that slot is still empty, so the first object constructed for an index becomes GL_GetGlobal(index)'s and is the one its own init runs for. MouseDriver_Ctor passes 2, KeyboardDriver_Ctor 1, DVTimer_Ctor 0, GLDisplay_Ctor 7 (the current display).

entries.name: GL_SetGlobal
entries.description: (index, value): stores value at 006c5f38 + index*4 and returns 0, unless value is non-null and the slot already holds one, when it stores nothing and returns 1.

entries.name: MouseDriver_Ctor
entries.description: (this): GL_ClaimGlobal(this, 2, this), constructs the fields at +4, +0xe, +0x16, +0x24 and +0x2c, and when 004809d8 returns this runs Mouse_Init and, if that succeeds, registers 004806f8 with Assert_AddHook. MouseInputDevice_Ctor runs it.

entries.name: MouseDriver_Dtor
entries.description: (this, flags): when GL_GetGlobal2 returns non-zero, Mouse_Shutdown(this) and GL_ClearGlobal(this, 2); Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. MouseInputDevice_Dtor runs it. The DVTimer_Dtor shape.

entries.name: Mouse_Init
entries.description: Registers Mouse_WndProcHook into the WndProc filter chain and, when bit 0 of the driver's first dword is set, runs the empty Mouse_InitNoOp, saves the bounds rect to +0x24 (MouseDriver_GetBounds) and sets it to {0, 0, 0x140, 400} with MouseDriver_SetBounds. Returns that bit.

entries.name: Mouse_Shutdown
entries.description: (driver): Mouse_Init's inverse. When bit 0 of the driver's first dword is set: WndProcHook_Unregister(Mouse_WndProcHook), clears that dword and restores the bounds Mouse_Init saved at +0x24 with MouseDriver_SetBounds; returns 1. Returns 0 otherwise. MouseDriver_Dtor runs it.

entries.name: MouseDriver_GetBounds
entries.description: (driver, out): copies the pointer's bounds rect {x0, y0, x1, y1} at driver+0xe..+0x1a into out.

entries.name: MouseDriver_SetBounds
entries.description: (driver, record): sets the bounds rect at driver+0xe..+0x1a from the record's first four ints and the shorts at driver+0x1e/+0x20/+0x22 from its +0x10/+0x12/+0x14.

entries.name: MouseDriver_GetBoundsRect
entries.description: (driver, out): copies the bounds rect at driver+0xe..+0x1a into out: the same code as MouseDriver_GetBounds, placed between MouseDriver_SetBounds and MouseDriver_SetBoundsRect. es2_xref finds no reference to it. VSHELL has the same copy in the same place (004054b2).

entries.name: MouseDriver_SetBoundsRect
entries.description: (driver, rect): copies the four ints of rect into the pointer's bounds at driver+0xe..+0x1a. es2_xref finds no reference to it. Byte-identical to VSHELL's MouseDriver_SetBoundsRect (004054dc).

entries.name: MouseDriver_AssertHookNoOp
entries.description: Empty body (PUSH EBP; MOV EBP,ESP; POP EBP; RET). MouseDriver_Ctor passes it to Assert_AddHook (pointer at 0048052f) when Mouse_Init returns non-zero; Assert_RunHooks calls each registered hook with its second argument. The DBSIM counterpart of VSHELL's 0040550a, which DVMouse_Ctor registers.

entries.name: Mouse_InitNoOp
entries.description: An empty function (PUSH EBP; MOV EBP,ESP; POP EBP; RET). Mouse_Init calls it when bit 0 of the driver's first dword is set.

entries.name: MouseDriver_ReturnZero
entries.description: Returns 0 (XOR EAX,EAX). Caller found by es2_xref: maybe_Input_SetMouseActive (00459cd8), which calls it when its flag argument is 0, differs from 0049e9ce and Input_GetMouseDevice_Thunk returns non-zero. One of four stubs between Mouse_InitNoOp and MouseDriver_GetState, in the order of VSHELL's 00405514, 0040551b, 00405520 and 00405527 beside DVMouse_InitNoOp.

entries.name: MouseDriver_NoOp
entries.description: Empty body. Caller found by es2_xref: maybe_Input_SetMouseActive (00459cd8), which calls it when its flag argument is non-zero, differs from 0049e9ce and Input_GetMouseDevice_Thunk returns non-zero. The counterpart by position of VSHELL's 0040551b.

entries.name: MouseDriver_ReturnZero2
entries.description: Returns 0 (XOR EAX,EAX); the body of MouseDriver_ReturnZero. No caller found by es2_xref. The counterpart by position of VSHELL's 00405520.

entries.name: MouseDriver_ReturnZero3
entries.description: Returns 0 (XOR EAX,EAX); the body of MouseDriver_ReturnZero. No caller found by es2_xref. The counterpart by position of VSHELL's 00405527.

entries.name: MouseDriver_GetState
entries.description: Returns 006c5fd4, the mouse driver's {int x, int y, int16 buttons} record.

entries.name: Stub_ReturnZeroCopy
entries.description: Returns 0 -- a second copy of Stub_ReturnZero. Gau_RovingGunsightWidget calls it and ignores the result.

entries.name: MouseListener_Register
entries.description: Appends {enabled=1, eventMask, callback} to the first free slot (of 10) in the mouse-listener table at DAT_006c5f5c that Mouse_DispatchEvent fans events out to. Returns the slot index or -1 if full. Same {enabled,mask,fn}-triple-array idiom as WndProcHook_Register's table and the keyboard-binding table read by Key_WndProcHook -- DBSIM reuses this shape for at least three unrelated subscriber lists.

entries.name: MouseListener_Unregister
entries.description: Clears slot param_2's enabled flag in the mouse-listener table at DAT_006c5f5c.

entries.name: Mouse_RecomputeScale
entries.description: Recomputes DAT_004a2de4/DAT_004a2de8, the 16.15 fixed-point (gameSize<<0xf)/clientSize factors Mouse_DispatchEvent uses to rescale window-client mouse coordinates into game space. Reads the window's current client rect, so it must be re-run on resize.

entries.name: Mouse_WarpCursorToPoint
entries.description: Rescales a game-space point to client coordinates (inverse of Mouse_RecomputeScale's factor), ClientToScreens it and calls SetCursorPos. Three callers, all gated on a live mouse device: Gau_RovingGunsightWidget centres the pointer on the gunsight as the cockpit is built, AlertPanel_SetFocus puts it on the focused widget's centre, AlertPanel_Leave restores the position the panel saved at its own +0x302.

entries.name: Mouse_DispatchEvent
entries.description: (kind, lParam, buttons): calls Mouse_RecomputeScale while the factor at 004a2de4 is 0, scales lParam's client x and y by the Q16 factors 004a2de4/004a2de8 into Mouse_State (006c5fd4/006c5fd8), rebuilds the button word 006c5fdc from bits 0 and 1 of buttons alone, and calls every enabled entry of the ten-slot listener table 006c5f5c whose mask has bit kind set, with &Mouse_State.

entries.name: Mouse_WndProcHook
entries.description: (hwnd, msg, wParam, lParam): a MainWndProc filter. WM_SIZE (5) calls Mouse_RecomputeScale. The five mouse messages go to Mouse_DispatchEvent(kind, lParam, buttons), kind 0 move, 1 left down, 2 left up, 3 right down, 4 right up. buttons carries wParam's MK_LBUTTON as 1 and its MK_RBUTTON doubled, as 4 -- except WM_RBUTTONDOWN, which passes 2 for the right button, and the two left messages, which set or leave bit 0 by the message itself. Returns 1 for move and the left pair, 0 for the right pair and anything else.

entries.name: MouseState_StaticInit
entries.description: Borland static initialiser (_INIT_ entry 004a7bd0, priority 0x20; frameless): Rtl_ReturnArg(Mouse_State (006c5fd4)), the empty constructor of Mouse_State.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 004809cc; init table entry 004a7bd0

entries.name: GL_GetGlobal2
entries.description: Returns GL_GetGlobal(2) in EAX (the decompile drops the return). MouseDriver_Ctor and MouseDriver_Dtor compare their object with it.

entries.name: DVTimer_Ctor
entries.description: (this, divisor): GL_ClaimGlobal(this, 0, this); when this is GL_GetGlobal0's instance, DVTimer_Init (00480a6c)(this, divisor) and, if that returns non-zero, Assert_AddHook(DVTimer_AssertHookNoOp (00480ab7)); counts one live destructor (*Rtl_DtorCountPtr += 1) and returns this. RTTI 'DVTimer' (class record 004621e6). es2_xref finds calls from Sim_InitMissionSession and Kind0InputDevice_Ctor (0045bfcc). ES1's DVTimer_Ctor (ES1DBSIM 0006c6f8) builds the same object and its init programs the PC timer, where this one's stores the divisor and returns the bit. The MouseDriver_Ctor shape.

entries.name: DVTimer_Dtor
entries.description: (this, flags): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr; for a non-null this, when GL_GetGlobal0 returns non-zero, the empty DVTimer_DtorNoOp (00480abc)(this) and GL_ClearGlobal(this, 0); Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. RTTI 'DVTimer''s destructor (class record 004621e6 +0x28). es2_xref finds one call, from Sim_ReleaseSessionObjects. ES1's DVTimer_Dtor (ES1DBSIM 0006c758) removes its interrupt handler where this calls the empty function.

entries.name: DVTimer_Init
entries.description: (this, divisor): stores the int16 at this+4 and returns this+0 & 1. GL_ClaimGlobal has just cleared this+0, so from DVTimer_Ctor it returns 0 and the assert hook is never added. ES1's DVTimer_Init (ES1DBSIM 0006c790) installs the PC timer's interrupt handler at that divisor first.

entries.name: DVTimer_SetRate
entries.description: (this, divisor): stores the int16 at this+4 and returns 1. ES1's DVTimer_SetRate (ES1DBSIM 0006c7bc) programs the PC timer with the divisor before the store. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: GL_ClearGlobal
entries.description: (unused, index): stores 0 at 006c5f38 + index*4.

entries.name: GL_GetGlobal0
entries.description: GL_GetGlobal(0), the DVTimer's slot of 006c5f38; returns it in EAX (the decompile drops it).

entries.name: DVTimer_AssertHookNoOp
entries.description: Empty body. DVTimer_Ctor passes it to Assert_AddHook (pointer at 00480a13) when DVTimer_Init returns non-zero.

entries.name: DVTimer_DtorNoOp
entries.description: Empty body. es2_xref finds one call, from DVTimer_Dtor (00480a2c), before its GL_ClearGlobal.

entries.name: GLDisplay_New
entries.description: (kindName, bitmapHeader): GL_RegisterClassItems, then Mem_New's a 0x48-byte display and runs GLDisplay_CtorAndOpen(display, kindName, bitmapHeader) on it; returns the display. es2_xref finds no reference to it.

entries.name: GLViewport_Ctor
entries.description: GLViewport constructor (vtable 004a2e28, RTTI name 'GLViewport', 0x239 bytes, over GLBase 004a3380): constructs the rect at +0x210 (RectI_Ctor) and +0x220, then copies the viewport held at GL_GetGlobal7()+0x40 (0x81 dwords from +4, then +0x208..+0x22c) and clears +0x230, +0x231 and +0x235. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's GLViewport_Ctor.

entries.name: Raster_InstallRenderContext
entries.description: Installs a render context: DAT_006c5ff4 = ctx, and PTR_DAT_004a362c = ctx+4, its clip block. The block's mode sits at ctx+0x208 -- 0 none, 1 the single rect at ctx+0x210, 2 the region list the block holds -- and CockpitView_ApplyViewState is what puts a view's context into mode 2 with the herc's .HD/.ED canopy regions. THE ctx+4 OFFSET IS LOAD-BEARING for reading brush code: the fill brush Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch reads at clipBlock+0x228 is the field callers write as ctx+0x22c, and the line brush at clipBlock+0x224 is ctx+0x228.

entries.name: GLDisplay_CloseCurrentAtExit
entries.description: Frameless atexit handler that GLDisplay_Ctor and GLDisplay_CtorAndOpen pass to _atexit (pointers at 00480e6b and 00480eb7): GLDisplay_Close on GLDisplay_GetCurrent's display when there is one and GLDisplay_GetFlags has bit 0 set. Its disassembly matches VSHELL's GLDisplay_CloseCurrentAtExit (004529fc) instruction for instruction.

entries.name: GLDisplay_Ctor
entries.description: (display, kindName): GL_ClaimGlobal(display, 7, display), so the first display built becomes GL_GetGlobal7's current one; registers an assert hook and an atexit handler, clears the flags dword +0 and stores GLDisplay_DriverIdFromName(kindName) at +0x30, the driver id Raster_SelectRenderTarget installs. Does not open the display. Screen_CreateBackBuffer and HddMap_BuildTerrainRaster build 0xa0-byte 'BMP_8' displays with it, then GLDisplay_Open.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00480e4c; name table at 004a2ea0

entries.name: GLDisplay_CtorAndOpen
entries.description: (display, kindName, bitmapHeader): GLDisplay_Ctor's body followed by GLDisplay_Open(display, bitmapHeader).

entries.name: GLDisplay_Dtor
entries.description: (display, flags): GLDisplay_Close(display), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. HddMap_BuildTerrainRaster destroys its BMP_8 display with it.

entries.name: GLDisplay_Open
entries.description: (display, bitmapHeader): when flags +0 is still zero: the first call ever (counter 004a2e44) runs GLDisplay_FirstOpenNoOp; then RasterDriver_OpenDisplay(driver id +0x30, bitmapHeader, display+4). On success allocates two 0x22c-byte clip blocks (RectI at +0x20c), initialises the first for the display's width and height (+8, +0xc) with ClipBlock_Init and copies it into the second, stores them at +0x40 and +0x44 (the block GLDisplay_SetClipBlock replaces), zeroes +0x34..+0x3c, sets flags bit 0 and returns 1. Returns 0 when already open or when RasterDriver_OpenDisplay fails.

entries.name: GLDisplay_Close
entries.description: (display): GLDisplay_Open's inverse. When open (flags bit 0): Mem_Delete of the clip block +0x40 (the one at +0x44 is not freed), clears the flags, RasterDriver_CloseDisplay(driver id +0x30, display+4), and decrements the open count 004a2e44, running GLDisplay_LastCloseNoOp when it reaches 0. Returns 0.

entries.name: Raster_SelectRenderTarget
entries.description: (display): makes display the current GL display (global 7) and installs it into the rasterizer. GLDisplay_ClearCurrent always returns 0, so the early return of 1 when a display is already current never runs: the current display is cleared and replaced. Then RasterDriver_InstallRoutines(display+0x30); copies display +0x4..+0x2c to 004a366a.. (004a366a is the row-pointer table Raster_SpanBitmap writes through); calls g_RasterRoutines' SetVisiblePage, SetSourcePage and SetDrawPage slots with +0x34, +0x38, +0x3c; Raster_InstallViewport(+0x40); stores +0x44 at 004a362c; returns 0. Called by HddMap_BuildTerrainRaster, Sim_EndFrame and Screen_CreateBackBuffer.

entries.name: GLDisplay_DriverIdFromName
entries.description: (display, name): looks name up in the three-entry table at 004a2ea0 ('VGA_8', 'VGA_4', 'BMP_8') and returns the matching raster driver id from 004a2eac: 1, 0 or 3; an unknown name returns the terminator 4. display is not read. The decompile drops the return; it is MOV EAX,[EBP+EDI*4-0x10].
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 004811e4; tables at 004a2ea0 and 004a2eac

entries.name: GLDisplay_GetAttribute
entries.description: (display, which): a jump table returning 0 +8 (width), 1 +0xc (height), 2 +0x28, 3 +0x2c, 4 +0x10, 6 +0x14, 7 +0x18, 9 +0x1c, 10 +0x20, 11 +0x24, for 5, 8 and 0x10 the globals 004a57bd, 004a4fb9 and 004a36a6, and 0 for anything else.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile and disassembly at 00481244 and its six callers

entries.name: GLDisplay_SetAttribute
entries.description: (display, which, value): the setter twin of GLDisplay_GetAttribute. 9, 10 and 11 store value at +0x1c, +0x20 and +0x24 and, when display is GL_GetGlobal7's current one, mirror it to 004a3682/004a3686/004a368a (the live copy Raster_SelectRenderTarget fills from display+4..); 2 calls the routine pointer 004a57e0 with (value, display+4) and, for the current display, re-copies +0x28/+0x2c to 004a368e/004a3692; 0x10 stores value in 004a36a6 (what GetAttribute 0x10 returns); 0x11 calls the routine pointer 004a5844 with value. Returns 1, or 0 for any other which. Screen_CreateBackBuffer and HddMap_BuildTerrainRaster call it with (display, 9, 0).

entries.name: GLDisplay_GetCurrent
entries.description: GL_GetGlobal(7): the current display. A second copy of GL_GetGlobal7 (0048d892), called by Raster_SelectRenderTarget.

entries.name: GLDisplay_GetFlags
entries.description: (display): returns the display's first dword, its flags; bit 0 is set while it is open. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's GLDisplay_GetFlags (00452fc2).

entries.name: GLDisplay_ClearCurrent
entries.description: GLDisplay_SetCurrent(0): clears global 7. Returns 0 always, because GL_SetGlobal always stores a null.

entries.description: GLBitmap destructor (vtable 004a3084, RTTI name 'GLBitmap', 0x1a bytes): (bmp, flags) reinstalls the vtable, Mem_DeleteArray of +0x16 when the int16 +0x14 is non-zero and of +0xe when +0xa is non-zero, GLBase_Dtor(bmp, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. HddMap_BuildTerrainRaster runs it on a local with flags 2. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's GLBitmap_Dtor.

entries.name: GLBitmap_LoadPalette
entries.description: (bitmap): GLDisplay_LoadPalette(GL_GetGlobal7's display, 0, the bitmap's colour count int16 +0x14, its colours +0x16). es2_xref finds no reference to it. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's GLBitmap_LoadPalette (004530b0).

entries.name: GLBitmap_RemapPalette
entries.description: (bitmap, palette, out): for each of the bitmap's colours (count int16 +0x14, 32-bit colours at +0x16) writes GLPalette_FindNearestColour(palette, colour) as one byte of out. es2_xref finds no reference to it. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's GLBitmap_RemapPalette (004530d4).

entries.name: GLBitmap_RemapPixels
entries.description: (bitmap, table): rewrites each of the int16 +4 * int16 +6 pixel bytes at the data pointer +0xe through the 256-byte table. The bitmap form of GLFont_RemapPixels, beside GLBitmap_RemapPalette. VSHELL's 00453114 is the same loop with the count chosen by the bitmap's type nibble (byte +9). No caller found by es2_xref.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0048156c; es2_naming diff against VSHELL 00453114

entries.name: Bitmap_Blit
entries.description: Bitmap_Blit(bitmap, {int x, int y}, flags) -- the engine-wide sprite/background blit. flags bit 1 (value 2) mirrors horizontally, bit 0 (value 1) flips vertically, 3 does both; confirmed at the reticle corner-bracket draw (0044401d..0044403a) which draws one corner sprite four times with flags 0/2/1/3, offsetting x by the bitmap's width field (+6) for flag 2 and y by its height field (+4) for flag 1. Used with flags=2 to produce the cockpit's opposite side view from the single authored side bitmap.

entries.name: Bitmap_BlitRect
entries.description: (bitmap, point, flags, rect): Bitmap_Blit's sub-rectangle twin. Hands the bitmap at +4 to GL_BlitRect with GL_GetGlobal7's display; a packed bitmap (+0x12 non-zero) is first unpacked by Bitmap_UnpackToScratch, whose buffer Bitmap_UnpackScratch and returned size stand in for the data pointer +0xe and size +0xa for the call and are swapped back after, the buffer going to Mem_Delete unless Bitmap_UseCallerScratch is set. Matches VSHELL's GLBitmap_DrawRect (004531e4) but for the callee names. No caller found by es2_xref.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00481628; es2_naming diff against VSHELL 004531e4

entries.name: Bitmap_BlitScaled
entries.description: (bitmap, point, flags, size{w, h}): Bitmap_Blit's scaled twin. Hands the bitmap at +4 to GL_BlitScaled with GL_GetGlobal7's display; a packed bitmap (+0x12 non-zero) is first unpacked by Bitmap_UnpackToScratch, whose buffer Bitmap_UnpackScratch and returned size stand in for the data pointer +0xe and size +0xa for the call and are put back after, the buffer going to Mem_Delete unless Bitmap_UseCallerScratch is set. es2_xref finds calls from CockpitView_SetView, VideoMode_BlitBitmap, VideoMode_BlitBitmapFlags and VideoMode_BlitBitmapSized (two).

entries.name: Bitmap_BlitRotatedUnpacked
entries.description: Rotated blit of a bitmap object. When the object's packing type (+0x12) is non-zero, Bitmap_UnpackToScratch unpacks it into Bitmap_UnpackScratch, the object's size (+0xa) and data pointer (+0xe) are swapped to the scratch copy for the blit and restored after, and the scratch is freed unless Bitmap_UseCallerScratch is set. Then Bitmap_BlitRotatedScaledThunk with the object's +4 rows,cols pair.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Bitmap_BlitRotatedUnpacked(void *bitmap, int *position, int flip, int *size, short angle)

entries.name: Bitmap_SetScratchOverride
entries.description: (unused, enable, buffer): stores enable at Bitmap_UseCallerScratch (006c5ff8) and buffer at Bitmap_UnpackScratch (006c5ffc). While the flag is set, Bitmap_UnpackToScratch returns 0 without unpacking and Bitmap_Blit, Bitmap_BlitRect, Bitmap_BlitScaled and Bitmap_BlitRotatedUnpacked blit a packed bitmap from the caller's buffer and leave it allocated. Matches VSHELL's 004533a8 (0048e188/0048e18c). No caller found by es2_xref.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile and disassembly at 004817ec; readers of 006c5ff8 in the decompile

entries.name: Bitmap_UnpackToScratch
entries.description: Unpacks a bitmap object's data (+0xe, length +0xa) into a fresh Bitmap_UnpackScratch buffer sized by the packed data's first dword: a MemRWStream over the data past that dword, a decoder over it chosen by packing type +0x12 (1 RLERStream, vtable 004a17c8; 3 LZHRStream, vtable 004a1820), and Stream_Read of that many bytes. Returns the unpacked size; for any other type it allocates the scratch and returns 0 without decoding, and when Bitmap_UseCallerScratch is set it returns 0 at once.

entries.name: HudFont_GlyphWidth
entries.description: One glyph's advance width: the fixed width at font+0xc when that is not -1, otherwise the per-glyph width byte at font+0x2a indexed by char - firstCharCode. Every retail font stores -1 and is therefore proportional.

entries.name: HudFont_MeasureString
entries.description: Sums HudFont_GlyphWidth over a NUL-terminated run. Callers that align a run subtract 1<<XCoordShift from the result to drop the trailing advance past the last glyph.

entries.name: HudFont_CellHeight
entries.description: Returns font+0xa, the glyph cell height (file offset 0x0e; 13 for .HFN, 10 for .DFN). This is the glyph art's height, not the ink height at font+0x16 that labels centre by.

entries.name: HudFont_CellHeight2
entries.description: Returns the int16 at font+0xa, the glyph cell height: a second copy of HudFont_CellHeight, which sits just before it. 004387d0 centres a label on it. Byte-identical to VSHELL's Font_CellHeight (00453fa8).

entries.name: HudFont_DrawGlyph
entries.description: Blits one glyph: height from font+0xa (file 0x0e cellHeight), width from HudFont_GlyphWidth, bit depth from font+0x12 (file 0x16, 8 in every retail file), pixels from the pool at font+0x22 indexed through the per-glyph offset array at font+0x26. Draws with its top row at y - font+0x16 (file 0x1a, the ink height), which is the other half of Label_SetRect's vertical rule.

entries.name: HudFont_DrawString
entries.description: Draws a NUL-terminated run with a .DFN/.HFN font at a caller-supplied top-left, advancing the pen by each glyph's own width. A display-wide alignment override at renderContext+0x231 (1 = right, 2 = centre against the field width at +0x235) shifts the whole run first; it is 0 in the cockpit.

entries.name: Raster_DrawLine
entries.description: (from, to): draws a line between two {x, y} points with the pen at the installed clip block's (PTR_DAT_004a362c) +0x224: mode 0 a colour, a top byte of 4 resolved through g_RasterColourRamps and any other non-zero top byte drawing nothing; mode 2 a remap through g_RasterRoutines_RemapSpans with the pen's +4; other modes nothing. Both points move by (+0x20c - +0x21c, +0x210 - +0x220) when +0x208 is set. Clip mode +0x204 0 draws the line whole and 1 clips it to the rect +0x20c with Line_ClipToRect, drawing nothing when it misses; a colour pen then draws through g_RasterRoutines_DrawLine, a remap through Line_ScanConvertToSpanRegion into 004a36a9 and its span routine. Any other clip mode walks the block's list from last to first: a rect region clips a copy of the line (Line_ClipToRect) and scan-converts it; at the first span region the line, clipped to +0x20c (returning when it misses) and scan-converted into 004a36ad, is intersected with each span region (SpanRegion_Intersect); each piece goes to the pen's span routine, g_RasterRoutines for a colour; other region types are passed over.

entries.name: Line_ClipToRect
entries.description: (a, b, rect{x0, y0, x1, y1}): clips the segment a-b in place against the inclusive rect, against y0, x0, y1 and x1 in that order, each time moving the outside endpoint to the crossing computed from it in 64 bits (truncating). To move b it first exchanges the two points (XCHG) and leaves them exchanged, so the result can hold the endpoints in the other order. Returns 0, leaving the points as they were, when both endpoints lie beyond the same bound; otherwise 1. Raster_DrawLine clips through it for clip mode 1 and for each rect of a clip list.

entries.name: Line_ScanConvertToSpanRegion
entries.description: (a, b, out): writes the int16 span region of a one-pixel line: top row min(y), count |dy| + 1, then an {x0, x1} pair per row -- {x, x} on each row of a vertical line, one row {xmin, xmax} for a horizontal one, and otherwise the run of x a Bresenham walk from the smaller-x end puts on each row. Raster_DrawLine fills the result with the pen's span routine.

entries.name: Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch
entries.description: (count, points): generic polygon draw, dispatching on the brush at *(int*)(clipBlock + 0x228), a {mode, colour} pair; the points are translated by (+0x20c - +0x21c, +0x210 - +0x220) first when clipBlock+0x208 is set. A ring of fewer than three points, and brush mode 4, draw in the brush colour through a temporary brush at +0x224: one point through Gfx_PlotPixel, two through Raster_DrawLine, and mode 4 as a line loop over the ring closing back to the first point -- the outline pass. For three or more: mode 0 fills through g_RasterRoutines slot 0 with the brush colour, a plain palette index when the colour's top byte is 0, and when it is 4 the entry (shade * length) >> 8 of the g_RasterColourRamps ramp its low word names, shade being its third byte; any other top byte draws nothing. Mode 1 is Raster_FillContourPolygon, modes 5 and 7 g_RasterRoutines_BitmapPolygon, mode 6 g_RasterRoutines_RemapSpans with a pointer to the brush's second field; any other mode draws nothing. The span fills scan-convert with Poly_ScanConvertToSpanRegion and clip per the clip mode at +0x204: 0 none, 1 Poly_ClipToRect against the rect at +0x20c, otherwise each region of the block's list (a rect region clipped by Poly_ClipToRect, a type-2 one intersected with SpanRegion_Intersect). Raster_DrawPolygonReversed calls it with the ring reversed.

entries.name: Raster_DrawPolygonReversed
entries.description: (count, points): Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch on the ring reversed. For three or more points it copies them last-to-first into a local ring, and when the brush at clipBlock+0x228 is mode 5 it also points the brush's +8 list (a bitmap fill's corner list) at a reversed local copy for the call and restores it after; it reverses no other brush list, so a mode-1 brush's per-vertex shade list at +0xc keeps its order and slot j of the reversed ring takes shade j. One or two points pass through unreversed, zero draws nothing. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Gfx_FillPolygonReversed (00455b02), identical but for the rel32 call.

entries.name: Raster_DrawPolygonEitherWinding
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Gfx_FillPolygonEitherWinding (00455b9b), byte-identical: hands a zero-or-negative shoelace sum to Raster_DrawPolygonReversed, anything else to Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch. PolyFill_Fill fills through it.
