entries.name: Raster_FillRect
entries.description: (rect): fills the inclusive rect {x0, y0, x1, y1} with the brush at the installed clip block's (PTR_DAT_004a362c) +0x228. Mode 0: g_RasterRoutines_FillRect with the colour, a top byte of 4 resolved through g_RasterColourRamps and any other non-zero top byte drawing nothing; mode 6: g_RasterRoutines_RemapRect with the brush's +4; mode 4: the rect's edges with Raster_DrawLine under a temporary pen {0, colour} at +0x224, (x1, y0)-(x0, y0), (x0, y1)-(x0, y0), (x0, y1)-(x1, y1) and (x1, y0)-(x1, y1), the pen put back after; other modes nothing. For modes 0 and 6 the rect moves by (+0x20c - +0x21c, +0x210 - +0x220) when +0x208 is set; clip mode +0x204 0 draws it whole, 1 its Rect_Intersect with the rect +0x20c, and any other walks the block's list (int16 count +0, entries from +4) from last to first: a rect region's Rect_Intersect goes to the mode's routine; at the first span region the rect, intersected with +0x20c (returning when empty), is made a span list with SpanList_FromRect (004a36ad), and each span region's SpanRegion_Intersect with it goes to g_RasterRoutines (slot 0) whatever the mode; other region types are passed over.

entries.name: Rect_Intersect
entries.description: (a, b, out): intersects two rects {x0, y0, x1, y1} (inclusive) into out and returns out, or 0 when they do not overlap. Raster_FillRect and Region_CopyRectBetweenPages clip with it.

entries.name: SpanList_FromRect
entries.description: (rect{x0, y0, x1, y1}, out): int16 y0 at out+0, the row count y1 - y0 + 1 at out+2, then one int16 pair {x0, x1} per row. Raster_FillRect calls it. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's SpanList_FromRect (00457634).

entries.name: Raster_FillSpanList
entries.description: (spans, origin): copies a span list {int16 top row, int16 row count, {x0, x1} per row} to PTR_DAT_004a36a9 translated by origin -- plus (clipBlock+0x20c - +0x21c, +0x210 - +0x220) when clipBlock+0x208 is set -- and fills it with the brush at clipBlock+0x228: mode 0 through g_RasterRoutines slot 0 with the brush colour (a type-4 colour resolved through g_RasterColourRamps), mode 6 through g_RasterRoutines_RemapSpans with the brush's data; other modes return. Clips per the clip mode at clipBlock+0x204: 0 none, 1 the rect at +0x20c (SpanList_ClipToRect), otherwise each region in the block's list, a type 0 region through SpanList_ClipToRect and a type 2 through SpanRegion_Intersect, filling each piece.

entries.name: SpanRegion_Intersect
entries.description: (a, b, out): intersects two span regions ({int16 top row, int16 row count, then an {x0, x1} int16 pair per row}) row by row into out; returns out, or 0 when no row overlaps. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's SpanRegion_Intersect. Raster_DrawLine, Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch and Raster_FillRect clip against span regions with it.

entries.name: SpanList_ClipToRect
entries.description: (rect, spans, out): clips a span list {int16 top row, int16 row count, {x0, x1} per row} to rect {x0, y0, x1, y1}: rows outside the rect's rows and leading rows that miss its columns are dropped, x ranges are clamped, and a row that misses after the first hit becomes the empty span {1, 0}; the count ends at the last hit. Writes to out and returns it, or 0 when no row survives. Raster_FillSpanList and Region_CopyRectBetweenPages clip with it.

entries.name: Raster_SetColourRamps
entries.description: (first, count, records, extra): copies count 8-byte records {int16 *entries, int16 length} from records into g_RasterColourRamps starting at index first, two LODSD/STOSD per record; loads extra into EBX and does not read it. Callers found by es2_xref: GLDisplay_SetColourRamps, Palette_SetRampsToRange (00430518) and Palette_SetRampsToRangeList (00430590), which first fill each record's entry list with runs of consecutive int16 values. Matches VSHELL's 00457a48.

entries.name: maybe_Cursor_SetImage
entries.description: Empty: returns at once. The cockpit cursor-slot functions call it with a .DCI cursor's bitmap (+4) and hotspot (+8) on the paged path, where they call maybe_Driver3_SetCursorImage on the scroll-window path; the name is inferred from those arguments.

entries.name: Cursor_SyncPosition
entries.description: Stores the pointer position in param_1: to DAT_004a3638/3c when DAT_004a365e is set, bracketed by g_RasterRoutines slots 31 and 30 (maybe_ hide/show cursor) when DAT_004a3634 is set; otherwise to DAT_004a3662/66. Driver 3 fills both slots with empty stubs. Driver3_SyncCursorPosition is driver 3's copy of the same routine.

entries.name: Cursor_GetPosition
entries.description: (out): copies the pointer position at 004a3638/004a363c -- the slot Cursor_SyncPosition writes when 004a365e is set -- into out. Gunsight_ClickSurface_Paint, HddCommandScreen_SynthesizeListClick and Input_BuildPlayerDevice read it.

entries.name: Raster_FillContourTriangle
entries.description: Fills a triangle of three {x,y} vertices by interpolating its three palette indices in contour bands: it cuts the triangle at every whole index between the highest and lowest corner and flat-fills each band (Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch, writing the band's upper index into the installed brush's colour) with that index, so a point takes the ceiling of its interpolated index. Equal corners fill flat; a degenerate triangle draws nothing.

entries.name: Raster_FillContourPolygon
entries.description: Brush mode 1 of Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch, (count, points): a polygon shaded per vertex. Maps each vertex's ushort shade from the brush's list at +0xc to a palette index through the ramp the brush colour's low word names (8-byte records at 004a4fbd: +0 entry array, +4 int16 length; entry (shade * length) >> 8), fans triangles from vertex 0 and fills each with Raster_FillContourTriangle, with the brush switched to mode 0 meanwhile. Restores the brush's colour and mode 1 after.

entries.name: Region_CopyRectBetweenPages
entries.description: (region, point): Region_CopyBetweenPages for a type-0 region: adds point, and the clip block's (PTR_DAT_004a362c) translation (+0x20c - +0x21c, +0x210 - +0x220) when +0x208 is set, to the rect at +4 and passes the rect and point as given to g_RasterRoutines_CopyRect: whole in clip mode +0x204 0; its Rect_Intersect with the rect +0x20c in mode 1, nothing when they miss; in any other mode, for each entry of the block's list (count +0, entries from +4) from last to first, a rect region's Rect_Intersect through g_RasterRoutines_CopyRect and a span region's SpanList_ClipToRect (into 004a36a9) through g_RasterRoutines_CopySpans, other region types passed over.

entries.name: Region_CopySpansBetweenPages
entries.description: (region, point): Region_CopyBetweenPages for a type-2 region: copies the span list +4 points to into the scratch list 004a36a9 points to, adding point, and the clip block's translation (+0x20c - +0x21c, +0x210 - +0x220) when +0x208 is set, to the top row and to each x0 and x1, and passes it with point to g_RasterRoutines_CopySpans: whole in clip mode +0x204 0; cut to the rect +0x20c by SpanList_ClipToRect (into 004a36ad) in mode 1; in any other mode, for each entry of the block's list from last to first, cut to a rect region (SpanList_ClipToRect) or intersected with a span region (SpanRegion_Intersect), other region types passed over.

entries.name: Region_CopyBetweenPages
entries.description: (region, point): copies the area a region covers from the raster source page to the draw page: Region_CopyRectBetweenPages for a type-0 region, Region_CopySpansBetweenPages for type 2, nothing for another type. A region is {int type; ...}: type 0 carries a rect {x0, y0, x1, y1} at +4, type 2 a pointer to a span list ({int16 top row, int16 row count, {x0, x1} per row}) at +4. es2_xref finds 15 calls, from CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand, CockpitView_StepViewTransition, Widget_DrawToCockpit, MessagePort_CopyBoxBetweenPages, LedBmBarGraphH_DrawBitmapSpan, LedBmBarGraphV_DrawBitmapSpan and PreferencesPanel_Run.

entries.name: Region_SaveRect
entries.description: (region, buffer): wraps buffer in a stack bitmap header the size of the region's rect (translated by the drawing context's offset when +0x208 is set) and grabs the screen into it with Bitmap_GrabClipDispatch(header, rect, 0).

entries.name: SpanRegion_PixelCount
entries.description: (spans): sums x1 - x0 over a span list's rows into EAX: the INC after each add increments the x1 it loaded, not the sum, so a row counts one pixel fewer than Region_SaveSpans (00487e5e) copies. Its bytes end at MOV EAX,EDX with no POP, LEAVE or RET, so execution runs on into Region_SaveSpans.

entries.name: Region_SaveSpans
entries.description: (region, buffer), hand-written: Region_Save for a type-2 region. Copies each row of its span list from the screen into buffer through the raster routine 004a5818 (buffer, row, x0, x1), advancing buffer by x1 - x0 + 1. When the drawing context's +0x208 is set it first translates the list into 004a36a9, adding CX + ctx+0x210 - ctx+0x220 to the top row and DX + ctx+0x20c - ctx+0x21c to each x, with ECX and EDX as the caller left them: Region_Save has the region pointer in both.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00487e5e and its call in Region_Save (00487f2d); Region_Save's callers load EDX with the region they push

entries.name: Region_Save
entries.description: (region, buffer): copies the screen pixels a region covers into buffer: Region_SaveRect for a type-0 rect, Region_SaveSpans for a type-2 span list, called with the region in ECX. The message ports, AlertPanel_Enter and CockpitView_SetShakeBand save screen areas with it, each pushing (region, buffer). A region is {int type; ...}: type 0 carries a rect {x0, y0, x1, y1} at +4, type 2 a pointer to a span list ({int16 top row, int16 row count, {x0, x1} per row}) at +4.

entries.name: Region_PixelCount
entries.description: Returns the number of pixels a region covers: Rect_PixelCount for type 0, 00487e3c for type 2 (span list), 0 otherwise. The message ports size their two save-under buffers with it. A region is {int type; ...}: type 0 carries a rect {x0, y0, x1, y1} at +4, type 2 a pointer to a span list ({int16 top row, int16 row count, {x0, x1} per row}) at +4.

entries.name: Region_RestoreRect
entries.description: (region, point, buffer): wraps buffer in a stack bitmap header the size of the region's rect (format 8, flags 0x10) and draws it at point with Bitmap_BlitClipDispatch.

entries.name: SpanRegion_Restore
entries.description: (region, point, buffer): for each row of the region's span list, offset by point (and the drawing context's translation when +0x208 is set), hands the row's slice of buffer to the span routine 004a5820 as (src, y, x0, x1), advancing through buffer by each span's width.

entries.name: Region_Restore
entries.description: (region, point, buffer): puts saved pixels back: 00487f6c for a type-0 rect, 00487fb0 for a type-2 span list. The counterpart of Region_Save. A region is {int type; ...}: type 0 carries a rect {x0, y0, x1, y1} at +4, type 2 a pointer to a span list ({int16 top row, int16 row count, {x0, x1} per row}) at +4.

entries.name: Raster_DrawEllipse
entries.description: (rect): rasterizes the ellipse inscribed in rect {x0, y0, x1, y1} -- centre ((x0 + x1) >> 1, (y0 + y1) >> 1), half-extents a = |x1 - x0| >> 1 and b = |y1 - y0| >> 1 -- with a midpoint algorithm into a span list at PTR_DAT_004a36ad and fills it with Raster_FillSpanList about the centre. The list has 2b rows starting b above the centre; each y from b down to 1 writes its {-x, x} span from both ends of the list at once, so the filled shape is 2a + 1 wide by 2b tall and sits half a row above the centre. The brush at clipBlock+0x228 decides the shape: mode 0 fills the ellipse; mode 4 draws a one-pixel ring as two span passes with the mode switched to 0 between them and restored after; any other mode draws nothing. A zero half-width or half-height draws a vertical or horizontal line through Raster_DrawLine instead, in the brush colour through a temporary pen at +0x224.

entries.name: Math_AbsInt
entries.description: Returns |x| of an int32 by the sign-mask idiom (x ^ (x >> 31)) - (x >> 31).

entries.name: Bitmap_BlitClipDispatch
entries.description: (bitmap, position, flags): applies the installed clip block to a blit. Offsets the destination by the context's translation when ctx+0x20c is 1; then hands a type-1 (transparent) bitmap (byte +5 low nibble) to Bitmap_BlitTransparent, which clips it itself; otherwise dispatches on the clip mode at ctx+0x208 -- mode 0 unclipped through the routine at 004a582c, and modes 1 and 2 (mode 2 only when the block holds at least one region, ctx+4 non-zero) through g_RasterRoutines slot 28 (004a5834) with the rect at ctx+0x210, which driver 3's Driver3_BlitClippedRegion uses in mode 1 and replaces with the block's regions in mode 2; nothing otherwise.

entries.name: Bitmap_BlitRectClipDispatch
entries.description: (bitmapData, position, flags, rect {x0, y0, x1, y1}): draws that rect of the bitmap at position. Offsets position by the clip block's (PTR_DAT_004a362c) +0x20c/+0x210 less +0x21c/+0x220 when block +0x208 is 1, takes origin = position - rect's top-left, and calls g_RasterRoutines slot 28 (g_RasterRoutines_BlitRegion (004a5834)) with (bitmapData, &origin, &(rect offset by origin), flags). Caller found by es2_xref: GL_BlitRect. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Bitmap_BlitRectClipDispatch (00458c90).
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 004887b8; es2_naming diff against VSHELL 00458c90

entries.name: Bitmap_GrabClipDispatch
entries.description: (bitmap, point, flags): the reverse of Bitmap_BlitClipDispatch: zeroes the bitmap's data (+0xa, size +6), clears the low nibble of +5, sets the format byte +4 to 8 when it does not match the display depth 004a367a (8 or 4), offsets the point by the context's translation when +0x208 is 1, and reads the screen into it through the routine pointer 004a5830 -- unclipped for clip mode (+0x204) 0, clipped to the rect +0x20c for mode 1, and once per rect entry of the clip list for mode 2.

entries.name: Bitmap_BlitScaledClipDispatch
entries.description: (bitmapData, point, flags, size{w, h}): offsets the point by the current context's translation when its +0x208 is 1, then calls the scaled blit routine pointer at 004a5838 as (bitmapData, w, h, &point, clip, flags) with clip 0 for clip mode (+0x204) 0 and the context's rect at +0x20c for modes 1 and 2 (mode 2 only when the region count at +0 is positive). Unlike Bitmap_BlitClipDispatch it has no transparent-bitmap branch.

entries.name: Bitmap_BlitRotatedScaled
entries.description: Draws a bitmap into a rotated, arbitrarily-sized destination quad through brush mode 5, installing the brush {5, 4, &sourceQuad, dimensions}; mode 5 skips palette index 0 (Raster_SpanBitmap). Its first argument points at the bitmap's rows,cols pair (the bitmap object's +4/+6); the source quad is (0,0),(cols-1,0),(cols-1,rows-1),(0,rows-1). flip bit 2 mirrors it in x, bit 1 in y. The destination quad is (0,0),(w,0),(w,h),(0,h) from the size pair, each corner rotated by the binary angle and then translated by the position -- so that position is the rotated quad's top-left, not its centre.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Bitmap_BlitRotatedScaled(short *dimensions, int *position, unsigned char flip, int *size, short angle)

entries.name: Math_BuildRotation2DInto
entries.description: (out, angle): Math_BuildRotation2D(angle, out) -- the same call with the arguments the other way round. Bitmap_BlitRotatedScaled calls it.

entries.name: Math_Rotate2DPoint_Thunk
entries.description: One-line forwarder to Math_Rotate2DPoint with the same arguments.

entries.name: Bitmap_BlitTransparent
entries.description: The transparent/RLE sprite blitter. Rejects against the context's clip rect (ctx+0x210..+0x21c), then sets a per-call flag from whether the clip mode is 2 and sends every pixel run it emits either to the plain span writer (g_RasterRoutines_SpanCopy/g_RasterRoutines_SpanFill) or to the region-clipped one (g_RasterRoutines_SpanCopyRegion/g_RasterRoutines_SpanFillRegion). That flag is why a sprite drawn through a mode-2 context is cut to the canopy cutout scanline by scanline rather than to a rectangle. (bitmap, position, flags): the bitmap's int16 height +0 and width +2, and its data +0xa: a 0x10-byte colour table, then the code stream (SpriteCode_*): a code with bit 7 set is a run of code & 0x3f pixels, packed 4-bit indices into the colour table when bit 6 is clear (Raster_SpanCopy), one colour from the following byte when it is set (Raster_SpanFill); a code with the top two bits clear ends the row; 0x40 ends the sprite; any other 0x4x code skips transparent pixels. flags bit 0 flips the sprite vertically, bit 1 horizontally.

entries.name: SpriteCode_Count
entries.description: (code): code & 0x3f, the pixel count of a transparent-sprite code. Bitmap_BlitTransparent decodes every code with it.

entries.name: SpriteCode_IsRun
entries.description: (code): code & 0x80. Bitmap_BlitTransparent draws a run of SpriteCode_Count pixels for a code with it set.

entries.name: SpriteCode_IsLiteralRun
entries.description: (code): whether bit 6 (0x40) of a run code is clear. Bitmap_BlitTransparent then reads the run's pixels as packed 4-bit indices, (count + 1) / 2 bytes; with bit 6 set the run is one colour from the single byte that follows.

entries.name: Raster_SpanFillRegion
entries.description: (y, x0, x1, colour): calls the region-clipped raster routine at 004a5828 with (colour, y, x0, x1). Bitmap_BlitTransparent emits a one-colour run through it in clip mode 2.

entries.name: Raster_SpanFill
entries.description: (y, x0, x1, colour): calls the raster routine at 004a5824 with (colour, y, x0, x1). Bitmap_BlitTransparent emits a one-colour run through it when the clip mode is not 2.

entries.name: Raster_SpanCopyRegion
entries.description: (y, x0, x1, pixels): calls the region-clipped raster routine at 004a5820 with (pixels, y, x0, x1). Bitmap_BlitTransparent emits a literal run through it in clip mode 2.

entries.name: Raster_SpanCopy
entries.description: (y, x0, x1, pixels): calls the raster routine at 004a581c with (pixels, y, x0, x1). Bitmap_BlitTransparent emits a literal run through it when the clip mode is not 2.

entries.name: Math_NegateIf
entries.description: (flag, value): returns -value when flag is nonzero, else value. Bitmap_BlitTransparent calls it.

entries.name: SpriteCode_IsRowEnd
entries.description: (code): whether the top two bits (0xc0) of a code are clear. Bitmap_BlitTransparent then steps to the next row and moves x back by SpriteCode_Count, extended by SpriteCode_IsRowEndExtension's byte.

entries.name: SpriteCode_IsRowEndExtension
entries.description: (byte): 1 when the byte after a row-end code is non-zero with its top two bits clear, else 0. Bitmap_BlitTransparent then consumes it and moves x back by byte * 0x40 + count instead of count. The decompile drops the return.

entries.name: SpriteCode_IsEnd
entries.description: (code): whether code is 0x40, the end of a transparent sprite. Any other code with bit 6 set and bit 7 clear skips SpriteCode_Count transparent pixels.

entries.name: RasterDriver_FindRoutineTable
entries.description: Register convention: driver id in EAX, result in EAX. Walks g_RasterDriverTable's {int id, void **table} pairs and returns the matching table pointer, or the terminator's id (-1) when none matches. A matching entry with a null table returns 0.

entries.name: RasterDriver_InstallRoutines
entries.description: Looks the driver id up with RasterDriver_FindRoutineTable and copies g_RasterRoutineCount (36) dwords from the result into g_RasterRoutines with REP MOVSD. Returns 1, or 0 when the id is unknown. It does not test for a null table, which drivers 0 and 1 carry, so every install that returns has copied driver 3's.

entries.name: GLDisplay_FirstOpenNoOp
entries.description: Empty body. GLDisplay_Open calls it on the first open ever (open count 004a2e44 still 0).

entries.name: GLDisplay_LastCloseNoOp
entries.description: Empty body (pushes and pops EDI, EBX, ESI). GLDisplay_Close calls it when the open count 004a2e44 returns to 0.

entries.name: RasterDriver_OpenDisplay
entries.description: (driverId, bitmapHeader, info): calls into the driver's own routine table (RasterDriver_FindRoutineTable, looked up afresh for each call): slot 8 (bitmapHeader) and then slot 9 () must each return 0, else it returns 0; then slot 10 (), slot 11 (bitmapHeader, info) and slot 7 (info+0x24, info), and returns 1. GLDisplay_Open passes display+4 as info. Ghidra's fastcall prototype is wrong; all three arguments are on the stack.

entries.name: RasterDriver_CloseDisplay
entries.description: (driverId, info): calls slot 12 of the driver's own routine table (RasterDriver_FindRoutineTable) with info. GLDisplay_Close passes display+4.

entries.name: Raster_InstallViewport
entries.description: (viewport): copies the viewport's first 0x81 dwords to 004a33f0 and its dwords 0x81-0x8a to 004a35f4..004a3618. Raster_SelectRenderTarget passes the display's +0x40.

entries.name: Raster_SetClipBlock
entries.description: (block): stores the clip block pointer PTR_DAT_004a362c that the raster routines read. Raster_InstallRenderContext passes ctx+4; Raster_SelectRenderTarget calls it too.

entries.name: ClipBlock_Init
entries.description: (block, width, height): zeroes the region area +0..+0x200 and +0x204..+0x210 (clip mode +0x204 0, so unclipped), sets the rect's far corner +0x214/+0x218 to width-1/height-1, zeroes +0x21c/+0x220, and points the pen +0x224 at 004a361c and the fill brush +0x228 at 004a3624. GLDisplay_Open initialises a display's clip block with it.

entries.name: Gfx_PlotPixel
entries.description: Plots one pixel at an {x, y} pair with the pen at clipBlock+0x224 of the current drawing context (004a362c): pen mode 0 through g_RasterRoutines_PutPixel in its colour (a type-4 colour resolved through g_RasterColourRamps), mode 2 through g_RasterRoutines_RemapPixel; any other mode plots nothing. Translated by (+0x20c - +0x21c, +0x210 - +0x220) when +0x208 is set, then clipped per the clip mode at +0x204: 0 none, 1 the rect +0x20c..+0x218 inclusive, otherwise each region of the block's list (type 0 a rect, type 2 a span region), plotting through the first that contains it. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Gfx_PlotPixel.

entries.name: Driver3_LoadPalette
entries.description: Slot 13 of raster driver 3's routine table (pointer at 004a58b8), the slot GLDisplay_LoadPalette calls: (first, count, entries) programs the VGA DAC directly. Waits for vertical retrace (port 0x3da bit 3), writes the DAC state (port 0x3c7 & 3) to 0x3c9 when it is not 3, sets the write index 0x3c8 to first and, between CLI and STI, writes three bytes of each 4-byte entry to 0x3c9 for count entries. Matches VSHELL's 00459b3c.

entries.name: Driver3_ReadPalette
entries.description: Slot 14 of raster driver 3's routine table (pointer at 004a58bc): (first, count, out) reads the VGA DAC directly. Waits for vertical retrace (port 0x3da bit 3), reads one byte from 0x3c9 when the DAC state (0x3c7 & 3) is non-zero, sets the read index 0x3c7 to first and, between CLI and STI, reads three bytes per entry from 0x3c9 into out, storing 1 as each 4-byte entry's fourth byte. Screenshot_WritePal (00453d10), the palette file writer, calls g_RasterRoutines slot 14 with (0, 0x100, buffer). Matches VSHELL's 00459b7b.

entries.name: Driver3_SetBorderColour
entries.description: (colour): ENTER 0,0; CLI; reads port 0x3da to reset the attribute controller's flip-flop, then writes index 0x11 (the overscan colour register), the colour byte and 0x20 to port 0x3c0; LEAVE; RET -- with interrupts left disabled. No reference found by es2_xref. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Driver3_SetBorderColour (00459bc3).

entries.name: Driver3_Slot9ReturnZero
entries.description: MOV EAX,0; RET. Slot 9 of raster driver 3's routine table (pointer at 004a58a8); RasterDriver_OpenDisplay goes on to slots 10, 11 and 7 when slot 9 returns 0.

entries.name: Driver3_Slot10ReturnZero
entries.description: MOV EAX,0; RET. Slot 10 of raster driver 3's routine table (pointer at 004a58ac); RasterDriver_OpenDisplay calls slot 10 with no arguments and discards the result.

entries.name: maybe_Driver3_ClipCursorToScreen
entries.description: Frameless code between Driver3_Slot10ReturnZero and Driver3_Slot30NoOp, taking x in EAX and y in EBX, with ECX = 004a3648 and EDX = 004a3656: clears 004a587c and 004a5874, and for a negative x stores -x at 004a587c and 0 at [EDX]. No reference found by es2_xref. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's maybe_Driver3_ClipCursorToScreen (00459bec), whose role it shares.

entries.name: Driver3_Slot30NoOp
entries.description: Slot 30 of raster driver 3's routine table (004a5884): pushes and pops EBX, EDX, ESI, EDI and ES and returns. Cursor_SyncPosition calls slot 30 after storing the pointer position; Driver3_SyncCursorPosition calls this directly.

entries.name: Driver3_Slot31NoOp
entries.description: Slot 31 of raster driver 3's routine table (004a5884): pushes and pops EBX, EDX, ESI, EDI and ES and returns. Cursor_SyncPosition and Driver3_SyncCursorPosition call slot 31 before storing the pointer position.

entries.name: Driver3_StubNoOp1
entries.description: ENTER 0,0; LEAVE; RET, after Driver3_Slot31NoOp. No reference found by es2_xref. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Driver3_StubNoOp1 (00459c9a).

entries.name: Driver3_StubNoOp2
entries.description: ENTER 0,0; LEAVE; RET, after Driver3_StubNoOp1. No reference found by es2_xref. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Driver3_StubNoOp2 (00459ca0).

entries.name: Driver3_Slot32NoOp
entries.description: ENTER 0,0; LEAVE; RET. Slot 32 of raster driver 3's routine table (pointer at 004a5904); GLDisplay_SetAttribute's attribute 0x11 calls g_RasterRoutines slot 32 (004a5844) with the value.

entries.name: Driver3_Slot16NoOp
entries.description: ENTER 0,0; LEAVE; RET. Slot 16 of raster driver 3's routine table (pointer at 004a58c4), the slot maybe_g_RasterRoutines_SetSourcePage names.

entries.name: Driver3_Slot17NoOp
entries.description: Slot 17 of raster driver 3's routine table g_RasterRoutines_Driver3 (pointer at 004a58c8), the slot maybe_g_RasterRoutines_SetDrawPage reaches: ENTER 0,0 / LEAVE / RET.

entries.name: Driver3_Slot18NoOp
entries.description: Slot 18 of raster driver 3's routine table g_RasterRoutines_Driver3 (pointer at 004a58cc), the slot maybe_g_RasterRoutines_SetVisiblePage reaches: ENTER 0,0 / LEAVE / RET.

entries.name: Driver3_SetOrigin
entries.description: Slot 15 of raster driver 3's routine table (pointer at 004a58c0), what g_RasterRoutines_SetOrigin holds after RasterDriver_InstallRoutines: (page, point) calls Display_SetOrigin(page, point). It cleans up with a 16-bit ADD SP,0xc after pushing 8 bytes; the LEAVE that follows restores ESP from EBP. Byte-identical after normalisation to VSHELL's 00459cbe.

entries.name: Driver3_StubNoOp3
entries.description: Pushes EBX, EDX, ESI, EDI and ES, pops them and returns, after Driver3_SetOrigin. No reference found by es2_xref. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Driver3_StubNoOp3 (00459cd3).

entries.name: maybe_Driver3_SetCursorImage
entries.description: Empty: returns at once. Sits beside Driver3_SyncCursorPosition, driver 3's copy of Cursor_SyncPosition; the cockpit cursor-slot functions call it with a .DCI cursor's bitmap and hotspot when Display_UseScrollWindow is set, as they call maybe_Cursor_SetImage otherwise.

entries.name: Driver3_SyncCursorPosition
entries.description: Raster driver 3's copy of Cursor_SyncPosition: the same stores, with the routine-table slot 31 call before them, but it calls 004897c8 (driver 3's slot 30, Driver3_Slot30NoOp) directly where Cursor_SyncPosition calls slot 30 through g_RasterRoutines. AlertPanel_Leave calls it.

entries.name: Driver3_StubNoOp4
entries.description: ENTER 4,0; pushes and pops EBX, ES, ESI and EDI; LEAVE; RET, before Driver3_BlitClipped. No reference found by es2_xref. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Driver3_StubNoOp4 (00459d47).

entries.name: Driver3_BlitClipped
entries.description: Slot 26 of raster driver 3's routine table, the blit Bitmap_BlitClipDispatch calls: (bitmap, point, clipRect, flags) clips the bitmap at point to clipRect {x0, y0, x1, y1} inclusive, or to the surface when clipRect is null, then copies it in one of four orientations by flags bits 0-1: opaque when the bitmap's byte +5 has bit 0x10, otherwise skipping colour 0.

entries.name: Driver3_GrabClipped
entries.description: Slot 27 of raster driver 3's routine table (pointer at 004a58f0), the screen read Bitmap_GrabClipDispatch calls through g_RasterRoutines_Grab (004a5830): (bitmap, point, clipRect, flags) clips the bitmap's rect at point (int16 rows +0, cols +2) to clipRect {x0, y0, x1, y1} inclusive, or to the surface (stride 004a368e by height 004a3692) when clipRect is null, and copies the screen pixels under it into the bitmap's data (+0xa) in one of four orientations by flags & 3: 0 straight, 1 rows reversed, 2 columns reversed, 3 both. The reverse of Driver3_BlitClipped.

entries.name: Driver3_BlitClippedRegion
entries.description: Slot 28 of raster driver 3's routine table (pointer at 004a58f4), the routine Bitmap_BlitClipDispatch calls through g_RasterRoutines_BlitRegion (004a5834) for clip modes 1 and 2: (bitmap, point, clipRect, flags). When the installed clip block's mode (PTR_DAT_004a362c+0x204) is 2 it ignores clipRect and walks the block's region list (count +0, pointers from +4): a type-0 region calls Driver3_BlitClipped with the region's own rect (+4), a type-2 span region calls it once per row of its span list (top row uint16 +0, row count +2, {x0, x1} uint16 pairs from +4) with the rect {x0, row, x1, row}; other types are skipped. Any other mode calls Driver3_BlitClipped with clipRect. So in mode 2 an opaque bitmap is cut to the regions scanline by scanline. Byte-identical after normalisation to VSHELL's 0045a28e.

entries.name: Driver3_FillSpans
entries.description: Slot 0 of raster driver 3's routine table (pointer at g_RasterRoutines_Driver3 (004a5884)), what g_RasterRoutines slot 0 holds: (spans, colour) fills a span list {int16 top row, uint16 row count, {int16 x0, int16 x1} per row} with the colour byte, dword-aligned dwords for a span longer than 0x10 bytes and bytes otherwise, stepping the row address by the stride 004a368e. A list whose top row is negative skips its first -top rows' spans and starts at row 0. Raster_FillSpanList and Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch's mode-0 brush reach it.

entries.name: Driver3_RemapSpans
entries.description: Slot 1 of raster driver 3's routine table (pointer at 004a5888), what g_RasterRoutines slot 1 (g_RasterRoutines_RemapSpans (004a57c8)) holds: (spans, table) rewrites every pixel of a span list {int16 top row, uint16 row count, {int16 x0, int16 x1} per row} as table[pixel], the brush-mode-6 path of Raster_FillSpanList and Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch. For a negative top row it adds -top * 4 to the surface descriptor pointer (ECX, 00489f3e) where Driver3_FillSpans advances the span list (EDX), so it then takes row -top's offset plus row -top-1's offset as the start address and walks the spans from the list's first row.

entries.name: Driver3_CopySpans
entries.description: Slot 19 of raster driver 3's routine table (pointer at 004a58d0), the routine Region_CopySpansBetweenPages and Region_CopyRectBetweenPages call through g_RasterRoutines_CopySpans (004a5810): (spans, offset) copies each span of a span list {uint16 top row, uint16 row count, {int16 x0, int16 x1} per row} from (row - offset.y, x - offset.x) to (row, x) within the one surface, ordering the copy so overlapping source and destination are safe: rows bottom-up when offset.y > 0, each row right-to-left (STD) when offset.y is 0 and offset.x > 0, otherwise forward; returns at once for a zero offset. The right-to-left path pushes DS and its JCXZ at 0048a093 jumps past the POP DS at 0048a0a4 when a span is shorter than 4 pixels, so the exit POPs restore EBX..EDI shifted by one dword per such span (LEAVE still restores ESP). The top row is read with MOVZX, so the negative-row branch at 00489fb4 is skipped for every input.

entries.name: Driver3_Slot8ReturnZero
entries.description: Slot 8 of raster driver 3's routine table (pointer at 004a58a4): returns 0. RasterDriver_OpenDisplay calls slot 8 with the bitmap header first and goes on to slots 9, 10, 11 and 7 when it returns 0.

entries.name: Driver3_OpenDisplay
entries.description: Slot 11 of raster driver 3's routine table (g_RasterRoutines_Driver3), which RasterDriver_OpenDisplay calls with (bitmapHeader, info): allocates the surface's row-offset table into info+0, takes the width and height from the one-shot overrides when they are not negative (resetting them to -1) or else from the header, fills the rest of info and sets Display_ScreenRect and the origin to 0. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Driver3_OpenDisplay (004281fb).
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0048a0c8; es2_naming.py diff against VSHELL 004281fb

entries.name: Driver3_Slot7NoOp
entries.description: Slot 7 of raster driver 3's routine table (g_RasterRoutines_Driver3): returns at once. RasterDriver_OpenDisplay and GLDisplay_SetAttribute call slot 7.

entries.name: Driver3_CloseDisplay
entries.description: Slot 12 of raster driver 3's routine table, which RasterDriver_CloseDisplay calls: (info) frees the row-offset table at info+0 that Driver3_OpenDisplay allocated.

entries.name: Raster_GetPixel
entries.description: Driver 3's g_RasterRoutines slot 4: (point) returns the byte at the draw surface 004a366a: rowTable[point.y] (+4 + y*4) + point.x + base (+0).
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 0048a234; driver-3 table at 004a5894

entries.name: Raster_PutPixel
entries.description: Driver 3's g_RasterRoutines slot 5: (point, value) stores the byte at the address Raster_GetPixel reads.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 0048a255; driver-3 table at 004a5898

entries.name: Driver3_RemapPixel
entries.description: Slot 6 of raster driver 3's routine table (pointer at 004a589c), what g_RasterRoutines slot 6 (g_RasterRoutines_RemapPixel (004a57dc)) holds: (point, table) rewrites the pixel at {x, y} through the 256-byte table, pixel = table[pixel], addressing it through the surface descriptor at 004a366a (base +0, row offsets from +4). Gfx_PlotPixel calls it for a pen of mode 2 with the table at pen+4. Byte-identical after normalisation to VSHELL's 0045a57c.

entries.name: Driver3_DrawLine
entries.description: Slot 34 of raster driver 3's routine table (pointer at 004a590c), what Raster_DrawLine calls through g_RasterRoutines_DrawLine (004a584c): (colour, from, to) draws an unclipped Bresenham line of the colour byte between two {x, y} int32 points, swapping them so x increases and stepping rows by the signed stride 004a368e. Byte-identical after normalisation to VSHELL's 0045a5a8.

entries.name: Driver3_SpanRead
entries.description: Slot 21 of raster driver 3's routine table (pointer at 004a58d8), what Region_SaveSpans calls through g_RasterRoutines_SpanRead (004a5818): (buffer, y, x0, x1) copies x1 - x0 + 1 screen bytes into buffer, dwords then bytes; returns at once when x0 > x1. It loads y into EAX at 0048a34a and then MOV AX,DS (0048a353) overwrites EAX's low word before EAX indexes the row-offset table at 0048a35a, so the row read is (y & 0xffff0000) | DS, the same sequence as Driver3_SpanCopy and Driver3_SpanFill. Byte-identical after normalisation to VSHELL's 0045a638.

entries.name: Driver3_SpanCopy
entries.description: Slot 22 of raster driver 3's routine table, Raster_SpanCopy's: (pixels, y, x0, x1) copies x1 - x0 + 1 bytes from pixels to x0 of a row through the surface's row-offset table, dwords then bytes; nothing when x0 > x1. The row index is EAX after MOV AX,DS (0048a3a1, setting ES) has replaced the low word of the y it loaded (0048a398), so the row read at 0048a3a8 is (y & 0xffff0000) | DS rather than y.

entries.name: Driver3_SpanCopyRegion
entries.description: Slot 23 of raster driver 3's routine table (pointer at 004a58e0), what Raster_SpanCopyRegion and SpanRegion_Restore call through g_RasterRoutines_SpanCopyRegion (004a5820): (pixels, y, x0, x1). With the clip block's mode (PTR_DAT_004a362c+0x204) at 2 it walks the block's regions: a type-0 rect region whose rows hold y clamps x0..x1 to its x range, a type-2 span region whose rows hold y clamps it to that row's {x0, x1}, and each calls Driver3_SpanCopy with pixels advanced by the clamped start; other modes call Driver3_SpanCopy unclipped. Byte-identical after normalisation to VSHELL's 0045a6cc.

entries.name: Driver3_SpanFill
entries.description: Slot 24 of raster driver 3's routine table, Raster_SpanFill's: (colour, y, x0, x1) fills x0..x1 of a row with the colour byte, dwords then bytes; nothing when x0 > x1. The row index is EAX after MOV AX,DS (0048a4c2, setting ES) has replaced the low word of the y it loaded (0048a4b9), so the row read at 0048a4c9 is (y & 0xffff0000) | DS rather than y.

entries.name: Driver3_SpanFillRegion
entries.description: Slot 25 of raster driver 3's routine table (pointer at 004a58e8), what Raster_SpanFillRegion calls through g_RasterRoutines_SpanFillRegion (004a5828): Driver3_SpanCopyRegion's region walk, calling Driver3_SpanFill. It opens directly with MOV EBX,[004a362c], with neither ENTER nor PUSH EBP nor register pushes, reads its arguments at EBP+8..+0x14, which is the caller's frame, and ends with a bare RET. Through Raster_SpanFillRegion (PUSH EBP / MOV EBP,ESP, arguments y, x0, x1, colour) that makes colour = y, row = x0, x0 = x1 and x1 = colour, and EBX, ECX, ESI and EDI come back changed. Byte-identical after normalisation to VSHELL's 0045a7f9.

entries.name: Driver3_FillRect
entries.description: Slot 2 of raster driver 3's routine table (pointer at 004a588c), what Raster_FillRect calls through g_RasterRoutines_FillRect (004a57cc) for a mode-0 brush: (rect, colour) fills the inclusive rect {x0, y0, x1, y1} with the colour byte, bytes per row for a width up to 0x10 and dword-aligned dwords otherwise, stepping by the stride 004a368e. Byte-identical after normalisation to VSHELL's 0045a8bc.

entries.name: Driver3_RemapRect
entries.description: Slot 3 of raster driver 3's routine table (pointer at 004a5890), what Raster_FillRect calls through g_RasterRoutines_RemapRect (004a57d0) for a mode-6 brush with the brush's +4: (rect, table) rewrites every pixel of the inclusive rect {x0, y0, x1, y1} as table[pixel]. Byte-identical after normalisation to VSHELL's 0045a944.

entries.name: Driver3_CopyRect
entries.description: Slot 20 of raster driver 3's routine table (pointer at 004a58d4), what g_RasterRoutines_CopyRect holds: (rect, offset) copies the inclusive rect from (rect - offset) to rect within the one surface. When source and destination overlap it orders the copy by the offset's sign (rows bottom-up for offset.y > 0, right-to-left for offset.y 0 and offset.x > 0) and returns at once for a zero offset; otherwise it copies forward. Byte-identical after normalisation to VSHELL's 0045a99f.

entries.name: Driver3_ClearSurface
entries.description: Slot 35 of raster driver 3's routine table (pointer at 004a5910), reached through g_RasterRoutines_ClearSurface (004a5850): (ignored, colour) fills stride 004a368e * height 004a3692 bytes from the surface base (*004a366a) with the colour byte. Sim_DeathFlash calls g_RasterRoutines_ClearSurface (004a5850) twice with colour 0. Byte-identical after normalisation to VSHELL's 0045aada.

entries.name: Raster_FillBitmapPolygon
entries.description: g_RasterRoutines slot 33, which Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch calls for brush modes 5 and 7. Reads the brush at clipBlock+0x228: +8 the source quad, +0xc the bitmap dimensions pointer, and +0x10 a remap table only when the mode is 7 (otherwise it passes 0). Finds the top and bottom vertices, walks the two edges with Raster_BitmapEdgeSetup/Raster_BitmapEdgeStep and calls Raster_SpanBitmap per scanline within the clip rows. Reached only through the driver-3 table, so Ghidra auto-analysis had no function here.

entries.name: Raster_BitmapEdgeStep
entries.description: Steps an edge one row: decrements its row count and, at zero, moves to the next edge with Raster_BitmapEdgeSetup (returning 0 when none is left); otherwise adds the u, v and x steps. Returns 1 while the edge continues.

entries.name: Raster_BitmapEdgeSetup
entries.description: Advances an edge of Raster_FillBitmapPolygon from vertexIndex to the next vertex in the edge's direction (edge[0], +1 or -1, wrapping), storing its row count, the source-quad u,v at the start in 16.16 and their per-row steps (Math_Q16Divide), and the destination x start and step. Skips zero-height edges. Returns 0 when the walk reaches the bottom vertex.

entries.name: Raster_SpanBitmap
entries.description: Fills one scanline between two edges of Raster_FillBitmapPolygon, sampling the nearest texel through dimensions+2 (cols, the stride) and dimensions+0xa (the data pointer), clipped by the render context's clip mode. With remap null (brush mode 5) a texel of palette index 0 is not stored (OR AL,AL / JE at 0048ae87); with remap set (mode 7) every texel, index 0 included, is stored as remap[texel].
entries.signature: void __cdecl Raster_SpanBitmap(int *leftEdge, int *rightEdge, short *dimensions, unsigned char *remap)

entries.name: Driver3_BlitScaled
entries.description: Slot 29 of raster driver 3's routine table (pointer at 004a58f8), what Bitmap_BlitScaledClipDispatch calls through g_RasterRoutines_BlitScaled (004a5838): (bitmap, w, h, point, clipRect, flags) draws the bitmap (int16 rows +0, cols +2, data +0xa) stretched to w by h at point with a nearest-sample DDA, clipped to clipRect {x0, y0, x1, y1} or to the surface when it is null; with the clip block's mode at 2 it repeats per region instead (a type-0 region's rect, a type-2 span region's rows with x clamped to its spans). flags 1 mirrors the rows, 2 the columns, 3 both. Opaque when the bitmap's byte +5 has bit 0x10, otherwise colour 0 is skipped. Returns at once when w or h is 0.

entries.name: Raster_SpanTexturedClipped
entries.description: Draws the span at x DAT_004a5958, length DAT_004a0984, through the visible-run list at DAT_004a5954 ({x, length} pairs, DAT_004a5950 of them): for each run that overlaps it, advances the destination DAT_004a0980 and the u/v accumulators past the hidden pixels, trims the length at the run's end and calls Raster_SpanTextured. Returns at the first run that starts at or past the span's end. Raster_DrawPolygon uses it in mode 0 when ActiveScanlineClipSpans is set and either the context clip mode (+0x208) is 2 or maybe_g_DepthBufferEnabled is set; the run list is then the row's clip spans, or with the depth buffer the runs Raster_DepthTestSpan leaves.

entries.name: Raster_SpanTexturedShadedClipped
entries.description: Raster_SpanTexturedClipped for mode 1: the same visible-run walk, calling Raster_SpanTexturedShaded.

entries.name: Raster_SpanTexturedGouraudClipped
entries.description: Raster_SpanTexturedClipped for mode 2: the same visible-run walk, also advancing the ramp-row accumulator DAT_004a09c4 by DAT_004a09c8 per skipped pixel, calling Raster_SpanTexturedGouraud.

entries.name: Raster_SpanTexturedShadedQuadraticClipped
entries.description: Hand-written (ENTER 4,0), after Raster_SpanTexturedGouraudClipped: the visible-run walk of the clipped span routines for the second-order span, calling maybe_Raster_SpanTexturedShadedQuadratic (0046aed8, call at 0048b664). No reference found by es2_xref. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Raster_SpanTexturedShadedQuadraticClipped (0045b886).

entries.name: Raster_SpanTexturedGouraudQuadraticClipped
entries.description: Hand-written (ENTER 4,0): Raster_SpanTexturedShadedQuadraticClipped's walk for the Gouraud span, calling maybe_Raster_SpanTexturedGouraudQuadratic (0046af9c, call at 0048b72c). No reference found by es2_xref. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Raster_SpanTexturedGouraudQuadraticClipped (0045b93d).

entries.name: Raster_DepthTestSpan
entries.description: Per-pixel depth test and write for one span: walks DAT_004a5b00 dwords of the buffer from DAT_004a5af4 with a value starting at DAT_004a5af8 and stepped by DAT_004a5afc per pixel; where the stored dword is greater it writes the value and the pixel is visible. Collects the visible pixels as {x, length} runs at 004a595c (x = index + DAT_004a5af0), sets DAT_004a5950 to the run count and DAT_004a5954 to 004a595c, the list the ...Clipped span routines walk. Raster_DrawPolygon calls it per row when maybe_g_DepthBufferEnabled is set, with the buffer at g_DepthBuffer + (row * stride + x) * 4 and the value the edge's interpolated view depth ORed with (row + g_DepthBufferFrameTag) << 24.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0048b748 and its call site in Raster_DrawPolygon (004684fb)

entries.name: DepthBuffer_ClearWrappedRows
entries.description: (buffer): hand-written (ENTER). Sets to 0xffffffff every row r of the g_DepthBufferWidth-wide dword buffer with (r + g_DepthBufferFrameTag) & 0xff == 0, i.e. from row (-tag) & 0xff in steps of 0x100 below g_DepthBufferHeight, then decrements the tag byte g_DepthBufferFrameTag (004a5b04). No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: DepthBuffer_ClearWrappedRowSpans
entries.description: (buffer, rowSpans): hand-written (ENTER). DepthBuffer_ClearWrappedRows restricted to the spans of each cleared row: rowSpans holds an 8-byte {int count, {int x, int length} *spans} entry per row (the layout ClipRegions_BuildScanlineSpans builds for ActiveScanlineClipSpans), and each span's dwords are set to 0xffffffff. Decrements g_DepthBufferFrameTag (004a5b04) after. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Raster_FillViewportBuffer
entries.description: (buffer, colour): hand-written (ENTER). Fills g_DepthBufferWidth * g_DepthBufferHeight bytes of buffer with the colour byte, a dword at a time. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Raster_FillViewportBufferSpans
entries.description: (buffer, rowSpans, colour): hand-written (ENTER). For each of g_DepthBufferHeight rows fills each span of that row's 8-byte {int count, {int x, int length} *spans} entry with the colour byte (bytes to dword alignment, dwords, then bytes), advancing buffer by g_DepthBufferWidth per row. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: DepthBuffer_Alloc
entries.description: (width, height): allocates width * height dwords with Mem_NewArray into g_DepthBuffer (006c6014), zeroes them with _memset, and stores width in g_DepthBufferWidth (004a5b08) and height in g_DepthBufferHeight (004a5b0c). It is the one store to g_DepthBuffer (006c6014) in the decompile. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: ClipRegions_BuildScanlineSpans
entries.description: Flattens a loaded region list (rects + span blocks from CockpitClipRegions_Load) into a per-scanline span table of `rowCount` rows (0xf0 << VideoMode_YCoordShift, i.e. 240 or 480). Each row is {int spanCount, ptr to spanCount x {int start, int length}}, sorted by start. Stores the result in ActiveScanlineClipSpans. This -- not any colour key -- is the cockpit's 3D-viewport cutout mechanism.

entries.name: TSContext_Ctor
entries.description: TSContext constructor (vtable 004a5b51, RTTI name 'TSContext', 0x16 bytes): constructs the point at +4 (maybe_Point3I_Ctor) and the int16 triple at +0x10 (maybe_Point3S_Ctor). TSCamera_Ctor and the light constructors run it first.

entries.name: View_CtorBase
entries.description: Base view constructor (vtable 004a5b51): copies an int[3] position to +4..+0xc and a short[3] angle triple to +0x10..+0x14. The +4 triple is what View_GetActiveObject's readers take as the camera position.

entries.name: TSContext_Dtor
entries.description: TSContext destructor (vtable 004a5b51, RTTI name 'TSContext', 0x16 bytes): restores the vtable and frees the object when flag & 1.

entries.name: maybe_TSLight_SetIntensity
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's maybe_TSLight_SetIntensity (0045da4c).
entries.source: es2_naming.py diff DBSIM 0048bbe0 VSHELL 0045da4c: identical after normalisation; RTTI TSLight vtable slot

entries.name: Light_TransformToModelSpace
entries.description: Transforms a light's world position (+0x04) and direction (+0x10) by the given transform into the model-space copies at +0x22 and +0x2e. Those copies, NOT the world fields, are what Light_ComputeShadeForFace and Light_ComputeShadeForNormal read. Driven per composed node by Raster_SetModelTransform, gated on DAT_006cbc88.

entries.name: maybe_TSOmniLight_SetIntensity
entries.description: TSOmniLight vtable +0x04 (00497ac8), its override of maybe_TSLight_SetIntensity: (light, value) stores value at +0x1a as the base does, and also value * light+0x38 at +0x3c.

entries.name: TSCamera_Ctor
entries.description: TSCamera constructor (vtable 004a5b41, RTTI name 'TSCamera', 0x22 bytes): runs the TSContext constructor 0048bb34, then installs its own vtable.

entries.name: View_Ctor
entries.description: (view, renderTarget, perspectiveShift, nearPlane, position, angles): View_CtorBase(view, position, angles), then the vtable 004a5b41 at +0, the perspective shift at +0x1a, the near plane at +0x1e and the render target at +0x16 -- the fields Raster_InstallViewProjection reads; adds 1 to the count at Rtl_DtorCountPtr. Returns view.
entries.signature: void * __cdecl View_Ctor(void *this, void *renderTarget, int perspectiveShift, int nearPlane, int *position, short *angles)

entries.name: TSOrthoCamera_Ctor
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's TSOrthoCamera_Ctor (0045db40): (obj, a, b, c, d, position, orientation) View_Ctor(obj, a, b, c, position, orientation) -- where VSHELL's calls TSCamera_Ctor -- then the TSOrthoCamera table (004a5b31) and d at +0x22.

entries.name: TSBase_Dtor
entries.description: TSBase destructor (vtable 004a6a2c, RTTI name 'TSBase', 4 bytes): restores the vtable and frees the object when flag & 1.

entries.name: TSBase_Render
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's TSBase_Render (0045dba4).
entries.source: es2_naming.py diff DBSIM 0048bd3c VSHELL 0045dba4: identical after normalisation; RTTI ANCyclicSequence vtable slot

entries.name: Light_Register
entries.description: Adds a light object pointer to the active light list (DAT_006c6130, 10-slot max, dedups by pointer identity). Four call sites found by es2_xref: Light_GetOrCreateDirectional/Light_GetOrCreatePoint (pooled directional/point light getters, see their own entries), Light_ReregisterPersistent (re-registers a persistent light list Light_PersistentList into the active manager), and Light_CreateMissionSun (00461240).

entries.name: Light_Unregister
entries.description: Swap-removes a light pointer from the active light list DAT_006c6130 and decrements DAT_006c612c. The inverse of Light_Register.

entries.name: Light_ComputeShadeAtPoint
entries.description: (point int32[3]): sums a shade over the active light list (006c6130, count 006c612c) by Light_GetType: type 0 and type 1 each add Light_GetIntensity flat, without a direction test; type 2 adds intensity * (0x7ff * Light_GetRangeNumerator / (Light_GetFalloffOffset + |Light_GetModelPosition - point|)) >> 11 (Vec3_Subtract, Point3I_Magnitude). Returns the sum clamped to 0xff. Its one argument is the point; it reads a normal from nowhere. No caller found by es2_xref. Matches VSHELL's 0045dc30 after normalisation.

entries.name: Light_ComputeShadeForFace
entries.description: The per-face 'shade byte' (0-255, clamped) calculation feeding TSShadedPoly_Render (0047542c). TSSolidPoly_Render does NOT call it -- a solid poly carries no light term at all. NOT a simple angle calc -- a real light-accumulation loop over the active light list (DAT_006c6130, max 10 slots, count DAT_006c612c), dispatching per-entry on a type tag from Light_GetType: type 0 = ambient (adds a flat intensity from Light_GetIntensity unconditionally -- not populated by a retail mission, see Light_AddDirectional/PointHelper's entries), type 1 = directional (dot-product-like test via DotProductVec3Short_Thunk against the face's Normal point (param_1), only contributes when the result crosses a fixed threshold, i.e. face-vs-light-direction test), type 2 = point light (distance-attenuated: displacement from the light's position (Light_GetModelPosition) to the face's Center point (param_2) combined with the Normal via DotProductVec3Int_Thunk, divided by distance/range fields Light_GetRangeNumerator/Light_GetFalloffOffset). Params: param_1 = the poly's normal point (three shorts), param_2 = its centre point (same two pointers TSPoly_FrontBackVisibilityTest receives). Light_ComputeShadeForNormal (0048c060) is the terrain's variant; Light_ComputeShadeAtPoint (0048bdcc) sums the same list for a point alone, with no normal.

entries.name: Light_ComputeShadeForNormal
entries.description: The per-normal sibling of Light_ComputeShadeForFace, the one the terrain uses. Takes (short* normal, int* centre) and walks the same active light list, returning a shade byte clamped to 255. Directional (type 1) branch, which is the only one a retail mission populates: dot = DotProductVec3Short(normal, lightDir); if (dot < 0) shade -= (intensity * dot) >> 22. Normals arrive normalised to length 0x800 and the mission sun's direction vector is length 0x1000 at intensity 0x100, so the whole expression is shade = min(255, 512 * cos) -- IT SATURATES AT cos 0.5, i.e. every surface within 60 degrees of facing the sun gets the ramp's top row rather than a falloff. Flat ground sits at cos 0.544 and is pinned at 255. Called by Terrain_BuildCellSurfaceAndShade once per cell triangle at zone load.

entries.name: Raster_InstallViewProjection
entries.description: Installs a view's projection state into the rasterizer globals: perspective shift from view+0x1a (DAT_006c60ac), near plane from +0x1e (DAT_006c60b0), orthographic divisor from +0x22 (DAT_006c60b4) when the shift is 0, and from the render target at view+0x16 the clip rect +0x210..+0x21c. The projection centre DAT_006c60b8/bc starts as that rect's top-left and then has the target's +0x220 pair subtracted -- that pair being the .VUE projection centre plus the view's canvas origin, installed by CockpitView_ApplyViewState. Then builds the view's transform into 006c6018 (View_BuildTransform: euler +0x10, translation +0x04), inverts it (Transform_InvertRigid) into world-to-view, and installs that with Raster_SetViewTransform.

entries.name: Raster_SetViewTransform
entries.description: (viewTransform): Raster_SetModelTransform's twin for the view side. Installs viewTransform (the identity at 006c6080 for null) at 006c6078, rebuilds g_ModelToView = Transform_Concat(g_ModelTransformPtr, view), its inverse g_ViewToModel (Transform_InvertRigid) and g_EyeInModelSpace (the origin through that inverse). Raster_InstallViewProjection calls it.

entries.name: Raster_SetModelTransform
entries.description: Installs a transform as the renderer's current model transform (null means the identity at 006c6080); the pointer goes to g_ModelTransformPtr. Builds g_ModelToView = Transform_Concat(model, [006c6078]), its inverse g_ViewToModel (Transform_InvertRigid), and g_EyeInModelSpace (the origin through that inverse). When 006cbc88 is set it moves every registered light (list 006c6130, count 006c612c) into the model's space with Light_TransformToModelSpace, using the inverse of the model transform (Transform_InvertRigid on a copy). VSHELL's counterpart is Raster_SetModelTransform (0045e198).

entries.name: Raster_ModelToView
entries.description: (point, out): Transform_ApplyToPoint_Thunk by the current model-to-view transform g_ModelToView. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Raster_ModelToView.

entries.name: Raster_ModelToViewArray
entries.description: (count, src, dst): Transform_ApplyToPoint_Thunk(src, g_ModelToView, dst) for count 12-byte int32 points, the array form of Raster_ModelToView. No caller found by es2_xref. Byte-identical after normalisation to VSHELL's 0045e2ec.

entries.name: Raster_PerspectiveScale
entries.description: Scales a world-space extent to pixels at a given depth: (extent << DAT_006c60ac) / z, or (extent << 8) / DAT_006c60b4 in the orthographic mode. The beam draw uses it for half-width, flooring the result at 2.

entries.name: Raster_PerspectiveDivide
entries.description: The perspective divide, ahead of Raster_ProjectToScreen's centring: screenOut[0] = (viewPoint[0] << DAT_006c60ac) / viewPoint[1], screenOut[1] = (viewPoint[2] << DAT_006c60ac) / viewPoint[1], or both over DAT_006c60b4 with a shift of 0 (the orthographic mode). Returns screenOut. Dividing components 0 and 2 by component 1 is what fixes the view-space axis order as (across, DEPTH, up) -- the fact that says which component Terrain_DrawCellQuad's fog distance is. DAT_006c60ac is the focal shift installed from view+0x1a.

entries.name: Raster_PerspectiveDivideArray
entries.description: (count, view, screen): the array form of Raster_PerspectiveDivide: for each 12-byte view point writes {(x << 006c60ac) / y, (z << 006c60ac) / y} to an 8-byte screen point. With the focal shift 006c60ac at 0 it divides (x << 8) and (z << 8) by 006c60b4 instead, but that loop advances neither pointer nor the count, so for a nonzero count it repeats the first point forever. No caller found by es2_xref. Matches VSHELL's 0045e3ac after normalisation.

entries.name: Raster_ProjectToScreen
entries.description: Final projection step: screenX = x + DAT_006c60b8, screenY = DAT_006c60bc - y. That centre is the .VUE projection centre, not the middle of the viewport rect, and is where the gunsight reticle sits -- anything running parallel to the view axis vanishes there. APOCA's is 95 rows down a 240-row view.

entries.name: Raster_ProjectToScreenArray
entries.description: (count, src, dst): the array form of Raster_ProjectToScreen: for each 8-byte point writes {x + 006c60b8, 006c60bc - y}. No caller found by es2_xref. Byte-identical after normalisation to VSHELL's 0045e448.

entries.name: TSPoly_FrontBackVisibilityTest
entries.description: (normal, centre), both three-short points: with the focal shift 006c60ac at 0, rotates the normal into view space through g_ModelToView and returns 1 when its depth component is negative; otherwise returns dot(normal, g_EyeInModelSpace - centre). Called from all three flat poly renderers (TSSolidPoly_Render 00474db4, TSShadedPoly_Render 0047542c, TSTexture4Poly_Render 00474e9c) to pick the front or back surface colour. The same code as VSHELL's TSPoly_FrontBackVisibilityTest (0045e480).

entries.name: Raster_FrontFacing
entries.description: (normal, point): with no perspective (006c60ac zero) rotates the int16 normal by g_ModelToView's matrix and returns 1 when the result's second component (y) is negative, else 0; otherwise returns the dot product of the normal with g_EyeInModelSpace - point (positive when the face looks at the eye). TexPoly_Render picks the surface's front bitmap (+0) when it is positive and the back (+8) otherwise.

entries.name: Poly_ProjectShapeVertices
entries.description: The .DTS renderers' sibling of Poly_ProjectIndexedVertices: projects the current face's vertices (count 006c6968, index list 006c6976 from 006c696a) into the screen-point list 006cbb86 and sets its count 006cbc86. With 006c60ac zero it transforms each untouched vertex by g_ModelToView (0048da87) and projects it with a constant divisor (x << 8 / 006c60b4 + 006c60b8, -z << 8 / 006c60b4 + 006c60bc), memoising it as 2 in the state bytes 006c697e, and returns 0; otherwise it returns Poly_ProjectShapeVerticesPerspective's result. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Poly_ProjectShapeVertices. TSShadedPoly_Render, TSSolidPoly_Render and TSTexture4Poly_Render call it.

entries.name: Poly_ProjectIndexedVertices
entries.description: Projects the vertices the current face names -- DAT_006c6968 of them from DAT_006c696a into the index list DAT_006c6976, indexing the point array DAT_006c6970 -- into the screen-point list Poly_ScreenPoints / count DAT_006cbc86. Memoises per point in the state byte array DAT_006c697e: 0 untouched, 1 behind the near plane, 2 already projected, so a shared vertex is transformed once per shape. Takes no arguments. Returns non-zero when any vertex fell behind the near plane, which is the caller's signal to run Poly_ClipRingToNearPlane. Reads 12-byte int32 points. Two callers: BeamTracer_Draw (the ELF/ELF2 quad branch) and TexPoly_Render (0042fc34). The .DTS poly renderers (TSSolidPoly_Render, TSShadedPoly_Render, TSTexture4Poly_Render) use the sibling Poly_ProjectShapeVertices (0048c848) over 6-byte int16 point triples instead.

entries.name: Poly_ProjectViewVertices
entries.description: Projects the current ring's vertices from DAT_006c6970, already in view space, into Poly_ScreenPoints by the ring's vertex number (count 006c6968), marking each 1 (nearer than the near plane) or 2 (projected, screen point cached in Poly_ScreenCache), and returns 1 when any is behind the near plane, after copying the ring's view points into Poly_ViewCache; with none behind it sets the point count 006cbc86. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Poly_ProjectViewVertices (0045ea08).
entries.source: DBSIM decompile; es2_naming.py diff against VSHELL 0045ea08

entries.name: Poly_ClipRingToNearPlane
entries.description: Clips the current face's vertex ring against the near plane DAT_006c60b0 in view space, rebuilding the screen-point list Poly_ScreenPoints and returning the new count DAT_006cbc86. Walks consecutive index pairs: both projected emits the second, exactly one projected emits the crossing point (linear in view-space depth, plus the projection centre) and then the second if it is the projected one. Takes no arguments. Run only when Poly_ProjectIndexedVertices returns non-zero.

entries.name: Poly_ClipRingToNearPlaneWithUV
entries.description: (uvIn, uvOut): Poly_ClipRingToNearPlane carrying a per-vertex {u, v} int pair along. Walks the current face's index ring (count DAT_006c6968, indices from DAT_006c6976 + DAT_006c696a * 2): an edge with both ends projected (state byte 2) emits the end's screen point and copies its pair; an edge with one projected end emits the crossing of the near plane DAT_006c60b0 (view x and -y linear in depth, plus the centre DAT_006c60b8) with the pair interpolated by the same fraction, then the end if it is the projected one. Returns the new count DAT_006cbc86 (points at Poly_ScreenPoints). TSTexture4Poly_Render's g_TexturedPolyUseBitmapBrush branch calls it when Poly_ProjectShapeVertices returns 1.

entries.name: Poly_ClipRingToNearPlaneWithShade
entries.description: (shadeIn, shadeOut): Poly_ClipRingToNearPlane carrying a per-vertex uint16 shade along, interpolating it at each near-plane crossing by the same view-space depth fraction as the point. TSGouraudPoly_Render and TSAliasGouraudPoly_Render call it. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Poly_ClipRingToNearPlaneWithShade (0045f0d4).
entries.source: DBSIM decompile; es2_naming.py match/diff against the VSHELL function named in the description

entries.name: PolyFill_Fill
entries.description: Fills the screen polygon left in the point-list globals by Poly_ProjectIndexedVertices / Poly_ClipRingToNearPlane, through Raster_DrawPolygonEitherWinding -> Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch, then runs PolyFill_FillThenOutline's same outline pass without its mode-5 guard. Winding-agnostic: Raster_DrawPolygonEitherWinding measures the signed area and hands the other winding to Raster_DrawPolygonReversed. Takes no arguments -- everything is globals. Called by BeamTracer_Draw for each ELF chain quad, where the outline pass is inert because the beam installed its own brush.

entries.name: PolyFill_FillThenOutline
entries.description: (reversed): fills the screen ring Poly_ScreenPoints (count DAT_006cbc86; nothing when it is zero) with the brush the render context holds, through GL_DrawPolygonReversed when reversed is non-zero and GL_DrawPolygonDispatch otherwise. Then, when DAT_006c60d4 (the line colour) differs from DAT_006c60dc and PolyFill_FillBrush is not 5, it sets the fill colour to the line colour, sets PolyFill_FillBrush = 4 and draws the same ring again the same way -- an outline pass, not a second fill: mode 4 is Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch's line loop. The poly renderers ramp both colours before this runs, so the != test is on ramped bytes, not raw surface values. PolyFill_FillBrush/DAT_006c60dc are one brush {mode, colour} and are the DEFAULT one: the fill dispatches on whatever clipBlock+0x228 points at, normally this pair, so a caller that installs a brush of its own there (BeamTracer_Draw) leaves these writes inert. PolyFill_Fill (0048d4b4) is the sibling without the mode-5 guard.

entries.name: PolyFill_FillThenOutline_Thunk
entries.description: (backFacing): PolyFill_FillThenOutline(backFacing). Callers found by es2_xref: TSAliasSolidPoly_Render, TSAliasShadedPoly_Render and TSAliasGouraudPoly_Render (twice). Byte-identical to VSHELL's PolyFill_FillThenOutline_Thunk (0045f448).

entries.name: Raster_SaveState
entries.description: Saves the renderer's current model state into a slot: g_ModelToView (0x20 bytes), the model transform pointer 006c607c, the view transform pointer 006c6078, g_EyeInModelSpace, and, when 006cbc88 is set, a 0x16-byte model-space copy per registered light from +0x34. Its light loop steps the save slot but reads the light from the fixed address [006c6130] every pass, so only the first registered light's model-space copy is saved or restored. ShapeNode_InstallTransform saves each freshly composed node with it; ShapeInst_BindNodeTransformArray saves the object's base state.

entries.name: Raster_RestoreState
entries.description: Reinstates a Raster_SaveState slot: the model and view transform pointers, g_ModelToView, a recomputed g_ViewToModel (Transform_InvertRigid), g_EyeInModelSpace and the lights' model-space copies (Light_RestoreModelSpace). Its light loop steps the save slot but reads the light from the fixed address [006c6130] every pass, so only the first registered light's model-space copy is saved or restored. ShapeNode_InstallTransform uses it for a node already composed and to return to the object's base state.

entries.name: Light_DirectionOf

entries.description: (frame, pos): copies an int32 triple to frame+4..+0xc. Light_TransformToModelSpace writes the model-space position (light+0x1e+4 = +0x22, which Light_GetModelPosition returns) through it.

entries.name: LightFrame_SetDirection
entries.description: (frame, dir): copies an int16 triple to frame+0x10..+0x14. Light_TransformToModelSpace writes the model-space direction (light+0x2e, Light_GetModelDirection) through it.

entries.name: Light_GetType
entries.description: Returns light+0x16: 0 ambient (never created anywhere in the binary), 1 directional, 2 point.

entries.name: Light_GetIntensity
entries.description: Returns light+0x1a, the light's intensity, set through vtable slot +4.

entries.name: Light_GetModelPosition
entries.description: Returns light+0x22 -- the MODEL-space position Light_TransformToModelSpace writes, not the world-space +0x04.

entries.name: Light_GetRangeNumerator
entries.description: Returns light+0x38, the NUMERATOR of the point-light falloff (B * 0x20 = 1984). Easily swapped with Light_GetFalloffOffset (0048d97e), which returns +0x34; the two are adjacent, both int32, and reversing them turns a 1/d falloff into a constant.

entries.name: Light_GetFalloffOffset
entries.description: Returns light+0x34, the DENOMINATOR offset of the point-light falloff (A << 5 = 0). See Light_GetRangeNumerator for why the pair is worth stating explicitly.

entries.name: Light_GetModelDirection
entries.description: Returns light+0x2e -- the MODEL-space direction, not the world-space +0x10.

entries.name: Point3I_FromPoint3S
entries.description: (dst, src): widens an int16 triple into an int32 triple: z at dst+8, then x and y through Point2I_FromPoint2S. Returns dst. Light_ComputeShadeForFace, Light_ComputeShadeForNormal and TSPoly_FrontBackVisibilityTest use it.

entries.name: Light_ResetSystem
entries.description: Per-mission light system reset: zeroes PolyFill_LineBrush and PolyFill_FillBrush's first dwords, the ten active light slots at 006c6130 (not their count 006c612c), runs Light_EnableModelSpaceTransform, fills the default index list 006c60ec with 0..31, memsets the polygon pipeline's scratch block 006c6158-006cbc87 (0x5b30 bytes: clip rings, face state from 006c6968, Poly_ViewCache, Poly_ScreenCache, Poly_ScreenPoints and its count 006cbc86), registers g_TSObjectTypeRegistry's bucket, and reinstalls the identity transform 006c6080 (Transform_Reset) as both 006c6078 and g_ModelTransformPtr.

entries.name: Raster_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser (_INIT_ entry 004a7bd6, pointer at 004a7bd8) for the renderer's globals: Transform_Ctor on g_ModelToView (006c6038), g_ViewToModel (006c6058) and the identity transform 006c6080; maybe_Point3I_Ctor on g_EyeInModelSpace; Rtl_ReturnArg on the projection centre 006c60b8; RectI_Ctor on 006c60c0; LineBrush_Ctor on PolyFill_LineBrush (006c60d0) and FillBrush_Ctor on PolyFill_FillBrush (006c60d8); then Rtl_VectorNew for Poly_ViewCache (1000 x 0xc, maybe_Point3I_Ctor), Poly_ScreenCache (1000 x 8) and Poly_ScreenPoints (0x20 x 8, both Rtl_ReturnArg). entries.name: FillBrush_Ctor

entries.name: TSGroup_ReadFromStream
entries.description: TSGroup's vtable +0x0c load method (group struct is 0x28 bytes, built by the type registry's tag-0x00140014 ctor 0048e7a4). Reads four int16 counts into +0x20 indexes / +0x22 points / +0x24 surfaces / +0x26 polys, allocates +0x10 / +0x14 / +0x18 / +0x1c for each, then streams them. The surface array at +0x18 is surfaceCount int32s read RAW -- no conversion of any kind -- so the value a poly renderer indexes really is the file's own {int16 colour, int16 flag} pair packed into one int32.
